title: Analyst II, IT
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of critical minerals transforming the future. With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals are fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking an Analyst II, IT Business Applications, Canada and International to join our Information Technology team in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a fixed-term contract position (12 Months) supporting Business Applications across Vale Base Metals' Canada and International operations. The successful candidate will lead and coordinate application projects and enhancements while supporting the ongoing reliability and effectiveness of enterprise applications.

Reporting to the Supervisor, Business Applications, Canada and International, the Analyst I/II will work across business, IT, and vendor teams to deliver application initiatives from planning through implementation and transition to support.

## Key Responsibilities

## Project and Enhancement Delivery

• Lead application implementations, upgrades, enhancements, integrations, and other technology initiatives.

• Define project scope, objectives, deliverables, schedules, resource needs, and dependencies.

• Develop and maintain project plans, milestones, budgets, RAID logs, action registers, and status reporting.

• Coordinate cross-functional business, IT, and vendor teams to deliver agreed outcomes.

• Monitor progress and proactively address schedule, scope, resource, and delivery challenges.

• Coordinate requirements, testing, training, deployment, go-live, and transition-to-support activities.

## Application Support and Continuous Improvement

• Provide functional and technical support for assigned enterprise applications.

• Coordinate investigation and resolution of incidents, problems, and service requests with internal teams and vendors.

• Support application releases, upgrades, testing, deployments, and lifecycle activities.

• Maintain application documentation, operational procedures, and knowledge of materials.

• Identify opportunities to improve application performance, reliability, user experience, and support processes.

• Balance application supports priorities with project delivery commitments.

## Stakeholder Engagement

• Build strong working relationships with business users and key stakeholders.

• Serve as the primary point of coordination for assigned projects and initiatives.

• Provide clear, concise project updates to stakeholders and leadership.

• Facilitate project meetings, workshops, governance reviews, decisions, and follow-up actions.

## Risk, Governance & Change

• Identify, assess, track, and manage project risks, issues, dependencies, assumptions, and changes.

• Develop mitigation plans and escalate significant risks or blockers as required.

• Ensure projects comply with applicable cybersecurity, privacy, technology governance, and change-management requirements.

• Support business readiness, communications, training, and user adoption.

## About You

## Experience

• 3-5+ years of experience in IT, business applications, technology project delivery, or related field.

• Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating application implementations, upgrades, enhancements, or technology projects.

• Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies.

• Experience working with cross-functional business and technical teams, and external vendors.

• Knowledge of enterprise business applications and integrated technology environments.

• Understanding IT Service Management (ITSM) principles and support processes.

• Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

• Experience with incident management, service requests, and application support activities.

• Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.

• Strong organizational, planning, and time-management abilities.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a global team environment.

• Commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and customer service excellence.

• French and/or Portuguese language skills are considered an asset.

## Education

• College diploma or university degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Project Management, Engineering, or related discipline.

• Equivalent education and relevant experience may be considered.

## Preferred Qualifications

• PMP, CAPM, PRINCE2, PMI-ACP, or equivalent project management certification.

• Experience supporting applications used in Human Resources, Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, Health & Safety, or Operational business functions.

• Experience with project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, Azure DevOps, or Smartsheet.

• Familiarity with project management and Agile delivery methodologies.

• Experience working within mining, industrial, manufacturing, or asset-intensive environments is considered an asset.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence.

The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home. Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Pay Grade: F5T

## Minimum Starting Salary: CAD 89,244

Apply by: Friday, Nov 06, 2026

title: Director, Voisey's Bay Operations
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Director, Voisey's Bay Operations to join our Leadership Team supporting our Vale Newfoundland and Labrador Operations.

This role is a permanent position, working a Monday to Friday schedule, based in St. John's, with significant travel to the Voisey's Bay Mine Site.

The Director of Voisey's Bay Operations holds overall accountability for the strategic leadership and operational performance of the Voisey's Bay mine site, a complex remote mining operation in Northern Labrador. The Director provides leadership across mining, processing, infrastructure, logistics, workforce, community commitments, and site services, with accountability for delivering safe, sustainable, and reliable operational performance.

Voisey's Bay encompasses two surface open-pit mines, two underground mines, processing and port facilities, tailings, utilities, maintenance, engineering, laboratories, power generation, transportation, accommodations, medical and recreational facilities, as well as significant externally contracted services.

The Director leads within the unique operating environment of Voisey's Bay, balancing safety, production, cost, and long-term value with the challenges of a remote fly-in/fly-out operation, including complex logistics, severe northern weather, environmental sensitivity, workforce rotations, supply-chain constraints, and site isolation.

The Director establishes the long-term strategic direction for Voisey's Bay Operations within a five-to-ten-year planning horizon, translating the Base Metals strategy into operational priorities, business plans and performance objectives. The role is accountable for strengthening organizational capability, optimizing assets, removing operational constraints, advancing technology and positioning Voisey's Bay for safe, sustainable and competitive long-term performance.

Voisey's Bay is located within the traditional territory of the Labrador Innu and Labrador Inuit. The Director plays an important leadership role in advancing Vale's commitments under the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and Nunatsiavut Government, including commitments related to employment, development, business participation,

environmental stewardship and the surrounding communities. More than 25% of the Voisey's Bay workforce comprises Labrador Inuit and Innu employees.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Provide leadership for health, safety, and operational risk, ensuring effective governance, systems, and controls are in place to manage major hazards, contractor safety, and operational risks.

• Lead overall operational performance to achieve safe, sustainable, and reliable production while meeting productivity, quality, cost, and business objectives.

• Lead the ramp-up and optimization of mining and processing operations, identifying and removing operational constraints and driving continuous improvement in throughput, reliability, and performance.

• Manage the complexities of remote northern operations, including workforce rotations, logistics, transportation, weather-related challenges and supply-chain requirements.

• Ensure effective stewardship of site assets and capital, optimizing asset performance and executing capital investments to support long-term reliability, capacity, and sustainable operations.

• Lead and develop a high-performing workforce and leadership team, including unionized, non-unionized, professional, and technical employees, with a focus on workforce planning, talent development, succession and performance.

• Establish and continuously improve operational systems, processes, and technologies to strengthen safety, productivity, reliability and long-term organizational capability.

• Ensure compliance with environmental, legal, regulatory, and IBA commitments, while modelling the organization's values and maintaining strong relationships with Indigenous and community stakeholders.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Flexible work arrangements

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## About You

## Education:

• Undergraduate degree in Mining Engineering is required. A relevant engineer discipline may be considered.

• MBA or relevant postgraduate business qualification is considered an asset.

## Experience:

• Minimum of 15 years of progressive mining leadership experience, including significant leadership experience in underground mining operations, with demonstrated accountability for safety, production, cost, people, and overall operational performance.

• Demonstrated experience building effective relationships with Indigenous partners, communities, government and key stakeholders.

• Significant experience operating in a remote fly-in/fly-out environment, with demonstrated ability to manage the logistical, workforce and operational complexities of remote northern operations.

## Skills:

• Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing unionized, non-unionized, professional and technical teams.

• Strong background in operational risk, asset management, maintenance, capital planning, project execution and contractor management.

• Strong knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador occupational health and safety requirements and associated operational risk management practices.

• Proven strategic and commercial acumen, with the ability to translate long-term business strategy into operational plans and results.

• Demonstrated change leadership and organizational agility, including the ability to lead technology adoption, operational transformation and growth.

• Exceptional leadership presence, emotional intelligence and the ability to influence, engage and build trust across diverse stakeholder groups.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role. At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first

gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

description:

title: Research and Insights Analyst
employer: Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
description:
Research and Insights Analyst Department of Education and Early Childhood DevelopmentContract Open CompetitionFredericton

## At the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (EECD),

## we are dedicated to fulfilling New Brunswick`s educational mission.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

?Who we are:

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

## What you will do:

The Research and Insights Analyst supports evidence-informed decision-making across EECD by conducting research, analysis, and knowledge synthesis activities that inform departmental priorities and strategic initiatives. Working under the direction of the Research and Insights Lead, the position contributes to the development of actionable insights through the collection, analysis, and interpretation of qualitative and quantitative information. The role supports research projects, evaluations, environmental scans, and reporting activities while helping to strengthen the Department's capacity to use evidence in policy, program, and operational decision-making.

The successful candidate`s primary responsibilities will include:

## Research and Knowledge Synthesis

• Conduct literature reviews, environmental scans, jurisdictional reviews, and other research activities to support departmental priorities.

• Source, review, and synthesize academic research, best practices, policy documents, and program information into concise and accessible summaries.

• Prepare research briefs, evidence summaries, presentations, and other knowledge products for internal stakeholders.

## Data Analysis and Insight Development

• Support qualitative and quantitative data analysis activities, including survey analysis, focus groups, interviews, and other research methods.

• Assist in identifying trends, patterns, and emerging issues within research findings and administrative data.

• Contribute to the development of reports, dashboards, presentations, and recommendations that support decision-making.

• Use research and analytical tools to organize, analyze, and communicate findings effectively.

## Research Project Support

• Support the planning, coordination, and implementation of research, evaluation, and analytical projects.

• Assist in defining project objectives, timelines, deliverables, and data requirements for departmental initiatives.

• Contribute to the collection, validation, and organization of data and information required for research activities.

## Operational and Administrative Support

• Maintain research records, project documentation, and data files in accordance with established processes and standards.

• Support the development and maintenance of research tools, templates, procedures, and internal documentation.

• Assist with quality assurance activities to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of research outputs.

## Responsive and Collaborative Support

• Respond to emerging and time-sensitive requests for research, analysis, and information.

• Collaborate with branch and departmental staff to provide evidence, data, and insights in support of priority initiatives.

• Contribute to a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and evidence-informed practice.

## Reporting and Collaboration

• Report to the Research and Insights Lead.

• Work closely with colleagues across Assessment and Analysis Services, Educational Services, and other EECD branches to support research and analytical priorities.

• Contribute to the successful delivery of strategic initiatives, including the Education Plan and other departmental priorities.

## Who you are:

You are a curious, analytical, and detail-oriented professional who enjoys transforming complex information into meaningful insights that support decision-making. You are skilled at gathering, synthesizing, and interpreting both qualitative and quantitative information, and can communicate findings clearly to a variety of audiences. You thrive in a collaborative environment, balance multiple priorities effectively, and demonstrate strong judgment when responding to emerging requests.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Need to have:

• Bachelor`s degree in psychology, statistics, or business, or a related field with a minimum of 2 years of experience.

• Experience conducting research activities, including literature reviews, environmental scans, and information synthesis.

• Familiarity with qualitative and quantitative research methods and analytical approaches.

• Experience working with research, surveys, spreadsheets is considered an asset.

• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to identify key findings and translate information into meaningful insights.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing reports, summaries, and presentations.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated ability to respond effectively to changing priorities and emerging information needs.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability on your application.

## Nice to have:

• Experience in public sector, education, policy, or research-intensive environments.

• Experience supporting program evaluation, performance measurement, or continuous improvement initiatives.

• Experience communicating research findings to non-technical audiences and decision-makers.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

• Communication

## Technical Competencies:

• Report Writing and Knowledge Translation

title: Mechanical Trades Supervisor
description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Power Production - Lingan Generating Station

Location: Lingan, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Regular, Full-time - On site

Closing Date: November 12th, 2026

We are currently looking for a Mechanical Trades Supervisor to join our Power Production team in a permanent position. Reporting to the Maintenance Superintendent, you will be responsible for the day-to-day supervision of Mechanical Trades at Lingan Generating Station.

Key elements of this role include:

## As a Mechanical Trades Supervisor:
Primary Responsibilities
• Provide leadership, supervision, and technical direction for the maintenance, repair, and troubleshooting of mechanical equipment across thermal generating stations.

• Plan, coordinate, schedule, and oversee maintenance and utility work in collaboration with Operations, Planning, Engineering, Procurement, and other functional teams.

• Support multiple generating stations through a scheduled field presence to ensure maintenance activities are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with operational requirements.

• Lead maintenance teams by assigning work, monitoring performance, and optimizing resources to achieve reliability, safety, and productivity objectives.

• Foster a strong safety culture by ensuring compliance with all Occupational Health and Safety requirements, supporting High Risk Work processes, and promoting safe work practices.

• Develop, coach, and support employees through ongoing performance management, skills development, and knowledge transfer.

• Coordinate activities across shifts and departments to support plant reliability and operational performance.

• Ensure maintenance work is executed safely, cost-effectively, and in alignment with station objectives.

Secondary Responsibilities
• Collaborate with station leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to support maintenance planning and operational goals.

• Ensure compliance with environmental regulations and support environmental management system requirements and initiatives.

• Prepare and maintain documentation, including maintenance reports, work procedures, safety documentation, and employee performance evaluations.

• Participate in leadership development, continuous improvement, and workforce capability-building initiatives.

• Promote teamwork, accountability, and operational excellence within the maintenance and utility teams.

• Support compliance with applicable NERC/NPCC reliability standards and regulatory requirements.

• Maintain accountability for personal safety and the safety of employees, contractors, and others under your direction.

This position is considered a safety sensitive position. as such, the successful candidate must comply with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Policy which requires a confidential pre-employment alcohol and drug test in accordance with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Procedure.

These skills will make you successful:

You recognize yourself in most of the following competencies, and where possible possess the skills and experience listed below:

## Qualifications:

• Education: Journeyperson/Red Seal Certification in an Industrial Trade, Mechanical Engineering degree eligible for membership with Engineers Nova Scotia, or a Mechanical Technologist Diploma eligible for membership with TechNova.

• Experience: You must have a minimum of 5 years' experience in a modern power generation facility or other heavy industrial environment with a thorough knowledge of preventative maintenance programs, continuous improvement programs and maintenance planning and scheduling.

• Safety Advocacy: Strong advocate for safety with a demonstrated track record of enhancing organizational safety culture.

• Additional Assets: Other Certifications, diploma, or trade qualifications are advantageous.

## Skills and Abilities:

• Industrial Acumen: Experience in fast-paced, multi-faceted, service-oriented heavy industrial operations is beneficial.

• Communication: Excellent oral and written communication skills.

• Interpersonal Skills: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to function effectively in a team environment.

• Self-Starter: Proven organizational and analytical skills with demonstrated multi-tasking abilities.

• Technical Proficiency: Strong computer skills.

About Us
The Marine Services division of the Department of Public Works maintains and operates the provincial ferries including: Englishtown, Little Narrows, Country Harbor, LaHave River, Tancook Islands, and Digby Neck. Our Marine staff help to further connect and expand Nova Scotia's transportation network; all the while ensuring the safe and efficient operation of our Ferries. Our provincial ferries operate 24 hours a day, 365 days per year.

If you're looking for an exciting and challenging opportunity and career growth, with a daily view of our beautiful Atlantic waters, then we have your perfect opportunity.

About Our Opportunity
The Provincial Mobile Service Mechanic is responsible for performing preventative maintenance, annual renewal and related marine repairs as established by Department policy and Transport Canada Marine Safety for all Ferries servicing the Province of Nova Scotia primarily in Cape Breton.

Primary Accountabilities
In addition, the repairs being carried out are to be done in a manner which is cost effective while at the same time minimizing ferry "downtime". Core to this position is the ability to be versatile in adapting to the needs of the operations while executing marine repairs in accordance with the Department's preventive maintenance policy, OEM requirements and Transport Canada guidelines.

Qualifications and ExperienceYou have completed High School and a Provincial Certificate of Qualification in the Truck and Transport, Heavy Equipment, or Automotive Trade, plus five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience. In addition, you have demonstrated oral and written communication skills and the ability to work in a team environment. A valid Nova Scotia driver's license is required. Please include a current Driver's Abstract with your application. Provincial Certificates of Qualification in Heavy Duty Equipment or Marine experience would be considered an asset. Knowledge of computer controlled engine diagnostic technology and competency would also be considered an asset. The successful completion of training and knowledge of the Occupational Health and Safety Act, First Aid and WHMIS would also be considered assets. You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required. We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, skill-testing of basic math/literacy assessment, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.Benefits

The position requires regular travel throughout the province, including assignments away from the employee's designated work location. Travel may involve overnight stays and remaining at another work location for several consecutive days. Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.Additional Information
There is one (1) opportunity for a Year-Round position based in the Miller Lake mechanical branch.

Normal hours of work are 8am - 4:30pm. If equipment breaks down, we will count on you to help things get up and running again. Therefore, you will be on-call outside of your regular work schedule.

Qualifications and Experience

506-877-7707 or visit www.moncton.ca/careers for information on the hiring and application process at the City of Moncton.

WORKING AT THE CITY OF MONCTON:
Moncton is a vibrant and culturally rich community. It is the first officially bilingual city in Canada, as well as one of the best places in Canada to do business. Moncton is also known as the economic, sports, tourism and entertainment hub of Atlantic Canada. City of Moncton employees strive to maintain the city's reputation as one of the best places in Canada to live, study, work and play.

This position is a unionized position. The City of Moncton offers an attractive salary and benefits package in accordance to the City Hall Employees Association / PSAC Local 60200 Collective Agreement.

## CHEA Collective Agreement

## City of Moncton Salary and Wage Scale

Page Break

EDUCATION:

• Must have post-secondary education from an accredited institution where specialized computer skills were acquired or have a minimum of 1 year of experience performing electronic disclosure.

• High School graduate or equivalency.

EXPERIENCE:

• Background in a police environment would be an asset.

• Experience and knowledge of police records and filing systems would be an asset.

• Experience working with Adobe products would be an asset

LANGUAGE:

• The ability to function fluently in both official languages (English and French) is a requirement. As per provincial language proficiency standards, functional is determined to be at the Intermediate+ (2+) level or higher.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• Knowledge of techniques, methods and procedures around the use of a variety of databases and police information systems to enter, search/query, verify, link data, manipulate, report on (in preformatted report forms) and print data from electronic formatting applications and/or Records Management Systems.

• Knowledge of electronic formatting applications and associated hardware and software, for scanning, imaging and uploading complex forms of data such as photos, audio and video clips.

• Knowledge of the information management process, basic knowledge of police terminology, and familiarity with documents collected throughout an investigation (such as Investigation Reports, banking documents, contracts, and warrants) in order to properly organize incoming data for entry into electronic formatting applications. This knowledge is also required in order to review, extract and analyze all investigative materials for consistency, while ensuring the information is compliant with established rules and standards.

• Knowledge of relevant sections of the Access to Information and Privacy Acts, Government and Departmental Security and Records Management procedures for the handling of protected and classified material(s), as well as departmental policy to protect and handle investigative data. Understanding of basic principles of case law is required in order to recognize and understand the importance of keeping investigative material in the same context as received for conversion and capture into electronic case management applications.

• Proofreading and editing techniques are required to read investigative documents (such as investigator reports, surveillance reports, scanned paper exhibits); to identify key data (such as Persons, Locations, Telephone Numbers) requiring vetting before being uploaded into the specified electronic formatting application

• Listening, reading and comprehension skills are required to understand and accurately apply policy and procedures (i.e. Business Rules) for data entry, transcribing and linking duties.

• Writing skills are required in order to maintain detailed notes suitable for presentation, and ability to testify in court to explain actions and observations while handling investigative material(s) and the use of electronic case management applications to disclose investigative data.

• Communication skills are required to discuss data from source documents that may require further clarification from the Disclosure Team Leader prior to capturing the data in the electronic case management applications.

• Must have extensive computer knowledge of spreadsheets and databases, word processing, Windows applications and email. Example: Groupwise/Excel/Word/PowerPoint. Will be required to use RCMP programs such as PROS (Police Reporting Occurrence System) and CPIC(Canadian Police Information Centre).

• Must have excellent time management skills; attention to detail; the capacity to prioritize by assessing situations to determine urgency; ability to develop a work schedule, set goals, create / implement action plans and monitor progress towards goals; and ability to make clear, timely decisions.

• Must have a high degree of accuracy and concentration and perform quality work especially when faced with a busy environment.

OTHER:

• Must have minimum keyboarding skills of forty (40) WPM.

• Must be willing to upgrade skills as required by changes in the workplace.

• It is a condition of employment that the incumbent must be of the highest integrity and character and will be subjected to RCMP security screening. This involves background and character investigation of successful applicants and their immediate families. This is required prior to the necessary level of security clearance being granted for this position. Must maintain necessary RCMP security clearance requirements for this position throughout the duration of employment. Similarly, the incumbent's use of all police information will be in accordance with R.C.M.P. policy, regulations and directives. Since the work is of a confidential nature, the incumbent must be prepared to undertake an Oath of Affirmation of Secrecy.

EFFORT AND JUDGEMENT:

• Intellectual effort is required to comprehend and comply with an extensive and detailed set of Business Rules. This involves working in a number of different electronic formats, as well as inputting and processing a variety of data types. There is a requirement to quickly switch between the various electronic formats while correctly adhering to different sets of business rules (i.e. each form has its' own set of business rules).

• Judgement is required to make limited data entry decisions, as the Business Rules are not exhaustive and do not describe every piece of data to be entered. Determinations required may include deciding if a person's name is an alias, a typing error or a new subject for example. Intellectual effort is required to determine how to correctly handle the data in question through system checks, knowledge of the file and source investigators.

• Decisions and steps taken are generally made in accordance with established guidelines, processes and policies. The correct interpretation and application of policy and procedures (i.e. Business Rules), is imperative for the accurate and meaningful analysis of the investigative data entered by the investigative team. Errors made could cause considerable loss of work time and productivity.

• The position requires appropriate diplomacy and discretion.

• Must use judgment and professionalism in dealing with clients.

• Requires a high level of judgment appropriate to applying established practices, policies or procedures to standard work assignments and resolving frequent problems.

SUPERVISION:

• Must be able to work with minimal supervision and make decisions that reflect the established objectives of the department. Also requires initiative or ingenuity to resolve frequent minor problems in situations not always covered by established practices, procedures or policies.

• No requirement to supervise other employees; however, may be required to provide limited advice and guidance to new employees on occasion.

CONDITIONS OF WORK:

• The incumbent may be required to work overtime on short notice. Scheduled start time can range between 6:30 AM and 8:30 AM.

• Required to spend extended periods of time in a seated position focused on computer monitors and performing repetitive motions.

• This position may be subjected to highly sensitive and confidential information and be of graphic nature that may have a strong emotional impact and stress. Graphic material may include but is not limited to murder scenes and victim(s), autopsy photos, sexual assault videos, 911 audios and material relating to child exploitation investigations.

• The working conditions are in concurrence with the CHEA/PSAC Local 60200 Collective Agreement. This position is based on a thirty-five (35) hour workweek.

description:
Position Type:
Permanent

2026-12-14

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

TeleHealth provides residents of Nova Scotia and PEI in non-emergency situations a standardized phone number to call and speak about their symptoms or illness with a registered nurse, 24 hours a day, seven days a week. TeleHealth Nurses provide telephone triage, health information and professional nursing care to more than 100,000 patients annually through the use of information and communication technologies, and with the support of computer-based decision support software, clinical guidelines, protocols and other resources.

TeleHealth Nurses work from their private home office. Working 8-hour shifts on a rotating schedule creates a good work-life balance, however, 10- and 12-hour shifts can be accommodated. During a regular work day, the TeleHealth nurse may receive up to 40 calls per shift. No two calls are the same - the TeleHealth Nurse will encounter a wide variety of health care concerns including but not limited to the fields of pediatrics, obstetrics, and geriatrics.

TeleHealth leaderships provide on the job training, frequent feedback and coaching. We understand the challenges that come from working remotely so we ensure that support is available for the nurses 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

We currently have Part-time and Full-time work from home opportunities available in both Nova Scotia and PEI servicing both provinces. Please note you are required to be licensed to practice within the province you reside.

## Duties and Responsibilities:

• Navigates the guidelines and search functions, applies established policies and guidelines, assesses the patient's condition/situation and documents the assessment.

• Reviews recommendations to the caller which are congruent with nursing guideline standards and clinical judgment.

• Provides information which is clinically relevant and empowers the caller to make appropriate decisions, including the decision to self-care.

• Accurately and completely documents clinical and other relevant notes within the computer software program in a timely manner throughout and immediately after the call.

• Liaises effectively between caller and third party in critical situations, such as need for ambulance transport, police intervention, suicidal caller, suspected or actual child abuse or other situations in which information is not consistent or may be disputed.

• Adheres to time utilization guidelines and ensures that personal workflow supports the service to better meet the demand for Telecare services.

## Qualifications and Requirements:

• Clinical nursing experience, preferably in an acute care environment, such as Emergency Department, general medical-surgical or intensive care unit, and/or relevant community health setting, such as public health. Minimum 3 years of clinical experience (5 years preferred).

• An active license and good standing as a Registered Nurse with the provincial nursing body legislated to regulate and license nurses and compliance with all applicable laws pertaining to the practice of nursing in the province.

• Diploma from recognized and/or accredited nursing school. Bachelor degree is preferred.

• Excellent communication, telephone and customer relation skills.

• Good critical thinking, sound clinical decision-making and problem-solving skills.

• Basic knowledge and competence in the use of computers and keyboarding.

• Reliable wired internet connectivity utilizing approved High Speed DSL, Cable or FiberOp.

• Appropriate home space meeting requirements as cited in "Work at Home" guidelines.

• Ability to travel if needed.

• Fluency in English (oral and written) is required and fluency in English and French (oral and written) is preferred.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the citizens we serve. We are committed to building an inclusive team that represents a variety of backgrounds, cultures, races, perspectives and skills. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities. title: Construction Manager – High-Rise Residential Construction
description:
Umbrella Design is partnering with a client developing a 30-storey residential tower in Halifax, Nova Scotia, and is seeking a highly experienced Construction Manager to lead this landmark project.

The ideal candidate will bring a proven track record of delivering multiple high-rise residential developments, overseeing every stage of the project from preconstruction through to occupancy and closeout. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a significant development in Atlantic Canada's largest city.

## What you will do:

• Be accountable for the overall delivery of one 30-storey project (>$100M in value): scope, schedule, budget, quality and safety.

• Lead the project's construction team, including the Site Superintendent and Project Manager, over its 4-year build-out.

• The Construction Manager is the owner's senior construction lead. You set the project strategy, hold the budget and schedule, manage contracts and consultants, and give the site and project teams what they need to build efficiently, safely and to the highest standards.

• Responsibilities

• Project Leadership: Take full ownership of project delivery from preconstruction to occupancy and closeout. Set direction for the site and project teams and hold them to clear targets.

• Budget and Cost Control: Own the construction budget. Approve and track costs, manage change orders and contingency, and forecast cost-to-complete.

• Master Schedule: Set and maintain the master project schedule. Work with the Site Superintendent to align site sequencing with procurement, approvals and owner milestones.

• Contracts and Procurement: Lead tendering, trade award and contract negotiation. Manage subcontractor and supplier performance, claims and disputes.

• Safety: Champion a culture of safety across the project. Ensure full compliance with Nova Scotia OH&S standards and that site safety programs are properly resourced.

• Design and Consultant Coordination: Lead coordination with architects, engineers and other consultants. Manage RFIs, design changes and constructability reviews before they reach the field.

• Permits and Approvals: Manage permits, inspections and regulatory approvals with the municipality and other authorities.

• Quality and Handover: Set quality standards and oversee inspection and deficiency programs. Lead commissioning, occupancy and turnover to the owner.

• Risk Management: Identify and manage commercial, schedule and site risks. Plan for weather, market conditions, labour availability and neighbourhood impacts.

• Team Development: Recruit, mentor and evaluate the site and project management team.

## What you bring:

• 12+ years in construction, with at least 5 in a senior construction or project management role on high-rise residential work.

• A track record of delivering projects over $100M on budget and on schedule.

• Strong command of construction contracts, cost control and scheduling, with experience in tools such as Procore and Primavera P6 or MS Project.

• Proven ability to lead superintendents, project managers, consultants and trades.

• A degree or diploma in engineering, construction management or a related field is an asset, as is a PMP or Gold Seal certification.

## Communication and Reporting

• Report directly to the owner as their primary construction representative. The Site Superintendent and Project Manager report to you. Prepare monthly cost, schedule and progress reports for the owner, and lead regular owner, consultant and project team meetings.

## Compensation and Benefits

• Full time- 3 year contract

• Base salary of $160,000 to $190,000, based on experience

Submit your resume with a project list. For each project, include the building type, number of storeys, project value, your role and dates.

## Temporary 1-year Contract, with possibility of renewal

## About CMHA of NB

The Canadian Mental Health Association of New Brunswick Inc. (CMHA of NB) is part of a nationwide, voluntary organization that that envisions a country where mental health is a universal human right. CMHA of NB work is guided by the mission of ensuring that all people in New Brunswick experience good mental health and well-being.

CMHA of NB is STEADFAST and has long fought to improve the state of mental health in New Brunswick, yet acknowledges that the work is ongoing and remains committed to this important task. CMHA of NB is INCLUSIVE and strives for all people in New Brunswick to see themselves represented and served by CMHA of NB. The organization values the voice of those who have experienced mental illness and recognize a diverse range of mental health approaches.

CMHA of NB is PROACTIVE, with leaders who value action over mere talk, and is committed to innovation and forward-thinking to continually address and improve mental health in New Brunswick. Furthermore, CMHA of NB is COMPASSIONATE, approaching its mission with empathy, care, love, and kindness.

CMHA of NB, being COLLABORATIVE, mobilizes and marshals resources, partners, and people to come together to realize necessary changes in our communities and in the mental health system in New Brunswick. CMHA of NB provides a wide range of services and supports to people who are experiencing mental illness, their families, friends, and the public. One of the core goals of these services is to help people with mental illness develop the personal tools to lead meaningful and productive lives.

## Position Summary:

Under the supervision of the provincial office of Integrated Youth Services - New Brunswick (IYS-NB), and in collaboration with the Interdisciplinary Research Chair on Child and Youth Mental Health, the Scientific and Clinical Coordinator will support the implementation of a capacity-building initiative within the IYS-NB learning health system. This includes the development and application of evidence-based tools and practices related to measurement-based care (MBC) across the IYS-NB network.

## Main Responsibilities:

Management, Coordination, and Leadership

· Co-supervise research coordinators working in local IYS sites to integrate measurement-based care into clinical practice.

· Participate in managing the budget for IYS initiatives.

· Oversee the creation and maintenance of required documentation, including plans, timelines, budgets, deliverables, reports, and stakeholder contributions.

· Contribute to hiring processes, contracts, training, and supervision of students and staff.

· Serve as co-lead on coordination and governance committees (e.g., coordination committee).

· Actively participate in strategic and research meetings with provincial and national partners.

· Contribute to the preparation of annual reports, progress documents, and other required deliverables.

· Support the execution of other interdisciplinary projects associated with the Chair.

· Perform other duties as required within the scope of the position.

Research, Implementation, and Knowledge Translation

· Develop a collaborative implementation plan for measurement-based care across IYS-NB sites with provincial partners.

· Prepare and facilitate team meetings and manage communications and relationships with involved partners.

· Support the development of knowledge translation products such as practical guides, workshops, and clinical implementation manuals related to measurement-based care.

· Contribute to the development and implementation of technological infrastructure and data collection processes required for measurement-based care.

· Provide coaching and consultation to clinical staff at IYS sites to support the implementation of measurement-based care practices, ensuring effective data capture and optimal use.

· Collaborate with youth, family members, and First Nations partners to ensure that measurement-based care resources are accessible, inclusive, and culturally appropriate.

· Ensure that the implementation of measurement-based care in clinical practice reflects the voices and needs of youth and families.

· Participate in the implementation of research projects related to integrated youth services (e.g., protocol review, ethics applications, data collection, analysis and interpretation, participation in team meetings, collaboration with governmental and non-governmental partners).

· Contribute to knowledge dissemination (e.g., scientific articles and posters).

Qualification:

· Master's or PhD in psychology, social work, or a related clinical field.

· Current membership, or eligibility for membership, in a recognized professional association.

· Minimum of 3 years of clinical experience working with youth and families, preferably in community or integrated service settings.

· Demonstrated experience in implementing measurement-based care or evidence-based practices in clinical and multidisciplinary contexts.

· Experience in training and supervision.

· Strong experience and skills in community-based research and project management.

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate research into practice.

· Proficiency in both English and French languages and experience working with First Nations communities are strong assets.

· A valid Work Permit is mandatory for temporary residents.

· Residency in New Brunswick (NB) or willingness to relocate is mandatory.

· Satisfactory Criminal Record and Vulnerable Sector Check is mandatory.

## Core Competencies:

· Interpersonal Relationship

· Networking

· Communication

· Service Orientation

· Self-Development

· Accountability

· Values, Ethics, Integrity

## Other Attributes:

## Working Conditions:

## · Work Environment:

o Ocasional travel within New Brunswick to attend meetings, community events, and community partners engagements.

o Collaborative and team-oriented work culture, with engagement across multiple departments and external partners.

## · Work Hours:

o Full-time position with a standard workweek of 35 hours.

o Occasional evening and weekend work may be required.

## · Physical & Mental Demands:

o Requires sustained periods of sitting, working at a computer, and attending virtual or in-person meetings.

o Fast-paced environment with multiple priorities, requiring strong time management and decision-making skills.

o Emotional resilience needed when handling sensitive mental health-related topics and high-stakes advocacy.

o High level of autonomy and accountability, requiring strategic thinking and proactive problem-solving.

Downhome Magazine is looking for a personable, motivated and relationship-focused Account Manager to join our sales team. - Downhome Magazine

- Inside Labrador Magazine
- Downhome Events & Sponsored Events
- Great Auk Winery

Travel is part of the job, so being comfortable and self-motivated to get out there and meet people is important.
Who You Are
You might be an experienced account manager, media salesperson or advertising representative. Or maybe you're a seasoned sales professional who already travels the province., knows the businesses and communities in your territory and has spent years building relationships and a strong network.

- Naturally personable and comfortable building genuine relationships
- Confident communicating with businesses and decision makers
- Self-motivated and comfortable taking the lead

- Able to manage multiple clients, brands and projects simultaneously

Sales and account management experience is preferred. Experience in media, advertising, retail, tourism or corporate sales is considered an asset.
Why Downhome?
This position isn't just one sales job selling one product. You'll be working with one of Newfoundland and Labrador's most recognized media and lifestyle brands while helping grow a diverse portfolio that reaches into print, digital, events, tourism and emerging products. One day you'll be talking advertising with a local business, the next you could be developing an event partnership, introducing a client to a new digital opportunity or helping them find a creative way to reach the Downhome audience.

The Department of Emergency Management is responsible for leading disaster and emergency planning, preparedness, response and recovery activities on behalf of the Province of Nova Scotia. The objective of the Department is to ensure that Nova Scotians are safe, prepared and resilient in the face of disasters and emergencies. The Department leads the coordination and co-operation of partners and resources during provincial-level critical incidents, supports municipal and other partners in regional-level and local events, administers the province's 911 service, maintains critical communications infrastructure and supports operations of our regional emergency management centres. The Department also works to ensure critical government services continue to function during and after critical events.

The Planning and Preparedness Branch enhances preparedness, reduces vulnerabilities, and ensures a coordinated response to critical incidents and emergencies by:

• Standing up and deploying the Nova Scotia Guard

• Reviewing comprehensive emergency management programs by the province and municipalities and ensuring they are robust

• Conducting thorough risk assessments and advising on mitigation strategies

• Administering the Disaster Financial Assistance program to ensure recovery takes place as quickly as possible

• Leading strategic policy, including the management of federal and regional agreements and management of legislation, regulations, policies, establishing standards and preparedness initiatives

• Supporting effective risk management and business continuity for the Province, municipalities, and critical infrastructure partners

• Managing the resiliency office

The successful candidate will work under minimal direction and have a very good knowledge of office practices and procedures and a comprehensive knowledge of departmental functions.

description:
## Join Our Team and Inspire the Next Generation of Women+ in Skilled Trades

Are you looking for a great team environment where your work makes a real difference? Do you enjoy traveling throughout our beautiful province and inspiring girls and women+ to explore rewarding careers in the skilled trades?

If you're looking for a meaningful career with a collaborative team dedicated to creating opportunities and strengthening New Brunswick's skilled trades workforce, we'd love to hear from you.

## About MAP Strategic Workforce Services Inc.

MAP Strategic Workforce Services Inc. (MAPSWS) is a provincial non-profit organization committed to promoting careers in the skilled trades while fostering inclusive and welcoming workplaces across New Brunswick. Through our four provincial programs, NB-MAP, New Boots, First in Trades (FIT), and the Skilled Trades Exploration Program (STEP), we connect New Brunswickers with career opportunities, build strong industry partnerships, and support the growth of a diverse skilled trades workforce.

We are currently seeking a full-time New Boots Coordinator to join our team. Reporting to the Executive Director, the successful candidate will coordinate and deliver the New Boots: Progressing Women+ in Skilled Trades program throughout New Brunswick.

New Boots is a provincial initiative that encourages girls and women+ to explore careers in the skilled trades through hands-on activities, mentorship, networking, career exploration, and employer engagement.

## Key Responsibilities

• Promote and advocate for skilled trades career pathways to girls, women+, and youth throughout New Brunswick.

• Support the growth of the New Boots network by engaging participants, mentors, employers, and industry partners while connecting members with employment opportunities, hands-on workshops, networking events, and visits to post-secondary institutions.

• Deliver presentations and represent MAPSWS at career fairs, schools, conferences, industry events, and community organizations.

• Plan, coordinate, and facilitate hands-on skilled trades activities in schools across New Brunswick. This is a core responsibility of the position and requires extensive planning, regular travel, transporting program materials, setting up activities, and engaging with students throughout the province.

• Success in this role requires confidence working directly with youth, speaking in front of groups, and representing the organization throughout New Brunswick.

• Contribute to regular content creation and management of social media platforms (ie: Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn).

• Develop, maintain, and strengthen relationships with government departments, employers, industry associations, unions, educational institutions, community organizations, and New Boots network members.

• Prepare quarterly reports and maintain accurate program documentation and records.

• Collaborate in the planning and delivery of MAPSWS events, including conferences, career fairs, workshops, school activities, networking events, and community outreach initiatives.

• Collaborate with the Executive Director and MAPSWS team to support strategic initiatives and ensure the successful delivery of program objectives.

• Carry out other duties as assigned.

## Essential Qualifications

• Applicants must clearly demonstrate how they meet the following qualifications:

• University degree, college diploma, Red Seal certification, or current apprenticeship in a designated skilled trade.

• Preferred areas of study include Skilled Trades, Education, Social Sciences, Communications, Marketing, Career Development, or related disciplines.

• Valid Class 5 driver's license with access to a reliable vehicle.

• Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout New Brunswick, including regular overnight travel.

• Ability to obtain a Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening.

## Asset Qualifications

• Preference may be given to candidates who possess one or more of the following:

• Bilingualism (English and French, both written and spoken).

• Knowledge of New Brunswick's skilled trades sector and apprenticeship system.

• Experience working with Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives and/or Equity-Deserving Groups.

• Experience facilitating workshops, presentations, or educational programming.

• Experience building partnerships with industry, employers, educational institutions, government, or community organizations.

• Teamwork and collaboration

At MAP Strategic Workforce Services, you'll become part of a passionate team committed to creating opportunities for New Brunswickers and strengthening our skilled trades workforce.

About Us
The Labour Standards Division is responsible for the Labour Standards Code and related regulations, which establish the basic rights and responsibilities of provincially regulated employers and workers in Nova Scotia. The legislation provides a dispute resolution mechanism and enforcement tools for addressing complaints under the Code and establishes licensing and registration requirements in relation to the recruitment and hiring of foreign workers.
We help people understand and comply with our legislation and provide a fair, accessible and responsive dispute resolution system.
We know our work can be challenging and often deals with people in difficult situations ? we strive to create a welcoming, respectful, safe, supportive, and inclusive workplace culture.

About Our Opportunity
As the Manager, Information and Dispute Resolution, you will play an important leadership role in supporting the effective delivery of inquiry and dispute resolution services within the Labour Standards Division.
In this role, you will lead a team responsible for providing information, resolving disputes, and supporting the administration and enforcement of the Labour Standards Code and regulations. You will oversee day-to-day operations, manage workflow and resources, monitor service quality, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how services are delivered to Nova Scotians.
You will also manage complex complaint files, applying your knowledge of labour standards legislation, regulations, and legal principles to evaluate evidence and make well-reasoned decisions. Your ability to balance operational demands, sound decision-making, and people leadership will help support fair, timely, and consistent services for employers and workers.
This is an opportunity for an experienced leader who enjoys solving complex problems, developing people, and contributing to quality public service.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Manager, you will provide leadership and operational oversight to ensure information and dispute resolution services are delivered effectively, consistently, and in a timely manner.
Your key responsibilities will include:

• Manage complaint intake, assignment and workflow in the division, monitor key performance indicators and recommend and implement changes to support continuous process improvement.

• Manage a team of officers and provide effective guidance to support their settlement, investigation and adjudication work.

• Review and provide feedback on officers' written adjudication work ensuring their investigation work is complete, they have correctly applied the legislation and their decision is sound.

• Manage a small caseload of complex files, conduct thorough investigations in an impartial, fair and timely manner, make findings of fact and legal findings, and issue written reasoned decisions.

• Promote a safe, supportive, inclusive, and welcoming workplace that values diversity, fosters employee recognition and encourages employee development and engagement.

Through your leadership and sound judgement, you will help promote consistent administration of labour standards legislation, fair dispute resolution, quality decision-making, and effective service to Nova Scotia employers and workers.

You have a degree in a related field such as law plus several years of relevant experience.
You demonstrate relevant experience in interpreting, applying, and analyzing legislation, regulations, or policies. You have well developed investigation related skills with experience in areas such as research, issue recognition, and fact finding. You have an aptitude for dealing with complex issues, strong analytical skills, tact and diplomacy, and capacity for decisive action.
You are a motivational leader who embraces the values of kindness, integrity, accountability, personal learning and growth, respect, innovation, and collaboration. You apply the concepts of equity, diversity, and inclusion to all areas of your work and support your team and colleagues to do the same.
You have well-developed planning and organizational skills with the ability to multi-task and adapt in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities and deadlines. You are a problem solver and innovator who generates, promotes, and implements new ideas, and resolves concerns. You have excellent communication skills, both oral and written, and use these skills to foster effective relationships with others, including collaborative relationships to achieve common goals.
You have experience dealing with frustrated and upset individuals and can deescalate situations by seeking to understand others' perspectives, remaining calm and respectful, and communicating effectively.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The Early Childhood Development Division is responsible to ensure the bridging of early childhood services (public, community and private services) and school services to build a continuum of learning from birth to high school graduation. Early childhood programs and services have been aligned with the seven school districts, both geographically and linguistically.

The vision for Early Childhood in New Brunswick is that all children will grow to their fullest potential with dignity, a sense of self-worth, and a zest for living and learning. It is a holistic vision that seeks to provide the environment and resources needed to support dynamic development in young children who are: curious, courageous and confident in their pursuit of knowledge and skills; secure in their linguistic and cultural identities; respectful of diversity; and contributing to the development of a just and democratic society that nurtures connection and care for life on earth.

The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is hiring knowledgeable, collaborative, and results oriented individuals to fill the role of Early Learning Consultant in the Anglophone East School District territory.

## What will you do:

Reporting to the Regional Director of Early Childhood Services and working within the early childhood teams in the Anglophone East School District, the successful candidates will be part of a team of Early Learning Consultants who provide pedagogical guidance, coaching and mentoring to early childhood educators and directors through individual on-site coaching, the establishment of communities of practice, and professional development workshops/learning opportunities aligned with the values, goals and principles of the New Brunswick Early Learning and Child Care Curriculum Framework.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Assess curricular practices using the Collaborative Assessment Tool -Validation (CAT-V.) to support annual quality improvement plans related to curriculum implementation and long-term sustainability.

• Collect, analyze, and synthesize relevant data and information to support the goals and priorities of the Professional Learning Strategy.

• Apply coaching and mentoring strategies that foster a culture of continuous improvement where early childhood professionals (educators, administrators, inclusion support workers) develop self-awareness, strengthen practice and engage in reflective practices.

• Co-construct, plan and modify professional learning modules and workshops in collaboration with the Early Learning Specialist to ensure alignment with the curriculum framework through reflection, observation and feedback from the early learning and childcare sector.

• Promote continuous quality improvement through the development, implementation, and monitoring of Quality Improvement Plans (QIPs).

## Who You Are:

You believe that investing in people is the most powerful way to create lasting impact. Naturally curious, approachable, and collaborative, you have a talent for bringing people together around a common goal. You easily build trusting relationships, approach challenges with confidence, and recognize opportunities where others see obstacles. Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

• Extensive knowledge of and practice in the Early Learning and Child Care Curriculum Framework.

• You have experience in facilitating meetings and trainings for groups, either virtually or face-to-face, and in coaching individuals.

• You can adapt quickly, provide high quality customer service, and collaborate with other team members and partners.
