title: Network & Telecom Analyst II
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Network & Telecom Analyst II to join our IT Operations & Projects team in Voisey's Bay, Newfoundland and Labrador.

The role is a permanent on-site position, working 2 weeks on, 2 weeks off rotational schedule.

Reporting to the Supervisor, Network & Telecom, the Network & Telecom Analyst II is responsible for the operation, maintenance, support, and continuous improvement of network infrastructure, wireless networks, telecommunications systems, cloud connectivity, and associated communications technologies across Vale Base Metals. This includes routing and switching, network security, Wi-Fi, VoIP and unified communications, LTE services, cloud networking, monitoring platforms, and supporting physical network infrastructure.

The successful candidate will work closely with business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and service providers to ensure secure, reliable, and cost-effective network and telecommunications services that support operational excellence across both Canadian and international operations. The role also contributes to cybersecurity initiatives, service delivery improvements, incident management, and technology projects while ensuring compliance with Vale's technology standards and service management practices.

## Key Responsibilities

## Network & Telecom Operations

• Support and maintain network infrastructure including routing, switching, wireless, telecommunications, and cloud connectivity.

• Manage and monitor network performance, availability, and reliability.

• Support VoIP, unified communications, LTE, SD-WAN, MPLS, and related technologies.

• Maintain technical documentation, asset inventories, and network standards.

## Service Delivery & Performance

• Monitor service levels and drive continuous improvement initiatives.

• Participate in incident, problems, changes, and release management processes.

• Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex network and telecom issues.

• Generate operational reports and contribute to KPI and service performance metrics.

## Cybersecurity, Risk & Compliance

• Support cybersecurity initiatives for network and telecom infrastructure.

• Ensure compliance with security standards, policies, and industry best practices.

• Identify and mitigate technology risks, vulnerabilities, and performance issues.

• Support business continuity and disaster recovery planning.

## Vendor & Stakeholder Management

• Collaborate with business partners, technology teams, contractors, and vendors.

• Monitor service provider performance and contract compliance.

• Support infrastructure projects, upgrades, and technology deployments.

• Provide cross-functional support across Network, Cloud, Hosting, End User Services, AI, and Operational Technology environments.

## About You

## Experience

• Minimum 5 years of experience supporting enterprise network and telecommunications environments.

• Experience with Cisco, Juniper, Huawei, or equivalent networking technologies.

• Experience supporting cloud connectivity and hybrid cloud environments.

• Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Experience working with external vendors and managed service providers.

## Work Schedule & Travel - MUST

• This position operates in a 24/7 operational environment and requires participation in a rotational work schedule of 14 days on / 14 days off, working 12-hour shifts. Shifts may be scheduled from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM, based on operational requirements. Candidates must be willing and able to work weekends, statutory holidays, and other rotational schedules as required.

• Successful candidates must be willing and able to workdays, nights, weekends, statutory holidays, and on-call rotations as required.

• Travel between operational sites may be required to support field services, project deployments, technology upgrades, and operational incidents.

## Education

• Diploma or Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Network Engineering, or a related field.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong understanding of routing, switching, wireless, telecom, and network security technologies.

• Knowledge of firewalls, VPNs, IDS/IPS, and cybersecurity principles.

• Experience with cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.

• Understanding of ITIL service management practices.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

## Preferred Qualifications

• CompTIA Network+, CCNA, CCNP, or equivalent certifications.

• Experience in industrial, mining, manufacturing, or operational technology environments.

• Experience with network monitoring and observability tools

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Relocation Assistance

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodation is equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration

that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for

employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Pay Grade: F5T

Apply by: November 28, 2026

About Us
The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada, the mandate of the PPS is rooted in its commitment to ensuring fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of criminal and provincial offences.
We are looking for the brightest legal minds, who also reflect the rich diversity of our province! We don't just accept difference – we celebrate a supportive culture of diversity and belonging. We strive to create an environment where different perspectives and experiences are welcomed and valued. We encourage applications from those that equally value and champion equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA).

About Our Opportunity
As the Chief Crown Attorney, you will supervise and manage the conduct of the Crown Attorneys and the prosecution cases undertaken by the Public Prosecution Service.
Reporting to the Director of Public Prosecutions, you will conduct prosecutions and provide management, guidance and leadership for the staff of this division of the NSPPS. In this role you will ensure compliance with instructions or guidelines issued by the Attorney General or the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this position you will have a Bachelor of Laws Degree, have a practicing membership with the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society, plus 10 years' experience in the practice of criminal law. Previous experience in the conduct of significant prosecutions and appeals is preferred.
Your significant criminal litigation experience in the various levels of court; extensive up-to-date knowledge of criminal law (statutes and caselaw) and the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, the Rules of Evidence and the rules respecting summary conviction and indictable appeals is required.
You will have demonstrated competence in the areas of substantive and procedural criminal law, as well as provincial statute offences and regulations, advocacy, media and public relations skills. Your proven organizational skills in conducting major prosecutions; balancing case work and managerial functions are necessary to be successful in this role.
The superior communication skills you have developed are required in order to clearly explain complex factual and legal issues orally and in writing. In addition, you will have strong interpersonal skills including leadership, team building, ability to motivate others and to work cooperatively with other components of the criminal justice system.
Your proven administrative skills and experience in supervising legal staff is also needed. Familiarity with government administrative and operational policies is preferred.
The Government of Nova Scotia has adopted the LEADS Leadership Framework. During the interview, candidates will be expected to express how they have demonstrated the key behaviours and capabilities required to effectively lead in a caring and inclusive environment. LEADS Domains includes Leads Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions and Systems Transformation.
Please follow LEADS (novascotia.ca) for more information.

About Us
Nova Scotia is rich in natural resources – including biodiversity, forests, provincial parks and the land we manage. The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for the development, management, conservation and protection of forest, parks and wildlife resources and the administration of the province's Crown land. Together we are working with Nova Scotians to build a better future through sustainable natural resource management as we all benefit from the natural health and wealth of the province.

About Our Opportunity
Like a property law office, the Land Strategy and Planning Branch manages all aspects of Crown land transactions. The Crown Land Information Management Centre is responsible for maintaining a registry of conveyancing documents, survey plans and maps of Crown land holdings, providing access to Crown land records, researching Crown interests in land, and maintaining the Crown Cadastral Database.

As the Information Processing Technician, you will maintain an accurate and complete register of Crown land ownership records, administer and provide user support for the department's electronic document management system, and provide Crown land information to internal and external clients.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Information Processing Technician, we count on your strong attention to detail and organizational skills to maintain an accurate and complete register of Crown lands ownership records. In addition, you are the primary system administrator of the Crown lands electronic document management system, a significant business application used by multiple provincial governments departments to access current and historical Crown land information. This position also completes digitization of Crown land records, ensuring appropriate standards are followed to maintain the integrity, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of the captured information, in compliance with the Government Records Act, Public Archives Act, Freedom of Information Protection of Privacy Act, Personal Information International Disclosure Protection Act and provincial/corporate records management policies and standards.

title: Vice President, Finance and Administration
description:
SLEMON PARK CORPORATION

SLEMON PARK CORPORATION

POSITION DESCRIPTION

POSITION TITLE: Vice President, Finance and Administration
REPORTING TO: President
Date of Preparation/Revision: November 2026

POSITION SUMMARY

Slemon Park Corporation is a provincial Crown corporation that manages a business and residential community focused on aerospace, training, and real estate development. The Vice President, Finance and Administration serves as the Corporation's Chief Financial Officer (CFO). The role maintains a strong internal control environment and oversees the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of financial information and reporting. As a member of the senior management team, the Vice President contributes to strategic planning, analysis, and corporate direction. The role also leads risk management and supports the integrity, security, and stability of the Corporation's information technology systems. The position requires advanced knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and a working knowledge of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) to guide the development and implementation of sound financial policies and procedures.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Financial Management and Accounting
Lead the Corporation's financial management, accounting, reporting, budgeting, and compliance activities, including:
• Lead the preparation of annual operating and capital budgets.

• Manage the timely preparation of monthly financial statements, program reports, and reconciliations required by divisional managers.

• Monitor actual performance against budget and direct financial analysis, including identifying priorities for further review.

• Ensure timely filing of payroll and commodity tax remittances.

• Lead the year-end preparation of financial statements.

• Coordinate the year-end audit, review audit recommendations, and implement necessary changes.

• Prepare ad hoc reports and analyses that identify emerging trends and their potential impact on the Corporation's strategic plan.

• Inform corporate strategy through analysis of trends, demographics, external policy developments, and internal divisional data.

• Advise all levels of management on financial management and accounting matters.

• Manage the Corporation's cash flow and investments.

• Oversee compliance with the Corporation's procurement and contracting policies.

• Develop and maintain accounting policies in accordance with GAAP and IFRS.

• Leadership of Accounting and Human Resources Staff and External IT Services
Lead and guide the Corporation's accounting and human resources staff.
• Ensure that transactions comply with GAAP, applicable provincial requirements, and the Corporation's financial policies and procedures.

• Coach and motivate staff, provide opportunities for internal and external training, communicate strategic priorities, and provide the guidance and support needed to achieve assigned objectives.

• Lead and coordinate the relationship with the external IT service provider, including capital renewal planning, service-level requirements, and information security needs.

• Policies, Procedures, and Risk Management
Lead the development and continuous improvement of policies, procedures, and controls that support consistent operations, protect assets from theft, fraud, and loss, and preserve confidentiality.
• Monitor changes in legislation, market conditions, and corporate strategy, and recommend responsive updates.

• Develop and update corporate policies, including the Whistleblower Policy and Procurement Policy.

• Design, implement, enforce, and evaluate accounting, human resources, and business continuity policies and controls to protect assets and maintain the integrity of financial reporting.

• Manage relationships with banking and investment institutions, including account access, new accounts and services, signing authorities, and service as an authorized signatory.

• Control access to information systems and ensure effective backup processes for administrative, property management, general ledger, hotel, food and beverage, and retail point-of-sale systems.

• Liaise with software and IT support providers to coordinate updates, resolve errors, and implement new features.

• Design and update corporate compensation scales.

• Manage the Corporation's insurance policies.

• Financial and Management Information Systems
Provide leadership in the timely development, review, and presentation of financial statements and management reports.
• Manage deadlines for monthly and year-end statements and remittances by guiding and supporting accounting and human resources staff.

• Monitor accounting standards, identify new or changing requirements, and advise the Corporation on policy choices and updates.

• Review and approve monthly financial reports before distribution to end users.

• Work with managers, directors, and executives to ensure reports meet business needs, and implement changes or new reports as required.

• Develop and write the annual Budget and Business Plan.

• Coordinate and provide financial information to external organizations, including the Canada Revenue Agency, Statistics Canada, and the Province of Prince Edward Island.

• Serve as the primary liaison with the Corporation's lenders, coordinating loan agreements and related drawdowns.

• Board of Directors and Board Committees
• Attend meetings of the Board of Directors, Audit and Finance Committee, and Governance Committee.

• Serve as Corporate Secretary and prepare minutes for meetings of the Board and its committees.

• Present financial and other information to the Board and its committees.

Perform other duties and special projects as required or requested.

EXPECTED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in business administration or a related field.

• Professional accounting designation.

• Extensive senior-level leadership and financial management experience.

• Sound knowledge of accounting and auditing principles.

• Strong working knowledge of GAAP and IFRS.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office, accounting systems, and point-of-sale software.

• Knowledge of HST, employment standards, and related legislation.

• Strong interpersonal, leadership, conflict-resolution, collaboration, planning, and strategic-thinking skills.

• Demonstrated problem-solving, negotiation, and motivational abilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

WORKING CONDITIONS

• Scheduled Working Hours - This is a full-time position.

• Physical, Mental, and Visual Requirements
The position requires the ability to manage tight deadlines and perform effectively under pressure. Strong organizational, written and verbal communication, leadership, strategic thinking, and interpersonal skills are essential.

Department: Justice

About Us
The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court, and Bankruptcy Court. The courts act independently from the government to address individual cases.
For more information on the Department of Justice Court Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Court_Services/

About Our Opportunity
As the Court Officer (Administration), you may schedule court hearings held in all levels of Court, manage a caseload of files, and act as the liaison between the Court, and members of law enforcement agencies, the legal profession, and the public. You may also scrutinize documents and determine corrective measures where necessary. The incumbent will also perform quasi-judicial duties as assigned as a Staff Justice of the Peace appointed under the Justice of the Peace Act. You will perform your duties in accordance with, and as assigned under, the Court Officials Act.

Primary Accountabilities
The Court Administration responsibilities include:

• Schedule Court cases and respond to inquiries and information requests from the public.

• Prepare and distribute court orders and dockets.

• Document management, Exhibit control, statistical data collection, and general accounting.

• Scrutinize documents, apply relevant Acts, statutes, policies, procedures, and determine corrective measures where necessary.

• Review documents with self-represented parties, and provide legal information and referrals as required.

• Manage a caseload of files to ensure effective and efficient client service.

• Train and mentor new staff in day-to-day operational activities.

• Liaise with the Judiciary and legal profession and communicate with legal professionals and self-represented parties on behalf of the court.

• You may be required to attend Court and perform Court-related functions.

Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate must have two years of post-secondary education in a related discipline plus one-year related experience, ideally in a legal environment, or an acceptable equivalent.
The successful candidate must also:

• Have experience and competency in keyboarding (combination of speed and accuracy), data entry and other standard computer applications including MS Office products

• Possess excellent proofreading, spelling and grammar skills

• Have superior organizational abilities and strong prioritization skills

• Have excellent attention to detail

• Have the ability to meet tight deadlines

• Work independently and as part of a team

• Have tact and discretion

• Have general accounting skills, scheduling skills and/or interviewing and assessing skills. demonstrate an understanding and knowledge of the Rules and Statutes that govern the courts as well as a sound working knowledge of legal documents, forms, court procedures and legal terminology.

• Demonstrate a high level of initiative and problem-solving abilities and readily accept responsibilities. Errors can result in significant impacts for justice system participants.

• Be fair and impartial to all clients using a high degree of confidentiality while exercising your excellent interpersonal and communication skills, particularly listening skills, when dealing with difficult people in complex, sensitive and stressful situations.

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, typing test, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.
Training and/or experience in mediation and non-conflict resolution and bilingualism, with oral and written skills in English and French, would be considered assets.

Equivalency
Include, but not limited to:

• A 1-year certificate/diploma in a related discipline plus 2 years of related experience

• 3 years of related experience with exposure to the justice system

PLEASE NOTE: Candidates will not be considered for an interview if applications are incomplete or are missing information. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day (typically the hours are 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, this may vary depending on operational needs).

• Your personal resiliency is essential to meet the emotional demands of this position. You may be immersed in high stress situations and encounter distraught and difficult individuals.

• Handling of some exhibits may be mentally or physically disconcerting.

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located in Halifax, NS.
Candidates may be required to obtain training in Firearms Safety in relation to handling evidence and may be required to successfully complete the Nova Scotia Certified Transcribers qualification. This position will require an enhanced level of security screening for an external application.
Some travel and overtime may be required.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths.

title: Distribution Asset Strategy Engineer
description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Enterprise Asset Management

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia

Type of Employment: Permanent, Full-Time

Closing Date: November 11, 2026

We are looking for a Distribution Asset Strategy Engineer to join our Enterprise Asset Management team.

Reporting to the Manager, Asset Performance, the Distribution Asset Strategy Engineer is responsible for the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of distribution asset strategies, lifecycle plans, risk models, and investment recommendations that support the safe, reliable, resilient, and cost-effective operation of Nova Scotia Power's distribution system.

The role serves as an asset owner within Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) for distribution assets, working closely with Operations, Distribution Engineering, Distribution Planning, Capital Delivery, Reliability, and Regulatory Affairs to ensure asset risks, performance trends, asset condition, lifecycle requirements, and investment needs are understood and appropriately addressed through risk-informed decision making.

The position provides an opportunity for a developing or intermediate level engineer to build or expand expertise in asset management, risk assessment, reliability engineering, capital planning, and utility operations while contributing to the long-term stewardship of Nova Scotia Power's distribution infrastructure.

Key elements of this role include:

## Standards Governance & Continuous Improvement

• Support the overall governance and periodic review of distribution asset standards, specifications, and asset management requirements by NS Power subject matter experts.

• Work with Engineering, Operations, and Reliability teams to ensure standards, maintenance practices, and asset strategies remain aligned.

• Support development and maintenance of asset management strategies, supporting documentation, and other asset knowledge repositories as appropriate.

• Identify opportunities for process improvements and implementation of best practices.

## Distribution Asset Strategy & Lifecycle Planning

• Lead the distribution asset strategy committee and provide support to various working groups.

• Support development and implementation of distribution asset strategies, asset management plans, lifecycle plans, and risk mitigation programs.

• Maintain asset strategies and lifecycle plans for overhead and underground distribution assets, including poles, conductors, cables, transformers, switchgear, voltage regulation equipment, reclosers, capacitor banks, and associated equipment.

• Support the development of appropriate asset replacement, refurbishment, modernization, and resiliency programs through the asset strategy committee with input from Standards, Operations, Reliability and Engineering.

• Assist in evaluating emerging technologies and industry trends and assessing applicability to Nova Scotia Power's distribution system.

• Incorporate climate adaptation, wildfire mitigation, storm hardening, and resiliency considerations into overall asset strategies and investment plans as appropriate.

## Asset Health, Risk & Reliability

• Develop and maintain asset health, criticality, risk, and performance models for distribution assets.
Analyze inspection, maintenance, condition assessment, outage, and failure data to identify emerging risks and performance trends.

• Support reliability investigations, asset failure reviews, and root cause analyses, ensuring lessons learned are incorporated into asset strategies and investment recommendations.

• Monitor key performance indicators and asset health metrics to support risk-informed decision making.

• Assist in identifying opportunities to improve reliability, reduce risk, and optimize lifecycle costs.
Capital Planning, Regulatory Support

• Provide risk-based analysis and recommendations to support project justification, and prioritization of distribution asset investments.

• Support the Distribution Capital team by ensuring proposed capital investments are aligned with asset health, feeder risk profiles, and enterprise risk management objectives.

• Support the preparation of regulatory filings, investment justifications, and business case materials by providing asset risk, condition, and lifecycle management inputs.

## Industry Engagement & Innovation

• Participate in industry forums, working groups, and knowledge-sharing activities.

• Monitor industry developments, emerging technologies, and best practices through organizations such as CEATI and EPRI.

• Support adoption of innovative asset management approaches, data analytics tools, and reliability improvement practices.

These skills will make you successful:

## Education & Experience

• Registered, or eligible for registration, as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) in Nova Scotia.

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Industrial Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

• 5-8 years of experience in a combination of electric utility engineering, distribution operations, system planning, asset management, reliability engineering, capital planning, or a related role.

• Experience with distribution assets, utility operations, reliability analysis, asset management, or infrastructure planning is considered an asset.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze technical information and make sound engineering recommendations.

• Proven commitment to safety and continuous improvement.

## Technical/Job Specific Knowledge and Abilities

• Strong knowledge of electric utility distribution systems, including overhead and underground assets such as poles, conductors, cables, transformers, switchgear, reclosers, voltage regulation equipment, capacitor banks, protective devices, and associated distribution infrastructure.

• Demonstrated understanding of distribution engineering standards, material specifications, design practices, construction standards, and technical governance processes.

• Understanding of asset management, lifecycle planning, reliability, and risk management principles.

• Familiarity with condition assessment, asset health evaluation, and infrastructure investment planning.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.

• Ability to work with large datasets and develop meaningful insights to support decision making.

• Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

• Ability to work collaboratively across Operations, Engineering, Reliability, Planning, and Capital Delivery teams.

• Experience with data analytics, reliability analysis, asset management systems, or power system studies is considered an asset.

• Demonstrated commitment to safety, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

Job Summary
This position works in the field of Prosthetics in the assessment and treatment of clients with physical and neurological disabilities, and includes the design, fabrication and fitting of suitable prostheses. The successful candidate will provide intervention to a wide range of patients in inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation environments. The candidate will be required to independently manage a client caseload providing exposure to a variety of disabilities or illnesses requiring the use of all basic prosthetic skills.

Functioning as a member of the interdisciplinary team, the Prosthetist/Orthotist IIA consults with other health professionals and makes recommendations regarding the clients’ overall rehabilitation program. This includes the provision of client education and the provision of advice and guidance as to the design, limitations and use of prostheses. The successful candidate will also provide training to clinical students and interns as well as technical staff.

Work is performed with considerable independence and initiative and is evaluated through conferences, chart audits and evaluation of results obtained.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly lifts a variety of materials up to 25lbs and occasionally over 50lbs, such as lifting heavy casts and other products. Many of the items are awkwardly shaped, making lifting and moving difficult.
Physical effort includes constant standing to perform work tasks, being placed in awkward positions and crawling to verify the stability and safety of the client when wearing the device.
Auditory concentration includes listening to multiple stakeholders while working in a noisy environment.
Must exercise higher than normal levels of attentiveness when working with shop equipment to ensure safety.
Required to work under deadlines to have devices ready for clients.

Job Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized (approved) Prosthetic/Orthotic clinical program is required.
Current and continuing Certification by Orthotics Prosthetics Canada is required.
Minimum of three years of experience within the last five as a Prosthetist is required.
A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

If there are no applicants meeting these qualifications, applications from Graduates of a recognized Prosthetics and Orthotics Program who are eligible to complete Residency will be considered.

description:

On Call: No

## Job Summary:

The Pension and Benefits (P&B) Specialist is responsible for administering employee pension and benefit programs, recommending plan changes and serving as a resource to staff and managers on related issues and ensuring accuracy of employee data.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Provides guidance and advice to employees regarding pension and benefits, utilizing exceptional interpersonal skills and knowledge of each union group and their respective Collective Agreements, legislative requirement and carrier guidelines.

• Collaborates with the Labour Relations team to interpret collective agreement wording related to group benefits and pension eligibility.

• Reviews collective agreement wording and provides recommendations to Senior Manager for discussions in bargaining to strategize on standardization of practices.

• Establishes employee benefits eligibility, coverage, effective dates and payroll premium deduction set-up in accordance with union contracts and benefit policy agreements and ensures all necessary information is entered in SAP and the benefit administrator site.

• Ensures timely administration of benefit enrollment forms and coordinates all required documentation to be sent internally and to third party carriers.

• Completes monthly audits and analyzes results to ensure accuracy and integrity of the system (e.g. mandatory enrollments, benefit cost shares while on leaves etc.). If errors are identified, makes recommendations for resolution and future improvements to processes.

• Prepares reports and analysis for use by the team and the finance department for recommendation on write-offs and collections for benefit premium arrears.

• Monitors and reports on key performance indicators to evaluate areas for improved efficiency.

• Monitors employee leave of absences, creates payment schedules and enters employee benefit/pension cheques in SAP for payment of premiums.

• Prepares letters for initial eligibility and change in enrollment status advising employees of their eligibility or termination of coverage including while on leave of absences; prepares and couriers letters to employees to confirm selections.

• Liaises between VON employees and benefit and pension carriers.

• Communicates with managers regarding job content, specific objectives, personal performance and action plans to achieve performance objectives.

• Fulfills all responsibilities in accordance with the requirements of the organizational system (e.g. Bylaws, Standards, Policies, applicable legislation).

• Participates in continuous decision-making to promote continuous quality improvement using LEAN principles.

• Actively participates in the development and ongoing improvement of processes within the Total Compensation team.

• Work towards fulfillment of program/department goals.

## Common Responsibilities:

• Promotes the goals and values of VON and their role as an integrated community care provider.

• Promotes a safe and healthy workplace ensuring workplace conduct and activities are in accordance with the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations and compliant with the VON Safety Management System, including all Policies, Safe Work Practices and Procedures.

• Abides by all VON policies and work practices.

• Abides by all confidentiality and protection of personal information policies, regulations and practices and ensures appropriate safeguards are in place within their role.

• Works in collaboration with other staff in a team approach to service delivery.

## External and Internal Relationships:

• Engage with cross functional team members, Senior Directors, Directors, Managers and employees to advice on processes and procedures.

• Engage with employees in providing benefits and pension information.

• Collaborates with service providers related to pension and benefit sector.

## Education, Designations and Experience:

• Post-secondary education with degree/certificate in Human Resources Management

• Related courses in Pension and Benefits, or other related field considered an asset.

• Minimum of 3 years' experience with administering Group Benefits plans (health, dental, life insurance, LTD, AD&D, optional insurance) and Pension Administration (Defined Benefit Pension Plans preferred).

• Certified Employee Benefit Specialist (CEBS) designation is an asset.

• Knowledge of the provincial group benefits legislation.

• Experience in a unionized environment/health care environment considered an asset.

## Skill Requirements:

• Proficiency in Windows OS and MS Office Suite programs.

• SAP experience a definite asset.

• Demonstrated commitment to working in an environment with high confidentiality and discretion.

• Demonstrate effective time management, planning and organizing of days' work activities.

• Able to work both independently and within a team.

• Strong organizational skills with an ability to prioritize, multi-task and handle competing deadlines.

• Exercising good judgment in decision making and conflict resolution.

• Strong customer service skills.

• Must demonstrate attention to detail.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills.

• Ability to problem solve and adjust to rapidly changing priorities in a deadline driven environment.

• Strong customer service skills.

• The use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) may be required

## Other:

• A current and original copy of a satisfactory Criminal Records Check is required.

• A Vulnerable Sector Search and/or Child Abuse Registry Check may be required.

title: Project & Shutdown Management Lead
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking Project & Shutdown Management Leads to join our Project Execution Team in Long Harbour, NL.

These permanent positions will be on a 4x10s schedule, working either Monday to Thursday or Tuesday to Friday at our Long Harbour Operations Site.

As a Project & Shutdown Management Lead, you will lead $10-15M annual projects, which includes the management and coordination of all activities from FEL 1 studies to AFE approval, execution, and handover to the Project Owner. This also includes management of detailed engineering design, procurement, project controls, systems, construction support, and management services for individual projects.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Execute approved Capital, Operating, and Period projects and shutdowns from FEL 1 through final execution including related commissioning/operational readiness (12–24-month horizon).

• Lead PHRs, JHAs, MOCs, Lift Plans, and manage the Project Risk Registry as required for the safe execution of the project.

• Provide updates to Superintendent on additional tasks required (Field Work Instructions-FWI) and Contract Change Orders (CCO) to complete the project, along with impact to schedule and mitigation actions.

• Ensure adequate contractor audits are performed for quality, qualifications, compliance, and invoice auditing with support from the project engineer.

• Perform regular field visits to ensure compliance with commissioning, quality, and operational readiness processes.

• Manage, monitor, and report on project/shutdown costs, cash forecasts, and variance explanations with the Projects Controls Coordinator.

• Liaise with the Service Procurement Group while managing requisitions and performing Technical and Commercial Evaluations.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Flexible work arrangements

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• A Bus Service departing from the St. John's vicinity

## About You

## Education:

• A minimum of post-secondary education in an engineering, technical, or trades discipline.

• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Professional Engineer (P. Eng) or Professional Technologist (P. Tech) designation would be an asset.

## Experience:

## • Minimum 5 years' experience in a project management-related role.

## Skills:

• Preferred knowledge and understanding of VPS Technical and project management principles and strategies.

• Strong project management skills.

• Strong interpersonal, time management and organization skills.

• Experience using SAP would be an asset.

• Ability to use Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

IWK Health is a respected academic health sciences centre located in Halifax, Nova Scotia, providing tertiary and primary care for two million children, youth, adults and families each year across the Atlantic region. We have a team of approximately 4000 employees, physicians, volunteers and learners at sites across Nova Scotia. People build careers with IWK Health with our focus on training and mentorship opportunities. We recognize each other's talent and celebrate our successes. We collaborate in modern facilities or virtually from home, align our work to our values, and enjoy access to enhanced benefits and wellness programs. We are proud to support our patients, families and communities and are grateful for the generous donor support we receive.

Promoting an anti-racist environment, and calling out discrimination as we work and provide care, is important to us. We are located in Mi'kma'ki, the unceded and ancestral territory of the Mi'kmaq people. Working in Mi'kma'ki and providing care to those across Atlantic Canada is a shared privilege with the original inhabitants who have lived here for many thousands of years prior to colonization. There are 13 First Nation communities across Nova Scotia, and more than 50 historic African Nova Scotian communities who also have a long, deep, and complex history dating back over 400 years. We have the highest percentage of people with disabilities in the country. Nova Scotia has the highest proportions of transgender and non-binary people than any other province or territory in the country. We are active in our work to eliminate discrimination, but have more work to do to build that trust, acknowledge our biases and reduce the barriers our diverse communities face. We want IWK Health to be a safe and supportive space of equity and belonging in the care we provide and the employment we offer. We welcome all interested persons who self-identify as Indigenous, Black/African Nova Scotians, Persons of Colour, Immigrants/Newcomers, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ to apply to support our goal for our workforce to be representative of the patients, families, and communities that we care for at all job levels.

## The Opportunity

Located in Halifax, Nova Scotia, the IWK Health Centre, the Children's Hospital of the Maritimes, provides quality care to women, children, youth and families. IWK Psychology is strong and growing, with over 50 doctoral and MA psychologists and assistive roles. Our Predoctoral Internship in Clinical Psychology is CPA accredited.

This role will work as part of an interdisciplinary Pediatric Pain Management team that provides tertiary family centered care for children and youth, and their families, with chronic pain. Assessments and treatment are provided by a team including physicians, clinical nurse specialists, clinical psychologists, and physiotherapists. Treatment often includes a combination of physical treatment and exercise, cognitive-behavioral and acceptance and commitment therapy techniques, and medications. The Psychologist works as part of an interdisciplinary team to provide assessment, treatment and consultative services for youth and their families. The successful candidate will also have the opportunity to deliver coping skills training in a group-based format and will share responsibility for program development and program evaluation.

## Hours of Work

Working hours will are flexible, within M-F 8-4 schedule.

## Your Qualifications

• Completion Ph.D./PsyD degree in Clinical Psychology from a CPA/APA accredited university program, or equivalent, required.

• Completion of a CPA/APA accredited predoctoral internship/residency program required.

• Registered, or eligible for registration, with the Nova Scotia Board of Examiners in Psychology.

• Minimum five (5) years of formal training and clinical experience in child/adolescent psychology required.

• Demonstrated experience in assessment, diagnosis and treatment with health psychology required.

• Experience with evidence-based pediatric pain methods preferred.

• Experience with Research preferred

• Experience with program evaluation preferred

• Knowledge in a range of psychological interventions for pain management (e.g., cognitive behavioral therapy, acceptance and commitment therapy, biofeedback). Experience in evidence-based psychological interventions for children and youth with somatization.

• Conversant in anatomy & physiology of pain and biopsychosocial models of pain and pain management preferred.

• Experience working in a multidisciplinary team or pediatric pain clinic setting preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to effectively consult and work with parents, other health care providers, and social service and education agencies required.

• Experience in a range of psychological interventions for general mental health concerns in youth (e.g., cognitive behavioral therapy, acceptance and commitment therapy, dialectical behavioral therapy).

• Background and experience in educational settings, having an understanding in various approaches to managing youth living with pain in schools.

• Demonstrated excellent verbal and written communication skills required.

• Demonstrated excellence in clinical care required.

• Knowledge of program-based care an asset.

• Demonstrated excellent time management, organization, and problem-solving skills required.

• Demonstrated commitment and champion of family-centered care required.

• Competencies in other languages an asset including French, would be a significant asset.

Thank you for your interest in IWK Health.

Job Title: Power Electronics Engineer

Location: Hackett's Cove, NS

Nautel Sonar is a specialized division within Nautel Ltd., which excels in designing, developing, and manufacturing cutting-edge sonar and sonar sub-systems. Nautel Sonar, provides a comprehensive range of OEM sonar products as well as complete "wet end" sonar sub-systems.

Role Description

Within this specialized division, the Power Electronics Engineer will play a critical role in the design, development, and implementation of advanced sonar systems for underwater applications. You will be part of a talented engineering team responsible for creating cutting-edge technology solutions to meet the demands of the marine defense and research sectors.

Qualifications
Your Qualifications

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in electrical engineering, or a related field.

• Strong understanding of power electronics, amplifiers, , and control systems.

• Background in Systems Engineering practices and processes.

• Understanding of New Product Introduction Processes.

• Proficiency in using industry-standard tools for system design and analysis.

• Understanding of modern serial communication protocols.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues.

• Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

• Ability to be immediately cleared for Controlled Goods (Canadian Citizenship/PR) is a requirement of this role.

Responsibilities
Your responsibilities will include:

• System Design and Development: Contribute to the design and development of sonar systems, including power amplifiers, control and monitoring, power electronics, filtering, matching, and communication interfaces. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate sonar technology into larger systems.

• System Integration: Contribute to the integration of sonar systems with existing platforms and infrastructure. Work closely with software and mechanical teams to optimize system performance and enhance overall functionality: collaborating to developing hardware and software specifications as well as verification and validation documents.

• Customization and Adaptation: Support the development of custom products as opportunities arise.

• Defense Documentation: Contribute to, and review, industry standard documentation as part of the product development and program execution.

• Testing and Validation: Participate in the development and execution of comprehensive testing procedures to assess sonar system performance and accuracy. Analyze test results and identify areas for improvement, making necessary adjustments to achieve product requirements.

• Sales Support: Work with the sales team to develop innovative, cost effective and competitive responses to various sales inquiries. Contribute to pre-sales communication, requirements negotiation, and Request for Proposal or Quote (RFP/RFQ) Responses for new and upgraded sonar system and sub-system components.

• Production Support: Work with Production and Quality teams to ensure high quality and cost- effective production of sonar systems and sub-system components.

• Team Collaboration: Contribute to sonar engineering projects, ensuring adherence to system requirements, timelines, budgets, and quality standards, and communicate technical concepts effectively.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including acoustics experts, electrical engineers, software developers, and project managers as well as other internal stakeholders such as Sales, Customer Service, and Operations, to create robust and reliable sonar solutions.

• Continuous Improvement: Contribute to continuous improvement efforts regarding key Engineering processes and activities.

• Troubleshooting and Support: Provide technical support to resolve any issues related to sonar systems in operational deployments or during testing phases.

• Compliance and Regulations: Ensure that all sonar systems adhere to industry standards, regulations, and safety guidelines.

This is an opportunity to join an industry-leading small company with a growing team. You will have the opportunity to work with a collaborative engineering team to influence designs and processes and ensure continuous improvement.

## Join Our Automotive Services Team and Help Keep Atlantic Canada Moving!

Are you someone who feels a sense of reward and satisfaction when helping others? Are you passionate about roadside safety? Do you have a strong mechanical aptitude and interested in all things automotive? If yes, we have a great career opportunity for you!

As an Emergency Roadside Service (ERS) Technician, you'll be the reassuring face of CAA Atlantic on the roadside, delivering trusted towing and roadside assistance with professionalism, safety, and care. Every day brings new challenges and opportunities to make a real difference - whether you're rescuing a Member with a flat tire, towing a vehicle to a repair shop, delivering fuel on a rainy night, or boosting a battery during a winter storm. We do all that and more for our Members!

In this hands-on, fast-paced role, you'll take pride in providing safe and efficient towing services while performing a wide range of roadside support, from lockouts to tire repairs and battery installations. You'll use your mechanical know-how and problem-solving skills to assess situations quickly and get Members back on their way - all while communicating clearly and courteously with Members and Dispatchers to ensure timely, dependable service.

We're looking for safety-minded, reliable team players who thrive in dynamic environments and take ownership of their work. Flexibility is key - our Members count on us around the clock, and you'll be ready to assist during evenings, weekends, and holidays when help matters most. If you're known for your positive spirit, calm under pressure, and dedication to excellent service, you'll fit right in with our trusted team of ERS Technicians at CAA Atlantic.

This position follows a shift rotation schedule: 4 days on followed by 4 days off, 12 hour shifts.

This position is classified as safety sensitive. As part of CAA Atlantic's commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace, successful candidates will be required to complete and pass a pre-employment drug and alcohol test as a condition of employment.

Qualifications
• Air Brake Endorsement (required) and a valid driver's licence with a clean driving record.

• Strong mechanical aptitude and comfort working with vehicles.

• Excellent problem-solving and customer service skills, even under pressure.

• Willingness to work a variety of shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

• A positive, reliable, and safety-conscious attitude.

Responsibilities
• Provide safe and efficient towing services for Members.

• Deliver roadside assistance such as lockout service, tire changes and repairs, fuel delivery, and battery boosts.

• Support battery testing, sales, and installation for CAA Atlantic Battery Service Program.

• Communicate clearly and courteously with Members and Dispatchers to ensure timely service.

• Maintain company vehicles, tools, and equipment in clean and reliable working condition.

• Follow all safety, traffic, and company operating procedures.

title: Manager, Applied Research Services
description:
What happens when great ideas meet industry challenges? Innovation with real-world impact.

As the Manager, Applied Research Services, you will help shape the future of applied research at NBCC by connecting faculty, students, industry, and community partners to solve meaningful challenges. From securing research funding and building strategic partnerships to supporting responsible research practices, you'll play a key role in turning ideas into outcomes that benefit learners, employers, and communities across New Brunswick.

If you're passionate about innovation, collaboration, and creating opportunities through research, this is your chance to make a lasting impact.

Location: Any NBCC location

Qualifications

## Education/Experience:

• Doctoral degree preferred.

• 5 years' experience in research administration.

• Extensive leadership and management experience, preferably in a post-secondary environment.

• Demonstrated success securing research funding and developing collaborative industry/community research partnerships.

• Familiarity with the Atlantic Canadian innovation ecosystem (e.g., Springboard, Planet Hatch, Venn Innovation) would be an asset.

## Technical Skills:

• Ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and a high degree of professionalism and confidentiality.

As part of the College Office of Research Enterprise (CORE) and reporting to the CORE's Director, the Manager of Applied Research Services is responsible for advancing research at NBCC by developing strategic industry and community partnerships, securing research funding, and managing research services to ensure responsible research conduct. The Manager plays a key role in strengthening the College's research capacity, supporting faculty and researchers, and creating meaningful applied research training opportunities for students.

title: Senior Payroll Administrator
description:
Title: Senior Payroll Administrator

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-Time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Senior Payroll Administrator to oversee the payroll operations across multiple entities within our organization. Senior Payroll Administrator ensures the accurate and timely preparation, documentation, distribution, and reconciliation of the payroll process. They provide day to day support to payroll administrators, maintain compliance with all relevant regulations, policies, and procedures, while continuously improving payroll systems and processes. Senior Payroll Administrator collaborates with HR, finance, other departments, vendors and professional associations to resolve payroll-related issues, provide exceptional service to employees, and support the organization's strategic goals through effective payroll management.

## In this role, you will:

• Support the payroll team in processing a biweekly payroll for multiple entities while ensuring accuracy and processing timelines are met.

• Process and handle retiree payroll and provide vacation relief to payroll administrators.

• Troubleshoot payroll processing software errors (ADP).

• Respond to and resolve inquiries and escalations (JIRA ticket system).

• Work with both the Payroll and HR teams across Canada to clarify and resolve issues.

• Coordinate payroll processing with external service providers when necessary.

• Adhere to and interpret policies and union collective agreements in payroll processing.

• Provide training, technical review, task coordination and guidance to payroll administrators on a daily basis.

• Assist Finance in monthly GL Reconciliations including, income tax, CPP, EI, WSIB and EHT.

• Reconcile Kronos (MyTime) hours to WFN import hours and approve prior to pay run.

• Assist the with reconciliation and processing of T4s/RL1s, T4As & T2200s and reconciliation of WCB overpayments.

• Prepare and balance final payroll wire payments, required tax filings and other payroll-related reports.

• Run daily and biweekly interfaces, update, maintain, and load employee information in the payroll software.

• Assist the with special projects and other responsibilities as required.

• Document and maintain relevant procedures, tools and communications.

• Assist with internal and external audits by providing necessary payroll information and documentation.

• Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant legislation affecting payroll and ensure compliance with all regulations.

## What we are looking for:

• 4-5 years of progressive experience in payroll administration, including experience in a leadership or supervisory role.

• 1-2 year post-secondary diploma or certification in Accounting, Payroll, Bookkeeping, or a related field (or equivalent combination of education and experience).

• Payroll Compliance Practitioner (PCP) certification completed or currently enrolled with a commitment to completion.

• Strong knowledge of payroll regulations, practices, and legislation.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook) and payroll systems, preferably ADP Workforce Now.

• Experience with Kronos (MyTime) is an asset.

• Exceptional attention to detail and mathematical accuracy.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to investigate and resolve payroll discrepancies.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to manage sensitive issues with diplomacy and empathy.

• Ability to prioritize, multitask, and work effectively under pressure in a deadline-driven environment.

• Fluency in both French and English is considered an asset.

## Working Conditions:

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

title: Parts Sepcialist
description:
## Parts Specialist - Saint John

## Reporting to the Parts Manager

Are you ready to take ownership of a critical department and make a real impact? As our Parts Specialist you will be the first line of escalation for parts issues, a strategic partner to the Service team, and a leader who drives best-in-class standards. You'll challenge inefficiencies, coach team members, and ensure that parts availability supports peak equipment performance and internal and external customer satisfaction.

## What You'll Do

Own the integrity of parts departmental processes, ensuring consistent application and ongoing improvement. Provide regular, constructive coaching to junior team members to foster growth, accountability, and alignment with best practices.

Act as the first line of escalation for parts-related issues, proactively stepping into complex or high-friction situations to drive resolution while maintaining clear communication with technicians, Service management, and customers.

Take full ownership of the parts process - from counter and phone orders to internal Service requests - ensuring timely fulfillment and follow-up.

Partner with the Senior Buyer to anticipate stock usage trends, review consumption data, and maintain inventory levels that match demand and seasonality.

Contribute to forecasting discussions to prevent shortages or excess inventory.

Collaborate closely with the Service team to anticipate upcoming repairs, major jobs, and fleet maintenance requirements.

Actively seek and incorporate technician feedback to continuously refine stocking strategies and improve parts availability.

Proactively source new and alternative parts solutions to reduce equipment downtime.

Coordinate inbound and outbound shipments efficiently for internal and external customers.

Maintain disciplined inventory control practices, including cycle counts and participation in annual physical inventory.

Manage warranty parts, and vendor return processing in alignment with reporting standards and supplier requirements.

Keep the parts environment organized, efficient, and reflective of operational excellence.

Other duties as directed by the Parts Manager.

## What We Expect from You

Strong personal accountability - proactively stepping into complex or high-friction situations, driving resolution and maintaining clear communication across the team.

The ability to challenge inefficiencies and implement practical, data-informed improvements.

Coaching mindset: provide consistent feedback and foster a culture of continuous improvement.

Solutions-oriented approach, balancing customer urgency with cost control.

Commitment to a high-performance culture built on measurable outcomes and industry best practices.

## What You Bring

5+ years of progressive parts experience, preferably in heavy equipment or material handling.

Strong parts technical aptitude with the ability to read and interpret parts diagrams and equipment specifications.

Demonstrated knowledge of industry-standard parts processes.

Proven understanding of inventory control principles, forecasting, and consumption trends.

Excellent time management and the ability to prioritize and execute under pressure.

Forklift operation experience (training provided if required).

Ability to lift to 70 lbs.

Valid driver's license & driver's abstract.

Exceptional organizational discipline and attention to detail.

Red Seal Parts certification considered an asset.

Degree in supply chain management or business administration will be considered an asset

Certification as a Supply Chain Management Professional will be considered an asset

## Why You'll Love This Role:

This is not just a parts job - it's a chance to lead, influence, and drive excellence in a critical department. If you thrive in a high-performance environment, enjoy coaching and developing others, and take pride in owning processes end-to-end, this is the role for you.

Develop your career with us by submitting your resume via email.

No Phone Calls

title: Service Dispatcher
description:

Are you a seasoned administrative professional with strong communication and organizational skills interested in building a career with a growing organization?

If so, Prime Material Handling Equipment Limited would love to hear from you!

We are the largest company in Atlantic Canada dedicated exclusively to material handling equipment; we have been providing our customers with high quality equipment, rentals, parts and service since 1993. With branches located in Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, we are looking for a Service Dispatcher in our Moncton Branch to join our growing team.

## As a Service Dispatcher you will:

· Receive calls from customers and assess the type of service mechanical/maintenance work needed

· Schedule and coordinate all service calls as calls are received

· Dispatch field and remote technicians to specific jobs based on the technician's area of expertise on the equipment present at customer sites

· Maintain on-call schedule for all Field and Remote Technicians

· Assess troubleshooting requests addressed by technicians and transfer them to the Technical Communicator for a resolution

· Keep track of the technician workloads to ensure that work is allocated effectively and efficiently amongst technicians

· Utilize technician time efficiently by minimizing lost time between, before and after jobs and minimize travel cost
