title: Building Superintendent
description:
## Building Superintendent

## The Opportunity

Fundy Harbour Group is a family-owned and locally operated business that is growing and expanding. We are seeking a practical, service-minded Building Superintendent to help launch and operate a 79-unit luxury apartment building at South-West at Fundy Quay. This is a hands-on, resident-facing role focused on keeping the property safe, clean, functional and well maintained. The Building Superintendent combines routine and preventative maintenance, resident service, vendor coordination, inspections, emergency response and disciplined recordkeeping to protect the asset and support a hospitality-driven living experience.

## Key Responsibilities

## Building Operations and Maintenance

• Conduct daily and scheduled inspections of common areas, building systems, entrances, parking areas, amenity spaces, service areas and mechanical rooms.

• Perform minor repairs and maintenance within the approved scope of the role, including basic plumbing, hardware, painting, drywall touch-ups, filter changes, light replacement and furniture adjustments.

• Receive, prioritize, document and complete assigned resident maintenance requests promptly and professionally.

• Identify recurring issues, recommend preventive action and support equipment care, energy conservation, warranty protection and long-term asset performance.

• Maintain organized tools, supplies, inventory, mechanical rooms and service areas.

## Vendors, Inspections and Turnover

• Escalate specialized work to qualified trades and coordinate access and follow-up for HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety, elevator, security and building automation contractors.

• Coordinate with property management on preventative maintenance schedules, service contracts, regulatory inspections and recurring building concerns.

• Support suite turnover, move-in and move-out inspections, deficiency tracking, warranty items and preparation of suites and common areas for occupancy.

• Maintain accurate work-order notes, inspection records, incident reports, contractor attendance logs, inventory records and outstanding-action lists.

## Resident Service, Safety and Emergency Response

• Communicate professionally with residents regarding access, inspections, repairs, service interruptions and maintenance scheduling.

• Monitor and respond to safety risks, leaks, odours, noise concerns, heating or cooling issues, access concerns and other conditions affecting resident comfort or building performance.

• Participate in emergency response for water leaks, power issues, fire alarms, security incidents, elevator outages, severe weather and other urgent building matters.

• Collaborate with property management, concierge, porter, cleaning, landscaping and snow-removal teams to maintain strong standards of cleanliness, organization and curb appeal.

• Follow company policies, building rules, occupational health and safety requirements, safe lifting practices and established emergency procedures.

## Qualifications

• Three to five years of experience in residential building maintenance, facilities operations, a superintendent or maintenance technician role, hotel engineering, or a comparable hands-on building operations position.

• Practical knowledge of general plumbing, HVAC and electrical basics, access control, fire/life safety systems, mechanical rooms and common-area maintenance.

• Sound judgment to troubleshoot routine issues, complete work safely and recognize when a licensed trade or specialized vendor is required.

• Strong resident-service, communication, organization and prioritization skills, including the ability to remain calm during urgent situations.

• Ability to use digital work orders, inspection records and maintenance logs, and to provide clear documentation and follow-through.

• Current First Aid/CPR, WHMIS, Fall Protection and Lockout/Tagout Awareness training, or the ability to complete required training before or shortly after starting.

• Ability to lift up to 50 lb and perform the physical requirements of the role, including standing, walking, carrying, bending, climbing permitted stairs or ladders, and working in mechanical and common areas.

• Availability for the evening and weekend on-call rotation.

## What We Provide

• Company-provided tools and secure on-site storage.

• Company uniform and annual clothing allowance.

• Company phone or reimbursement of approved mobile-phone costs for on-call responsibilities.

• Paid on-call response outside regular working hours.

• Competitive pay, annual incentive, benefits and paid vacation.

• A supportive team that values initiative, craftsmanship and professional resident service.

## How to Apply

Please apply on Career Beacon or submit your resume in confidence to Tristan Desrosiers at Tristan.Desrosiers@canhs.ca

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Property Manager
description:
## Property Manager

## The Opportunity

Fundy Harbour Group is a family-owned and locally operated business that is growing and expanding. We are seeking a results-driven Property Manager to lead the day-to-day management of a residential portfolio anchored by South-West at Fundy Quay, with additional responsibility for Vimy Estates and Fundy Harbour Estates. Approximately half of the role will be dedicated to South-West at Fundy Quay. At this new 79-unit luxury apartment building, the Property Manager will help deliver a responsive, hospitality-driven resident experience while coordinating the people, vendors, systems and property operations required to protect the asset and achieve strong financial performance.

## Key Responsibilities

## Resident Experience and Property Operations

• Serve as a visible and responsive point of contact for residents, addressing inquiries, concerns and service issues with professionalism and timely follow-through.

• Set and maintain consistent operating and service standards across the assigned residential portfolio, with particular focus on the hospitality-driven experience at South-West at Fundy Quay.

• Coordinate day-to-day activities among resident services, building operations, maintenance, cleaning, security and other service partners.

• Conduct regular property inspections, identify operational and capital requirements, assign corrective actions and verify completion.

• Coordinate move-ins, move-outs, key and access transfers, suite inspections and resident onboarding.

• Maintain accurate property records, issue logs, incident documentation, lease information and follow-up commitments.

## Leasing and Revenue Management

• Manage residential leasing and vacancy activity, including showings, applicant screening, lease preparation, renewals and tenant onboarding.

• Monitor vacancy, upcoming lease expirations, rental market conditions and leasing performance, and recommend action to support occupancy and revenue objectives.

• Ensure rental agreements and landlord and resident obligations are administered consistently, including rent collection, approved rent increases, service fees and resident responsibilities.

• Identify practical opportunities to improve property revenue while maintaining service quality and resident trust.

## Maintenance, Vendors and Compliance

• Coordinate with the maintenance team and external contractors on service requests, preventative maintenance, repairs, renovations, deficiencies, warranty items and capital improvements.

• Administer and monitor service contracts for cleaning, security, maintenance and other property services, ensuring expectations for scope, schedule, quality and cost are met.

• Coordinate required building inspections, testing and regulatory servicing, and support environmental, insurance and life-safety compliance for each assigned property.

• Promote a safe environment for residents, visitors, employees and contractors and ensure urgent issues are escalated and documented appropriately.

## Financial and Performance Management

• Monitor annual operating and capital budgets for the assigned properties.

• Monitor operating performance, expenditures, recoveries and commitments; investigate variances and coordinate corrective action.

• Prepare clear operational reports and provide timely updates on occupancy, resident issues, maintenance, contracts, risks and capital priorities.

• Work with internal stakeholders to reduce controllable operating costs, strengthen vendor performance and improve portfolio results.

## Qualifications

• Post-secondary education in property management, business administration, building operations or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• Demonstrated residential property management experience, including resident relations, leasing, inspections, maintenance coordination and day-to-day operations.

• Working knowledge of rental agreements, contract administration, service providers, operating budgets and property reporting.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with residents, contractors, maintenance staff and internal stakeholders.

• Excellent organization and time-management skills, with the ability to manage conflicting priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• High level of initiative, judgment, maturity, dependability and attention to detail.

• A collaborative approach, openness to feedback and a consistent commitment to accurate, professional service.

## What We Provide

## Set up to succeed

• An opportunity to shape the operating culture and resident experience at one of the portfolio's signature residential properties.

• A supportive, locally based team that rewards initiative, accountability and strong service.

• Competitive pay, annual incentive, benefits and paid vacation.

## How to Apply

Please apply on Career Beacon or submit your resume in confidence to Tristan Desrosiers at Tristan.Desrosiers@canhs.ca

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Dr. Jacob Matz's orthopaedic surgery practice is seeking an organized, dependable and patient-focused Medical Office Administrator to manage daily office operations and support efficient patient care. The successful candidate will work closely with Dr. Matz within a group practice alongside eight other orthopaedic surgeons and their medical office assistants. Patient reception and communication

Electronic records and correspondence

• Ensure relevant referrals, reports, imaging information and correspondence are available for scheduled appointments.

• Prepare and proofread physician correspondence and clinical documentation from dictation or draft material within the electronic medical record.

• Prepare administrative portions of patient forms and reports for physician review.

• Process incoming and outgoing documents and coordinate authorized requests for patient records.

• Communicate with pharmacies, consultants, family physicians and other health care providers as directed.

Office operations

• Order and maintain office and examination room supplies.

• Maintain clean, organized examination rooms and coordinate cleaning and restocking.

• Assist with the care and maintenance of office equipment.

• Complete daily opening and closing procedures.

• Develop and maintain efficient office procedures and tracking systems.

• Collaborate with other medical office assistants to coordinate shared office needs and coverage.

• Medical Office Administration or Medical Office Assistant diploma, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

• Previous experience in a medical office or a comparable administrative setting.

• Knowledge of medical terminology and medical office procedures.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, email and electronic document management.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including accurate spelling, grammar and proofreading.

• Ability to prepare, organize and maintain patient records.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with discretion.

## Assets

• Previous experience in an orthopaedic or other surgical practice.

• Experience coordinating referrals, surgical bookings and wait lists.

• Familiarity with provincial fee codes, Medicare billing, WorkSafeNB and third-party billing.

• Experience using electronic medical record systems, particularly PS Suite, CHR or Profile.

## Personal Attributes

• Compassion, patience and sensitivity to patients' needs.

• Strong organization, planning and time-management skills.

• Accuracy and attention to detail.

• Ability to prioritize competing demands, meet deadlines and remain professional in a busy office.

• Initiative, sound judgment and the ability to work independently.

• A collaborative approach and reliable follow-through.

This position is based in a group practice with eight other orthopaedic surgeons and their respective medical office assistants. The regular work week is 40 hours. title: Office Administrator
description:
## Title: Office Administrator

## Department: Administration

## Reports to: Director of Resident Care or, in their absence, the Administrator.

## Location: The Northside Community Guest Home

## Purpose

Provide administrative and clerical support across departments to support the daily operations of the Home. Maintain accurate records, prepare documents, coordinate meetings and supplies, and assist with resident-related administrative processes in collaboration with management and staff.

Administrative support and communication

• Provide administrative support to management and staff across departments.

• Prepare and distribute letters, memos, emails, reports and other documents.

• Coordinate meetings, prepare meeting materials, record and distribute minutes, and assist with committee surveys and documentation.

• Scan, copy and distribute nursing and 24-hour reports at the beginning of each workday.

• Check incoming mail and distribute correspondence and reports to the appropriate staff.

• Maintain current telephone directories and departmental contact lists.

## Records and documentation

• General filing of Admin and resident files

• Complete administrative updates for new admissions, resident room changes and deaths, following established checklists and information provided by nursing staff.

• Prepare, update and distribute admission forms, nursing and CCA forms, resident-specific documents, laboratory labels and other required materials.

• Maintain forms binders and ensure current documents are available to staff.

• Print and file annual licence renewal documentation for licensed staff.

• Identify missing or incomplete information and follow up with the appropriate staff.

## Inventory and supplies

• Monitor inventories of nursing, wound care, resident personal care and other designated supplies.

• Complete regular stock checks and place orders within established procedures and approved authority.

• Organize, label and distribute supplies to departments and resident care units.

• Coordinate staff purchases of nursing supplies according to established procedures.

• Report supply shortages, ordering concerns and delivery issues to the appropriate staff.

## Resident service coordination

• Maintain blood and specimen collection lists to reflect admissions, room changes and changes communicated by nursing staff.

• Prepare and distribute monthly blood collection lists and replenish blood tube holders on resident care units.

• Maintain resident hair salon schedules and prepare weekly appointment lists.

• Prepare monthly salon billing documentation accurately and within established timelines.

## Office operations and confidentiality

• Operate office equipment, including printers, label makers, the postage machine and laminator.

• Arrange confidential document shredding according to established procedures.

• Protect resident and employee privacy and maintain the confidentiality of organizational information.

• Follow facility policies, workplace safety requirements and infection prevention and control practices.

• Participate in required meetings, in-service training and quality improvement activities.

## Qualifications

• Completion of an Office Administration program or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

• Previous administrative or clerical experience; experience in a healthcare or long-term care setting is an asset.

• Experience preparing documents, maintaining records and recording meeting minutes.

• Familiarity with inventory tracking, ordering and basic billing processes is an asset.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, email and web browsers.

• Ability to organize and prioritize work, manage interruptions, meet deadlines and maintain accurate records.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively across departments.

• Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information.

## Working conditions and equipment

• Work takes place in an office environment within a long-term care home and involves computer use, document handling and movement throughout the facility.

• Duties include organizing and distributing supplies and using standard office equipment. Use safe handling methods, appropriate equipment and assistance when required.

• Regular interaction with residents, families, staff and service providers requires a courteous and professional approach.

• Work involves interruptions, competing priorities and time-sensitive requests.

## Hours of work

• Regular hours are Monday-Friday (8 hour days)

• Other related duties may be assigned within the scope of the position.

title: Specialist, Standard and Cost Model
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?Who We Are
We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

The Opportunity
We are currently seeking a Standard & Cost Model Specialist to join our Finance team in Sudbury. This is a permanent position for an existing vacancy.

In this role you will shape financial strategy, influence key business decisions, and drive value across Vale's Ontario Operations. This role will lead the development of standardized financial frameworks, cost models, and operational evaluations that support strategic planning, business performance, and continuous improvement. Working closely with Finance, Operations, Technical Services, and Supply Chain teams, you will play a critical role in advancing financial discipline, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and identifying opportunities to improve profitability and operational efficiency across the business.

Additionally, in this position you will:
• Lead initiatives that drive business value, cost optimization, operational performance, and financial decision-making.

• Develop, maintain, and govern Ontario Operations First Principles Cost Review (FPCR) and Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) models and frameworks.

• Standardize cost structures, cost center reporting, and financial processes across Ontario Operations to improve transparency, consistency, and benchmarking.

• Provide financial leadership for operational evaluations, business cases, scenario planning, and strategic investment decisions impacting profitability and production.

• Drive continuous improvement, reporting standardization, financial controls, and best practices across the Ontario Operations FP&A function.

• Lead cross-functional special projects, evaluating financial impacts, challenging assumptions, and ensuring successful implementation of value-generating initiatives.

• Partner with Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Technical Services, and Business Planning teams to support integrated business planning and long-term strategic objectives.

• Ensure compliance with financial policies, governance requirements, and cost-management standards while fostering a culture of accountability and financial discipline.

What We Offer You
• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

About You

## Education:

• Undergraduate degree in Engineering, Economy, Business, Finance or a related field.

• Professional accreditation such as P. Eng., MBA, CPA an asset.

## Experience:

• Minimum 10 years of experience in related role.

## Skills:

• ERP, database, and spreadsheet proficiency

• Cross-functional communication and stakeholder management

• System implementation and process improvement expertise

• Collaboration, leadership, and influencing skills

• Finance and Operations experience

• Change management and continuous improvement capabilities

• Ability to inspire engagement and drive change initiatives

Why Sudbury
Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are needed for the green economy. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

Include to Transform
At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Minimum Starting Salary: $112,800

title: Chief Executive Officer
description:
Higher Talent is excited to conduct a search for a passionate and confident Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for Food First NL, located in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador.

## WHO WE ARE:

Food First NL is a provincial non-profit with more than 25 years of experience leading programs and advocacy across Newfoundland and Labrador. Our team of more than 20 staff works to advance everyone's right to food in Newfoundland and Labrador by advocating, organizing, taking action, and valuing people. Together, we work towards a vision of a province where everyone can eat with joy and dignity.

If you'd like to read more about our Mission, Vision, and goals, you can find them here in our Strategic Framework. Food First NL is entering a new phase of strategic planning, with a new Strategic Framework being completed during the course of this recruitment process. The incoming CEO will play an important role in helping shape and advance this next chapter for the organization.

## THE ROLE:

The CEO is responsible for the overall management and strategic direction for Food First NL. This includes ensuring the financial sustainability of the organization, facilitating strategic and operational planning, building and expanding relationships and partnerships, building capacity among staff and ensuring effective program delivery, overseeing responsible financial management and administration, and supporting effective governance.

This role also offers a unique opportunity to advocate for the well-being of all residents of Newfoundland and Labrador. Food First NL is a prominent organization in this province's public conversation, and we don't take that responsibility lightly. At Food First NL, we value authenticity, accountability, and equity, all while working to highlight and amplify the strengths in our communities. We do this work because we believe a better food system is possible.

## ABOUT YOU:

As CEO, you will provide strategic leadership to Food First NL, working closely with the Board of Directors, staff, partners, funders, and community stakeholders to advance the organization's mission and long-term impact.

• Leadership and Governance: You will lead the organization's short- and long-term strategic planning, organizational development, and annual work planning. Working closely with the Board of Directors, you will support effective governance, policy development, organizational decision-making, and the implementation of strategic priorities. You will foster a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board Chair and Directors, keeping the Board informed and engaged while supporting the recruitment, orientation, and development of new Board members.

• Fund Development and Financial Management: You will provide strategic oversight of Food First NL's financial sustainability and lead efforts to build a diverse and strong funding base. This includes identifying and pursuing funding opportunities across government, private, philanthropic, and other sectors, as well as exploring opportunities for revenue generation. You will build and maintain strong relationships with funders and ensure timely, accurate, and compelling financial and narrative reporting that clearly demonstrates the impact of their contributions. You will also provide oversight of organizational financial planning, budgeting, and management, ensuring resources are aligned with strategic priorities and the long-term sustainability of the organization.

• Communications, Public Relations, and Advocacy: As a key ambassador for Food First NL, you will serve as the organization's public face and lead spokesperson. You will represent Food First NL with confidence and credibility through media interviews, presentations, panel discussions, conferences, and other public forums. To set the conditions for success, you will oversee the development and implementation of effective communications strategies. As an advocate, you will bring Food First NL's messages about policy change to the public and to all levels of government. You'll work as part of multiple coalitions, connect with partners across the country, and oversee the research and writing that creates the foundation for policy change.

• Human Resources and Organizational Development: You will provide strategic oversight of Food First NL's human resources, ensuring the organization has the people, skills, and organizational capacity required to achieve its goals. Valuing people is one of Food First NL's core pathways to impact. As CEO, you will support a positive, collaborative, and inclusive workplace culture. Staff will look to you to ensure that Food First NL is always intentionally working to better understand and implement ideas of equity and justice. Alongside the leadership team, you will review and evolve Food First NL's organizational structure and human resource policies and practices. You will provide oversight to recruitment, orientation and training, supervision, performance management, and professional development.

• Network and Partnership Development: You will be a relationship-builder and connector, developing and maintaining strong partnerships with organizations, agencies, community leaders, champions, funders, and other stakeholders across Newfoundland and Labrador and beyond. You will identify opportunities for collaboration, build strategic relationships, and represent Food First NL in networks and partnerships that strengthen the organization's reach and impact.

## WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT:

• An attractive total compensation package and a comprehensive benefits package including:
• Annual leave of 15 days to start, with 1 additional day per year of service to a maximum of 30 days.

• 15 Paid Public Holidays plus 3 days closure between Christmas and New Years.

• 12 Community Service and Food Provisioning days.

• Ample sick and personal leave time available as needed.

• Group Insurance Plan inclusion after 90 days.

• Starting Salary: Between $81,995 and $91,105 depending on experience. A cost of living increase is applied annually every February. Seniority-based increases are also applied annually until the top of the salary band (currently $100,216) is reached. Salary is set according to a salary scale and is not negotiable.

• Collaborative, entrepreneurial culture with local decision-making.

• A home base in St. John's with a flexible work environment with the opportunity for a hybrid of in-office and remote work and regular provincial and national travel.

• A significant amount of provincial travel is necessarily done by car - you don't need your own vehicle for this role, but you do need a valid drivers' license and a clean driving record.

## EQUITY

Food First NL recognizes that systemic barriers related to gender, race and ethnicity, Indigeneity, ability, physical and mental health, age, and socio-economic status limit or prevent people's equal access to power and resources within society. In order to address these barriers within our own organization and the broader community, Food First NL is committed to practicing equity in all aspects of our work, including hiring.

If you are ready to step into this exciting opportunity and bring your leadership, expertise and passion for advancing everyone's right to food in Newfoundland and Labrador to Food First NL, apply today!

title: Legal Services Technician 1-2
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50286

Department: Public Prosecution Service

Location: SYDNEY

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 10-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Nova Scotia Public Prosecution Service (PPS) was established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada. The Public Prosecution Service is responsible for all prosecutions and appeals within the jurisdiction of the Attorney General.
With the guiding mission of providing fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of offences, the PPS prosecutes charges laid under the Criminal Code and under Nova Scotia statutes such as the Occupational Health and Safety Act. The Head Office is in Halifax and there are regional offices located throughout the province.
The core functions of the Nova Scotia Public Prosecution Service are to:

• Represent the Crown in the conduct of criminal trials and quasi criminal appeals before all levels of courts.

• Participate in the development of criminal law and criminal prosecutions policy.

• Provide advice to police in respect of prosecutions generally or in respect of specific investigations

For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit https://novascotia.ca/pps/

About Our Opportunity
As the Legal Services Technician 1-2, you will work in a team environment providing legal assistance, case management, file management and secretarial/administrative support for Crown Attorneys of the Public Prosecution Service. Your knowledge of legal terminology and specialized criminal law procedures will be put to the test as you use your understanding of the prosecution process and court proceedings to support the Public Prosecution Office.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role you will be creating, tracking and managing all Public Prosecution Service criminal and administrative files. In the trial/appeal process, you will prepare legal documents including affidavits, subpoenas and orders, briefs, factums and memoranda, while ensuring that the highest PPS and Court standards of accuracy and completeness are met in a highly confidential office setting.
You will respond to requests from all levels of government, private law firms and the public for information and assistance and acts as a referral source for victims of crime to Victim Services agencies.

Qualifications and Experience
To be successful in this role you will have a certificate or diploma from a Paralegal program or Legal Assistant program. An acceptable combination of education/training and experience may be considered.
Demonstrated experience in an automated environment using Microsoft Word, Outlook or similar transferrable programs is required. Your proficient and accurate transcription skills (handwritten or dicta methods), as well as strong typing skills.
As the ideal candidate you will have strong attention to detail, prioritization and organizational skills with the ability to combine speed and accuracy while under pressure to meet deadlines. You are able to deal effectively in a multifaceted and sometimes stressful environment (often in confrontational and sensitive situations) while ensuring confidentiality.
Fairness and impartiality must be displayed at all times with clients and other staff, police, and defense lawyers, and all duties and responsibilities are to be carried out with the highest degree of confidentiality.
Must have demonstrated excellent verbal and written skills, a high degree of initiative, problem solving, independent work habits, and readily accept responsibility.
The following are considered assets in this position:

• Exposure to the justice system and government services

• Experience with JEIN and PICS

• Working knowledge of the STAR/STOR central file management system or other filing systems

• Demonstrated understanding of the prosecutions process, experience working with legal documents and forms, understanding of court proceedings and legal terminology

• Legal research and retrieval of relevant case law using electronic tools (e.g., Quicklaw, Westlaw, CanLII and/or legal libraries)

All successful candidates must be able to pass appropriate background checks.
We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day (8:30 AM to 4:30 PM)

• May be required to work overtime on occasion

• Mental Pressures Include: balancing multiple priorities, high demand for accuracy and attention to detail, tight deadlines

• Physical Pressures Include: sitting at a desk and keyboarding for extensive lengths of time, lift/move/carry heavy file boxes

• Nature of the work environment (prosecution of criminal offences) may bring staff into contact with individuals who are verbally abusive and physically threatening

• You will be exposed to graphic and disturbing material of a nature which would not be encountered in ordinary workplaces (e.g. photographic materials involving victims of violent crime)

• You will be working with highly distraught victims of crime which can create a stressful and emotionally draining work environment

• Public reaction to certain prosecution case results can produce stress in the general social (outside of the office) environment

Additional Information
This is a permanent full-time employment opportunity, located in Sydney, NS.

What We Offer
• Career development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace - our employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

Pay Grade: TE 13 - TE 19

Salary Range: $1,719.61 - $1,967.62 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your electronic application.

If you require an accommodation throughout the recruitment process, please contact us at competitions@novascotia.ca.

description:

Reporting to the appropriate Manager, Benefit Payment Services, you will be responsible for calculating benefits, allowances, and awards for injured workers, including wage reviews, long-term assessments, and Permanent Physical Impairment (PPI) awards. You will evaluate income data from various sources, applying relevant policies, and ensuring accurate loss of earnings calculations. Strong communication skills are essential for collaborating with internal teams and external stakeholders, such as employers, injured workers, and third-party representatives. Additionally, you will ensure compliance with internal guidelines and resolve any discrepancies or missed payments.

Salary And Hours Of Work:
• Hours of work are those required to perform the assigned tasks but shall not be less than 35 hours per week, 7 per day. Monday to Friday between 8:00-5:00 PM.
• The hourly rate for this position is $30.28. CUPE 1866 employees receive Step 1 of the pay band for the position appointment.

## Responsibilities

• Performing initial benefit calculations, including 12-week wage reviews, annual reviews, and long-term disability assessments. Calculating cost transfers, care allowances, weekly allowances, and Permanent Physical Impairment (PPI) awards. Processing Gradual Return to Work evaluations and apply TD1 exemptions.
• Processing calculations related to Canada Pension Plan Disability (CPPD) benefits and employer disability insurance (e.g., Sunlife). Evaluating how injured workers' receipt of CPPD benefits, employer disability benefits, and other supplemental incomes affect WorkSafeNB loss of earnings calculations and benefits.
• Handling internet payments, regular loss of earnings (RLOE) payments, salary payments and corrections, as well as inter-jurisdictional payments. Proactively identifying and resolving any missed payments.
• Collecting wage and income information from various sources such as the Canada Revenue Agency, T4 slips, and Records of Employment. Reviewing and assessing documents to ensure accuracy and completeness for loss of earnings calculations, applying appropriate analysis as required.
• Engaging with Managers, Team Leads, Benefit Payment Specialists, Claims Adjudicators, Case Managers, Medical Aid and Disability Coordinators, and Quality Management Services teams to ensure seamless information flow and decision-making. Liaising with employers, injured workers, and third-party representatives (e.g., disability insurers, Employment Insurance, Social Development) to provide accurate information and support the claims process.
• Ensuring proactive and transparent communication across all channels, addressing questions and providing updates to both internal and external stakeholders to enhance collaboration and service delivery.
• Other duties as required based on operational needs or specific project requirements.

## Qualifications

• A one (1) year post-secondary diploma or certificate in office administration, business, or a related field.
• One (1) year of relevant experience.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Case Management system, and Adobe Acrobat Pro to handle documents, communications, and workflow processes efficiently. Strong mathematical and analytical skills to accurately calculate benefits, including interpreting multiple income sources, timeframes, and applying relevant policies and legislation to determine compensation for injured workers. In-depth knowledge of policies, legislation, and directives related to benefit calculations and workers' compensation to ensure compliance and provide accurate information.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

## Competencies:

• Adaptability
• Ensuring Accountability
• Teamwork and Collaboration
• Client-focused Service
• Information Gathering and Processing
• Digital Literacy
• Resilience
• Analytical Thinking
• Problem Solving
• Enabling Communication

Linguistic profiles for these positions include English written and spoken and Bilingual (English and French) written and spoken.

Your primary workspace will be from your in-home office, with the occasional expectation of in person meetings, for that reason, working from outside the province of New Brunswick, or country, is not permissible.

If you are interested in pursuing these opportunities with WorkSafeNB, please apply online at www.worksafenb.ca by November 20, 2026.

We thank all those who apply however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted.

For more information about WorkSafeNB, or this and other employment opportunities, please visit our website at worksafenb.ca.

## About Us

The team at WorkSafeNB is passionate about promoting health and safety in New Brunswick workplaces. We strive to make New Brunswick the safest place to work. However, injuries do occur, and when they do, we are committed to providing caring recovery and return to work services, benefits, and compensation to injured workers and their families. Culture is the heartbeat of the organization. The stronger it is, the further we go! Selected by our employees, our WorkSafeNB values shape our culture. We put our values of Accountability, Collaboration and Trust into ACTion. We demonstrate accountability by taking pride in and ownership of our work so we can take care of our clients and other New Brunswickers. Through collaboration, we build strong partnerships and innovate to achieve better outcomes. Trust guides our organization; we lead and listen with empathy and embrace diversity, inclusion and belonging. These ACTions shape us.

The Nuclear Medicine Technologist IIA is responsible for performing standardized and complex diagnostic and therapeutic Nuclear Medicine procedures. The philosophy of a Family Care Team (FCT) is to deliver care that is patient-centered, comprehensive, team-based, culturally safe, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety. This philosophy supports providers and care teams to meet clients where they are using an inter-professional collaborative approach where care is provided in the right place, at the right time, by the right provider in a manner that best suits the client’s need. The team will ensure clients are treated with respect, dignity, and compassion, and enable strong and trusting relationships with providers and staff. FCT’s will enable the delivery of a range of quality care for clients within their own communities while facilitating interdisciplinary work amongst healthcare providers. The FCT for the Gander/ Gander Bay will include the geographical areas of Gander and Gander Bay.

Definition of work:
The Primary Health Care Program is seeking an advanced professional Clinical Dietitian II for the Gander/Gander Bay FCT. The Clinical Dietitian II is responsible for the provision of nutrition care (i.e. screening, assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation) to clients of the FCT as well as the planning, implementation, coordination and evaluation of nutrition services. The principles of the FCT align with the patient health home model of care; using a collaborative health care team approach, from various health disciplines, in the provision of primary health care services to clients.

This position functions with a high degree of independence and initiative. The successful incumbent will report to the Regional Manager of the Gander/Gander Bay Family Care Team. Primary Health Care Program and will maintain accountability to the Regional Professional Practice Consultant for Dietitians for integrity and professional practice issues.

Nutrition services will include (but is not limited to) health promotion, disease prevention, nutrition counselling (group and individual) and chronic disease management. In this role, the Dietitian will support the development, implementation and evaluation of nutrition practice, program and quality improvement initiatives within the FCT; participate in evidence informed practice, education and community capacity building; and play a lead role in the development of primary health care initiatives using a nutrition lens.

Clients in this primary health care setting have diverse nutritional needs and may include frail elderly, clients with acute and/or chronic disease and those at risk for malnutrition; as such the dietitians practice will reflect the needs of the clients/community. Care will be provided face to face and virtually as necessary and appropriate. The dietitian will apply their skills of advocate and change agent to support the FCT's mission; collaborate with the FCT team in the provision of care; engage with acute care and community supports in the provision of care; assist clients with navigation through the health system; and mentor other dietitians and team members.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. Travel throughout the region may be required.

Required qualifications:
• Successful completion of Bachelor’s Degree specializing in Applied Human Nutrition or equivalent field of science as approved by the NLCD, supplemented by a 1-year internship and a Registered Dietitian (RD) professional designation.
• Registration with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Dietitians is required.
• Two (2) years’ experience within the last five (5) as a Clinical Dietitian.
• Thorough knowledge of nutritional health promotion strategies; nutritional interventions to prevent and manage acute and chronic disease; clinical nutrition care processes; behavior change theory; primary care nutrition risk screening strategies and pathways; clinical nutrition presentations requiring referral to secondary health care services; and the broader health system and community supports.
• Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with inter-professional team members, patients/residents/clients and their families in a one-to-one and group environment.
• Demonstrated effective written communication skills required for client documentation, report writing and professional communication
• Demonstrated ability to assume professional responsibility for safe, ethical and effective practice.
• Demonstrated supervisory and leadership skills.
• Demonstrated ability to function effectively in a diverse and changing environment.
• Demonstrated ability to lead practice initiatives within the nutrition/dietetics community of practice.
• A valid Newfoundland and Labrador Class IV Driver's License.

• The use of a private vehicle is a condition of employment.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position.
• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority.

Job Summary
Licensed Practical Nurses are valuable members of the Resident Care Team in long-term care. They provide quality nursing care to residents by assisting in their daily living activities, providing personal care, and promoting independent living. In long-term care, the LPN role is directed towards meeting the resident’s physical, social and spiritual needs through partnerships with the resident, the resident’s family, and other members of the interprofessional team. The LPN as appropriate is accountable for the planning and supervision of care, within their scope of practice. They are accountable to provide support and direction to Personal Care Attendants, monitor resident outcomes, intervene if necessary, and reassess and adjust the plan of care or resident assignment as needed, in consultation with the Registered Nurse.

Long-term care settings are often complex. Residents have diverse needs resulting from such conditions as chronic illness and functional and cognitive impairments. This population includes frail or elderly adults, individuals with physical and intellectual disabilities and/or individuals with mental illness. The work environment is fast paced with frequent contact with the public, residents, and other health professionals.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly requires physical exertion and handling, moving, pushing, or pulling objects between 10 – 15 lbs. and occasionally required to support, lift, or move patients/objects up to 30 lbs.
Regularly required to work in awkward, cramped positions (bending/kneeling/stretching) and constantly standing and moving about.
Regularly pushes and pulls objects using light to medium forces and stands and walks.
Regularly requires visual concentration to give medications, read orders/referrals, patients’ charts/document, observe and treat patients combined with time pressures and deadlines.

Job Qualifications
Successful completion of an approved Licensed Practical Nursing program.
Current and continuing practicing licensure as a Licensed Practical Nurse with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Nurses is required.
Current BLS certification is required.
Gerontology experience is preferred.
Knowledge of seniors’ issues and support best practice in gerontological care.
Ability to deal effectively with end-of-life issues.
Demonstrated strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to maintain effective working relationships.
Demonstrated initiative and the ability to work independently.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

*The successful applicant must complete in house training in order to care for residents requiring mechanical ventilation at the first available opportunity.

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Director, Case Management
description:
## About us

At WorkplaceNL, we provide compensation and support to injured workers and their employers during recovery, rehabilitation, and safe return to work. We also work with employers, employees, health care providers, stakeholders, and our community partners to provide occupational health and safety education and help prevent workplace injuries and illnesses in the province.

## The opportunity

We are currently looking for two director positions to lead our teams responsible for ensuring injured workers receive benefits to which they are entitled, while facilitating recovery from workplace injuries, and supporting timely return to work.

Reporting to the Vice President of Prevention and Workplace Services, these roles will also guide the development, implementation and evaluation of strategies, policies, objectives, and performance metrics - to ensure injured workers are provided with quality services that promote recovery and safe return to work.

## More about the role

Some key responsibilities of these director positions include:

Job Summary
Licensed Practical Nurses are valuable members of the Resident Care Team in long-term care. They provide quality nursing care to residents by assisting in their daily living activities, providing personal care, and promoting independent living. In long-term care, the LPN role is directed towards meeting the resident’s physical, social and spiritual needs through partnerships with the resident, the resident’s family, and other members of the interprofessional team. The LPN as appropriate is accountable for the planning and supervision of care, within their scope of practice. They are accountable to provide support and direction to Personal Care Attendants, monitor resident outcomes, intervene if necessary, and reassess and adjust the plan of care or resident assignment as needed, in consultation with the Registered Nurse.

Long-term care settings are often complex. Residents have diverse needs resulting from such conditions as chronic illness and functional and cognitive impairments. This population includes frail or elderly adults, individuals with physical and intellectual disabilities and/or individuals with mental illness. The work environment is fast paced with frequent contact with the public, residents, and other health professionals.

Job Demands
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
Regularly requires physical exertion and handling, moving, pushing, or pulling objects between 10 – 15 lbs. and occasionally required to support, lift, or move patients/objects up to 30 lbs.
Regularly required to work in awkward, cramped positions (bending/kneeling/stretching) and constantly standing and moving about.
Regularly pushes and pulls objects using light to medium forces and stands and walks.
Regularly requires visual concentration to give medications, read orders/referrals, patients’ charts/document, observe and treat patients combined with time pressures and deadlines.

Job Qualifications
Successful completion of an approved Licensed Practical Nursing program.
Current and continuing practicing licensure as a Licensed Practical Nurse with the Newfoundland and Labrador College of Nurses is required.
Current BLS certification is required.
Gerontology experience is preferred.
Knowledge of seniors’ issues and support best practice in gerontological care.
Ability to deal effectively with end-of-life issues.
Demonstrated strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to maintain effective working relationships.
Demonstrated initiative and the ability to work independently.
A satisfactory record of work performance is required.

*The successful applicant must complete in house training in order to care for residents requiring mechanical ventilation at the first available opportunity.

• You are comfortable working in a digital environment; you take responsibility for acquiring knowledge about advancing technology, and you are committed to using technology to create an exceptional student experience.

## Relevant Skills and Knowledge:

• You demonstrate a commitment to inclusion, diversity, equity, accessibility and anti-racism.

• Possess a curiosity and interest in data and analytics.

• A positive, self-starter that will seek out opportunities to learn and add business value to the Analytics team and the organization.

• Ability to translate business requirements to develop report prototypes that lead to business buy-in and refinement of the final deliverables.

• Experience gathering and documenting detailed business requirements for reporting solutions.

• Excellent Analytical skills and strong attention to detail.

• Excellent communication skills and presentation skills.

• Excellent interpersonal and collaborative skills.

Responsibilities

## What you will be doing…

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Institutional Research and Effectiveness and as part of the Business Analytics Team, you will:

• Develop a strong understanding of business processes for Academic Operations & Planning, Institutional Research, Finance, and HR in order to be able to better support their Business Intelligence needs for the College through an understanding of how reports and information can enable them to perform their role more effectively.

• Analyze Information and reporting business requirements, explore and evaluate various options, develop prototypes using reporting and dashboard tools up front in the project life cycle thereby validating the requirements, eliminating ambiguity and providing early visibility to business on the final solution.

• Work closely with the team in designing and developing reports, dashboards and implementing report security solutions.

• Participate and assist in User Acceptance testing, train users on usage of the tool and the solution.

• Working collaboratively with the team to perform administrative functions with our BI tools including Cognos BI, Microsoft Power BI, and Microsoft Fabric tools and capabilities. This will include setting up and maintaining report security, scheduled jobs, automated report delivery, and report migration between environments.

• Build and maintain collaborative relationships with Business Analytics Team members, Office of Learning and Transformation and Digital Innovation & Technology personnel and with business stakeholders.
