title: Director, Entitlement and Extended Claims
description:
## About us

At WorkplaceNL, we provide compensation and support to injured workers and their employers during recovery, rehabilitation, and safe return to work. We also work with employers, employees, health care providers, stakeholders, and our community partners to provide occupational health and safety education and help prevent workplace injuries and illnesses in the province.

## The opportunity

We are currently looking for two director positions to lead our teams responsible for ensuring injured workers receive benefits to which they are entitled, while facilitating recovery from workplace injuries, and supporting timely return to work.

Reporting to the Vice President of Prevention and Workplace Services, these roles will also guide the development, implementation and evaluation of strategies, policies, objectives, and performance metrics - to ensure injured workers are provided with quality services that promote recovery and safe return to work.

## More about the role

Some key responsibilities of these director positions include:

• Overseeing the day-to-day running of all operations within the departments.

• Developing, attracting, retaining, motivating and supervising an effective management team to achieve objectives.

• Involving key stakeholders, workers and employers in proactive early and safe return to work initiatives, effective claims management and workplace safety.

• Overseeing technology advancements (and other projects) to ensure teams are successful in integrating systems and operational practices that help modernize service delivery.

• Creating benchmarks and setting evidence-based outcomes that mobilize teams to enhance delivery and impact change, while communicating results.

• Ensuring timely action with relevant parties, to respond to, and impact change.

• Adopting a continuous improvement approach to assessing and evaluating programs and services, with a focus on improving efficiency and removing non-value-added activities.

• Travel is required.

## Ideal qualifications

• A university degree in a social science, health care, business, public administration, commerce, or a similar discipline, preferably at the master's level.

• Five or more years of experience in a leadership role, with management capacity to effectively work in a team environment.

• Strong leadership abilities and exceptional interpersonal communication and planning abilities - including five years of management experience.

• Ability to think strategically, analytically and use good judgement in providing oversight and solutions to support the delivery of public services.

• Skilled problem solver with the ability to manage issues and work independently.

• Experience implementing key performance indicators and using evidence to inform change.

• Strong communication skills and abilities - both oral and written.

## What success looks like

A successful candidate must see their values and workstyle resonating with our purpose - to improve the quality of life through safe workplaces that support our clients. As a successful candidate, y ou possess a dynamic leadership style focussed on:

• Leading yourself by being self-aware, managing your performance and health, developing yourself, and demonstrating character that is inline with our values .

• Engaging others through fostering their development, contributing to creating a healthy organization, communicating effectively and building strong teams.

• Achieving results by setting direction, strategically aligning your decisions with our values and purpose, implementing decisions and assessing and evaluating outcomes.

• Developing coalitions through purpose-built partnerships and networks that create results.

• Transforming systems by thinking analytically and critically - questioning and challenging the status quo, encouraging innovation, orienting yourself to the future and orchestrating change.

## Why work with us

We offer a comprehensive rewards package that includes competitive compensation, group health, dental and vision benefits, as well as a generous paid leave program and enrollment in the Public Service Pension Plan.

Our team members can also take advantage of flexible work arrangements, including a hybrid work-from home model; opportunities for training, growth and career advancement, in a safe and welcoming environment.

## About Us

At WorkplaceNL, we focus on improving quality of life for the people of Newfoundland and Labrador through safe workplaces and support for our clients. We provide occupational health and safety education and help prevent workplace injury and illness. We also provide compensation and support to workers, and their employers, during recovery and return to work.

title: Senior Program Manager
description:
Title: Senior Program Manager

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Program Manager is responsible for leading strategic programs, service innovations, and operational improvement initiatives across the Health in Emergencies (HIE) portfolio. The role focuses on the development, piloting, implementation, and evaluation of new programs, services, and operating models that strengthen HIE's ability to deliver effective domestic health emergency preparedness, response, and recovery activities. The position provides oversight of multiple concurrent programs and projects, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, operational needs, and community impacts. Working collaboratively with technical health specialists, relief/recovery and operational teams, and cross-functional stakeholders, the Senior Program Manager establishes standardized project and program management approaches, systems, governance processes, and reporting mechanisms to enhance consistency, accountability, and performance across HIE. The role drives continuous improvement, supports evidence-informed decision making, and contributes to the successful scaling and sustainability of priority services and programs.

## In this role, you will:

• Support the planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of strategic programs and initiatives within the Health in Emergencies portfolio.

• Design, pilot, and assess new services, programs, and operating models to address emerging organizational and community needs.

• Apply strong analytical and problem-solving skills to interpret data, identify trends, assess risks, and support evidence-based decision-making.

• Analyze program data, budgets, financial forecasts, operational metrics, and stakeholder feedback to drive informed decision-making and continuous improvement.

• Identify opportunities to enhance program effectiveness, operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and service delivery through innovation and process improvement.

• Manage multiple concurrent programs and projects, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities, operational requirements, budget allocations, timelines, and performance objectives.

• Monitor program progress, dependencies, risks, issues, financial performance, and resource requirements, implementing mitigation strategies as needed.

• Develop and maintain program plans, project schedules, governance frameworks, performance indicators, budget tracking mechanisms, and reporting processes.

• Lead the development and implementation of standardized project and program management methodologies, tools, templates, and processes across Health in Emergencies.

• Support the optimization and adoption of project management, reporting, and collaboration platforms to improve coordination, visibility, financial accountability, and operational effectiveness.

• Establish and maintain consistent approaches to project intake, prioritization, resource allocation, budgeting, tracking, reporting, and evaluation across the department.

• Prepare reports, dashboards, presentations, financial analyses, and briefing materials to support senior leadership decision-making.

• Collaborate with technical health experts, operational teams, emergency management personnel, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure successful program delivery and responsible stewardship of resources.

• Foster stakeholder engagement and build strong working relationships to advance strategic objectives and achieve program outcomes.

• Support organizational change management initiatives related to new programs, systems, processes, and service delivery models.

• Develop and implement monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks to measure program performance, outcomes, financial sustainability, and impact.

• Capture and share lessons learned, best practices, and recommendations to support knowledge transfer and organizational learning.

• Contribute to domestic emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and surge operations by providing program management leadership, resource coordination, and budget oversight.

• Ensure programs and initiatives remain adaptable and responsive to changing operational priorities, emerging risks, budget pressures, and evolving organizational needs.

• Represent Health in Emergencies on internal working groups, committees, and project teams, as required.

• Perform other related duties in support of Health in Emergencies strategic and operational objectives.

## What we are looking for:

• University degree in Public Health, Health Sciences, Emergency Management, Business Administration, Project Management, Finance, or a related discipline; Master's degree considered an asset.

• Minimum 6+ years of experience managing complex programs, projects, strategic initiatives, and associated budgets within health, emergency management, humanitarian, public sector, or related environments.

• Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent programs and projects, including budget oversight, resource allocation, and financial forecasting in a fast-paced and evolving operational environment.

• Experience leading the design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and financial management of programs, services, or strategic initiatives.

• Experience establishing or enhancing project management frameworks, governance structures, financial controls, systems, and reporting processes.

• Experience leading pilot projects, service innovation initiatives, continuous improvement efforts, or organizational change initiatives.

• Experience working with multidisciplinary teams, including technical subject matter experts, operational personnel, and finance stakeholders.

• Experience developing and presenting reports, briefings, dashboards, financial analyses, and recommendations for senior leadership.

• Strong knowledge of program and project management principles, methodologies, governance practices, and financial management best practices.

• Strong planning, organizational, portfolio management, and budget management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.

• Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong facilitation, communication, negotiation, and relationship management skills.

• Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and coordinate work across teams without direct supervisory authority.

• Experience developing performance measurement, monitoring, evaluation, financial reporting, and accountability frameworks.

• Knowledge of risk management, change management, financial stewardship, and continuous improvement methodologies.

• Ability to translate strategic objectives into operational plans, resource requirements, budget plans, and measurable outcomes.

• Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, financial analysis, and business intelligence tools (e.g., Microsoft Project, Planner, SharePoint, Power BI, Power Platform, or equivalent).

• Strong analytical skills, including the ability to interpret financial, operational, and performance data to support decision-making and resource optimization.

• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment and adapt to changing priorities, operational requirements, and budget considerations.

• Knowledge of emergency management, public health, health systems, or humanitarian operations is considered an asset.
PMP, PgMP, PRINCE2, Agile, Lean, Change Management, or other relevant professional certification is considered an asset.

• Ability and willingness to support domestic emergency response operations, including deployment or surge assignments as required.

## Working Conditions:

• Occasional requirement for prolonged standing with infrequent breaks in order to perform the requirements of the role.

• Requires significant attention to detail and concentration and ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• The work pace is often unpredictable with significant time pressures.

• Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, and make decisions under pressure, work at an unpredictable pace.

• The role includes fieldwork, deployment to emergency operations, and office-based work during non-deployment periods.

• Some domestic or international travel to generally safe locations; exposure to moderate adverse conditions requiring attention to personal safety.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, conflicting deadlines.

• Work requires interactions with clients who may be agitated, or are experiencing stressful situations.

• In a large-scale emergency, where staff numbers are compromised or additional resources are required provide disaster relief and/or emergency field operational support.

• Will be required to work extended hours during peak periods on short notice.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

title: Civil Engineering Technologist - Intermediate
description:
## SUMMARY

Reporting to the director of technical services, the incumbent performs a variety of technical and operational tasks; assists in the development, design and execution of maintenance, renovation and construction work on municipal infrastructure, such as roads, signage, water, sewer and storm water systems, and others; and inspects sites, solves problems, plans preventive maintenance of City assets, and ensures compliance with plans and specifications.

## DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Collaborate in the development, writing and design of technical plans and specifications

• Design, analyze, revise and update plans and specifications manually and using computer-assisted software (AutoCAD Civil 3D)

• Participate in the technical planning, execution, supervision and inspection of construction and repair work on roads and water, sewer and storm water systems

• Ensure that work is performed in accordance with approved plans, specifications, applicable legislation, existing conditions and established timelines

• Prepare progress and final reports

• Calculate the quantities and costs of materials and labour required to complete projects

• Monitor the installation of asphalt during road rehabilitation projects to ensure that contractors meet the quantity and quality requirements specified in their contract

• Verify compliance of documents with applicable standards, regulations and other requirements, and communicate with applicants to propose modifications or alternatives

• Collect and compile data required for analysis, preparation of plans and updating of databases and computerized maps

• Work with utility companies to locate utilities at work sites

• Prepare tender documents for crushed stone and other materials, analyze bids and make recommendations to the supervisor

• Perform technical tasks related to infrastructure maintenance programs

• Report any anomalies detected or improvements needed during the execution of work to management, and analyze and resolve routine technical issues that may arise during construction

• Participate in the planning and study of projects by conducting preliminary analyses, preparing reports and researching new products and technologies

• Liaise with internal departments, public utilities, government agencies, the public, contractors, consultants and other external firms to share or obtain technical information

• Process and follow up on verbal and written requests from residents, businesses and property owners

• Perform any other technical functions, not limited to those mentioned above, required to assist in the completion of projects and the smooth running of operations

• Utilize computer-assisted design and drafting software (AutoCAD Civil 3D), geodetic measuring devices (GPS) and geographic information systems (GIS) and apply the principles of data collection

• Assist with the management of road and sub-road assets

• Perform any other tasks, technical and otherwise, required to assist in the completion of projects or for the smooth running of operations

## MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

## Education

• High school diploma or equivalent and a college diploma in civil engineering technology or a related discipline

## Professional designation

• Professional Technologist (PTech)

## Training

• Standard first aid and CPR

• Additional certifications and training may be required, depending on operational needs

## Driver's license

• Class 5

## Experience

• Five (5) years' experience in engineering in a municipal setting

## Knowledge

• Good command of spoken and written French and English

• Extensive knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

• Extensive knowledge of regulations and standards related to municipal infrastructure

• Extensive knowledge of computer-assisted design and drafting software (AutoCAD Civil 3D)

• Extensive knowledge of the use of geodetic measuring devices (GPS), geographic information systems (GIS) and the principles of data collection

• Extensive knowledge of construction materials, the reading of plans and specifications, construction methods, the supervision of construction work, the assessment of site conditions, and enforcement of specifications

• Basic knowledge of surveying

## Skills

• Ability to strategically initiate, develop and implement work and projects

• Ability to read and interpret plans, specifications and technical reports

• Ability to work independently and as part of a team

• Initiative, methodical approach, sense of organization and observation, ability to manage priorities, and attention to detail

• Ability to analyze and synthesize information, reason logically and exercise sound judgment to solve problems and make informed and independent decisions

• Ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt quickly to changes and urgent demands

• Interpersonal skills to communicate effectively and respond calmly to requests

• High ethical standards

• Positive attitude with respect to the interests of the municipality and the community in general

• Punctuality and regular attendance

• Physical ability to do the work assigned

• Good past record of job performance

• Respect for the City of Dieppe's confidentiality rules and organizational values

## WORK SCHEDULE

• As per current collective agreement - Forty (40) hours per week

## SALARY

• Based on the current collective agreement

## CLOSING DATE

• The deadline to submit an application is November 16th, 2026 at 23 h 59.

N.B.: The above statements reflect the characteristic aspects of the job in question and are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. They should not, however, be considered an exhaustive list of all the responsibilities, duties, abilities, and inherent requirements of the position. All staff members may, from time to time, be required to perform duties outside their normal responsibilities, as needed.

Note: Please note that the municipality officially declared itself a francophone city offering bilingual services in 2000 (Municipal Administration Language Policy A-9). French is the City's working language, and all staff must be able to speak and write in French and English.

title: Instructor, Pipelaying
description:
New Brunswick Community College (NBCC) is committed to transforming lives and communities. The College is currently seeking dynamic and competent individuals for the position of Instructor, Pipelaying. When you work at NBCC, you are a valued team member and a part of a community of leaders who are driven by learning excellence and social and economic development.

Position Type: Casual position to deliver a customized introductory training program. Initial delivery is anticipated to be approximately 3-4 training days.

Location: Moncton, NB (Offsite Training Facility)

Salary Range: $33.85 to $52.08 hourly, based on experience and level of post-secondary education.

Qualifications

## Education/Experience:

• Diploma, certificate, or apprenticeship training in Civil Construction, Heavy Equipment Operation, Construction Engineering Technology, or a related field with relevant years of industry experience.

• A minimum of three (3) years of recent experience in civil construction, underground utility installation, pipelaying, heavy equipment operation, or a closely related field.

• Experience working with underground infrastructure projects, including water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, and utility installations.

• Equivalent combinations of education, industry experience, and professional certifications may also be considered

Technical Skills:

• Working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite is required.

• Demonstrated experience operating excavators and other heavy construction equipment safely and efficiently.

• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, blueprints, specifications, and site plans.

• Strong knowledge of excavation techniques, trenching practices, soil conditions, grading, and underground utility installation.

• Experience conducting equipment inspections, troubleshooting, and routine maintenance.

• Knowledge of municipal water, sanitary sewer, and storm sewer infrastructure installation practices.

• Familiarity with applicable industry standards, specifications, and safe work practices related to underground utility construction.

## Professional Skills:

• Highly flexible with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with students, colleagues, and industry partners.

• Ability to maintain a high degree of professionalism and safety awareness in both classroom and practical training environments.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills, analytical ability, and sound judgment.

• Self-motivated, service-oriented, and results-driven.

• Ability to work effectively under pressure in a fast-paced and changing environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team.

• A commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and staying current with industry practices.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.

Assets:

• Experience coaching, mentoring, supervising, or training employees, apprentices, students, or junior staff is considered an asset.

• Experience delivering classroom, practical, field-based, or workplace training in civil construction, underground utilities, heavy equipment operation, or related trades is considered an asset.

• Heavy Equipment Operator certification and industry certifications such as Trench Safety, Confined Space Entry, First Aid, Occupational Health and Safety, or Traffic Control are considered assets.

Candidates must clearly demonstrate how they meet these qualifications on their resumes. Other combinations of education and experience may be considered as equivalent.

All applicants must be eligible to work in Canada at the time of application. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Business Development Operations Manager and as a member of the faculty team, the instructor is responsible for planning and preparing instructional materials and resources; establishing and managing a positive learning environment; instructing and evaluating students; building and sustaining professional relationships with students, colleagues, community partners, and stakeholders; as well as other related duties.

## Specific instructional areas may include, but are not limited to:

• Underground utility installation - water mains, sanitary sewers, storm drainage systems, and utility pipelines

• Trench excavation, shoring, and trench safety practices

• Pipe installation, alignment, jointing, testing, and backfilling techniques

• Site grading and earthworks

• Heavy equipment operation and safety

• Excavator operation and preventive maintenance

• Reading and interpreting construction drawings, blueprints, and site plans

• Construction surveying and grade control

• Soil types, excavation methods, and compaction techniques

• Water and wastewater infrastructure construction

• Construction site safety and regulatory compliance

• Equipment inspection, maintenance, and documentation

• Project planning and site preparation

• Environmental and sustainable construction practices

• Environmental protection measures and regulatory requirements applicable to civil construction projects

• Installation of hydrants, valves, service connections, manholes, catch basins, and related underground infrastructure

• Watermain testing, flushing, disinfection, and commissioning procedures

• Safe use of hand tools, power tools, trenching equipment, compaction equipment, and dewatering systems

• Selection and application of pipe materials, fittings, accessories, and underground utility components

• Industry standards and best practices related to municipal water and sewer construction, including AWWA standards

The successful candidate will deliver an introductory-level training program focused on foundational pipelaying skills and industry best practices.

At NBCC, you will join a purpose-driven organization that is shaping the future of New Brunswick through education, workforce development, and community impact. In addition to meaningful work, we offer:

## PROJECT COORDINATOR (BAND LEVEL 6)

## This position is funded through an external grant

The University will consider applications from qualified permanent staff who may be interested in a secondment, subject to departmental approval

NL Inclusive STEM Project aims to provide experiential learning opportunities for LEARN students, prospective K-12 teachers (PTs), and Internationally Educated Teachers (IETs) to help participants realize their full personal and professional potential. The project is delivered in partnership with NL Schools and a range of community organizations, such as the YMCA and public libraries, with the goal of expanding after-school STEM programs in NL Schools and/or community centers. With a specific emphasis on newcomer and refugee students, the primary objectives of the project are to provide LEARN students with experiential STEM and language learning opportunities to develop their interest in STEM subjects, postsecondary education, and STEM careers; and to connect prospective K-12 teachers with relevant supports and services to help them become inclusive STEM teachers in NL.

## DUTIES

Reporting to the Project Lead, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project activities, including engaging prospective STEM teachers. The successful candidate will help build relationships with community partners and develop services and programs for LEARN students, PTs, and IETs. Primary duties include coordinating and overseeing the daily operations of the after-school programs across partner schools and community centers, addressing issues as they arise; assisting with and, in some cases, leading after­school programs at partner NL Schools and community centers; developing program schedules, activities, and curriculum materials tailored to the needs of newcomer students; organizing special events, workshops, and family engagement activities; assisting with the development and maintenance of project media-related activities; assisting with the recruitment, training, and supervising STEM program leaders, volunteers, and program staff; supporting student registration, attendance tracking, and family communication, including arranging interpretation and translation support as needed; and performing other project duties as required. The role involves occasional local travel within the St. John's area and may require work outside regular working hours.

## QUALIFICATIONS

Considerable experience (minimum 5 years) teaching at the K-12 level, including strong knowledge of STEM, experience in professional development of K-12 teachers, and knowledge of student supervision and data privacy best practices; completion of a bachelor's degree in education is required; or an equivalent combination of experience and training may be considered. The ideal candidate is organized, empathetic, and passionate about equity in education, with experience working with diverse cultural communities and an understanding of newcomer settlement challenges. A vulnerable sector check or background check, a valid driver's license, and reliable transportation are required. Additional language skills relevant to the newcomer community and prior experience supporting a school-based or education-related nonprofit program are considered assets. A master's degree is preferred.

The Psychiatric Registered Nurse I is a clinical position resulting from the recommendations of the Towards Recovery: The Mental Health and Additions Action Plan for Newfoundland and Labrador. The Action Plan identifies a number of initiatives as a part of a Stepped Care Approach to Mental Health and Addictions Services throughout the province.

One of these initiatives, Mobile Crisis Response (MCR) (Memphis Model) is a collaborative approach in which police and mental health professionals work together in responding to mental health crisis in the community. The psychiatric nurse will participate as a member of the crisis intervention team in provision of appropriate interventions in Mental Health crisis situations through the utilization of community base mental health approaches. The successful candidate will work closely with the RCMP in the ongoing operation of the team/service.

In keeping with the Stepped Care Approach to Mental Health and Addictions Services, this position will be responsible for providing professional standards of regional psychiatric nursing interventions for patients presenting to the ER with mental health concerns. Regional services to ER departments will be accommodated through telephone consultations and the use of Telehealth as required.

This position will work closely with the Regional Social Worker, who will work a corresponding shift in CNRHC.

The successful candidate will exercise a significant degree of independent clinical judgement, quick decision making and the ability to assess and intervene competently in various mental health concerns including crisis situations. Clinical services include, but are not limited to, mental health assessment, treatment and intervention in collaboration with the Emergency Room team, the Mental Health team and the Department of Psychiatry.

The dual role of this position includes membership on the MCR team and provision of Mental Health Services in the ER. This involves assessment, treatment, follow up and support of individuals with mental health and addictions needs throughout various mental health and addictions programs and services.

The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong, dedicated network of supports and staff to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW): Strengthening Children, Youth, Families & Community represents a coordinated and comprehensive range of programs and services delivered by community-based service providers that promote the safety, wellbeing of children, youth, and families. These includes parent/family, youth, family violence and sexual violence prevention and intervention programs within community contexts.

The CFW Specialist: Strengthening Children, Youth & Families & Communities is accountable for contributing to and providing recommendations for the development, planning, interpretation and application of effective CFW: Strengthening Children, Youth & Families & Communities programs, program standards, and policies and procedures to ensure the coordinated delivery of culturally attentive and responsive programs and services.

This includes providing program and practice leadership and support to regional community-based programs to enhance and improve outcomes for vulnerable and at-risk children, youth and their families as well as consultation and advice to the internal Child & Family Wellbeing service delivery system, particularly as it pertains to Strengthening Children, Youth, Families, and Community programs.

Reporting to the Director, Child and Family Wellbeing: Strengthening Children, Youth, Families and Community, this position provides leadership, functional direction, consultation, and support in promoting and implementing the vision, principles, and practice standards of the Child and Family Wellbeing Practice Framework.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Specialist, you contribute to the consistent, effective, and efficient delivery of Child & Family Wellbeing: Strengthening Children, Youth, Families & Community programs. Key responsibilities include:

• interpreting and clarifying legislation, program standards, policies, procedures and the Child & Family Wellbeing Practice Framework to CFW Managers, Supervisors, Social Workers, other CFW team members, community partners and service providers to ensure the delivery of human centered programs and services in alignment with the Children and Family Services Act, Adoption Records Act and the Act Respecting First Nations, Inuit, and Metis Children, Youth, and Families.

• providing expert advice, program performance and outcome results, and other statistical data related to Child & Family Wellbeing: Strengthening Children, Youth, Family & Community programs in your region to senior management.

• fostering community collaboration/program support and development, by advising and consulting with community service providers in the region on collaborative delivery of services which promote the safety and well-being of children, youth and families.

• providing support and consultation to program professionals, supervisors, and managers to support access to Child & Family Wellbeing: Strengthening Children, Youth, Families & Community programs, supports, and services in a coordinated and timely manner.

• facilitating effective communication within the service delivery continuum, and between service delivery and program and service delivery and community-based service providers.

• acting as liaison with program divisions in head office on all matters related to policy, program development, standards, delivery models, and system enhancements.

description:
R.K. MacDonald Nursing Home

OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST
Permanent Full-time position

The Home is seeking a dynamic, compassionate person; committed to excellence and quality practice environments; with demonstrated team leading skills; and enthusiastic about a profession in Long Term Care to fill the role of Occupational Therapist. Reporting to the Director of Clinical Services, the Occupational Therapist is responsible for encouraging growth through the provision of programs and services to residents according to established standards and administrative policies. This will involve promotion of health and optimal occupational performance; prevention of disability; assessing resident's needs, and planning, implementing, evaluating and documenting a plan of care. Occupational Therapists work as part of a multi-disciplinary team.

## Key Responsibilities:

Professional Accountability -Carries out assessment, plan implementation, plan evaluation and education in accordance with RK policies and procedures, the Occupational Therapy Code of Ethics, the National Occupational Therapy Act of Nova Scotia;

Communication and Collaboration: Establishes and maintains effective communication with residents, relevant others and professional colleagues;

Assessment / Treatment / Education- Participates in screening and prioritizing referrals to Occupational Therapy to determine the individual's need for Occupational Therapy Services as required. Identifies the resident, based on each unique situation, and identifies the resident's support system (e.g., family, significant others, caregivers, community, etc;

Planning: Engages the resident in the goal setting process to identify the resident's priorities;

Implementation - Engages the resident in treatment (either individual or group) by providing interventions with an aim to maximize occupational functioning and minimize barriers that impede occupational engagement. Implementation of the plan involves promotion of safety, choice, and risk engagement.;

Evaluation -Evaluates, communicates, and documents expected and unexpected responses to care, to the resident, his/her support system, and the health care team. Evaluates and monitors broad outcomes including healthy living, and reducing hospitalization.;

Safe Work Practices - The R.K MacDonald Occupational Health and Safety Home Policy establishes employee expectations for working safely. To achieve these expectations employees at all levels of the organization must adhere to Core Values of Safety and Safety Responsibilities.

## Professional Qualification / Education / Experience/Competencies

• Minimum of 3 years recent experience in a Long-Term Care setting and /or Community with emphasis on adaptive equipment (Red Cross Specialized Equipment Program) and responsive behaviours is an asset.

• Bachelor of Science Degree in Occupational Therapy or Masters of Science in Occupational Therapy Entry Level, from an accredited University.

• Registered member of the College of Occupational Therapists of Nova Scotia.

• Safety Certification such as BCLS, CPR, NCPI,

• Current membership with the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists with active participation in professional activities preferred

• Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

• Ability to organize, develop and initiate ideas and programs.

• Demonstrate good communication skills, verbally and in writing.

## Our Story - Freshest Because It's Raised Right Here:

Country Ribbon Inc. is proud to provide customers with nutritious and delicious fresh and frozen chicken products produced from its farm, feed mill, and processing facilities, located in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador.

With a long history in the province, Country Ribbon Inc. is on an ambitious path. Country Ribbon Inc. employs over 300 people and markets its products under Country Ribbon, Pinehill and other brand names. Unique in Newfoundland and Labrador, the company is the province's only fully integrated chicken producer and processor, being involved in every stage of the process, from farm to plate. Country Ribbon always goes the distance to ensure quality and safety in what we do. A proud contributor to the poultry industry in Newfoundland and Labrador and beyond, Country Ribbon Inc. is an anchor in the local agriculture economy and is integrated with the region's retail, restaurant, and poultry supply chain. To find out more, click on https://www.countryribbon.com/.

## The Opportunity?

We believe that our success depends upon having the right people in the right jobs with the ability to work well together. We are currently accepting applications for a Feed Mill Supervisor at our Topsail Road location. Under the direction of our Feed Mill Manager, this position is tasked with ensuring the safe, effective and efficient operations at our Feed Mill which includes our grain storage and handling facilities at Cochrane Pond and Long Pond.

• Identify continuous improvement initiatives to improve productivity, reduce waste, and optimize feed mill performance.

• Ensure compliance with Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), HACCP policies, and applicable regulatory standards.

• Assist in managing inventory levels and coordinate materials and supplies to ensure uninterrupted production and efficient feed mill operations.

• Manage employee attendance, timekeeping, and leave records, ensuring accurate documentation and efficient payroll support.

• Strong leadership skills and a motivated approach to their work.

• Post-secondary education in Mechanical/Industrial Engineering Technology, food production, or another relevant field.

• 3+ years of supervisory experience.

• Excellent interpersonal skills and a proven ability to work successfully as a team member.

title: Employee Services Coordinator
description:

Do you take pride in accuracy, attention to detail, and helping others navigate important moments throughout their employment journey? We are looking for an Employee Services Coordinator to join our team and help support payroll and benefits services for employees across the College.

Position Type: Term | Duration: 1 year

Location: Any NBCC campus location

Salary Range: $2,098.00 to $2,932.00 bi-weekly (Management/Non-Union Pay Band 3)

Qualifications

## Education & Experience:

• Diploma or degree in a related field with a minimum of 2-3 years of experience in a similar position.

• Payroll Compliance Practitioner (PCP) certification is considered an asset.

• Experience processing payroll for both hourly and salaried employees.

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including functions such as XLOOKUP and Pivot Tables, along with experience using other Microsoft Office applications.

• Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with employees, managers, and stakeholders at all levels.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• High ethical standards and a deep respect for confidentiality and the protection of personal information.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to investigate and resolve complex payroll issues.

• Sound judgment, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.

• Self-motivated with the ability to work independently while contributing positively within a team environment.

• Ability to manage competing priorities and adapt to changing demands.

• A continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify opportunities and make practical recommendations.

Candidates must clearly demonstrate how they meet these qualifications on their resumes. Other combinations of education and experience may be considered as equivalent.

All applicants must be eligible to work in Canada at the time of application. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

Responsibilities
At NBCC, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As Employee Services Coordinator, you will play an important role in supporting the employee experience by ensuring payroll and benefits services are delivered accurately, efficiently, and with a high degree of care and confidentiality. Working closely with employees, managers, Finance, and People & Culture teams, you will help ensure our people receive the support they need throughout their employment journey while contributing to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen our services and processes.

• Serve as the primary point of contact and subject matter expert for payroll and benefits-related inquiries.

• Coordinate and oversee full-cycle payroll processing for multiple employee groups, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable legislation.

• Process employee lifecycle transactions including hires, compensation changes, transfers, leaves of absence, and departures.

• Administer and reconcile employee benefits, pension-related transactions, and payroll deductions.

• Ensure compliance with organizational policies, collective agreements, and federal and provincial payroll legislation.

• Maintain accurate and confidential employee records in accordance with privacy and records management requirements.

• Prepare payroll reconciliations and year-end activities.

• Support internal and external audits by preparing documentation and ensuring payroll records are accurate and complete.

• Collaborate with Finance and internal and external stakeholders on payroll and benefits-related matters.

• Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, reduce risk, and enhance service delivery.

• Participate in special projects, system enhancements, ERP initiatives, and continuous improvement activities.

At NBCC, you will join a purpose-driven organization that is shaping the future of New Brunswick through education, workforce development, and community impact. In addition to meaningful work, we offer:

• An inclusive culture where people feel valued, supported, and connected.

• Opportunities to grow as a leader through continuous learning and development.

• Membership in the New Brunswick Public Service Pension Plan.

• Access to an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).

Bedford, Nova Scotia

Micco Companies is a proudly family-owned group of businesses based in Bedford, Nova Scotia. We operate across a vibrant mix of industries from retail, hospitality and fitness to cannabis production, beverage alcohol, logistics, and more. With over 350 employees, we're proud to be deeply rooted in our local communities and committed to service excellence.

## The Role

Reporting to the Controller, the Senior Accountant will serve as a key liaison between Accounting and Operations, ensuring alignment between financial reporting and business performance. The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in public accounting, financial controls, and operational finance, with additional experience in industries such as manufacturing, warehousing, or real estate considered highly valuable.

This is a hands-on role designed for an experienced accounting professional who thrives in a fast-paced, agile environment. The Senior Accountant will support financial accuracy, operational efficiency, and strong financial controls across assigned business segments.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

• Manage day-to-day accounting activities for assigned business segments, including general accounting functions.

• Experience integrating Accounting with operational functions is highly valued.

• Minimum 3+ years of progressive Finance/Accounting experience, including responsibility for full-cycle accounting, financial reporting, and month-end close.

English fluency required.

title: Manager, Pension Administration
description:
Some would say we're in the pension business. We like to say we're in the people business. One that focuses on creating an inclusive and diverse culture for everyone who comes through our doors. One that puts our 68,000 members at the heart of everything we do because they deserve nothing less than a secure, stable future to build upon. One that can include YOU.

## Who we are:

Provident10 is the largest pension plan in Newfoundland and Labrador and one of the largest pension plans in Atlantic Canada - representing 1 in 8 Newfoundlanders and Labradorians. Our team proudly oversees the pension administration and investment management of the over $13 billion Public Service Pension Plan Fund.

## Future Focused. People Centric. The foundation for our vision.

For us that means creating a seamless experience for members and a positive culture for our employees; ensuring the organization remains efficient and agile, as we continue to make smart investments for growth - all while embracing technology and ensuring a consistent experience for our members.

## What it's like to work at Provident10

We're proud to have been named one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for 2026, for the fifth year in a row! We earned the designation by focusing on elevating the employee experience and making Provident10 a great place to work.

## We're committed to offering a total rewards program to employees, including:

• Membership in a defined benefit pension plan with employer matched contributions. Vested members of the Public Service Pension Plan can rest assured knowing that they will receive a predictable retirement income for life, without having to worry if their benefits will run out or be terminated.

• Comprehensive health and dental plan, including new wellness initiatives like in-house vaccination clinics and mental health support programs.

• Learning and development program focused on supporting employees in reaching their career goals.

• Maternity leave top-up program for new and expecting parents.

• Performance management program with the potential for annual salary increases and a short-term incentive.

• Progressive annual leave program with a minimum of 15 paid days.

## The Opportunity

Our Pension Administration department is looking for a someone who has a keen ability to lead and build teams, and who has a strong background in client care excellence for the role of Manager, Pension Administration. Reporting to the VP, Pensions, the successful candidate will use their leadership skills to provide coaching and guidance to team members and provide oversight for all pension related activities.

## Your key activities will include:

• Provide coaching and guidance to members of the Pension Administration team.

• Evaluate the performance of team members and completes the annual review for each individual.

• Identify knowledge gaps within the team and recommend a plan to address those gaps.

• Recommends efficiencies, enhancements, and resource requirements to the VP, Pensions.

• Ensure compliance with applicable Privacy Principles and legislation.

• Ensure that all process documents are up to date and accurate, ensuring changes are made as needed.

• Oversee the accuracy of benefit payments and pension records.

• Defines customer needs & expectations & develop action plan to address.

• Liaise with other pension plan sponsors and administrators, external lawyers, consultants, actuaries, and auditors.

• Define appropriate KPI's and utilize visual management systems to measure progress against Corporate and personal objectives.

• Develops, implements and measures workflow management systems, member self-service and pension calculation tools, procedures, and internal standards and controls.

## What you'll bring to the role

• The completion of a college or university related program, supplemented by 3 years of leadership experience.

• Prior experience working with pension administration, related provincial legislation, or other experience in financial services would be considered an asset.

• An eagerness to learn new technology.

• You are a self-starter, with strong interpersonal and communication skills, and a high degree of accountability.

## Salary Range: $99,700 - $140,500

Application Deadline: Applications will be accepted until November 10th, 2026. We will begin reviewing applications as they are received, and interviews will be scheduled with eligible candidates throughout the posting period. Early submission is encouraged.

Provident10 is an Equal Opportunity Employer that welcomes and celebrates the differences that every individual brings. While only those individuals selected for an interview will be contacted, we extend our appreciation to all applicants for your interest. If you require an accommodation during the recruitment process, please reach out to our People & Culture team at humanresources@provident10.com and we will work with you to provide the support you need.

We actively promote diversity in our workplace, provide equitable opportunities for growth, and support initiatives that advance inclusion and belonging. Our dedication to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging ensures that we not only thrive as a company but also contribute positively to our community, our members, and our industry.

title: Technical Service Representative - Moncton (12-Month Term)

Are you a tech-savvy problem solver with a passion for customer service? Atlantic Lottery is seeking a Technical Service Representative to support a service territory spanning across Moncton and surrounding areas. This field-based role requires regular travel throughout the assigned territory. In this hands-on role, you'll be responsible for servicing and maintaining lottery terminals and related equipment across Video Lottery and Retail Lottery sites, ensuring maximum uptime and compliance with service standards.

You'll work independently, traveling extensively within your territory, and play a key role in preventative maintenance and servicing/repairing equipment at retailer locations while maintaining positive relations. You will ensure maximum up time of all assets delivering on key performance metrics while meeting our Service Level Agreements (SLA's).

## Why Join Our Team?

• Work with innovative gaming technology in a hands-on role that combines technical problem-solving and customer service.

• Enjoy the freedom and variety of field-based position where you'll manage your day and make a visible impact.

Position Type: Full-Time, 12-Month Term

Application Deadline: November 17, 2026

Qualifications
Education and Experience:

• Educational Requirements: An Electronics diploma or a certified Engineering Technology diploma from a recognized post-secondary institution.

• Experience: 1 to 3 years of experience in Technical and Customer Service roles.

• Physical Requirements: Ability to lift and move weights up to 50 pounds.

• Driving Requirements (Corporate Vehicle Provided):
• A clean and valid driver's abstract.

• A valid driver's license as required by law.

• Work Schedule: Willingness to work shifts, including evenings and weekends, as needed.

• Age Requirement: Must be 19 years of age or older.

• Residency Requirement: Must reside within the assigned service territory or within a reasonable commuting distance that enables timely response to service calls throughout the Moncton region.

Professional Skills:

• Strong analytical skills, including the ability to analyze and interpret complex technical issues, identifying trends, root causes, and potential solutions.

• Ability to resolve technical issues efficiently by applying critical thinking and using available resources.

• Excellent listening, communication, and collaboration skills.

• Strong motivation and eagerness to learn new technologies, applications, and tools relevant to the role.

• A desire to build exceptional client experiences and is passionate and curious to help clients meet their needs and solve their concerns.

• Proficiency in MS Office.

• Ability to multi-task, problem-solve, prioritize and competently handle a variety of activities with a high degree of accuracy in a fast paced, customer-driven environment.

Assets:

• Gaming experience

• Troubleshooting experience

• A+ and Network+

• Service Now

• Cisco Meraki

Special Condition of Employment for Field Employees:

• Must be able to successfully complete First Aid/CPR training within provincial requirements.

• Steel toe boots/shoes are a requirement.

• Must complete Defensive Driving course.

## Work Location & Flexibility

• Field-based remote position supporting a service territory across Moncton, NB and surrounding areas. Extensive daily travel throughout the territory is required.

## Compensation

• Salary Band: $62,600 - $93,600

• Candidates can expect to start around $66,510, with placement dependent on experience, skills, market conditions, and internal equity.

## AL Benefits

• Extended health coverage (medical, dental, vision)

• Basic life insurance and disability coverage

• Defined Benefit Pension Plan

• Three weeks' vacation annually (pro‑rated), 13 paid statutory holidays, and a vacation purchase program

• Wellness support, including wellness programs, 3 personal care days, and a 24/7 Employee & Family Assistance Program

• Two paid volunteer days per year

• Career advancement opportunities

## Recruitment Process

We've made meaningful enhancements to our hiring practices in recent years. Our typical recruitment process includes:

• Two in‑person interviews

• An assignment and/or scenario‑based questions

• Behavioral or cognitive assessments

• Verification of relevant certifications (as applicable)

All interviews are conducted in English, our primary working language, unless otherwise specified.

Only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Successful candidates will undergo reference checks and a mandatory criminal background check. Additional financial, educational, or credential verifications may be required depending on the role.

## Role Commitment

To support employee development, business continuity, and knowledge transfer, individuals who accept this position are expected to remain in the role for a minimum of 18 months before being eligible to apply for or transfer to another position within Atlantic Lottery.

This expectation applies to both external hires and employees moving into the role from another position.

## Internal Candidates

Internal applicants must be in good standing, including meeting expectations on their most recent performance review, and must not be on probation. Consideration may also include factors such as performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, attendance, and completion of mandatory training.

A Predictive Index (PI) assessment will be completed or shared with the hiring leader as part of the evaluation process.

## Internal Recruitment Considerations

For internal recruitment processes, preference may be given to employees currently occupying regular or term positions with AL. Selection decisions will consider business needs, approved staffing requirements, organizational headcount parameters, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.

## Eligibility to Work in Canada

Candidates must have all required work permits, visas, and authorizations and be eligible to work in Canada at the time an offer is made. It is the candidate's responsibility to secure these requirements.

Atlantic Lottery welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Atlantic Lottery is not participating in the Temporary Foreign Worker (Labour Market Impact Assessment) Program, Provincial Nominee Programs, or the Atlantic Immigration Program at this time. Support for any other immigration programs for new hires is subject to internal policies, operational needs, and program restrictions and is not guaranteed.

Responsibilities
What You'll Do:

• Provide exceptional technical support by diagnosing and resolving issues with gaming technology to keep equipment operating reliably.

• Maintain and install gaming equipment at retail and destination locations, ensuring a seamless experience for customers and players.

• Build strong customer relationships by delivering professional, responsive service and clear communication in the field.

• Support operational success by helping meet service commitments and minimizing equipment downtime across your service territory.

• Collaborate with internal teams to troubleshoot complex issues, share insights, and support new initiatives and product launches.

• Promote safe and compliant operations by following established standards, policies, and regulatory requirements.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. We are dedicated to building a workforce that reflects the diversity of our customers and communities in which we live and serve. If you require an accommodation for the recruitment/interview process (including alternate formats of materials, or accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations), please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

## Salary (pay basis): $35.52-$58.34 hourly

The opportunity
With five major maintenance bases across the country—including our Heavy Maintenance facility in Halifax and Line Maintenance bases in Toronto, Montreal, Calgary, and Vancouver—Jazz offers Aircraft Maintenance Engineers (AMEs) the opportunity to work with a dedicated team that prioritizes safety, professionalism, and technical excellence. Our AMEs play a critical role in keeping our fleet operating safely and reliably, and we take pride in fostering an environment where your expertise is valued and your work truly matters.

If you’re a Licensed AME who takes pride in safety, technical accuracy, and working as part of a dependable, professional team, you’ll find a strong fit with Jazz’s heavy maintenance division - Jazz Technical Services (JTS). You must bring a commitment to precision; a focus on maintaining aircraft to the highest regulatory and Company standards; and dedication to contributing to a safe, efficient, and collaborative maintenance environment. Are you looking for a workplace where your expertise is respected, your development is supported, and your career can continue to progress? If this aligns with your goals, we welcome you to join our award winning team in Halifax.

## Key responsibilities

• Under the direction of the Crew Chief or ACA perform inspection(s) and assist with dismantling, assembly, repair and/or overhaul of aircraft systems and components on Company aircraft.

• Troubleshoot aircraft defects, identify root causes and determine appropriate corrective actions in accordance with approved maintenance data and procedures.

• Perform assigned maintenance tasks to maintain aircraft airworthiness in compliance with approved maintenance data, Company policies, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Identify, document, and report aircraft defects or other issues affecting safety, serviceability, or operational status.

• Support and mentor Apprentices as required.

• Perform duties in accordance with established policies and procedures while giving primary consideration to personal safety, and the safety of co-workers and customers.

• Perform other related duties, as assigned.

## Required qualifications

• Valid Transport Canada AME License Category S.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a Restricted Area Identification Card (RAIC).

• Valid Canadian-issued driver’s license with no restrictions or conditions.

• Ability to obtain and maintain an Airport Vehicle Operator’s Permit (AVOP).

• Willing and able to work varying shifts.

• English language fluency or working knowledge. (Must be able to communicate effectively with English-speaking teams at their base and across the country).

## Preferred qualifications

• Current Transport Canada endorsement on a Jazz aircraft type.

## Benefits of joining our award-winning team

• Enjoy exclusive employee travel programs across the Air Canada network, giving you and your family access to incredible destinations.

• Secure your long-term financial well-being with our competitive, employer-supported retirement savings programs (defined contribution pension plan or voluntary group RRSP) for permanent employees.

• Benefit from a comprehensive health and wellness package, including health, dental, life, and accident insurance to keep you and your loved ones protected.

## About Jazz Aviation LP

Jazz Aviation LP (Jazz) is the primary operator of Air Canada Express services, connecting people and communities to approximately 70 destinations across North America.

With over 4,200 dedicated professionals, Jazz fosters a workplace united by purpose and supported by programs and policies that promote safety, diversity, and wellness. Jazz is proud to be recognized for its strong commitment to people and culture. Visit our Company Awards and Recognition page to learn more about the honours we've earned.

Join our award-winning team and be part of shaping the future of regional aviation!

To support your success, we can provide accommodations for people with disabilities, such as adjustments or assistive measures to remove barriers during the recruitment process. If you require any accessibility support, please contact us at taleosupport@flyjazz.ca.

Jazz values diversity and we empower our employees to foster an internal culture of inclusion. Jazz is committed to providing equitable opportunities for employment and career advancement and we will continuously work to create inclusive and accessible work environments to maximize individual potential as well as psychological health and safety. Meeting the needs of passengers is critical to our success and we recognize the importance of a workforce that is reflective of the communities we serve.

description:
## WHO WE ARE:

## OVERVIEW OF THE ROLE:

We are seeking an experienced Quality Assurance (QA) Analyst for a client opportunity supporting the testing and quality assurance of web-based applications and digital services. The successful candidate will bring strong hands-on experience in both manual and automated testing, working collaboratively with development teams to ensure the delivery of high-quality, reliable solutions.

This role involves close collaboration with the existing QA Test Lead and Agile delivery team, contributing to test planning, execution, automation, defect management, and continuous improvement of QA practices.

## WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING IN THE ROLE

• Support hands-on testing and quality assurance activities across web-based applications and services.

• Develop, maintain, and execute comprehensive test plans, scenarios, scripts, and test cases.

• Perform functional, regression, integration, smoke, and negative testing to validate application functionality and reliability.

• Develop, maintain, and execute automated tests using appropriate testing frameworks and tools.

• Support the integration of automated testing into existing CI/CD pipelines to improve testing efficiency and consistency.

• Identify, document, track, and validate defects through to resolution.

• Collaborate with developers, Business Analysts, and product management teams to review requirements, clarify acceptance criteria, and ensure adequate test coverage.

• Support user acceptance testing (UAT), including test preparation, execution, defect tracking, and issue resolution.

• Contribute to testing documentation, reporting, and the continuous improvement of QA processes and practices.

• Work closely with the existing QA Test Lead and Agile delivery team to support successful project delivery.

## WHAT SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS YOU'LL NEED:

• 5+ years of experience in software quality assurance, preferably testing complex web-based applications within Agile environments.

• Strong hands-on experience with both manual and automated software testing methodologies.

• Experience developing, maintaining, and executing automated test scripts using Python-based frameworks or testing tools such as Pytest, unittest, Selenium, or Cypress.

• Proven experience in test planning, defect management, regression testing, and test execution.

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing integration, preferably using GitLab.

• Strong experience working within Agile/Scrum delivery teams and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.

• Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and manage testing activities across concurrent development initiatives.

• Experience supporting UAT activities and ensuring test coverage aligns with business and technical requirements.

## ASSETS/NICE-TO-HAVES:

• Experience with public-sector digital services and online forms.

• Familiarity with Django-based applications.

• Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.

• Knowledge of Docker and containerization technologies.

• Experience with performance or security testing.

## WHY MARINER?

We believe in making a positive impact in the communities where we live and work! Not only are we passionate about nurturing a thriving technology sector here in Atlantic Canada, but we are also committed to solving technology challenges that will make an impact worldwide. Technology is everlasting, and we take pride in connecting world class talent to world class projects and business solutions.

If you are an IT Professional, Software Professional, or Management Consultant, that is passionate about career development, data, and problem solving, we want to hear from you! If this sounds like someone you know, share this with them so they do not miss the opportunity to experience Mariner!

To achieve this, we know we need to be all in on training and development of our team so we can continue to move the needle in the technology sector together. Of course, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to our team, but our competitive edge is the development and training that our team experiences every day.

Be part of our vibrant community that values diversity and embraces inclusion at every level. We are committed to fostering a culture where individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives. Our collaborative environment celebrates the richness of ideas and experiences, and we believe that by embracing diversity, we can achieve greater innovation and excellence together. Come and help us create a workplace that reflects the beautiful tapestry of our global community.

## Join our growing team!

Applications are invited from highly motivated and experienced health care practitioners who are interested in the exciting challenge of working as a Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) in the Paramedicine and Medical Transport Division of NL Health Services. This position will involve working on the ground and air Provincial Programs. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) is a highly responsible, clinical position, accountable for the provision of quality, safe, skilled care of emergent and routine nature to patients within the province requiring inter-facility transport or at the scene of traumatic or acute medical incidents.

In a team environment, the Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will be responsible for providing direct patient care including assessment and intervention of all medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients ranging in age from newborn to the elderly. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will use critical thinking and professional judgment within their scope of practice and within a medical control system with written protocols and through medical consultation with a physician when necessary. This position is also responsible for promotion and maintenance of quality and safety standards and ensures maintenance of clinical proficiencies and competencies. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will report directly to the Integrated Air Operations Manager of Paramedicine and Medical Transport. The successful candidate will report to Goose Bay/Sheshatshiu.

## Duties include but are not limited to:

• Performs comprehensive assessments, physical examinations, advanced treatments, triage, and interventions for all pre-hospital scene or inter-facility requests, encompassing medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients

• Applies treatment therapies and interventions for medical disorders and traumatic injuries, in accordance with protocols

• Adheres to all policies, procedures, guidelines, and applicable operational standards in the performance of assigned duties.

• Functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units

• Completes patient treatment charting, records all pertinent patient information to include vitals, neurological signs, assessment findings and treatment provided.

• Ensures confidentiality of patient information

• Provides leadership and scene management during mass casualty incidents in the absence of an incident command supervisor

• Preceptors and mentors Primary Care Paramedic students during field placements to ensure students meet required competencies

• Participates in Continuing Medical Education (CME)

• Maintains, cleans, and conducts duty checks of ambulances, equipment, and supplies and restocks when necessary

• Recognizes cultural diversity

• Provides orientation to new employees, and on the job training to staff and students

• Travel is required

• Perform interfacility transports using program aircraft.

• Maintain flight status

• Constantly lifts, pushes, and pulls patients on stretchers (which requires up to 35lbs of push/pull force or greater as the terrain and weather conditions can contribute to increased push/pull forces) often in challenging environments, not always conductive to proper ergonomics to and from planes and ambulances;

• Loading and carrying equipment/patients weighing between 10 – 50 lbs or more than 50 lbs. The work must be completed urgently which can contribute to increased forces required in pushing/pulling and lifting.

• Constantly/regularly sits, stands, walks, and works in awkward or cramped positions, as well as bends, kneels, and stretches to provide patient care.

• Visual concentration is required to prepare medications, monitor equipment, and patient condition during in-flight transport; time pressures when transporting critically ill or injured patients to care centers within time frames for life-saving interventions.

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an PCP

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador?

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation

• Current BLS certification

• Current certification in ACLS, PALS, ITLS, NRP, ICS 100, or willingness to complete

• Successful completion of aircraft safety training and basic flight physiology training

• Effective oral and written communication skills

• Critical and sound decision making skills

• Confidence to manage a variety of situations

• Ability to perform various medical procedures and operate a variety of medical equipment

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is?required

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct including vulnerable sector check from the RCMP or local police authority

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.
