Applications are invited from highly motivated and experienced health care practitioners who are interested in the exciting challenge of working as an Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) in the Paramedicine and Medical Transport Division of NL Health Services. This position will involve working on the ground and air Provincial Programs. The Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) is a highly responsible, advanced clinical position, accountable for the provision of quality, safe, skilled care of emergent and routine nature to patients within the province requiring inter-facility transport or at the scene of traumatic or acute medical incidents.

In a team environment, the Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) will be responsible for providing direct patient care including advanced assessment and intervention of all medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients ranging in age from newborn to the elderly. The Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) will use critical thinking and professional judgment within their scope of practice and within a medical control system with written protocols and through medical consultation with a physician when necessary. This position is also responsible for promotion and maintenance of quality and safety standards and ensures maintenance of clinical proficiencies and competencies. The Advanced Care Paramedic (ACP) will report directly to the Integrated Air Operations Manager of Paramedicine and Medical Transport. The successful candidate will report to Goose Bay/Sheshatshiu.

## Duties include but are not limited to:

• Performs comprehensive assessments, physical examinations, advanced treatments, triage, and interventions for all pre-hospital scene or inter-facility requests, encompassing medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients

• Applies advanced treatment therapies and interventions for medical disorders and traumatic injuries, in accordance with protocols

• Adheres to all policies, procedures, guidelines, and applicable operational standards in the performance of assigned duties.

• Functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units

• Completes patient treatment charting, records all pertinent patient information to include vitals, neurological signs, assessment findings and treatment provided.

• Ensures confidentiality of patient information

• Provides leadership and scene management during mass casualty incidents in the absence of an incident command supervisor

• Preceptors and mentors Advanced and Primary Care Paramedic students during field placements to ensure students meet required competencies

• Participates in Continuing Medical Education (CME)

• Maintains, cleans, and conducts duty checks of ambulances, equipment, and supplies and restocks when necessary

• Recognizes cultural diversity

• Provides orientation to new employees, and on the job training to staff and students

• Travel is required

• Perform interfacility transports using program aircraft.

• Maintain flight status

• Constantly lifts, pushes, and pulls patients on stretchers (which requires up to 35lbs of push/pull force or greater as the terrain and weather conditions can contribute to increased push/pull forces) often in challenging environments, not always conductive to proper ergonomics to and from planes and ambulances;

• Loading and carrying equipment/patients weighing between 10 – 50 lbs or more than 50 lbs. The work must be completed urgently which can contribute to increased forces required in pushing/pulling and lifting.

• Constantly/regularly sits, stands, walks, and works in awkward or cramped positions, as well as bends, kneels, and stretches to provide patient care.

• Visual concentration is required to prepare medications, monitor equipment, and patient condition during in-flight transport; time pressures when transporting critically ill or injured patients to care centers within time frames for life-saving interventions.

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic program

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation

• Current BLS and ACLS certification

• Current certification in PALS, ITLS, NRP, ICS 100, or willingness to complete

• Successful completion of aircraft safety training and basic flight physiology training

• Effective oral and written communication skills

• Critical and sound decision making skills

• Confidence to manage a variety of situations

• Ability to perform various medical procedures and operate a variety of medical equipment

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is?required

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct including vulnerable sector check from the RCMP or local police authority

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Competition # E22698-2026

At NB Power we are a team committed to offering the best customer experience, ensuring energy security, and accelerating a sustainable clean energy transition. Why? Because we're New Brunswickers too, we care about our customers and future generations, and today we are actively looking for a new member to join us.

The Mactaquac Generating Station began generating electricity in 1968. Since the 1980s, concrete portions of the hydro station have been affected by a chemical reaction called alkali-aggregate reaction. The reaction causes the concrete to swell and crack and has required substantial annual maintenance and repairs. NB Power is proposing a project to ensure the station can operate to its intended 100-year lifespan with a modified approach to maintenance and adjusting and replacing equipment and concrete overtime.

As part of the Mactaquac Life Achievement Project, the Commercial Manager is responsible for leading and managing the end-to-end commercial functions of the project, ensuring the effective planning, execution, and oversight of commercial strategy, procurement, contracting, inventory management, and contract administration. The role ensures all commercial activities are delivered in a transparent, compliant, and cost-effective manner while supporting the successful delivery of project objectives.

## Key functions include:

• Commercial Governance
• Lead the commercial governance framework and continuously improve commercial processes, standards, and controls

• Provide commercial guidance to leadership and project stakeholders on contractual, financial, and commercial matters

• Procurement and Contract Management
• Lead procurement and oversee contract development, administration, and close-out in compliance with organizational standards

• Manage commercial risks, claims, variations, and disputes to support successful project delivery

• Contractor and Supplier Management
• Oversee contractor-led procurement and manage commercial relationships with contractors, consultants, and suppliers to ensure compliance and resolve commercial issues

• Inventory & Materials Management
• Oversee project inventory and warehouse operations, ensuring accurate material tracking and compliance with financial and contractual requirements

• Performance Reporting
• Develop KPIs, monitor commercial performance, and recommend corrective actions where required

## Our ideal teammate will have:

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Commerce, Supply Chain Management, Construction Management, or related discipline

• Seven years of relevant experience in procurement and contract management within large, complex construction or infrastructure projects, including a minimum of three years in a leadership role.

• Strong knowledge of commercial risk, claims management, financial analysis, and reporting

• Proven leadership, negotiation, communication, stakeholder management, analytical, and problem-solving skills

• Experience with project management and cost management systems is considered an asset

• Supply Chain certification will be considered as an asset

An equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered. Subject to competition response, the minimum qualifications may be modified.

An Eligibility List generated from this competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level within a period of up to 12 months.

title: General Manager
description:
## General Manager

## Dairy Farmers of Nova Scotia

## Truro, Nova Scotia | Salary range $130,000-$150,000 annually

## Overview

Dairy Farmers of Nova Scotia (DFNS) seeks a seasoned, approachable leader to help shape the future of dairy through close partnerships with producers, an elected Board and industry partners.

Based in Truro, this producer-funded organization represents 189 dairy producers and administers milk purchasing, sales and transportation, producer and transporter licensing, and production quotas, with delegated regulatory responsibilities. Its members produce over 220 million litres annually, with a farm gate value of $256 million.

## About the Role

Reporting to the Board, you will lead strategy and day-to-day operations, financial management, regulatory oversight and industry relations. You will develop an engaged team of six full-time employees, supported by contract resources, while strengthening culture and member relationships.

Key priorities include advancing Atlantic dairy processing capacity, supporting high standards of milk quality and animal care, and engaging the next generation of dairy consumers. Success requires listening, building trust and exercising sound judgment while upholding requirements and processes.

## Key Responsibilities

• Support the Board and committees with clear analysis, practical recommendations and timely reporting; translate strategy into operational plans and results.

• Lead budgeting, financial reporting and controls, monitor revenues and expenses, and ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources.

• Coach and develop staff, clarify roles and expectations, and oversee performance, compensation and human resource practices that support a positive culture.

• Oversee regulatory administration and enforcement; guide amendments through the Board, advisory committees and Natural Products Marketing Council, and ensure compliance with applicable legislation.

• Engage producers through responsive communication and consultation, navigate differing perspectives, and apply regulatory requirements and established processes consistently.

• Build relationships with government, processors, regulators and provincial and national dairy organizations; collaborate across the Maritimes on consistent procedures and represent DFNS at committees and industry forums.

• Advance processing capacity, quality improvements and animal care with partners, and oversee education, promotion and public relations to strengthen consumer engagement and market development.

## What You Bring

• Five years of progressive leadership experience in an environment with diverse stakeholders, including accountability for people, finances and organizational performance.

• Post-secondary education in Business Administration, Economics or a related field of study.

• Experience working with an elected Board and within a regulated environment, with sound governance judgment and the ability to turn strategic priorities into action.

• Strong budgeting, financial management and business planning skills, supported by experience developing and implementing strategic and operational plans.

• An approachable, trustworthy leadership style grounded in integrity, with a strong ability to communicate comfortably with various audiences.

• Demonstrated ability to motivate and develop teams, strengthen culture and guide change through clear expectations, collaboration and effective communication.

• Knowledge of the dairy industry, commodity boards or natural products is an asset, together with a strong commitment to supporting Nova Scotia's dairy sector.

## Why Dairy Farmers of Nova Scotia

This role offers the opportunity to influence the direction of a provincial industry while staying connected to the people who sustain it. You will work closely with the Board, develop a capable team and build regional and national relationships that help move industry priorities forward. For a leader who enjoys both setting direction and working through practical challenges, DFNS offers meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to make a lasting contribution.

To learn more about Dairy Farmers of Nova Scotia, please visit: https://www.dfns.ca/

## How to Apply

Please submit your resume online by clicking "Apply." For more information, contact Greg Dickie confidentially at gdickie@royerthompson.com. If you need accommodation during the selection process, please let us know.

We believe in employment equity, welcoming individuals from all backgrounds. We encourage applications from the following under-represented groups to self-identify in their resume or cover letter: Indigenous persons, racially visible persons, persons with a disability, women, and persons of a minority sexual orientation and/or gender identity.

Facet is a recruitment firm with an unshakeable belief that change is a good thing. People are not only our purpose, they are also our passion. Facet was created to recruit talented, established professionals who aspire to lead organizations. We are inspired by these individuals and believe they are at the core of building purpose-driven, dynamic, and forward-thinking workplaces.

title: Business Development Manager
description:
Position Description

Business Development Manager

October 2026

## Position Overview

The Partnerships and Business Development Team builds the relationships, collaborations, and financial opportunities necessary for RNS to deliver on its mandate. The team works across Nova Scotia's research and innovation ecosystem to strengthen research capacity, mobilize resources, and enable research that contributes to economic growth and productivity in the Province's priority sectors. The team plays a central role in developing and implementing RNS's strategic direction. It builds and maintains relationships with government, including elected officials, senior public servants, and departments and agencies, to ensure alignment with government priorities and a shared understanding of RNS's mandate, activities, and contributions. It also connects researchers, universities, industry, philanthropic organizations, and other partners around shared objectives, identifying opportunities to organize, coordinate and support research, address emerging needs, and attract additional investment.

Under the leadership of the Vice President, the team comprises two complementary functions:

• Partnerships: Develops and stewards strategic relationships, manages government and stakeholder engagement, builds networks and consortia, and strengthens RNS's position as a trusted and effective partner within Nova Scotia's research ecosystem.

• Business Development: Identifies and advances opportunities for new research initiatives, develops funding and revenue partnerships, works with internal and external partners to translate opportunities into viable programs and investments, and expands and improves the connections between RNS partners (including both researchers and research end users) and RNS research funding and support programs.

Working collaboratively across RNS, the team contributes to ongoing organizational strategy development by gathering intelligence, identifying emerging opportunities and challenges, and recommending improvements to RNS's programs, partnerships, and approaches. It works seamlessly with the operations team that is charged with executing RNS program offerings. It helps guide and coordinate organizational communications, ensuring that public and partner engagement is focused on RNS's mandate, strategic priorities, activities, and results.

The Business Development Manager leads the Business Development Activities of RNS and is responsible for driving new partnerships, diversifying revenue, and identifying new or modified approaches to organizing, coordinating, and supporting research in Nova Scotia.

## Key Responsibilities

## A. Pipeline and Revenue Development

• In support of RNS external relations plans, develop and manage a pipeline of new opportunities across the researcher community, government funders, institutes of higher education, industry partners, and philanthropic donors

• Support the development of strategy and tactics to identify new partnership revenue models, including co-funding, co-delivery, and contracted activity

• Establish new relationships with industry partners and philanthropic organizations

• Negotiate contracts to create positive benefit for RNS

## B. Business Development

• Lead new business development and improvements to existing activity with external partners and collaboratively with the RNS team

• Create and maintain a culture of continuous quality improvement to ensure that RNS offerings are meeting the needs of both current and potential partners

## C. Planning and Performance

• Develop and maintain an annual plan for stakeholder engagement, targeted partnership growth, revenue forecasts, conversion progress, and programmatic enhancement

• Perform against established (or agreed upon) targets and metrics for enhancing partnerships and related outcomes

• Gather sector intelligence and synthesize data from multiple sources for making recommendations to Senior Staff or Management

## D. Communications

• Support and execute organizational communication plans and related public relations

## E. Other duties

• Travel to meet with stakeholders and partners as needed

• Perform other duties consistent with the role as assigned

## Qualifications and Requirements

## Education

• Bachelor's degree in a related field required

• Graduate degree an asset

## Experience

• More than 5 years of progressive experience in partnership management, fundraising, business development, or strategic sourcing

• Experience managing database and CRM-related tools

## Knowledge, skills and abilities

• Familiarity with the research sector in Nova Scotia and associated stakeholder groups

• High degree of comfort with negotiation, proposal writing, and financial modelling

• Comfort negotiating agreements and securing favourable terms

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including spelling and grammar

• Competence in program management and independent activity scheduling

• Comfort navigating emerging technology, including generative AI tools

## Core Competencies

• Business development - builds a pipeline of opportunities and converts them into partnerships and revenue

• Negotiation - negotiates contracts and agreements that secure favourable terms for RNS

• Financial acumen - applies financial modelling and revenue forecasting to partnership opportunities

• Relationship management - builds relationships and resolves problems effectively with partners and stakeholders

• Service orientation - demonstrates exceptional commitment to partner needs

• Strategic alignment - aligns plans to broader organizational strategic goals

• Organization - manages multiple activities simultaneously and schedules work independently

• Continuous improvement - ensures RNS offerings meet partner needs as well as possible

title: Director of Operations
description:
Position Description

Director of Operations

October 2026

Operations Team

The Operations Team executes the programs and processes that deliver the RNS mandate. It is responsible for the effective, efficient, and accountable delivery of RNS' research investments and the management of its internal operations. The team manages the full lifecycle of RNS research funding, from selection through award administration, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation, providing responsive service to researchers, research institutions, and funding partners. It manages all financial control aspects of the corporation and ensures that investments are managed with integrity and appropriate oversight. The team maintains the administrative, information management, and technology systems necessary for effective organizational performance. It supports the Board and senior leadership through reliable information, sound operational policies, and timely reporting. The team contributes to the design and continuous improvement of programs and services, ensuring they remain aligned with RNS's strategic priorities.

Position Overview

The Director of Operations is a senior leadership role responsible for the effective and efficient delivery of the organization's strategic plan and management of its day-to-day administration and all internal services. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Director leads the Operations Team. The Director is a member of the senior management team, providing strategic direction on operational policy, program design, risk management, and stakeholder relations with the research community, partner institutions, and government funders. This position works closely with the Vice President.

Direct reports:

• Manager of Research Initiatives, Pre-Award

• Manager of Research Initiatives, Post-Award

• Operations Coordinator

• Accountant

## Key Responsibilities

## A. Leadership and Team Management

• Provide leadership, coaching, and performance management to direct reports

• Set annual objectives and priorities for the operations team, aligned with the organization's strategic plan

• Foster a culture of service excellence, integrity, and continuous improvement across the team

## B. Competitions and Program Management

• Oversee the design, launch, and delivery of research funding competitions, including calls for proposals, merit review processes, and adjudication

• Ensure competition processes are consistent with the organization's policies and applicable government funding agreements

• Monitor competition timelines and volumes, adjusting resourcing as needed to meet application and review deadlines

• Ensure programs are evaluated regularly to determine if they are delivering the organization's strategy

• Support the launch of new programs to meet the research priorities of the organization and needs of the research community

## C. Award Administration

• Oversee the administration of research awards from notification through to file close-out, including agreements, amendments, extensions, and reporting requirements

• Ensure award terms and conditions comply with organizational policy and government funding requirements

• Develop relationships with recipient institutions and researchers on award-related matters

• Oversee compliance reporting from award holders

• Ensure evaluation of research results

## D. Financial Oversight

• Oversee the Accountant's work on budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting

• Ensure financial controls, disbursement processes, and reconciliation practices meet organizational policies and government accountability requirements

• Support the CEO in the preparation of financial reports for the Board and for funders

• Liaise with external auditors and government funders on financial compliance matters

## E. Corporate Management

• Support the Board of Directors and its committees by setting up meetings, preparing minutes, ensuring reports are filed on time, monitoring the bylaws, board policies, and terms of reference for compliance, tracking directors' terms of office, etc.

• Contribute to regulatory reporting requirements, including semi-annual reports, annual reports, and three-year operating plans.

## F. Policy, Risk, and Stakeholder Relations

• Develop and maintain operational policies and procedures for competitions and award administration

• Identify and mitigate operational and financial risks associated with program delivery

• Represent the organization with academic institutions, research associations, and government departments on operational matters

• Contribute to organizational strategic planning as a member of the senior management team

• Prepare reports and briefing materials for the CEO and Board of Directors as required

## G. Organizational Operations

• Ensure that the processes required to deliver the Corporation's strategic plan (e.g. internet access, appropriate computer hardware and software, the online application portal) are effective and efficient

• Oversee the office lease and relationship with the landlord to ensure that the space functions for staff and visitors

• Support compliance with the Corporation's policies regarding the office and staff (e.g. occupational health and safety)

• Undertake regular review of the processes, programs and tools RNS staff uses to execute their responsibilities to ensure they are meeting their needs and the needs of the Corporation

## H. Other duties

• Perform other duties consistent with the role as assigned

## Qualifications and Requirements

## Education

• Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, science, or a related field required

• Master's degree an asset

## Experience

• Minimum 5-7 years of progressively responsible experience in research administration, grants/awards management, or program operations, ideally within a publicly funded or academic environment

• At least 3-5 years of experience in a leadership role managing staff

• Experience with government funding agreements, financial accountability frameworks, or public sector reporting requirements

• Demonstrated experience managing financial oversight functions, ideally including budgeting and disbursement processes

## Knowledge, skills and abilities

• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities, especially during peak periods

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a service-oriented approach to client support

• Strong understanding of the Canadian research funding landscape and academic research environment

• Knowledge of financial management principles and public sector accountability requirements

## Core Competencies

• Strategic leadership - translates organizational priorities into operational plans and team direction

• People management - builds, coaches, and motivates a small, high-performing team

• Problem solving - is resourceful in finding answers when unexpected questions or situations arise

• Financial acumen - reads and interprets budgets, financial statements, and reporting requirements

• Judgment and integrity - handles confidential award and competition information with discretion; manages conflict of interest situations appropriately

• Stakeholder relations - communicates effectively with academic researchers, institutional administrators, and government contacts

• Process improvement - identifies opportunities to streamline competition and award administration workflows

• Risk management - anticipates operational and compliance risks and puts mitigations in place

• Attention to detail - ensures accuracy and consistency in high-volume, deadline-driven processes

• Customer Service - encourages responsive positioning toward the research community and other stakeholder groups.

It supports the Board and senior leadership through reliable information, sound operational policies, and timely reporting. The team contributes to the design and continuous improvement of programs and services, ensuring they remain aligned with RNS's strategic priorities.

Position Overview

The Operations Coordinator provides operational and administrative support to Research Nova Scotia (RNS)'s research funding programs, applicants, and award holders. Reporting to the Director of Operations, the Coordinator will provide support in three areas:

• Program delivery and competition coordination

• Award administration and award holder support

• Organization operations

## Key Responsibilities

## A. Program and competition coordination

Working with the Operations team, the Coordinator will:

• Support the delivery of funding competitions and programs, including communications and follow-up with applicants, institutions, and reviewers

• Help applicants resolve submission and access issues

• Prepare agendas, take minutes, and follow up on action items for review panels, committees, and working groups

• Support reviewers' onboarding, including grant management system account setup and support during the review process

• Coordinate logistics for workshops, information sessions, and webinars

• Be competent in the programming and maintenance of the Corporation's online grants management portal and serve as backup to the primary administrator when required, providing coverage during absences and peak periods such as competition launches and deadlines

• Assist with portal tasks, setting up and updating competition forms, and running reports and data exports

• Help test changes and new releases before they go live, and report any issues found

## B. Post award support

Working with the Manager of Research Initiatives, Post-Award, the Coordinator will:

• Support the preparation of agreements for new award holders

• Ensure compliance with conditions of funding RNS policies and regulations for award holders

• Oversee regular reporting from award holders and their host organizations

• Keep the files of all current award holders up to date

• Monitor RNS's phone line and email accounts, serving as the first point of contact for applicants, institutions, and award holders on questions related to programs, eligibility, and the online portal

## C. Operations support

• Support website and social media postings

• Support the Accountant as required

• Support the senior management team

## D. Other duties

• Perform other duties consistent with the role as assigned

## Education and experience

• Bachelor's degree or diploma in a relevant field (e.g., science, health, social science, business, public administration), or an equivalent combination of education and experience

• Two to three years of experience in research administration, grants management, program coordination, or a similar role

• Experience supporting or administering an online application or grants management system is strongly preferred

• Experience in a research funder, university, not-for-profit, or government setting is an asset

## Knowledge, skills, and abilities

• Comfort learning and working with database-driven platforms, including troubleshooting, testing, and documenting processes

• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities, especially during peak periods

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a service-oriented approach to client support

• Familiarity with the research funding landscape in Nova Scotia and Canada

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and Adobe Acrobat

• Strong attention to detail and sound judgment in handling confidential information

title: Manager, Marketing & Communications
description:
Port Saint John is looking for a strategic, creative, and relationship-focused Manager, Marketing & Communications to join our Government Relations team.

In this highly visible role, you will shape how Port Saint John communicates with customers, partners, government, media, employees, and the public. You will lead integrated communications and targeted marketing initiatives that strengthen our reputation, showcase our infrastructure and trade connections, and build understanding of the Port's economic and social impact.

You will be a trusted communications advisor, a skilled storyteller, and a calm, credible resource when issues emerge. From developing compelling campaigns and executive materials to coordinating media relations, stakeholder communications, and crisis response, your work will help advance Port Saint John's priorities at home and around the world.

Qualifications
What you bring
• A post-secondary degree or diploma in communications, public relations, marketing, journalism, business administration, media studies, or a related discipline.
• Three to five years of progressive experience in communications, public relations, marketing, media relations, digital communications, stakeholder engagement, or a related field.
• Exceptional writing, editing, verbal communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to transform complex information into clear, accessible, and compelling content.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and experience with website content management, social media, email communications, digital advertising, analytics platforms, marketing automation, and creative tools.
• Bilingualism in French and English is considered a strong asset.
• An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience may be considered.

You will thrive in this role if you
• Bring curiosity, creativity, initiative, and sound judgment to your work.
• Can move confidently between long-term planning and fast-moving communications needs.
• Remain calm, responsive, and collaborative when managing sensitive or time-critical matters.
• Translate complex operational and industry information into stories that resonate with diverse audiences.
• Embrace innovation, use data to improve results, and persevere when facing obstacles.
• Value continuous learning and contribute to the development and success of your colleagues.
• Build inclusive relationships and engage meaningfully with communities, customers, partners, and stakeholders.

Responsibilities

## What you will do

Lead strategic communications, marketing, and brand storytelling
• Develop and implement communications plans that support Port Saint John's strategic priorities, organizational initiatives, stakeholder relationships, and public profile.
• Design and execute targeted marketing campaigns that promote the Port's infrastructure capabilities, trade corridors, services, and economic impact to regional, national, and international logistics audiences.
• Create, edit, and coordinate engaging content, including news releases, presentations, speeches, articles, briefing notes, letters, website content, employee communications, advertisements, promotional materials, key messages, and stakeholder resources.
• Maintain a consistent organizational voice, visual identity, and brand experience across communications channels, digital platforms, campaigns, and public-facing materials.
• Track and analyze digital marketing, website, and social media performance and use insights to strengthen future outreach.

Build media relationships and protect our reputation
• Develop and maintain effective relationships with local, regional, national, and industry media, including outlets covering maritime, supply chain, and logistics matters.
• Coordinate media inquiries, interview requests, news releases, background information, media events, and press conferences in collaboration with leaders and subject matter experts.
• Monitor media coverage, emerging issues, stakeholder concerns, and reputational risks that may affect Port Saint John.
• Prepare key messages, holding statements, questions and answers, briefing materials, and other resources that support timely and coordinated responses.
• Contribute to crisis and emergency communications planning, exercises, response activities, and post-incident reviews.
• Support coordinated information sharing with public agencies, port partners, and stakeholders during significant events.
• Exercise sound judgment and maintain confidentiality when managing sensitive, time-critical, or reputational matters.

Strengthen stakeholder, government, and customer communications
• Support communications and relationship-building with government officials, regulatory bodies, rights holders, community partners, port users, customers, industry representatives, and other stakeholders.
• Develop a strong understanding of the operations, priorities, and communications needs of key customers and major port users.
• Coordinate clear, timely communications and joint marketing initiatives that strengthen strategic customer and partner relationships.
• Prepare presentations, correspondence, backgrounders, speaking notes, briefing materials, and other resources for senior leaders.
• Coordinate communications materials, marketing displays, and logistics for stakeholder meetings, public engagement activities, government announcements, corporate events, and partner initiatives.
• Track stakeholder inquiries and complaints, coordinate responses with internal leads, and support timely follow-up and recordkeeping.
• Represent Port Saint John professionally on external committees, working groups, and communications networks, as assigned.

Support events, partnerships, and organizational priorities
• Provide communications and marketing support for Port Days and other corporate, community, stakeholder, and employee events.
• Coordinate speakers, presentations, promotional materials, media activities, event messaging, sponsorship communications, and post-event content.
• Support special projects, organizational initiatives, and emerging communications, marketing, and engagement priorities.

About Port Saint John
Port Saint John operates on the traditional and unceded territory of the Wolastoqey, Mi'kmaq, and Peskotomuhkati Nations. Our commitment to truth and reconciliation is grounded in respect for Indigenous cultures and heritage and in building meaningful relationships.
Port Saint John connects people and markets by building partnerships and developing innovative solutions that create economic and social value. With links to more than 350 ports worldwide and direct access to central Canadian markets through national rail networks and the Trans-Canada Highway, the Port is a key facilitator of trade within Canada's Atlantic Gateway.
Our transportation infrastructure provides a marine gateway to global markets while supporting prosperity, sustainability, and opportunity for our region.

Make an impact at a port on the move
If you are ready to use strategic thinking, creative storytelling, and strong relationships to help shape the profile and reputation of a growing Canadian port, we want to hear from you.
Bring your ideas, judgment, and communications expertise to Port Saint John-and help us connect our story to the world.

Posted Date: 2026-10-16

Closing Date: Open until filled.

Applications are invited from highly motivated and experienced health care practitioners who are interested in the exciting challenge of working as a Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) in the Paramedicine and Medical Transport Division of NL Health Services. This position will involve working on the ground and air Provincial Programs. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) is a highly responsible, clinical position, accountable for the provision of quality, safe, skilled care of emergent and routine nature to patients within the province requiring inter-facility transport or at the scene of traumatic or acute medical incidents.

In a team environment, the Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will be responsible for providing direct patient care including assessment and intervention of all medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients ranging in age from newborn to the elderly. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will use critical thinking and professional judgment within their scope of practice and within a medical control system with written protocols and through medical consultation with a physician when necessary. This position is also responsible for promotion and maintenance of quality and safety standards and ensures maintenance of clinical proficiencies and competencies. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) will report directly to the Integrated Air Operations Manager of Paramedicine and Medical Transport. The successful candidate will report to Goose Bay/Sheshatshiu.

## Duties include but are not limited to:

• Performs comprehensive assessments, physical examinations, advanced treatments, triage, and interventions for all pre-hospital scene or inter-facility requests, encompassing medical and traumatic conditions for a diverse group of patients

• Applies treatment therapies and interventions for medical disorders and traumatic injuries, in accordance with protocols

• Adheres to all policies, procedures, guidelines, and applicable operational standards in the performance of assigned duties.

• Functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units

• Completes patient treatment charting, records all pertinent patient information to include vitals, neurological signs, assessment findings and treatment provided.

• Ensures confidentiality of patient information

• Provides leadership and scene management during mass casualty incidents in the absence of an incident command supervisor

• Preceptors and mentors Primary Care Paramedic students during field placements to ensure students meet required competencies

• Participates in Continuing Medical Education (CME)

• Maintains, cleans, and conducts duty checks of ambulances, equipment, and supplies and restocks when necessary

• Recognizes cultural diversity

• Provides orientation to new employees, and on the job training to staff and students

• Travel is required

• Perform interfacility transports using program aircraft.

• Maintain flight status

• Constantly lifts, pushes, and pulls patients on stretchers (which requires up to 35lbs of push/pull force or greater as the terrain and weather conditions can contribute to increased push/pull forces) often in challenging environments, not always conductive to proper ergonomics to and from planes and ambulances;

• Loading and carrying equipment/patients weighing between 10 – 50 lbs or more than 50 lbs. The work must be completed urgently which can contribute to increased forces required in pushing/pulling and lifting.

• Constantly/regularly sits, stands, walks, and works in awkward or cramped positions, as well as bends, kneels, and stretches to provide patient care.

• Visual concentration is required to prepare medications, monitor equipment, and patient condition during in-flight transport; time pressures when transporting critically ill or injured patients to care centers within time frames for life-saving interventions.

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an PCP

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador?

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation

• Current BLS certification

• Current certification in ACLS, PALS, ITLS, NRP, ICS 100, or willingness to complete

• Successful completion of aircraft safety training and basic flight physiology training

• Effective oral and written communication skills

• Critical and sound decision making skills

• Confidence to manage a variety of situations

• Ability to perform various medical procedures and operate a variety of medical equipment

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is?required

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct including vulnerable sector check from the RCMP or local police authority

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Maintenance Planning & Asset Management Coordinator
description:
## Maintenance Planning & Asset Management Coordinator

Location: Dartmouth, NS

## Position Summary

Maritime Paper Products LP is a dynamic, team-oriented company and is honored to be one of Canada's Best Managed Companies. We believe that hiring the best people is a key part of our success. Providing excellence in both our packaging solutions and the relationships we build with our clients, we offer superior capabilities, including in-house graphic and structural design, platemaking, and manufacturing for retail-ready display. We support our customers through operations located in NS, NB, NL, and PE.

Reporting to maintenance management, the Maintenance Planning & Asset Management Coordinator will be responsible for providing excellent maintenance, clerical, and administrative planning services, which includes coordinating between maintenance management and production leadership to schedule planned maintenance projects including proactively anticipating and managing parts lead times to ensure minimal interruption of production and maintenance.

## Duties & Responsibilities:

## 1. Maintenance Planning & Work Management (30%)

• Administer and optimize all maintenance planning activities within LLumin CMMS.

• Develop and maintain preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs.

• Coordinate labor, contractors, tools, permits, and materials required to execute planned maintenance work.

• Improve workforce utilization through effective scheduling practices.

• Establish and maintain standardized job plans, procedures, and maintenance task libraries.

## 2. CMMS Governance & Digital Maintenance Leadership (20%)

• Serve as site champion and super-user for LLumin CMMS.

• Develop site standards for data entry, work order coding, failure analysis, and asset hierarchy management.

• Ensure accuracy and completeness of equipment master data.

• Manage CMMS training and user adoption.

• Lead implementation of CMMS enhancements and best practices including dashboard development.

• Drive integration opportunities between maintenance, purchasing, inventory, and financial systems.

## 3. Reliability & Predictive Maintenance (15%)

• Develop asset criticality rankings.

• Monitor equipment performance trends and analyze failures and recurring downtime events.

• Support implementation of condition-based and predictive maintenance programs.

• Identify reliability improvement opportunities.

• Lead root cause analysis efforts.

• Support FMEA development and reliability improvement projects.

## 4. Inventory & Spare Parts Management (15%)

• Manage maintenance inventory strategy and support annual inventory audits and cycle counting.

• Establish critical spare parts lists by asset criticality.

• Monitor inventory turns, stock levels, obsolescence, and usage trends.

• Recommend stocking levels based on failure history and lead times.

• Analyze spare parts consumption trends and cost drivers.

## 5. Maintenance Analytics & Financial Reporting (10%)

• Develop and maintain maintenance KPIs.

• Conduct trend analysis on downtime, reliability, labor utilization, and maintenance spending.

• Analyze maintenance cost by asset, production area, and failure mode.

• Prepare monthly and annual maintenance performance reports.

• Quantify return on investment for maintenance initiatives.

## 6. Asset Lifecycle & Capital Planning (10%)

• Maintain long-term asset replacement forecasts and identify assets approaching end-of-life.

• Develop lifecycle cost models and replacement recommendations.

• Support preparation of annual capital requests.

• Develop 3-year and 5-year capital replacement plans.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Engineering Technology Diploma, Industrial Technology Diploma, Mechanical Engineering Technician, or related discipline.

• Reliability certification.

• CMRP, CMRP-equivalent, or reliability training are considered an asset.

• 5+ years industrial maintenance experience.

• Experience with CMMS administration and reporting.

• Experience in inventory management, maintenance planning, reliability, or asset management.

• Experience using business analytics (Power BI) and KPI reporting tools and advanced Excel.

## Preferred Technical Skills

• LLumin CMMS or equivalent platform.

• Maintenance budgeting and forecasting.

• Inventory management.

• Reliability engineering principles including Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and FMEA methodology.

title: Owner/General Manager
description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our confidential client, is seeking to fill an Owner/General Manager position to join an automotive mechanical repair company franchise opening in Corner Brook, NL.

## Position Summary

The Owner/General Manager is responsible for the daily management, operational performance, financial results, and long-term growth of the automotive mechanical repair company. The candidate will purchase 10% ownership interest from the existing owner through a separate share purchase agreement. This is a working management position requiring a strong mechanical background, practical leadership experience, and the ability to oversee both shop operations and the broader business. The successful candidate will help emphasize customer experience, sales growth, team development, operational efficiency, and profitability.

In addition to employment responsibilities, the individual is expected to demonstrate an ownership mindset, contribute to business planning, protect the company's interests, and work collaboratively with the majority owner. The position combines hands-on operational leadership with business management and minority ownership, while maintaining a clear distinction between salary earned for work performed and financial rights arising from share ownership.

## Key Responsibilities:

## Overall Business Management

• Manage the day-to-day operations of the mechanical company, including shop activities, service delivery, staffing, scheduling, and customer commitments.

• Establish operational priorities and implement processes that improve productivity, service quality, and profitability.

• Work with the majority owner to establish annual business objectives, budgets, and growth plans.

• Monitor business performance and recommend improvements to revenue, operating costs, and customer service.

• Represent the company professionally with customers, suppliers, employees, and business partners.

## Mechanical Operations and Technical Leadership

• Apply practical mechanical experience to oversee diagnostics, repairs, maintenance, and other technical services.

• Provide hands-on technical assistance when required, particularly for complex jobs, troubleshooting, or training.

• Supervise mechanics and service personnel to ensure work meets established quality and safety standards.

• Coordinate workflow, job assignments, scheduling, labour utilization, and completion deadlines.

• Ensure work orders, estimates, parts usage, labour hours, and customer invoices are accurately documented.

• Maintain shop equipment, tools, facilities, and inventory in an efficient and safe condition.

• Establish and enforce consistent service procedures and technical standards.

## Financial Management and Profitability

• Be accountable for day-to-day financial and operational performance within the approved budget and delegated authority.

• Monitor revenue, labour costs, parts costs, gross margins, overhead, cash flow, and profitability.

• Review financial statements and management reports with the bookkeeper, accountant, and majority owner.

• Monitor technician productivity, billable hours, labour recovery, job costing, and pricing.

• Oversee purchasing, inventory management, invoicing, accounts receivable follow-up, and cost control.

• Prepare operating budgets and financial forecasts for review and approval.

## Employee Management and Development

• Recruit, onboard, train, supervise, and retain qualified employees.

• Establish clear roles, performance expectations, and accountability standards.

• Conduct performance reviews and address performance concerns appropriately.

• Develop employees' technical skills, productivity, and professional capabilities.

• Manage scheduling, attendance, workload allocation, and workforce planning.

## Customer Relationships and Business Development

• Maintain strong relationships with existing customers and develop new business opportunities.

• Resolve customer complaints and service issues promptly and professionally.

• Ensure estimates, service commitments, pricing, and delivery expectations are communicated clearly.

• Build relationships with suppliers, contractors, fleet operators, and other relevant commercial partners.

• Identify opportunities to expand service offerings, increase repeat business, and improve customer retention.

• Support marketing, sales, and business development initiatives in collaboration with the majority owner.

## Responsibilities as a 10% Shareholder

• Act in the company's best interests and meet the legal obligations applicable to the individual's role as a shareholder and, if applicable, director or officer.

• Participate in agreed business planning and shareholder discussions.

• Contribute operational knowledge and business recommendations to support long-term growth.

• Protect confidential business information, customer relationships, trade information, and company assets.

• Maintain open communication with the majority owner regarding significant operational risks, financial concerns, and business opportunities.

• Comply with the share purchase agreement, shareholders' agreement, corporate governing documents, and applicable law.

• Respect the distinction between personal shareholder interests and the responsibilities of the General Manager position.

• Support the long-term stability, reputation, and profitability of the company.

## Qualifications:

• Background in Automotive Mechanics- (Preferably Journeyman Red Seal), coupled with significant hands-on experience as a mechanic or mechanical technician, with strong diagnostic and repair capabilities.

• Proven progressive experience in management, or considerations will be made for those with strong automotive experience and leadership potential, coupled with strong operational and sales management backgrounds- a combination of those qualities will be considered an asset.

• Able and willing to contribute to a 10% Ownership opportunity for the franchise through a separate share purchase agreement. Specific financial details are to be discussed with shortlisted candidates being considered.

• Experience supervising mechanics, managing shop operations, or leading a mechanical service team.

• Strong understanding of service scheduling, labour productivity, inventory, parts purchasing, job costing, and customer service.

• Demonstrated leadership, organization, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to interpret financial and operational reports and make sound business decisions.

• Commitment to workplace safety, workmanship, customer satisfaction, and employee development.

• Entrepreneurial mindset and willingness to accept accountability for business performance.

## Job Details:

• Reports to: CEO

• Position type: Full-time, salaried management position with minority share ownership

title: Assistant Director Finance & Administration
description:
CAREER OPPORTUNITY

Position Title: Assistant Director Finance & Administration
Competition Number: 2026-54
Salary: $ 97,523.45 - $130,031.27
Closing Date: This position will remain open until it is filled.

The City of Corner Brook is seeking a qualified, experienced, and motivated professional to join our Finance & Administration Department team as Assistant Director of Finance and Administration. The Assistant Director of Finance and Administration is responsible for maintaining the City's general ledger, preparing financial statements and management reports, and overseeing month-end and year-end financial processes. The position supports treasury management, cash flow forecasting, banking and debt administration, annual audits, financial controls, and compliance with Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS) and applicable legislation. Responsibilities also include supporting operating and capital budgets, financial forecasting, long-range financial planning, improving accounting procedures and systems, and providing financial advice and reporting support to City departments, Council, and senior leadership.

A university degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline is required. A Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation is preferred; however, candidates pursuing their CPA designation with strong municipal or public-sector accounting experience may be considered. A minimum of five (5) years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience is required, including experience with general ledger maintenance, reconciliations, financial statements, budgeting, financial analysis, and external audits. Experience in municipal government, public-sector accounting, or a similarly regulated environment, along with knowledge of Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS), is considered an asset.

The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of municipal finance, financial controls, audit practices, and applicable legislation. Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills are required, along with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains) or a comparable accounting system are also required. A high degree of accuracy, integrity, confidentiality, and professional judgment is essential.

Work is primarily performed in an office environment, involving frequent interaction with City employees and occasional contact with residents. Extended periods of sitting or walking and occasional lifting or handling of files and office supplies may be required. The above responsibilities reflect the principal functions of the position and shall not be considered a detailed description of all duties of the job.

The City of Corner Brook will provide support throughout the recruitment process to applicants with disabilities, including accommodation that considers an applicant's accessibility needs. Candidates are encouraged to discuss specific needs with the City's Human Resources division, by emailing hr@cornerbrook.com

Please submit résumés giving complete details of qualifications to the Human Resources Office, via E-mail at careers@cornerbrook.com

The City of Corner Brook thanks all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Title: Assistant Director Finance & Administration
Reports To: Director of Finance & Administration
Department: Finance & Administration
Employee Group: Non-Management/Non-Union

## Position Overview

The Assistant Director of Finance and Administration is a senior professional accounting position within the Department of Finance & Administration. Reporting to the Director of Finance & Administration, this position is responsible for the integrity of the City's accounting records, financial reporting, treasury administration, audit coordination, and regulatory compliance activities. The Assistant Director ensures accurate and timely financial information is available to support decision-making, legislative compliance, and financial stewardship. The position provides technical expertise in municipal accounting, Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS), treasury management, financial analysis, the audit process, and financial control processes. The incumbent works collaboratively with internal departments, external auditors, government agencies, financial institutions, and other stakeholders to support the City's financial operations.

## Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & General Ledger

• Maintain the general ledger and chart of accounts.

• Lead month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close.

• Prepare reconciliations, working papers, variance analysis, and management reports.

• Support preparation of annual financial statements and note disclosures.

• Maintain audit-ready schedules for TCA, reserves, deferred revenue, debt, grants, receivables, payables, and accruals.

Treasury, Cash Flow & Debt

• Monitor cash flow and liquidity.

• Support banking, investments, debt servicing schedules, and financing requirements.

• Prepare cash flow forecasts and analysis.

• Coordinate with financial institutions and government agencies.

Audit, Compliance & Controls

• Coordinate annual audit requirements.

• Coordinate the year-end close process, including timelines, departmental information requests, accruals, deferred revenue, tangible capital assets, reserves, debt, and audit schedules.

• Track management letter points and corrective actions.

• Lead the design, documentation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of accounting controls, reconciliation processes, segregation of duties, and financial reporting procedures.

• Support compliance with PSAS and applicable municipal/provincial/federal requirements.

Budget, Forecasting & Analysis

• Support operating and capital budget preparation.

• Prepare variance analysis and financial forecasts.

• Assist with long-range financial planning and capital funding strategies.

• Provide analysis for Council/senior leadership as required.

Systems, Process Improvement & Cross-Department Support

• Improve accounting processes and standard operating procedures.

• Support ERP/accounting system optimization.

• Provide financial advice and reporting support to departments.

## Note

The above responsibilities reflect the duties necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and shall not be considered as a detailed description of all duties of the job.

## Education & Professional Designation

• A university degree in Commerce, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or a related discipline is required.

• A Chartered Professional Accountant designation is required; however, candidates pursuing their CPA designation with strong municipal/public-sector accounting experience may be considered.

## Experience

• Five (5) years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience.

• Experience with municipal government, public sector accounting, or a similarly regulated environment.

• Experience with general ledger, reconciliations, month-end/year-end close, and financial reporting.

• Experience preparing audit working papers and supporting external audit engagements.

• Experience with budgeting, financial management, accounting, and financial analysis.

• Experience with Public Sector Accounting Standards (PSAS).

## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Strong understanding of municipal finance principles, financial controls, and audit practices.

• Knowledge of applicable municipal, provincial, and federal legislation affecting financial operations.

• Advanced analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

• Strong ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.

• Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

• Experience using Microsoft Dynamics GP (Great Plains) or comparable ERP/accounting systems.

• High degree of accuracy, integrity, and professional judgment.

## Working Conditions

• This position will be required to work within an office environment, with minor fluctuations in working conditions.

• Frequent dealings with City employees and occasional dealings with residents.

• Sitting and walking for an extended period may occasionally be required.

• Lifting and handling of files and office supplies.

title: Engineer/Scientist I-IV (Reactor Physics)
description:
Engineer/Scientist I-IV (Reactor Physics)
One (1) Regular position
Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station, New Brunswick Canada
$39.22-$61.65 hourly based on 40 hours per week
Competition #E22699-2026

At NB Power we are a team, committed to offering the best customer experience, ensuring energy security, and accelerating a sustainable clean energy transition. Why? Because we're New Brunswickers too, we care about our customers and future generations, and today we are actively looking for a new member to join us.

NB Power's Nuclear division is seeking an engineering/scientific professional for its Reactor Physics group. This position is responsible to ensure the safe fueling of the PLNGS reactor core, optimize fuel usage, and effectively manage reactivity following the reactivity management program.

## Key functions include:

• Carrying out reactor physics activities (e.g., reactor core monitoring, regional overpower protection program implementation, reactor fueling simulation activities, core evolutions simulations).

• Identifying and managing corrective actions relating to reactor physics. This could include governance and technical documentation updates, reactor physics simulations and analysis, and working with vendor partners to address issues as they arise to prevent reoccurrence.

• Updating and maintaining governance, processes, procedures, and other documentation associated with the Reactor Physics group.

## Our ideal teammate will have:

• A Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Engineering, Reactor Physics, Applied Science, or related discipline

• Strong knowledge or experience in at least one of the following areas of specialized expertise:
• Reactor physics analysis and modelling

• Subcritical analysis, simulation, and operation

• In-core fuel management

• Core surveillance (power, reactivity, and coolant flow)

• Core physics calibrations (Reactor Regulating System (RRS), Reactor Overpower (ROP), and thermal power)

• Thermal hydraulics (analysis and modelling, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer)

• Neutronics detector performance monitoring

• Familiarity with and knowledge of relevant codes and standards, such as:
• CSA N286.7-16 Quality Assurance of Analytical, Scientific, and Design Computer Programs

• REGDOC 2.4.3 Nuclear Criticality Safety

• REGDOC 2.5.2 Design of Reactor Facilities

• Strong written and verbal communication skills to document and share complex technical subjects with stakeholders.

• Note: candidates who possess an Engineering degree require immediate eligibility for registration as a Professional Engineer in the province of New Brunswick or agreement to pursue this designation.

An equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered. Subject to competition response, the minimum qualifications may be modified.

Due to security requirements at Canadian Nuclear facilities, the successful candidate will require a Site Access Security Clearance which includes verification of background information, references, a Criminal Record Name Check and a Canadian Security Intelligence Service security recommendation.

An Eligibility List generated from this competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level within a period of up to 12 months.

## We care for our team, and as a member you will have access to:

• Health & Dental plans that provide flexible options to meet your needs

• Health Spending Account, allowing for further flexibility

• New Brunswick Public Service Pension Plan, offering retirement financial security

• Wellness options, including our Employee Family Assistance Program

• Benefits that allow for financial protection in the event it is needed

• Various options for paid or unpaid leaves

• Representation of the IBEW Local 37 Union

• Career development and growth throughout the organization

• Competitive wages

title: Miramichi Privileging Advisor (N-B) PCN 1155341
description:
## This is the life-changing opportunity you've been looking for.

Horizon Health Network in beautiful New Brunswick is looking for a Privileging Advisor to join our team!

Horizon Health Network (Horizon) is seeking a driven, and detail-oriented individual to join our team as a Privileging Advisor. The ideal candidate will have experience in credentialing, privileging, medical affairs, health administration, regulatory compliance, professional affairs, or a related healthcare environment.

## Why you should work here

Working for Horizon gives you a career that provides an east coast lifestyle and the chance to make a big difference in the lives of New Brunswickers.

This position comes with competitive salary, paid time off, sick benefits, employer paid contributions into our government pension plan and a remote work policy.

Horizon is committed to enhancing our diverse and inclusive environment for our employees and patients. We believe in a healthcare system that equally supports all people regardless of race, ethnicity, national origin, social background, religion, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or sexual orientation. An environment based on a commitment to diversity and inclusion supports our goal of safe and quality patient care.

## Who you are

You have a worked in health care administration or a related field for a minimum of 2-4 years. You have an excellent proficiency level in Microsoft Office applications.

## Experience

• Minimum two to four years of experience in credentialing, privileging, medical affairs, health administration, regulatory compliance, professional affairs, or a related healthcare environment.

• Experience interpreting policies, by-laws, regulations, and professional practice standards.

• Experience working with physician leadership, governance committees, and senior stakeholders.

• Demonstrated experience managing multiple complex files and competing priorities in a high-volume environment.

## Education

• Bachelor's degree in Health Administration, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

• An equivalent combination of education and job experience may be considered.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Certification related to provider credentialing, medical staff services, regulatory affairs, project management, or healthcare administration.

• Experience within a regional healthcare system.

• Experience supporting medical staff governance and credential review processes.

• Knowledge of Accreditation Canada standards and healthcare regulatory frameworks.

Written and spoken competence in English is required at an advanced level.

## What you will do

## Credentialing and Privileging Leadership

• Lead the end-to-end credentialing, privileging, appointment, and reappointment processes for incoming medica/dental staff.

• Conduct initial assessment and verification of education, training, licensure, certifications, professional references, work history, and professional standing.

• Evaluate credentialing information to identify potential risks, concerns, inconsistencies, or compliance issues requiring escalation or further review.

• Ensure practitioner appointments and privileges align with organizational by-laws, professional standards, scope of practice requirements, and departmental needs.

• Interpret and apply complex credentialing standards, policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

• Provide expert guidance to leadership regarding eligibility, appointment requirements, privileging criteria, and credentialing risks.

## Medical Staff Governance Support

• Serve as a strategic resource to Department Heads and Medical Leadership throughout credential review and privileging decision making processes.

• Support medical staff governance activities by preparing, analyzing, and presenting complex credentialing information for review by credentialing and governance committees.

• Ensure credentialing recommendations are supported by complete, accurate, and validated practitioner information.

• Facilitate compliance with Medical Staff By-laws, Rules and Regulations, and organizational governance expectations.

• Support implementation of new privileging frameworks, policies, standards, and governance initiatives.

## Risk Management and Regulatory Compliance

• Identify, investigate, and resolve credentialing, regulatory, or compliance concerns that may affect practitioner appointments or privileges.

• Conduct risk assessments related to practitioner qualifications, professional conduct findings, licensure restrictions, malpractice history, and other credentialing indicators.

• Escalate significant risks and provide recommendations to appropriate leadership for consideration.

• Maintain ongoing compliance with applicable legislation, accreditation standards, professional regulatory bodies, and organizational policies.

• Participate in audits, investigations, accreditation activities, and quality reviews as required.

## Stakeholder Consultation and Relationship Management

• Build and maintain collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders involved in the credentialing and privileging process.

• Provide education and consultation to physicians, medical leaders, and administrative partners regarding credentialing requirements and governance processes.

• Act as the primary point of contact for complex credentialing inquiries and interpretation of privileging requirements.

• Facilitate resolution of sensitive and confidential issues while maintaining professionalism and discretion.

## Information Management and Confidentiality

• Maintain highly confidential practitioner information and ensure integrity of credentialing records and databases.

• Ensure documentation standards support organizational accountability, transparency, legal defensibility, and audit readiness.

• Generate reports and analyses to support medical leadership decision making.

• Maintain accuracy and completeness of credentialing and privileging information across multiple systems and repositories.

## Horizon Competency

Core competencies for non-bargaining positions are based on the LEADS in a Caring Environment leadership capabilities framework: Lead Self, Engage Others, Achieve Results, Develop Coalitions, and System Transformation.

In addition to LEADS, all positions need to demonstrate compassion, patience, and professionalism in all interactions, consistently upholding a respectful and supportive environment for patients, clients, families, and colleagues. Proactively addresses concerns and responds to emerging needs with empathy and diligence, contributing to high-quality, patient/client centered care.

description:
## JOB PURPOSE

As a member of the interdisciplinary team, the Community-based Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) delivers safe, person and population-centered care across lifespan within the scope of practice. The role supports health promotion, illness/injury prevention, and care management in both clinical and community settings, in collaboration with individuals, families, and community partners.

## ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

• Active registration with ANBLPN and be in good standing

• Current BCLS certification

• Minimum 2 years recent and direct experience (within last 5 years) in community-based nursing or a related area such as Addiction & Mental Health, Public Health, Harm Reduction, or Primary Health is required. A combination of relevant work experience and related education training will be considered.

• Commitment to complete area-specific training and certifications (i.e. Mental Health Interventions, Public Health Modules, Chronic Disease Management, immunization practices) as outlined during orientation and onboarding within a defined timeframe.

• Possess a valid driver's license and transportation, with the ability and willingness to travel within the region to support patient care, attend client appointment and participate in community-based activities as required.

• A valid passport may be required for staff hired to support Campobello Island within Area 2

• Good work and attendance record

• Ability to perform the duties of the position

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Patient Care:
