## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Maintenance Supervisor (Electrical Planner) to join our Coleman Mine team in Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a permanent on-site position. The work schedule is Monday to Friday.

As an Electrical Planner, you will be helping to facilitate the continuous improvement of the Maintenance team's performance, through the effective use of established processes and procedures. Your experience and skills will be accountable for the project planning of work for the Coleman Mine Department and may be required to provide relief supervision as needed.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Identify and escalate all critical issues that threaten the successful execution of the "work schedule" for completion by the Required End Date.

• Establish and maintain work relationships with the various key plant stakeholders including superintendents, supervisors, other planners, schedulers, and crew members.

• Relief supervisor as required which requires holding the crew accountable for safe behavior, housekeeping, teamwork, and professionalism; and work with the team to develop an interactive workplace environment.

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. Risk Management Specialist
One Regular, non-unionized position
Fredericton, New Brunswick, Canada
Salary range: $91,712 - $125,979 annually
Competition # E22696-2026

At NB Power we are a team committed to offering the best customer experience, ensuring energy security, and accelerating a sustainable clean energy transition. Why? Because we're New Brunswickers too, we care about our customers and future generations, and today we are actively looking for a new member to join us.

The Mactaquac Generating Station began generating electricity in 1968. Since the 1980s, concrete portions of the hydro station have been affected by a chemical reaction called alkali-aggregate reaction. The reaction causes the concrete to swell and crack and has required substantial annual maintenance and repairs. NB Power is proposing a project to ensure the station can operate to its intended 100-year lifespan with a modified approach to maintenance and adjusting and replacing equipment and concrete overtime.

As part of the Mactaquac Life Achievement Project, the Risk Management Specialist identifies, assesses, monitors, and mitigates risks that may impact project objectives, financial performance, compliance, and organizational reputation. Additionally, the Risk Management Specialist provides risk-based recommendations and collaborates with stakeholders to support informed decision-making and effective risk management practices.

## Key functions include:

• Develop, maintain, and integrate risk management processes, including risk registers, risk plans, governance frameworks, risk assessments, and mitigation activities across project, corporate, health and safety, and environment risk programs.

• Monitor and report on risks and controls through dashboards, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), and risk reviews, while supporting issue escalation, audits, compliance reviews, and risk oversight activities.

• Deliver risk management training, coaching, and cross-functional workshops to enhance risk awareness and promote effective risk management practices.

## Our ideal teammate will have:

• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Engineering, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline (candidates with a technical related diploma must have an additional two years of relevant experience)

• Eight years of risk management experience preferably in a large complex multi discipline project environment

• Experience with project management and project controls, including risk management, budgeting, scheduling, estimating, and contract administration

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite

As Site Manager, Sheriff Services, you are accountable for the efficient and effective delivery of Sheriff Services by managing and directing operational resources, monitoring performance, and developing Deputy Sheriff staff at justice centers throughout the province. You are responsible for one justice center, court facility or operations center. You perform all management functions related to the bargaining unit staff at that site, such as performance appraisals, discipline, scheduling and allocation of resources, budget management, risk management and communications. In addition, you provide support to all levels of court relating to the Sheriff Services mandate, court security, prisoner transportation and document service. The Site Manager, described as a 'sheriff's officer', is included in Section 2 of the Criminal Code of Canada under the definition of a peace officer; therefore, is entitled to exercise the authority of a peace officer in Canada.

This includes interpreting court orders properly and acting on the orders as required.

• Manages responses to operational pressures by overseeing the development of risk assessments, both dynamic and pre planned, contingency and emergency plans, with respect to all duties and functions performed by Sheriff Services by gathering, analysing, and interpreting sensitive information from various sources; writing operational plans and directing the execution of such plans whilst complying with relevant OHS legislation; manages the use and assignment of weapons including being proficient in the use of weapons, in accordance with policy.

title: Architectural Technologist/Designer
description:
Job Title: Architectural Technologist/Designer
Location: Fredericton, New Brunswick
TP - COD - 9445

Colpitts Developments is a family-founded, privately held real estate development and construction company with deep roots in Fredericton and a history spanning more than 30 years. Over that time, the organization has grown steadily into a fully integrated operation, delivering a broad range of residential, multi-residential, and commercial projects and maintaining a substantial portfolio of properties that it designs, builds, and manages long term.

Meridia is proud to partner with Colpitts Developments in their search for an Architectural Technologist/Designer to join their growing, in-house design team based in Fredericton.

## About Colpitts Developments

Colpitts Developments maintains an extensive portfolio of multi-residential, single-family residential, and commercial projects, located within the rapidly growing Greater Fredericton area. What distinguishes Colpitts in the local market is its fully integrated approach, managing every stage of the project lifecycle internally, from land acquisition and site servicing through design, permitting, construction, and long-term property management.

## Role Description

The Architectural Technologist/Designer plays a key role in delivering projects from early concept through construction within Colpitts' integrated design and build environment. In this role, you'll work closely with senior leadership, internal project managers, and consultants to develop practical, buildable designs across a diverse range of residential, multi-residential, and commercial projects.

Unlike a traditional drafting role, this position carries a high level of design responsibility and autonomy. The Architectural Technologist/Designer will be expected to apply sound design judgement, strong technical knowledge, and building code expertise while contributing creatively throughout the project lifecycle.

Your work will span concept design, site planning, permit and construction documentation, and construction coordination, ensuring quality, consistency, and feasibility at every stage.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Developing architectural drawings and design packages from concept through construction.

• Preparing permit-ready and construction-ready drawing sets for residential and multi-residential projects.

• Applying and interpreting building code requirements and relevant bylaws.

• Contributing to site planning, land-use layouts, and massing studies.

• Coordinating architectural design with structural, mechanical, electrical, and civil consultants.

• Conducting site visits to verify conditions and support design accuracy.

• Creating 2D and 3D drawings, models, and visualizations as required.

• Collaborating closely with internal construction and project management teams during active builds.

• Managing multiple projects while maintaining design intent, quality, and schedules.

## Qualifications

The ideal candidate brings a balance of technical strength, design judgment, and practical construction knowledge.

Your qualifications include:

• Diploma or degree in Architectural Technology or a related field.

• 5+ years of experience in an architectural design or technologist role.

• Strong knowledge of Canadian building codes; Part 3 requirements in particular.

• Experience with residential and multi-residential projects.

• Proficiency with CAD-based design software.

• Ability to independently develop accurate, buildable design solutions from concept through construction.

• Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Comfort working in a fast-paced, in-office team environment.

## Additional Assets

• Prior experience using Vectorworks, and/or openness to learn.

• Site planning and land development exposure.

• 3D modeling and rendering experience.

• Understanding of construction sequencing and coordination.

## Why Join Colpitts?

End?to?End Impact: See your work come to life. Contribute to projects from early concept and site planning through construction - then watch them succeed as long-term, Colpitts-owned assets in the community.

Meaningful Design Responsibility: Take real ownership of your work in an environment without rigid hierarchy, where your ideas, judgement, and technical expertise directly shape outcomes.

Integrated, In?House Team: Collaborate closely with design, construction, and project management professionals under one roof, enabling efficient decision-making and a strong connection between design and build.

Stability, Growth, and Culture: Build a long-term career with a family-founded organization known for employee retention, professional development opportunities, and a supportive, family-focused workplace.

title: Director of Maintenance
description:
Director of Maintenance-The Northside Community Guest Home

Department: Maintenance
Reports to: Administrator
Supervises: Maintenance Technicians and grant workers; coordinates and oversees contracted work
Location: The Northside Community Guest Home building and grounds

Purpose
Plan, organize and oversee the maintenance department to support the safe, reliable operation of the Home's building, grounds, equipment and mechanical systems. Coordinate preventive maintenance, repairs, contractors and capital projects in collaboration with the Administrator.

## Department leadership

• Assign and prioritize maintenance work, coordinate daily activities and monitor work quality and completion.

• Provide direction and job-related training to maintenance staff and grant workers, and address work concerns with the Administrator as needed.

• Coordinate maintenance activities with other departments to minimize disruption to residents, staff and services.

• Arrange contractor services within approved authority, communicate work requirements and monitor completion.

## Building and equipment maintenance

• Develop and maintain a preventive maintenance program, including schedules for inspections, testing, servicing, adjustments and repairs.

• Operate and maintain boilers and associated equipment and systems in accordance with operating procedures and applicable safety requirements.

• Perform routine boiler room maintenance, including cleaning boiler tubes, lubricating pumps, motors and gearboxes, replacing valve packings and servicing filters, within the scope of training and qualifications.

• Maintain ventilation equipment and emergency generator systems, and arrange required testing and servicing.

• Inspect and repair furniture, fixtures and equipment, including painting and refinishing as needed.

• Perform carpentry, plumbing, electrical, mechanical and other maintenance work within the scope of training and qualifications; arrange qualified contractors when required.

• Maintain the grounds and coordinate or perform snow removal and seasonal upkeep.

• Operate and maintain hand tools, power tools and groundskeeping equipment. Assist with heavy housekeeping and window cleaning when needed.

## Safety and maintenance records

• Maintain the Home's fire prevention and safety program within the maintenance department's responsibilities, including fire protection equipment inspections, servicing and logs.

• Maintain accurate operating, inspection, preventive maintenance and repair records for building equipment and mechanical systems.

• Identify and report equipment failures, unusual operating conditions and fire or safety hazards; arrange or carry out corrective action within approved authority.

• Follow applicable occupational health and safety requirements, building and equipment standards, inspection requirements and facility policies.

• Promote safe work practices, appropriate use of protective equipment and safe storage of tools, materials and supplies.

• Participate in quality assurance, risk management and in-service training. Protect resident privacy and maintain confidentiality.

## Budget and capital projects

• Assist with preparing and administering the department's budget, monitor expenditures and identify opportunities to control costs.

• Maintain appropriate inventories of tools, equipment and supplies, track usage and arrange purchases within approved authority.

• Work with the Administrator to identify capital project needs, define requirements, obtain cost estimates and oversee approved work through completion.

• Provide maintenance, equipment, expenditure and project updates to the Administrator as required.

## Qualifications

• High school diploma and a relevant trade school diploma or certificate in building or equipment maintenance. An electrical trade qualification is preferred.

• Relevant experience in building maintenance and mechanical systems; experience coordinating maintenance work and supervising staff is preferred.

• Practical knowledge of painting, carpentry, plumbing, electrical systems, mechanics, equipment repair and welding, with an understanding of when specialized services are required.

• WHMIS training and knowledge of safe work practices for maintenance activities.

• Ability to plan and prioritize work, solve maintenance problems, keep accurate records and communicate effectively with staff and contractors.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, email and web browsers.

## Working conditions and equipment

• Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs using safe lifting techniques and appropriate equipment.

• Work takes place indoors and outdoors and involves walking, standing, bending, kneeling, ladder use, lifting and moving materials and equipment.

• Duties involve hand and power tools, paints, maintenance supplies, boiler room equipment, and snow removal and lawn care equipment. Use appropriate protective equipment, safe handling methods and assistance when required.

## Hours of work

• Regular hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., subject to change based on facility needs. In an emergency, you may be contacted outside regular work hours and required to report to work.

• Other related duties may be assigned within the scope of the position.

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Disability Support Program (DSP), Income Assistance (IA), and Supportive Housing and Homelessness.

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports, staff, and partners to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
As the Secretary, you will be at the heart of our department's administrative engine, ensuring seamless operations and providing vital support to our staff.

You'll be the welcoming face at the front desk, assisting visitors and stepping in as a reliable backup for your fellow clerical team members. If you're enthusiastic about maintaining efficiency and making a positive first impression, we invite you to be a key part of our team.

Primary Accountabilities
This role is diverse, requiring your efficiency, confidentiality, and adaptability in a fast-paced environment. Your contributions will be integral to meeting tight operational deadlines and ensuring the smooth flow of our operations. Key responsibilities of yours include:

• Maintaining and organizing files using the STAR/STOR system, ensuring information retrieval is swift and accurate.

• Document management, including faxing, copying, scanning, and filing.

• Responding to Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy (FOIPOP) requests by promptly retrieving the necessary information to facilitate requests.

• Processing incoming and outgoing mail efficiently.

• Responding to general inquiries and routing calls to the appropriate contacts.

• Ensuring discretion when typing a range of documents, including confidential correspondence and reports, and entering client notes into the Integrated Case Management System (ICM).

• Ensuring files and documentation are organized and up-to-date.

• Scheduling meetings and managing calendars to keep operations on track.

Qualifications and Experience
You will have a one (1) year business course plus a minimum of two (2) years of related experience, or an equivalent combination of training and experience.
You thrive in a team-oriented environment, readily stepping in to support colleagues and displaying a proactive approach. You are proficient in Microsoft programs such as Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Excel, or equivalent office software. Your ability to navigate these tools efficiently is crucial to your role. You're comfortable working autonomously in a fast-paced, challenging work environment and manage tasks effectively. Demonstrating a high degree of tact and diplomacy is second nature to you, especially when dealing with sensitive issues. Meticulous organization is your forte and your keen eye for detail ensures nothing slips through the cracks. You demonstrate an ability to build and maintain positive working relationships and collaborate effectively.
While not required, familiarity with the Integrated Case Management (ICM) system would be a valuable asset.
We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Working for the PPS allows individuals to make a direct and meaningful impact on society by upholding the rule of law, protecting the safety and well-being of the community, and ensuring the fair treatment of those accused of prohibited conduct.

As a Medical Laboratory Technologist, your primary duties are in Serology (avian ELISA), Parasitology, Bacteriology and Histology sections.

description:
## Intake Adjudicator

We are currently looking for experienced Intake Adjudicators to work as a critical team member in our Claims Services Department. In this role you will be the expert in determining entitlement to compensation services and benefits. You will be accountable for the review and investigation of complex issues related to adjudication of all medical aid and lost time claims and recurrences.

## Role responsibilities

• Reviewing and investigating complex issues related to adjudication, benefit approval and payment of all lost time, third party, hearing loss, workplace fatality and industrial disease claims.

• Determining the relevancy of each piece of evidence, applying the proper weight to the evidence and determining whether further evidence is necessary.

• Calculating benefit rates for the initial 13 weeks on all new lost time claims. In cases where the payment is greater than 13 weeks, the Intake Adjudicator determines and establishes the long-term earnings base rate.

• Investigating all employer objections and corresponding with all involved parties prior to determining entitlement.

• Providing a detailed written decision, ensuring the worker's privacy is protected.

• Resolving any questions of disputed entitlement.

• Demonstrated decision making responsibilities and abilities, analytical, judgment, problem solving, investigative, research, organizational, interpersonal and communication skills.

title: Senior Engineer, Infrastructure / Mining
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Engineer, Mining / Infrastructure to join our Mines Technical Services team at Creighton Mine in Sudbury. This is a permanent position.

As a Senior Engineer, Mining / Infrastructure, you will work with mine operations and technical disciplines to make sure that our mines have the required infrastructure/mine systems to achieve current and long term mine plans. The successful candidates will be responsible for driving transformation and ensure the mine infrastructure systems are developed and operated in a safe, efficient, and cost-effective manner.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Anticipate and propose solutions to current and potential infrastructure risks.

• Modelling/estimating the capacities of the mine infrastructure systems (dewatering, ventilation, backfill, air/water) and ensure they can meet the forecasted demand of the 3-Year Mine Plan (3YP)

• Integrate recommended infrastructure designs from the Long-Range Planning group

• Identify opportunities to optimize existing mining footprint. i.e. Decommission infrastructure and systems and optimize for Capex and Opex.

• Identify, scope and cost mining infrastructure systems and annual capital development construction to achieve 3YP

• Develop Capex and Opex profile estimates for infrastructure and mine systems expansions projects.

• Coordinate the engineering input, including and not limited to project review for the project tollgate and maturity assessments and ensures follow-up actions are completed.

• Review proposed infrastructure solutions to confirm general conformance with related regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

• Provide feedback on any gaps or opportunities to ensure continuous improvement.

• Safety & Continuous Improvement: Embed safety into all engineering activities in alignment with the MTS Safety Plan, while identifying opportunities to improve safety, productivity, and cost efficiency.

• Infrastructure, Utilities & Water Management: Maintain and update mine level and section prints; manage infrastructure systems (drainage, pumping, backfill, air, LTE) and support the Water Management Program and related investigations.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## About You

## Education:

• Bachelor's degree in appropriate Engineering Discipline (Mechanical, Mining, Electrical).

• P.Eng. designation is required.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 3-5 years of progressive experience with designing and planning sandfill, water, compressed air, mechanical, and/or electrical systems

• Experience working within organizations and influencing stakeholders without direct authority

## Skills:

• A strong understanding of underground mining systems and infrastructure.

• Experience in modelling mining systems (e.g., ventilation, water, power, backfill, etc.).

• Substantial experience working onsite.

• Good communication and organization skills.

• Experience in the following areas is beneficial: Pre-feasibility and feasibility studies

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Our managers are expected to lead beyond their individual departments. Leadership & People Management • Communication & Relationship Management • Decision-Making & Problem Solving • Planning & Strategic Execution • Financial & Resource Management • Cultural Competence & Community Engagement • Adaptability & Continuous Improvement

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. In collaboration with the child's family, the Occupational Therapist will provide support to children and their caregivers to identify functional needs and work toward skill development and greater independence.

Assessment and intervention occur in the child's natural environments which may include home, daycare or school.

## What You'll Do

• Provide safe, best-practice occupational therapy assessment and intervention services to children and youth.

• Collaborate with community teams including nurses, social workers, physicians, school staff, mental health staff and case managers.

• In collaboration with individual communities, help create programs and interventions focused on developmentally appropriate skill development.

• Meet with member communities to identify gaps in services for young children and their families.

• Perform initial assessments and ongoing intervention as indicated.

• Refer to other services or programs as required.

• Maintain ongoing communication with families and community staff.

• Attend case plan meetings at schools or in communities, as needed.

• Daily documentation as per college standards.

• Prepare reports as required.

• Perform any other duties as may be assigned by the NSMTC Management.

## What You Bring

## Education and Professional Certification:

• Master's Degree in Occupational Therapy from a recognized institution.

• Current registration and good standing with the applicable Occupational Therapy regulatory body.

• An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered, provided all professional licensing requirements are met.

## Experience and Clinical Expertise:

• Experience conducting standardized occupational therapy assessments and developing recommendations for school-aged children and youth in areas such as fine motor and visual motor development, self-regulation, sensory processing, self-care, activities of daily living and mobility.

• Experience working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team would be considered an asset.

• Demonstrated ability to communicate clinical findings and recommendations in clear, accessible language.

• Experience working with First Nation communities and/or Indigenous organizations would be considered a strong asset.

## Professional Skills and Competencies:

• Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills.

• Demonstrated commitment to client-centred, culturally responsive and strengths-based approaches to care.

• Cultural humility, respect for Indigenous perspectives and a willingness to engage in continuous learning.

• Ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with children, families, educators, First Nation communities, clinical specialists and other stakeholders.

• Strong advocacy skills to support children, youth and families in accessing appropriate services and resources.

• Sound clinical judgment, critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and work independently.

• Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and community partners.

• Demonstrated professionalism, ethical decision-making and commitment to confidentiality.

• Flexibility and adaptability in responding to diverse client and community needs.

## Additional Requirements:

• Ability and willingness to travel throughout NSMTC member communities.

• Comfortable providing services in rural and community-based settings.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a variety of service delivery environments.

Working at NSMTC
Our employees are expected to contribute beyond their individual roles. They understand how their work supports NSMTC's broader strategic direction, communicate effectively, use good judgment in their day-to-day work, manage their responsibilities reliably, work collaboratively across the organization, and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Above all, we are looking for someone who understands how their work contributes to strong teams, programs, and services for First Nation communities.

Interested in Joining NSMTC?
If you are passionate about directly supporting First Nation communities and are motivated, collaborative, innovative, and possess excellent communication skills, we encourage you to apply for this position.

## What We Offer:

• A work culture that supports employee wellbeing, diversity, engagement, and a sense of belonging.

• Competitive salary, pension, and benefits package, including access to an Employee and Family Assistance Program.

• Collaboration with a team of passionate professionals working towards contributing to the growth and success of First Nations communities.

## Additional Information:

The NSMTC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all interested parties. However, if there are applicants of equal education, skills, and experience, preference may be given to members of our seven member communities.

## Application Deadline:

Please submit your resume and cover letter to Tammy Scott, Human Resources Manager at careers@nsmtc.ca by November 5, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.

We thank those who apply, but only individuals selected for further consideration will be contacted.

Applicants are responsible for the timely submission of applications.

title: Estimating Department Manager
description:
## BUILD YOUR CAREER AT BLACK & MCDONALD

Black & McDonald is an integrated, multi?trade service provider that safely delivers high-quality construction, facilities management, and technical solutions. We are a family-owned and family-run company that employs thousands of highly skilled and talented professionals across North America. With over 100 years of diverse market experience, we are a forward?thinking organization with a strong track record of delivering operational excellence and customer-focused solutions that stand the test of time.

## ABOUT THIS CAREER OPPORTUNITY

Reporting to the Regional Vice President, Maritimes, this role will work closely with an established team of approximately 8-10 estimators to help prioritize opportunities, coordinate bid activity, and bring together complete, competitive, and commercially sound submissions.

This is an opportunity for an experienced construction estimating professional who understands how complex bids come together and is ready to take on broader leadership responsibility within a well-established national organization.

Duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

• Manage a team of Estimators; assigning responsibilities and providing oversight, guidance, mentorship and coaching while generating continuous improvement amongst the team

• Oversee and/or prepare estimates of probable costs of materials, labour and equipment for projects based on contract documents, quotations, drawings and specifications

• Oversee price packages with suppliers, subcontractors, owners, designers and architects regarding tenders as required

• Assess risk on estimates and their order of magnitude to consistently formulate tender costs

• Overall functionality of the department to ensure efficiency and effectiveness

• Develop and maintain resource information on products, vendors, subcontractors, government requirements, etc.

• Develop and manage data/metrics to improve and support a successful estimating process

• Maintain and grow relationships with clients, consultants and subcontractors

• Actively participates in industry, client and community relations to enhance company image

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Lead and coordinate the work of approximately 8-10 estimators

• Support the review and prioritization of tender opportunities

• Coordinate estimating inputs and bring together complete bid submissions

• Review key elements including labour, materials, suppliers, scope, proposals, bid bonds, contractual requirements, project risk, and delivery timelines

• Work closely with the estimating team to ensure bids are complete, accurate, competitive, and commercially sound

• Partner with Operations and regional leadership to support project handover and execution

• Help strengthen estimating processes, communication, workflow, and consistency across the department

• Build collaborative relationships with internal teams, suppliers, subcontractors, consultants, and industry partners

## EDUCATION & SKILL REQUIREMENTS

• Degree in either construction or business management or engineering (Electrical, Mechanical or Civil), or; diploma in trade engineering technology, or; combined equivalent in-trade experience and office experience

• PMP designation, Gold Seal Certification, Construction safety certifications and/or MBA would be considered an asset.

• Experience managing teams

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

• Strong leadership and team management abilities

• Problem-solving and decision-making skills

## WORK EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

• Minimum of 5-10 years' experience in estimating

## SKILLS, ABILITIES, AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS

• In-depth knowledge of estimating platforms such as Accubid, Autobid, bid2win or Excel

• Construction scheduling, planning, and execution

• Understanding of construction documents

• Business operations processes

• Organization and time management

Please be advised that a Criminal Background Check and Professional Reference Check will be required as part of our employment screening and selection process. Additionally, all applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada, unless otherwise stated in the job posting.

Black & McDonald welcomes and encourages applications from persons with accessibility accommodation requirements. Accessibility accommodations are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the recruitment and selection process.

title: Bar Coordinator (Term, Core)
description:
## THE ORGANIZATION:

At Events East Group, we proudly manage and operate the Halifax Convention Centre, Scotiabank Centre and Scotiabank Centre Box Office. Our people and our community make us the favoured event destination for our guests. Whether we're attracting large delegations or hosting an elite group of athletes for an international competition, we are a catalyst for new opportunities and connections between Nova Scotia and the world.

## THE POSITION:

Events East Group is now inviting applications for the position of Bar Coordinator (Term, Core) till November 30,2026 with a possible extension to December 12, 2026 with our Catering team.

Reporting to the Senior Food & Beverage Captain, the Bar Coordinator is a senior team member who supports the coordination and execution of food and beverage services. This role combines hands-on service with an elevated level of operational awareness, helping to ensure consistent, guest-focused service, efficient delivery of operations, and adherence to departmental and regulatory standards. The Bar Coordinator oversees the daily work of developing team members offering guidance and mentorship to ensure work is completed accurately and on time. Flexibility is essential, as shift scheduling is based on events and operational needs.

## THE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

## Operations:

• Support the setup, maintenance, operation, and removal of food and beverage service areas, ensuring cleanliness, organization, and efficient management throughout events to meet service standards.

• Ensure point-of-sale systems are properly set up and ready to support accurate and efficient event service.

• Reinforce service expectations, collaborating with leaders to plan resources and proactively distribute work across the team in an equitable and appropriate way.

• Check work completeness and provide guidance to developing team members, escalating complex issues to the appropriate leader.

• Provide food and beverage service across various formats, including bar service, in accordance with company policies and applicable regulatory requirements, including Nova Scotia liquor control regulations.

• Maintain comprehensive knowledge of food and beverage offerings to support accurate, informed, and positive guest experiences.

• Remain attentive to evolving event needs, ensuring work is completed promptly while considering the broader event environment and sensitivities throughout the venue.

• Provide coverage and coordinate break schedules with support from Catering Captains, adapting to changing operational demands and ensuring uninterrupted service.

• Welcome all guests with an open and friendly demeanor, fostering positive relationships and proactively addressing guest needs to enhance their experience.

• Respond to guest requests with a service-first mindset, acting, as the first point of escalation for guest concerns and ensuring timely resolution or referral to the appropriate leader as appropriate.

• Collaborating with the Catering Captains, support responsible alcohol service by intervening when alcohol service must be denied.

• Collaborate with leadership to ensure all relevant information is available for effective decision-making and successful event delivery.

• Carry out end-of-shift responsibilities to ensure accurate financial reconciliation and effective event closeout.

• Use and maintain equipment and tools safely, adhering to operational standards, reporting any issues or repair needs to the appropriate leader.

• Assist with the safe handling, movement, and organization of food and beverage materials and equipment to support operational efficiency.

• Support inventory management practices by monitoring supplies, maintaining storage standards, and following procedures to ensure product quality and availability.

• Lead by example and promote consistent communication, collaboration, and organizational values within the team.

• Maintain professional conduct, including reliability, readiness to work, and adherence to personal hygiene and grooming standards.

• Perform other duties as required.

## Training & Development:

• Obtain and maintain all certifications required by the organization and applicable regulations to support operational readiness and compliance.

• Engage in continuous learning opportunities to maintain advanced knowledge of service standards, and support ongoing development and adaptability to operational needs.

• Support continuous improvement by adopting new methods, technologies, and practices to enhance operational effectiveness.

• Contribute thoughtfully to team discussions, training opportunities, and departmental initiatives to support a collaborative and effective work environment.

• Support the onboarding of new team members by sharing essential practical knowledge and assisting Catering Captains with initial training.

• Facilitate the development of team members by acting as a mentor, demonstrating service techniques, and offering formal training on operational standards.

## Health & Safety:

• Adhere to all departmental standards, guidelines, and procedures to ensure the safety of oneself, team members, and guests.

• Report safety hazards, near misses, and incidents promptly, taking appropriate action to address hazards when safe, and actively participating in the investigation process.

• Wear, use, and ensure the appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as required, re-porting any violations or damaged PPE within the team or onsite.

## THE PERKS AND BENEFITS:

• Paid vacation time

• Medical and personal days

• Uniforms and PPE provided

• Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) available through Telus Health
• Discounts

• Free counselling services

• Resources available for personal life needs

• Health Plan upon completing the probationary period

• Paid holidays or Holiday Pay for working on the holiday

• Paid bereavement leave

## THE PROFESSIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Education and Experience:

• Must meet the legal age requirement for serving alcohol in the province of Nova Scotia.

• High school diploma or equivalent secondary school is considered an asset.
• Basic math skills required.

• Serve Safe Certification is considered an asset.

• 2+ years in a liquor service position.

• 4+ years of experience in a food and beverage service position.
• POS (Point of Sale) experience is required.

• Demonstrated experience using Microsoft Excel is required.

• Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in written and spoken English.

Events East is committed to a workforce that is free of discrimination, values diversity and is representative, at all job levels, of the people we serve. We encourage applications from qualified African Nova Scotians, racially visible persons, women in non-traditional positions, persons with disabilities, Indigenous persons, and persons from the 2SLGBTQIA+ community. We encourage applicants to self-identify.

During the recruitment process, applicants have the right to request an accommodation. Any applicant invited to participate in testing or an interview and who requires an accommodation should discuss their needs, in confidence, with the Recruiter when selected.

TO APPLY: Apply via Career Beacon.

Please note, this is a bargaining unit position represented by UNIFOR Local 4005. This position is classified as "Bar Coordinator" and is paid as such as per the Collective Agreement. As this is a bargaining unit position, hiring is initially restricted to current employees represented by UNIFOR Local 4005 for at least the first fourteen (14) calendar days after the position is posted. Applications from individuals not represented UNIFOR Local 4005 will be reviewed for consideration after October 26.

APPLICATION DEADLINE: Applications will be reviewed as they are received until the position is filled.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

For further information, please visit our website at www.eventseast.com.

title: Adm Assistant II
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

• Deliver exceptional customer service while responding to inquiries and requests.

• Support a collaborative, professional, and service-oriented office environment.

• Manage competing priorities while ensuring accuracy and attention to detail.

## Experience

• Experience managing front-desk operations and serving as the first point of contact for visitors and stakeholders.

• Experience coordinating meeting rooms, meetings, and office logistics.

• Experience providing administrative support across multiple functions or departments.

• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Proven ability to work independently while maintaining a high level of professionalism and customer service.

## Education

• Post-secondary education in Business Administration, Office Administration, or a related field is preferred.

## Skills & Competencies

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and PowerPoint.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong customer-service mindset with the ability to build positive relationships with visitors, clients, vendors, and employees.

• Exceptional organizational and time-management abilities.

• Ability to multitask and effectively manage competing priorities.

• Professional appearance, demeanor, and interpersonal approach.

• Strong attention to detail and problem-solving capabilities.

• Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Experience within mining, natural resources, industrial, manufacturing, or corporate office environments considered an asset.

• Experience supporting onboarding or employee experience initiatives.

## What We Offer You

About Us
At the Department of Finance and Treasury Board, we provide financial leadership, analysis and policy advice that strengthen Nova Scotia. As stewards of the Province's financial affairs, we support responsible fiscal management through budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and advice to departments and public-sector partners.

If you are a highly analytical financial professional who enjoys interpreting complex agreements, building sophisticated costing models and translating detailed information into clear advice, this opportunity may be for you. This Financial Advisory Services Unit which supports the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is seeking a Labour Relations Financial Advisor to provide specialized analysis on compensation, workforce costs and education-sector funding.

About Our Opportunity
As the Labour Relations Financial Advisor, you provide expert financial analysis and advice on compensation, benefits, pensions, workforce costs and related funding for the education sector. You support the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development, regional education entities, the provincial Francophone school authority, and other publicly funded education organizations.

You develop and maintain integrated labour-cost models, interpret collective agreements and compensation provisions, cost proposed and approved settlements, validate wage and settlement claims, and incorporate compensation and workforce changes into budgets and forecasts. Your work connects agreement language, payroll and FTE data, education funding arrangements, and school-year workforce structures to produce timely, accurate and decision-ready advice.

Primary Accountabilities
As the Labour Relations Financial Advisor, you will:

• Develop detailed financial models and "what-if" scenarios to assess the current and future cost of bargaining proposals, settlements, compensation changes and workforce adjustments across education employers, bargaining units and employee groups.

• Analyze education-specific provisions such as salary schedules, hourly rates, work years, smooth-pay arrangements, substitute costs, paid leave, instructional or preparation time, pensions, benefits, retirement or service awards, and classification grievance outcomes.

• Create and maintain authoritative compensation, benefit, pension, allowance and FTE information using collective agreements, payroll records, submissions from education entities and financial systems.

• Provide confidential, time-sensitive analysis before, during and after collective bargaining, clearly presenting costs, assumptions, risks, options and longer-term impacts to negotiators and senior decisionmakers.

• Review wage and settlement claims in detail, confirm alignment with collective agreements and approved funding, investigate discrepancies, and recommend payments, recoveries or recurring budget-base adjustments.

• Integrate approved and anticipated labour-cost changes into annual budgets and monthly forecasts; monitor expenditures and FTEs; explain material variances; and recommend adjustments to maintain accurate financial plans.

• Prepare briefing materials, estimates support, fiscal-impact assessments, Treasury Board submissions and ad hoc executive analysis related to education-sector compensation and funding.

• Coordinate year-end accounting for assigned portfolios, including accruals, journal entries, recoveries, reconciliations, working papers and responses to audit enquiries.

• Conduct jurisdictional, labour-market and trend research to support assumptions, benchmarking, forecasts and long-term compensation and workforce projections.

• Work closely with education-entity representatives, departmental leaders, Financial Advisory Services colleagues, labour relations and compensation specialists, central agencies, payroll and human resources staff, and auditors while safeguarding sensitive information.

Qualifications and Experience
You have a bachelor's degree in a related field and five years of related experience, or an acceptable equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

You bring demonstrated experience analyzing complex financial, compensation or workforce information and building or modifying detailed financial models. You can interpret contracts, collective agreements, policies or other complex documents; identify financial implications and interdependencies; work with large datasets; and explain your analysis clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

You have advanced Microsoft Excel skills, strong attention to detail, and excellent writing, presentation and problem-solving abilities. You exercise sound professional judgment, protect confidential information, and can manage competing priorities and deliver accurate work under tight and changing deadlines.

While not required, it is considered an asset if you possess:

• A professional accounting designation, or progress toward one.

• Experience in a government, education or broader public-sector environment.

• Experience with collective bargaining, labour-relations costing, compensation analysis or settlement implementation.

• Experience analyzing payroll, salary-grid, pension, benefit, FTE, substitute or workforce-funding information.

• Experience preparing budget, forecast, year-end, audit, Estimates or Treasury Board materials.

• Experience using Microsoft Power BI to analyze data and develop dashboards, reports and visualizations that support financial analysis and decision-making.

• Knowledge of education-sector collective agreements, school-year workforce arrangements or public education funding.

• French-language skills.

We will assess qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following: written examination, standardized testing, oral presentation, interview and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education and experience. Applicants relying on equivalencies must clearly demonstrate them in their application.

Most of your time is spent in a comfortable office setting. Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day. You may be required to work overtime on occasion.

Reporting directly to the Board, the Executive Officer provides leadership in governance, financial management, membership engagement, advocacy, communications, events, and organizational development to ensure the Association delivers exceptional value to its members and advances the residential construction industry. • Recruit, mentor, supervise, and develop staff and contractors while fostering a collaborative, high-performing workplace culture.

• Prepare reports, presentations, recommendations, and correspondence while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality, and member service.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and strategic leader with experience in association management, business administration, nonprofit leadership, or a related field. They possess strong financial acumen, governance knowledge, relationship-building skills, and exceptional communication abilities. Experience working with Boards of Directors, government stakeholders, and member-based organizations is considered an asset.

• Financial planning and fiscal stewardship

• Strategic planning and execution

• Membership engagement and stakeholder relations

• Government relations and advocacy

employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50202

Department: Public Prosecution Service

Location: SHUBENACADIE

Type of Employment: Permanent

Closing Date: 05-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada, the mandate of the PPS is rooted in its commitment to ensuring fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of criminal and provincial offences.
We are looking for the brightest legal minds, who also reflect the rich diversity of our province! We don't just accept difference – we celebrate a supportive culture of diversity and belonging. We strive to create an environment where different perspectives and experiences are welcomed and valued. We encourage applications from those that equally value and champion equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA).

Why Choose Us?
A career with the Public Prosecution Service in Nova Scotia provides a unique opportunity to contribute to justice, public safety, and the overall well-being of the community while working in a professional, inclusive, and ethical environment.
We are a dedicated and passionate team with a determination to make a difference in the society we serve, utilizing our expertise and recognizing and applying an equity and inclusion lens to our work, in our training and development, workplace culture, communications, partnering and engagement to ensure we protect and reflect the communities we live in and serve.

What We Offer
1. Commitment to Justice and Public Interest:
This is achieved by performing prosecution duties with fairness, professionalism, and integrity. Employees actively contribute to upholding the principles of justice in Nova Scotia.
2. Mission and Goals:
Aligning with the Government of Nova Scotia's priority of fulfilling social responsibility for public safety, the PPS' mission and goals include providing excellence in public service, identifying, and managing resources effectively, applying best business practices, and fostering an environment for independent prosecutorial discretion that recognizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in ensuring representation reflective of the community.
3. Core Business Functions:
Employees at the PPS engage in core business functions that play a crucial role in the legal landscape of Nova Scotia. These functions include representing the Crown in criminal and quasi-criminal matters at all levels of court, handling appeals, providing legal advice and assistance to law enforcement, and actively participating in the development of criminal law and prosecutions policy.
4. Professional Development and High Ethical Standards:
The PPS is committed to maintaining a diverse team that reflects excellence, dedication to public service, and high ethical standards. Employees have the opportunity for professional development in a welcoming environment that values continuous improvement and recognizes diversity and inclusion contributes to a healthy and thriving workplace culture that allows team members to be their full selves at work, while upholding the highest ethical principles.
5. Community Engagement:
The PPS is focused on providing a service that is reflective of the community it serves. By fostering diversity and inclusivity, employees contribute to building a legal system that understands and respects the needs and perspectives of the broader community.
6. Impactful Contribution to Society:
Working for the PPS allows individuals to make a direct and meaningful impact on society by upholding the rule of law, protecting the safety and well-being of the community, and ensuring the fair treatment of those accused of prohibited conduct.
For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit the following link: https://novascotia.ca/pps/

About Our Opportunity
These positions are based in Central Region will report to the Chief Crown Attorney, Central Region, to whom the incumbent is accountable for the provision of competent prosecution services. The Crown Attorney will advise law enforcement agencies when requested. Other key responsibilities include conducting the prosecution of charges resulting from matters within the Public Prosecution Service mandate that result from law enforcement agency investigations and other prosecutions and duties as directed by the Chief Crown Attorney, Central Region.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a practicing member of the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society (or eligible to become so) and have a thorough understanding of the prosecution process, and competence in the areas of criminal procedures, evidence, and substantive criminal law. You must have one year experience working as a Crown Attorney or equivalent experience in a similar legal/justice role.
You may be required to travel throughout the province to prosecute cases and may be required to do so for extended periods of time.
Successful applicants may be required to provide a current Certificate of Standing from their law society, including all jurisdictions of which they are members, whether non-practicing or practicing.
The above qualifications will be assessed using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located in Shubenacadie, NS.
Must have access to reliable transportation as travel throughout the region and across the province is required.

description:
## Numéro de concours 49881

Program Admin Officer 3 (Translator)/Agent(e) de gestion de programmes 3 (Traducteur(-trice)), Permanent, HALIFAX

## Affaires acadiennes et Francophonie

Date de clôture : 05-Nov-26 (Les candidatures sont acceptées jusqu'à 23 h 59, heure de l'Atlantique.)

Notre objectif est d'avoir une main-d'œuvre diversifiée représentative de la population que nous servons, et ce, à tous les niveaux d'emploi. Le gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse a adopté une politique d'équité en matière d'emploi, et nous invitons les demandes de personnes autochtones, afro-néo-écossaises et d'autres groupes raciaux visibles, de personnes handicapées, de membres de la communauté 2SLGBTQIA+ et de femmes pour des emplois ou des postes où ces personnes sont sous-représentées. Si vous êtes membre d'un de ces groupes, nous vous encourageons à l'indiquer dans votre formulaire de demande, votre lettre d'accompagnement ou votre curriculum vitæ.
Veuillez noter que pour être prises en considération, les personnes présentant leur candidature doivent être parfaitement bilingues (français et anglais) et doivent soumettre leur lettre d'accompagnement et leur curriculum vitae en français et en anglais.

À notre sujet
L'Office des affaires acadiennes et de la francophonie (l'Office), une division du ministère des Communautés, de la Culture, du Tourisme et du Patrimoine, est l'organisme central de soutien du gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse fournissant aux institutions publiques des outils et des ressources pour la prestation de services en français. L'Office supervise la mise en œuvre de la Loi sur les services en français et de son Règlement.

L'Office entretient des relations avec des partenaires communautaires, gouvernementaux et sectoriels afin de veiller à ce que les priorités de la communauté acadienne et francophone soient prises en compte dans les politiques, les programmes et les services du gouvernement provincial.

L'Office reconnaît également les contributions de la communauté acadienne et francophone et soutient les initiatives de développement communautaire dans de nombreux secteurs.

Au sujet de ce poste
Relevant de la coordonnatrice du Programme de traduction, la personne choisie effectue des traductions et des révisions spécialisées, dans les délais impartis et avec précision, de l'anglais vers le français. Les traductions portent sur des documents, de la correspondance et des ressources complexes et sensibles, couvrant un large éventail de secteurs et de sujets, reflétant ainsi la diversité des mandats des ministères et des services gouvernementaux.

La personne choisie consultera les clients, les conseillera et leur apportera son soutien en ce qui concerne la communication en français et les bonnes pratiques de traduction, tout en veillant au respect de la Loi et du Règlement sur les services en français, ainsi que des politiques, procédures, normes de service et contrôles de qualité établis.

La personne choisie mènera également des recherches et des analyses, interprétera l'information et formulera des recommandations afin de répondre aux besoins des clients en matière de traduction et de communication, notamment par la compréhension de contenus techniques ou spécialisés pour produire des traductions précises.

La personne choisie contribuera à des initiatives visant à améliorer la qualité, l'uniformité et l'accessibilité des services en français et des communications gouvernementales en français. Elle participera également à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre de politiques, de programmes, de normes de service et de contrôles de la qualité en matière de traduction, en vue de renforcer le Programme de traduction et d'appuyer les obligations légales du gouvernement pour la communication et la prestation de services en français.

La personne choisie contribue aux services de traduction et de communication en français lors de situations d'urgence en dehors des heures de bureau habituelles. Cela nécessitera de travailler le soir et la fin de semaine, selon la nature de ces situations d'urgence et le moment où elles surviennent.

Qualités et expérience requises
Vous êtes une personne très motivée et soucieuse du détail, animée par la volonté d'obtenir des résultats de grande qualité et d'aider les clients à communiquer et à fournir des services en français. Vous faites preuve d'une curiosité naturelle et savez saisir les occasions d'apprendre rapidement de nouvelles choses. Vous excellez dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution, où vous savez gérer des priorités et des échéances concurrentes. Vous faites preuve d'initiative et de bon sens, tant lorsque vous travaillez de manière autonome que lorsque vous collaborez avec vos collègues et vos clients.

## De manière plus précise, vous remplissez les exigences suivantes :

• Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire en traduction ou dans une discipline connexe et vous avez au moins cinq (5) ans d'expérience professionnelle dans le domaine de la traduction. Une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience sera prise en considération.

• Vous êtes bilingue (français et anglais), avec un niveau avancé en lecture, en écriture et en communication orale.

• Vous êtes membre agréé d'une association professionnelle canadienne de traducteurs OU vous êtes en voie d'obtenir votre agrément OU vous remplissez les conditions requises pour l'obtenir.

• Vous vous spécialisez dans la traduction de l'anglais vers le français et possédez une expérience avérée dans ce domaine.

## Les éléments suivants sont considérés comme des atouts :

• Expérience dans l'interprétation des exigences légales et réglementaires liées à l'élaboration et à la prestation de services publics, ainsi que dans les conseils en matière de communication dans une langue minoritaire, de préférence le français.

• Expérience dans la direction ou la contribution à l'élaboration de politiques, de procédures, de normes de service et de contrôles de la qualité liés à la traduction de documents et d'information.

• Expérience en matière de conseil sur les moyens de mobiliser les communautés linguistiques minoritaires et de communiquer avec elles, notamment les membres de la communauté acadienne et francophone.

• Compréhension avérée des réalités et de la dynamique de la communauté acadienne et francophone en Nouvelle-Écosse.

•

Les candidatures fondées sur l'équivalence en matière de formation et d'expérience doivent démontrer cette équivalence dans la demande.

Avantages sociaux
Selon le type d'emploi et l'entente avec le syndicat, le gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse offre à son personnel une vaste gamme d'avantages sociaux, tels qu'un régime de retraite à prestations déterminées (en anglais seulement), une assurance des soins de santé, une assurance des soins dentaires, une assurance vie, une assurance maladie générale, des prestations d'invalidité de courte et de longue durée, des vacances et des programmes d'aide aux membres du personnel et à leur famille. Pour plus d'information sur l'ensemble de nos programmes d'avantages sociaux, cliquez ici : Avantages sociaux du personnel du gouvernement (en anglais seulement).

Ce que nous offrons
• Des services de développement de carrière vous donnant accès à des conseils, à des outils, à des ressources et à une formation continue à chacune des étapes de votre carrière.

• Un environnement de travail stimulant. Notre personnel se sent valorisé, respecté, intégré et écouté. Nous mettons en œuvre des politiques et des stratégies avant-gardistes.

• Une multitude de parcours professionnels.

• Un environnement de travail dynamique et axé sur la clientèle, où l'excellence du service et le travail d'équipe sont au cœur de nos préoccupations.

Classification: PR 13
Échelle salariale : 2 805,63 $ - 3 410,48 $ aux deux semaines

Le gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse a mis en place une politique d'équité en matière d'emploi, et nous encourageons les candidatures des personnes autochtones, afro-néo-écossaises, d'ascendance africaine, racisées, en situation de handicap, membres de la communauté 2SLGBTQIA+ et des femmes dans les métiers ou les postes où elles sont sous-représentées. Si vous appartenez à l'un de ces groupes, nous vous encourageons à l'indiquer dans votre demande électronique.

Déclaration relative aux mesures d'adaptation : Nous nous engageons à assurer un processus de recrutement inclusif et accessible. Les personnes qui postulent peuvent demander des mesures d'adaptation pour tout motif protégé par la loi sur les droits de la personne (Human Rights Act). Si vous avez besoin de mesures d'adaptation pendant le processus de recrutement, veuillez nous écrire à competitions@novascotia.ca.

Il s'agit d'un poste relevant d'une unité de négociation, initialement réservé aux fonctionnaires actuels représentés par le syndicat des employés du gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Écosse (NSGEU). Si vous postulez depuis l'extérieur du gouvernement, veuillez cliquer ici.

description:
Crown ProsecutorSpecialized ProsecutionsOffice of the Attorney GeneralDepartment of Justice and Public Safety
Permanent Positions Open Competition Moncton, Saint John and Fredericton

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is dedicated to the rule of law, the promotion of the public interest, and the impartial administration of justice and works to improve the safety, security and resiliency of communities and citizens.

The mandate of the Office of the Attorney General is to promote the impartial administration of justice and ensure the protection of the public interest in New Brunswick on behalf of the Crown. The Office includes the Division of Public Prosecution Services.

The Public Prosecution Services of the Department of Justice and Public Safety, Office of the Attorney General, is seeking individuals to join the Specialized Prosecutions Branch as Crown Prosecutors in Moncton, Saint John and Fredericton, with the potential for flexible work arrangements in accordance with the GNB Remote Work Policy. Please indicate your preferred location. If you are interested in a position in more than one location, please specify the locations of interest in order of preference in your cover letter.

## What you will do

As a member of the Public Prosecutions team, the successful candidate will handle criminal and quasi-criminal prosecutions in all levels of Court for offences under the Criminal Code of Canada, the Youth Criminal Justice Act, Control Drugs and Substance Act, Cannabis Act and Provincial Statutes. The work involves, but is not limited to, providing advice to law enforcement on investigations, advising on the laying of criminal and quasi-criminal charges, pre-trial preparation including interviewing witnesses and researching points of law and appearing before Provincial Court, the Court of King's Bench and the New Brunswick Mental Health Review Board.

Reporting directly to the Director of Specialized Prosecutions, in addition to carrying out the routine duties of a prosecutor, Crown Prosecutors with the Specialized Prosecutions Branch may be assigned to handle files in areas including but not limited to:

• Internet Child Exploitation (ICE)

• Organized Crime

• Indigenous Litigation

• Proceeds of Crime

• Fraud and financial crime

• Conflict of Interest files

• High Risk Offenders

• Coroners Inquests

• Criminal Code offences at all levels of Court

• Regulatory Offences

• Matters before the New Brunswick Mental Health Review Board

Flexible work arrangements in accordance with the GNB Remote Work Policy may be offered

## Who you are

Specialized Crown Prosecutors are part of a dynamic team and a system where the primary goal is to provide a safe and secure community. As a team player, you will possess strong interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to make good decisions under pressure and quickly. You will have strong negotiations and problem-solving skills.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Need to have (essential skills and qualifications)

• Law Degree; completion of Articling

• Membership in good standing or eligibility for membership to the Law Society of New Brunswick.

• Successful candidates will be required to undergo a criminal history clearance and security clearance check.

Lawyer

• Demonstrates basic knowledge and some criminal trial or litigation experience in court.

• Please state your date of admission to a Canadian Law Society.

Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Please state your language capability.

Candidates must demonstrate on their applications how they have acquired the education and experience for this position. Your resumé should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

Operational Requirements: The following operational requirement(s) is also required:

• Significant Travel - The incumbent will be required to cover courts throughout New Brunswick

• Possession of a valid driver's license

## Nice to have (Asset Qualifications):

• Experience in the conduct of jury trials

• A demonstrated interest or experience in ICE prosecutions

• Experience in advising law enforcement with respect to complex investigations

• Knowledge and experience in the area of judicial authorizations

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

Behavioural competencies:

The successful candidate will possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Analytical Thinking

• Flexibility

• Impact and Influence

• Self-Control and Stamina

## Wage

Lawyer from $90,277 - $143,106.86 annually based on admission date to the bar

The recognition and retention premium is based on written confirmation of admission to bar of a Canadian law society

description:
## ## Requisition Details:

Employment Status: Temporary, Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Work Schedule: Days
Anticipated End Date: May 2028
On Call: No
