Nova Scotia wage range available upon request.

## Job Summary:

Reporting to the Director, Talent Acquisition and Organizational Development, the Organizational Development Specialist is a key member of the HR team responsible for designing, developing and facilitating competency and capability training for leaders and staff in support of VON's strategic plan. The Organizational Development Specialist will partner with leaders at all levels to support their teams through development and deployment of programs related to change management, employee engagement, team development, and psychologically healthy organizational culture.

The OD Specialist will create a culture of leadership development through providing advice, coaching, expertise, and hands-on support to management and employees in a broad range of organizational development and design activities. This position will support job and organizational design to advance strategic goals and will recognize and develop the talents within the organization that will enhance the employee experience.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Establish the various components of the Talent Development framework that includes establishing manager/director level accountabilities, competencies, and development.

• Provide leadership and advice in the needs assessments, design and implementation of training and development interventions to ensure that VON management possesses the skills and attributes necessary to lead people and programs.

• Provide assessment, advice, leadership, and management of various learning initiatives to improve organizational effectiveness.

• Provide leadership in the development of a learning organization while making efficient use of the existing assets within VON.

• Facilitate corporate general orientation for all new staff and new leader onboarding program for new leaders.

• Develop programs to ensure VON management engages in a continuous learning cycle beginning with a strong onboarding program.

• Design and support engagement initiatives across the organization, inclusive of engagement survey design and execution.

• Support the Culture and Engagement Advisory Committee to realize their collective vision for VON.

• Manage the performance management and succession planning function of the organization ensuring that a system is in place which recognizes talent and identifies developmental requirements.

• Provide leadership, mentoring and development opportunities for management staff including appropriate cross-training, growth opportunities and initiatives.

• Monitor and stay current in the emerging fields of blended learning, e-learning, performance management and other HR developments.

• Develop, implement, maintain and interpret policies, procedures and programs designed to ensure the effective delivery of organizational development initiatives.

• Assist in the development and achievement of business unit and corporate business objectives through learning and development interventions.

• Incorporate adult learning principles, organizational development principles, instructional systems design principles, and relevant empirical research in the development of curriculum and materials for training delivery.

• Conduct training evaluations to assess knowledge transfer on the job.

• In collaboration with Director, Talent and Organizational Development, initiate, plan, execute, close, and control enterprise-level projects and impact events related to corporate learning and organizational development, specifically employee engagement, leadership development, change management and recognition.

• Determine project scope, resources, risk, quality, cost; Develop requirements' documents; Develop training plans; Define quality gates for each project methodology phase.

• Define critical success factors; Schedule and execute implementation and postimplementation plans.

• Conduct team diagnostics upon request; develop and implement suitable interventions to enhance team functioning and productivity.

• Coach individual leaders to achieve desired competencies and capabilities in alignment with leadership framework.

• Assess departmental, program, and/or organizational readiness for change; develop and execute appropriate change management interventions.

• Support leaders and teams in understanding their employee engagement data and developing and executing action plans to boost or maintain engagement levels.

## Common Responsibilities:

• Promotes the goals and values of VON and their role as an integrated community care provider.

• Promotes a safe and healthy workplace ensuring workplace conduct and activities are in accordance with the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations and compliant with the VON Safety Management System, including all Policies, Safe Work Practices and Procedures.

• Abides by all VON policies and work practices.

• Abides by all confidentiality and protection of personal information policies, regulations and practices and ensures appropriate safeguards are in place within their role.

• Works in collaboration with other staff in a team approach to service delivery.

## External and Internal Relationships:

• Strong collaboration with VON National and Regional leadership teams and Human Resources department.

• Establishes and maintains partnerships with learning vendors (i.e. McLean and Company and Rapid Leaning Institute) and ensures best practices in development and use of all learning materials.

• Establish and maintain open and effective professional relationships with internal stakeholders and external Organizational Development platforms and vendors.

## Education, Designations and Experience:

• Post-Secondary education in Education, Organizational Development, Business

• Administration or related discipline or combination of equivalent employment experience and education.

• Minimum of 7 years of experience in management specific to talent development, learning initiatives, performance management, succession planning, and leadership development.

• Experience in partnering with and influencing senior management to gain support, provide advice and create a learning culture.

• Proven experience leading projects from ideation, delivery and iteration to solve and meet business objectives.

• A Chartered Professional in Human Resources Professional (CPHR) designation would be considered an asset.

• Experience in health care industry is preferred.

## Skill Requirements:

• HR or Business Specialist - Expert in assisting managers be the best leaders they can be. Has strong knowledge/passion for organizational development, preferably in a large, complex organization. Has experience working within a unionized environment.

• Experienced Leader - Demonstrated success in a management role within a complex environment; able to communicate a vision, motivate, and create a collaborative, innovative learning culture.

• Strong coaching skills to both develop existing and emerging leaders

• Strategic thinker – Has the ability to formulate and articulate a plan and translate it into strategies and actions that will enable the organization to achieve its objectives.

• Business leader – Knows how businesses work and the role HR and specifically OD play in helping progressive organizations meet objectives; keeps current of trends and industry developments.

• High level of interpersonal skills to handle sensitive and confidential situations and documentation.

• Ability to prioritize and plan work activities, use time efficiently, manage competing demands and develop realistic action plans.

• Demonstrated accuracy and thoroughness of work to ensure quality.

• Excellent follow-up and relationship building skills.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

## Other:

• A current and original copy of a satisfactory Criminal Records Check.

• A Vulnerable Sector Search and/or Child Abuse Registry Check may be required.

• Ability to speak French is an asset in French Designated areas.

Working conditions and physical demands: This role requires a detail-oriented approach in a dynamic environment, with physical activity including lifting, carrying (using proper techniques), bending, reaching, kneeling, and other movements that emphasize good body mechanics. Individuals in the role are required to walk, sit, stand, and climb stairs throughout the day, with some tasks requiring fine hand movements.

title: Manager Home and Community Care (LPN) - Full-time
description:
## ## Requisition Details:

Employment Status: Regular, Full-time (1.0 FTE)
Program Name: Visiting Nursing
Number of Hours Bi-Weekly: 75
Work Schedule: Days
On Call: Yes
Existing Vacancy: Yes - we're currently hiring candidates for an existing vacancy in this position.

## Job Summary:

The Manager Home and Community Care (HCC) Registered Practical Nurse (RPN)/Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) provides professional and practice leadership to staff and is responsible for ensuring the provision of safe, effective quality client care within their program area. The position is accountable for working as part of an integrated regional management team to ensure the successful execution of site operational goals and for managing the delivery of in-home care services staff hiring, supervision and training, client service programs and team operations.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Directs and monitors delivery of client care services and day to day functions and performance of front-line staff in accordance with current regulatory guidelines and VON policies, procedures and standards.

• Assists staff, or completes risk assessments, investigations of issues, injuries and reporting related to client or employee incidents.

• Monitors performance related to funder expectations regularly and contributes to the development and implementation of quality improvement activities to achieve performance targets through monitoring of reported services.

• Guides new employees through the orientation process and ensures all probationary reviews and stay interviews are completed.

• Applies a working knowledge of the relevant collective agreements and application of local labour rules in daily decision-making activities.

• Participates in budget preparation, financial performance management.

• Completes reports for internal and external stakeholders conducting relevant analysis and ensuring timely submission.

• Completes or contributes to key performance indicators (KPI) and quality reports for internal and external stakeholders, conducting relevant analysis and ensuring timely submission, as required or requested

• In collaboration with internal stakeholders, develops team procedures and guidelines to ensure best practices are met in the completion of all tasks or programs.

• Builds and sustains strategic relationships with current, new and prospective VON partners, and community organizations.

• Receives and documents all employee, family and client complaints or issues related to service delivery; engages other VON managers in resolving the issue or complaint and escalates, if required, to the appropriate Director.

• Participates on the on-call rotation.

• Ensures occupational health and safety policies, programs and activities are performed by staff, in compliance with VON's health and safety policies and guidelines and the Occupational Health and Safety Act.

• Participates in local, regional or national team or committees as required such as Quality Care and Service, Joint Occupational Health and Safety, and Accreditation.

• Assesses and documents community needs and assists in developing business and funding proposals to meet emerging opportunities.

• Provides support for department presentations and reports.

• Completes risk assessments, investigations of issues, incidents or injuries as required.

• Facilitates front line staff development and growth using a team approach and working in concert with the practice leaders, educators, preceptors and clinical experts to facilitate excellent outcomes for quality care delivery, client service and provider safety, and service provider competence. This may include but is not limited to the use of competency assessments, annual performance development plans, individual learning plans, referral to practice educators and on-going mentorship.

• Provides service provider personnel with access to clinical advice, support and clinical reference resources within professional scope and in collaboration with other regulated health professionals.

• Assists with the delivery of in home nursing and home support care services as required and within the professional scope of practice.

## Common Leadership Responsibilities:

• Promotes the strategy of VON and its role as an integrated community care provider to all stakeholders and staff.

• Prioritizes and ensures alignment of emerging opportunities in the community with VON strategic plan.

• Provides leadership in navigating the requirements and complexities of unionized and non- unionized environments.

• Coaches, advises, motivates, and provides leadership to staff; creates a positive workplace for staff.

• Promotes the LEAN team management approach to ensure a common paradigm of management and discipline of management practices.

• Ensures there are mechanisms for all staff to come together to hear of organizational news and to provide feedback on what is working and what is not working.

• Ensures the completion of performance development and learning plans for all staff.

• Promotes common approaches to orientation, learning, motivating, recognizing and supporting staff when achieving organizational goals; such as meeting or exceeding KPIs, meeting or exceeding milestones.

• Provides leadership and commitment to building client and family engagement and following Accreditation Canada Standards.

• Provides leadership in the promotion of a safe and healthy workplace ensuring workplace conduct and activities are in accordance with the provincial Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulations, that KPIs related to safety are regularly reviewed by management, that appropriate investigations occur when needed, and plans to address issues are created and acted upon.

• Compliant with the VON Safety Management System, including all Safe Work Practices and Procedures.

• Promotes work/life balance fostering professional excellence and personal fulfilment and health.

• Promotes the use of technology-based systems for the capture, transformation and distribution of knowledge.

• Abides by all confidentiality and protection of personal information policies, regulations and practices and ensures appropriate safeguards are in place in the Region.

## External and Internal Relationships:

• Regularly liaises/communicates proactively and constructively with various members of the home care and clinical management teams.

• Builds and sustains strategic relationships with current, new and prospective VON partners, and community organizations.

• Develops effective internal relationships across departments to facilitate department objectives and responsibilities.

• Interacts with funder and partner organizations.

## Education, Designations and Experience:

• Post-secondary education in a related field.

• Registered Practical Nurse (RPN) or Licensed Practice Nurse (LPN) with current registration from a provincial regulatory body, without restrictions to practice.

• A minimum of 5 years' experience in health care and a minimum of 2 years' experience managing others in home and community care setting.

• Experience in community work and working with community partners in a collaborative way.

• Experience engaging with municipal, provincial and national external groups in a related field.

• Experience in negotiation, conflict management, financial management and working with staff and volunteers.

• Experience working in a unionized environment is an asset.

• RPN/LPNs actively enrolled in Bachelor of Nursing program is considered an asset.

• Canadian Nurses Association certification or other equivalent nursing leadership program is considered an asset.

## Skill Requirements:

• Excellent critical thinking, assessment and problem-solving skills.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Proficient in using Microsoft Office software, including PowerPoint, Word, Excel, and Outlook.

• Demonstrated ability to effectively structure daily work activities with minimal supervision.

• High level of organizational and interpersonal skills.

• Able to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment while balancing competing priorities.

• Ability to exercise innovation and identifying opportunities by practicing LEAN principles and methodologies.

• Strong public relations and networking skills.

• Demonstrated skillsets in leadership, and team building.

• Ability to accept and facilitate change.

## Other:

• Must have a personal vehicle or access to reliable transportation and possess both a current driver's license and proof of vehicle insurance, if applicable.

• A current and original copy of a satisfactory Criminal Records Check.

• A Vulnerable Sector Search and/or a Child Abuse Registry Check may be required.

• Willingness to travel regularly during the day as well as periodically overnight(s) to support sites and attend meetings.

• Ability to speak French is an asset in French Designated areas.

• Available to work flexible hours.

• Must be able to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

Working conditions and physical demands: This role requires a detail-oriented approach in a dynamic environment, with physical activity including lifting, carrying (using proper techniques), bending, reaching, kneeling, and other movements that emphasize good body mechanics. Individuals in the role are required to walk, sit, stand, and climb stairs throughout the day, with some tasks requiring fine hand movements.

## Job Summary:

Our client is seeking an experienced People and Culture Lead to join their team in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. Reporting to the Senior Operations People and Culture Manager, you will play a key role in leading the local People and Culture team and partnering with managers to foster a positive, inclusive and supportive workplace where people feel valued, empowered and able to perform at their best.

• Support offshore workforce planning, rotation schedules and crewing, keeping operational teams informed of gaps and risks.

• Work with hiring managers on recruitment, adverts and candidate assessment, manage agency and manning office relationships, and support onboarding, talent development and succession planning.

• Maintain local policies in line with global frameworks and local law, with diversity, equity and inclusion built in.

• Bachelor's degree, preferably in Human Resource Management or Business Administration.

• Professional HR qualification (CIPD, CPHR, or equivalent) preferred but not essential.

• Strong leadership and team development skills, with the ability to coach and standardise practice across a team.

• General business understanding and ability to think strategically, translating business objectives into people solutions.

• Proactive, solutions-focused approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

• Confident operating in ambiguous situations, with the judgement to navigate complexity and form clear recommendations.

• Excellent communicator and influencer — able to engage effectively across cultures, functions, and geographies.

• Experience with ESG reporting and local content measurement frameworks

• Strong knowledge of Atlantic Accord legislation and offshore development regulations.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for protecting and managing the forests, fish, and wildlife, and for overseeing the development of mineral resources in New Brunswick. The regional operations are responsible for activities and services associated with the operational delivery of forestry, fish and wildlife, forest fire management, and Crown land programs.

## What you will do:

As a member of the district administrative team, and reporting to the District Forest Ranger, the successful candidate will be responsible for providing overall administrative support to the district office.

## Key responsibilities:

The successful candidate will also be responsible for the following: selling permits; reconciliation of daily sales and vendor sales by outside agencies; providing assistance with monitoring of budget activity; providing administrative support to district resource staff, including typing, filing, composing routine correspondence, formatting and proofreading a variety of documents; providing reception services to the department and public, including answering the telephone, dealing with general inquiries, receiving fire call information and fish and wildlife management information; and performing other related duties as required.

## Who you are:

• You have excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• You excel at providing high-quality client services.

• You are at your best when challenged and thrive on getting results.

• You are recognized for your attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize deliverables.

• You are effective in working independently and collaboratively with colleagues and clients.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following.

## Essential Qualifications:

• High school diploma or equivalent, supplemented by a one-year related post-secondary diploma and a minimum of three (3) years of related work experience, including a minimum of one (1) year of experience providing client service in an office environment.

OR

• A high school diploma or equivalent and a minimum of four (4) years of related work experience, including a minimum of one (1) year of experience providing client service in an office environment.

An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English and French is required. Please state your language capability on your application.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration. Please ensure that preferred language for assessment is identified on your resume. Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

## Asset Qualification(s):

Preference may be given to candidates that demonstrate experience working in a financial environment. Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

Behavioural Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioural competencies:

• Client Service Orientation

• Concern for Order

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Results Orientation

• Teamwork and Cooperation

Technical Competencies: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

• Specialized subject matter expertise and knowledge of office administration and financial processes;

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

The New Brunswick Extra-Mural Program (EMP), often known as the "hospital without walls," has operated under the simple philosophy of helping New Brunswickers receive the care they need in the places where they are healthiest and happiest - their homes and communities. EMP makes a difference in the lives of those it serves by drastically reducing hospital admissions and greatly increasing patient satisfaction with its level of health care.

As part of EMP, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated, multi-disciplinary team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

To holistically coordinate the care of each patient, incorporating the nursing profession's values of knowledge, theory and practice. To assess, plan, implement and evaluate the needs of patients and significant others in the delivery of care and collaborate with all members of the interdisciplinary team in this approach.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Diploma in Nursing or a Bachelor's Degree in Nursing;

• Currently registered and in good standing, or eligible for registration, with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB);

• A minimum of two (2) years in the last five (5) years of specialized registered nursing experience with preference in the areas of family practice, surgical, palliative care or oncology in a patient unit that requires daily collaboration with various health disciplines and family members as part of reaching patient goals;

• A good driving record with a valid New Brunswick Class 5 Driver's License;

• Have a current CPR Level C certification or be prepared to obtain within 3 months;

• Ability to work efficiently as a member of the team and possess leadership and coaching skills, strong interpersonal skills, good judgment and decision making skills;

• Support student placement initiatives;

• Able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• A high regard for confidentiality; and

• Submit a valid and clean criminal record check.

All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Note: For any positions in the St. Stephen EMP unit, a valid Canadian passport or Nexus card will be required.

HOURS OF WORK Rotating days, evenings, nights, weekends, statutory holidays and on-call. Subject to change due to operational requirements.
ANTICIPATED START DATE As soon as possible
ANTICIPATED END DATE October 29, 2027
SALARY RANGE As per collective agreement
LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT Written and spoken competence in English and French is required.
CLOSING DATE November 4, 2026

## JOB SUMMARY

To holistically coordinate the care of each patient, incorporating the nursing profession's values of knowledge, theory, and practice. To assess, plan, implement and evaluate the needs of patients and significant others in the delivery of care and collaborate with all members of the interdisciplinary team in this approach.

The incumbent will be part of the Special Care home (SCH) unit and will provide support to the respective SCH in their regions. The goal of this team will be to ensure enhanced clinical support to the residents in the special care home by acting as a liaison nurse, providing vaccinations on site, coordinating care and performing the following tasks:

• Assessment of each resident in the SCH. During the assessment, staff will complete EMP forms, review the resident's chart, complete required requisition forms, review patient medications and continually re-assess the needs of the client

• Patient Care: provide oversight to ensure updates to the patient Care Plan, as required; teach/educate SCH staff or EMP LPN on individual care; identify gaps and coordinate referrals (to EMP other professionals or foot care, etc; identify extra support that might be required

• Collaboration with the SCH, Social Development and any other organizations as required

• Education: provide education to the resident and their circle of care as required and education to the SCH staff (ex: on Restore2mini, how and when to use it)

• Communication: communication will be a key component as EMP staff will need to communicate with several partners such as the Primary Care provider or Nurse practitioner, the client and their circle of care; the staff at SCH; and external agencies as needed (i.e. contact SD to re-assess a resident if their needs change; refer client to the Mental Health clinic, etc).

• Coordinate vaccination campaigns in the SCH and provide the vaccination to the residents of the SCH

description:
The Team Lead, Proposals & Strategic Opportunities plays a pivotal role in advancing Capstone's growth, strategic positioning, and business development momentum. title: Fleet Manager
description:
## Job Title: Fleet Manager
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia
TP-APA-10282

The Atlantic Pilotage Authority (APA) is a federal Crown corporation responsible for providing safe and efficient marine pilotage services throughout Atlantic Canada. Operating a fleet of pilot boats that support critical marine transportation activities across the region, APA plays an essential role in Canada's marine supply chain. Headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia, APA is committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety, reliability, and operational excellence.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is excited to partner with the Atlantic Pilotage Authority to recruit a Fleet Manager to join their team in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

Role Description
Reporting to the Director of Fleet & Infrastructure, the Fleet Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operational support, maintenance coordination, and technical oversight of APA's fleet assets. Acting as a key point of contact for vessel crews, contractors, and internal stakeholders, the Fleet Manager helps ensure fleet operations remain safe, reliable, and responsive to operational demands.

This is a highly visible and hands-on leadership role that combines technical marine expertise with operational coordination and problem-solving. Serving as the first point of contact for operational and maintenance-related issues, the Fleet Manager provides troubleshooting support, coordinates repairs and resources, and helps resolve challenges across APA's fleet, allowing leadership to focus on longer-term strategic priorities.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Serve as the primary operational contact for vessel crews, providing technical support and troubleshooting assistance.

• Coordinate and oversee fleet maintenance activities to ensure vessel reliability and operational readiness.

• Assess operational issues and coordinate appropriate corrective actions, including contractor engagement and escalation when required.

• Support the planning and execution of vessel dry dock periods, inspections, and repair programs.

• Work closely with vessel crews, contractors, and internal stakeholders to resolve operational and maintenance concerns.

• Build and maintain effective working relationships with contractors, service providers, and external stakeholders to support fleet operations and maintenance activities.

• Communicate and reinforce safe work practices, Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), and operational procedures.

• Monitor fleet performance and identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and reliability.

• Assist with maintenance planning, asset management initiatives, and regulatory compliance requirements.

• Travel throughout Atlantic Canada on a planned basis to support vessel operations and facilities.

• Provide leadership and operational support within a 24/7 marine environment, including occasional after-hours support when required.

Your Qualifications
The ideal candidate is a technically strong marine engineering or marine operations professional with a practical, operations-focused mindset. You enjoy troubleshooting complex issues, coordinating resources, supporting frontline crews, and serving as the go-to person when challenges arise. You thrive in fast-paced environments where technical expertise, sound judgment, and strong communication skills are equally important.

## Your qualifications include:

• Marine engineering certification is preferred; candidates with significant marine industry experience may also be considered.

• Experience supporting vessel operations, maintenance programs, or marine asset management activities.

• Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and resolve technical issues involving marine systems and equipment.

• Knowledge of vessel maintenance practices, regulatory requirements, and marine safety standards.

• Experience coordinating contractors, service providers, and technical projects.

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively with vessel crews, contractors, and operational stakeholders.

• Proven ability to prioritize competing demands and make sound decisions in a fast-paced operational environment.

• Leadership experience gained through operational, supervisory, or project-based responsibilities.

• Willingness to travel throughout Atlantic Canada on a planned basis, typically a few days per month.

• Experience working within a unionized environment is considered an asset.

By joining the Atlantic Pilotage Authority, you will play a critical role in supporting the safe and reliable operation of a fleet that serves ports throughout Atlantic Canada. This is an opportunity to work closely with experienced marine professionals while making a direct impact on operational performance, safety, and service delivery. You will join a respected organization with a strong reputation in the marine industry and a commitment to continuous improvement and employee development.

## APA offers

• A competitive compensation package.

• Annual performance incentive program.

• Defined benefit pension plan.

• Comprehensive benefits.

• Time-in-lieu program to support operational requirements beyond regular working hours.

title: Mechanical Project Coordinator - Commercial Department
description:
## BUILD YOUR CAREER AT BLACK & MCDONALD

Black & McDonald is an integrated, multi-trade service provider that safely delivers high-quality construction, facilities management, and technical solutions. We are a family-owned and family-run company that employs thousands of highly skilled and talented professionals across North America. With over 100 years of diverse market experience, we are a forward?thinking organization with a strong track record of delivering operational excellence and customer-focused solutions that stand the test of time.

## ABOUT THIS CAREER OPPORTUNITY

The Mechanical Project Coordinator plays a key role in the successful delivery of commercial mechanical construction projects across New Brunswick. Working closely with Project Managers, Operations Managers, Site Supervisors, Subcontractors, and Clients, the successful candidate will support project planning, procurement, scheduling, cost control, reporting, and project administration activities from project award through closeout.

This role provides an excellent opportunity for a motivated construction professional to develop project management skills while contributing to the delivery of complex mechanical construction projects within a collaborative and growth-oriented environment.

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Assist Project Managers with planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout of mechanical construction projects

• Promote and comply with all company health, safety, and environmental policies and procedures

• Support project cost tracking, forecasting, and productivity

• Build and maintain positive relationships with customer, supplier/vendor & sub-contractors

• Problem-solving and decision-making skills

2-5 years of experience in mechanical construction, project coordination, estimating, field engineering, or a related construction environment.

• Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines

• Effective verbal and written communication skills

• Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities

• Ability to work collaboratively with Project Managers, field personnel, subcontractors, suppliers, and clients

Experience with the following would be considered an asset:

• JD Edwards or other Oracle-based ERP systems

The starting salary will be determined based on several factors such as the successful candidate's qualifications, including but not limited to education and experience. title: Shared Finance Manager
description:
## About the Opportunity

Valley Region Solid Waste-Resource Management Authority and Tidal Transit Authority are seeking an experienced, strategic, and collaborative Shared Finance Manager.

This joint management appointment offers a unique opportunity to lead financial stewardship, internal controls, and long-term fiscal sustainability across two vital public authorities serving the Western Region of Nova Scotia. Splitting time equally between both organizations, you will serve as a key member of each management team, reporting directly to each General Manager and providing strategic financial advice to senior leadership and the Valley Regional Services Board.

Whether you are guiding capital budgets, modernizing financial software systems, or collaborating with municipal partners, this role allows you to make a direct, positive impact on environmental sustainability and accessible regional transit.

## Key Responsibilities

• Financial Reporting & Governance: Direct the preparation of monthly, annual, and recurring financial statements, cash flow forecasts, variance analyses, and statutory reports (including Service Nova Scotia and Municipal Relations). Coordinate annual external audits and liaise with independent auditors.

• Standards & Legislation: Thorough familiarity with Public Sector Accounting Board (PSAB) standards, provincial municipal regulations, and Nova Scotia's Municipal Government Act (MGA) and Authority By-Laws.

• Software & Systems: Considerable experience with computerized financial applications, enterprise accounting software, and office automation tools.

• Licensing & Travel: Valid Nova Scotia Driver's License and willingness to travel between sites across the region.

• Flexibility: Willingness and ability to work flexible hours when necessary to meet board schedules or budget deadlines

## Standout Assets

• A recognized professional accounting designation (CPA) in good standing.

• Demonstrated experience with shared service agreements or dual-reporting organizational models.

• Direct experience presenting financial packages to municipal councils, boards, or commissions.

## What We Offer

• Competitive Compensation: $95,000 - $123,000 annually, commensurate with qualifications and experience.

• Retirement Security: Enrolment in the municipal pension program with an 8% employer match.

• Health & Wellness: Comprehensive group health, dental, vision, life, and travel coverage (60% Employer / 40% Employee cost-shared).

The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible system of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Family Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court and Bankruptcy Court. As Site Manager, Sheriff Services, you are accountable for the efficient and effective delivery of Sheriff Services by managing and directing operational resources, monitoring performance, and developing Deputy Sheriff staff at justice centers throughout the province. You are responsible for one justice center, court facility or operations center. You perform all management functions related to the bargaining unit staff at that site, such as performance appraisals, discipline, scheduling and allocation of resources, budget management, risk management and communications. In addition, you provide support to all levels of court relating to the Sheriff Services mandate, court security, prisoner transportation and document service. The Site Manager, described as a 'sheriff's officer', is included in Section 2 of the Criminal Code of Canada under the definition of a peace officer; therefore, is entitled to exercise the authority of a peace officer in Canada.

Primary Accountabilities
• Delivers an efficient and effective service to client stakeholder groups by directing and coordinating all courthouse/facility security, prisoner transportation, prisoner management, jury management and civil enforcement/document service activities at a designated worksite(s). This includes interpreting court orders properly and acting on the orders as required.

• Responsible for the operational maintenance and financial management of a large fleet of Sheriff Services vehicles.

• Accountable for local resource planning and delivery, and staff scheduling to ensure the overall strategic goals of Sheriff Services are met by ensuring tactical plans are implemented and monitored, interpreting court orders and documents accurately, and taking remedial action where necessary.

title: Vice-President, Finance
description:
## Vice-President, Finance

Oceanex is seeking an experienced finance executive to join its Executive Leadership Team as Vice-President, Finance.

This is an opportunity to play a central role in the financial stewardship of a critical supply-chain link for Newfoundland and Labrador during a period of significant investment and growth.

Located in St. John's, NL and reporting to the Executive Vice-President, the Vice-President, Finance provides strategic financial leadership across an integrated transportation business that includes marine transportation, trucking, terminal operations and logistics services, and is directly accountable for the finance, accounting, taxation, customer pricing and procurement functions.

Working closely with the Executive team, shareholders and the Board of Directors, the successful candidate will help guide major capital investments, fleet renewal initiatives, financing strategies and corporate growth opportunities.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

• Shape and execute Oceanex's long-term financial strategy, annual budget, rolling forecasts and key performance indicators as a member of the Executive team.

• Lead the Company's finance organization, including accounting, taxation, customer pricing and procurement teams in St. John's and Montréal, and develop high-performing professionals.

• Provide financial leadership for fleet renewal and major capital investments and evaluate acquisition and organic growth opportunities.

• Lead relationships with commercial lenders and financial partners and develop funding strategies and negotiate financing arrangements.

• Own the customer pricing strategy and the procurement strategy and governance framework to optimize revenue, protect margins and control costs.

• Ensure the integrity of financial reporting (ASPE/IFRS), internal controls, tax and pension compliance, and the external audit.

• Present financial results, budgets, forecasts and capital proposals to the Board of Directors.

• Contribute to enterprise risk management and drive continuous improvement across finance systems and processes.

## Qualifications

• Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing.

• Minimum of 15 years of progressive accounting or finance experience, including at least five years in an executive role (Director level or above).

• Demonstrated treasury, banking and financing experience, including negotiation of credit facilities.

• Experience preparing and presenting financial results, budgets and strategic plans to a Board of Directors or equivalent governance body.

• Expert knowledge of Canadian accounting standards (ASPE/IFRS), Canadian tax legislation, internal controls and audit processes.

• Strong knowledge of cost accounting and its application to pricing, margin analysis and operational efficiency.

• Strong working knowledge of ERP systems, financial planning and analysis tools, and business intelligence platforms.

• Professional proficiency in English.

## Assets

• Industry experience in transportation and logistics (strong asset); experience in marine, infrastructure, industrial or manufacturing sectors is also an asset.

• Experience in capital-intensive industries, including fleet or major capital project financing.

• Bilingual proficiency in English and French (strong asset).

## Skills

• Strong strategic and commercial judgment.

• Demonstrated leadership of multi-disciplinary finance teams across multiple locations.

• Excellent verbal communication and relationship-building skills as well as written communication skills.

• Ability to influence across all levels of an organization.

• Strong commercial and business acumen with the ability to link financial performance to operational drivers.

You are interested and believe you have the skills we are looking for? Please forward your resume and cover letter as soon as possible to:

## www.oceanex.com/hr

Oceanex Inc. is committed to equity in employment and encourages all qualified individuals to apply. We thank all candidates for their interest but wish to advise that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. No telephone inquiries please.

OCEANEX INC. is Atlantic Canada's leader in intermodal transportation and has serviced the Newfoundland market for more than 100 years. We provide door-to-door transportation service from anywhere in North America to destinations in Newfoundland and Labrador.

We offer our employees a positive work environment, competitive salaries, and excellent benefits as well as an entrepreneurial environment with solid career progression based on a result driven culture. When you are a member of the Oceanex team, you enjoy a stable career where your ideas are encouraged, and skills valued.

We are very proud of our strong team of 400 employees and their exceptional commitment to safety, the environment, and our customers.

description:

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Advisor - Workforce Deployment strengthens workforce readiness and operational effectiveness across both preparedness and response. The role advances workforce planning, capability development, training, tools, processes, and continuous improvement during non-response periods, while providing strategic guidance and supporting the timely deployment of personnel during active operations. Working collaboratively with operational leaders and stakeholders, the Senior Advisor translates workforce needs, data, and lessons learned into practical solutions that improve deployment outcomes, service continuity, and the organization's ability to meet community needs.

## In this role you will:

• Lead the timely deployment of personnel across teams and locations, aligning workforce capacity with changing operational needs and resolving resource constraints in dynamic environments.

• Serve as a trusted advisor and Workforce Deployment subject matter expert, providing strategic guidance and actionable recommendations that strengthen operational practices, service integration, and organizational readiness

• Partner with operational leaders and stakeholders to identify workforce and service delivery needs, align priorities, and develop practical solutions that improve readiness, deployment outcomes, and community impact.

• Strengthen operational accountability through workforce planning and reporting, budget oversight, risk identification, and compliance with organizational policies and applicable regulations.

• Build workforce capability by providing technical guidance, learning support, coaching, and mentorship, and by supporting orientations, training, exercises, and after-action reviews.

• Translate lessons learned, emerging practices, and workforce data into recommendations and improvements that strengthen preparedness, service delivery, and performance against objectives.

• Lead or contribute to projects, service improvements, and change initiatives that modernize workforce deployment practices, strengthen systems and processes, and support adoption of new tools and ways of working.

• Develop and continuously improve workforce planning tools, operational resources, and knowledge-sharing practices that support informed decision-making and service continuity.

• Champion culturally safe, equitable, accessible, and inclusive workforce planning and deployment practices that respond to the diverse needs of the communities we serve.

## What we are looking for :

• Qualifications include a minimum of 6-9 years' experience and a 3-year college diploma or university degree in social sciences, community development, Indigenous studies, public administration or a related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience. May require a graduate diploma/degree in a related field and/or a professional degree, certification, or designation.

• Ability to articulate complex processes, standards, and practices to non-technical audiences.

• Experience working with diverse communities, including Indigenous, rural, and underserved populations.

• Fluency in English and French is required.

• Occasional requirement for prolonged sitting with infrequent breaks in order to perform the requirements of the role.

• Occasional requirement for prolonged standing with infrequent breaks in order to perform the requirements of the role.

title: Distribution Manager
description:
## Job Title: Distribution Manager
Location: Debert, Nova Scotia
TP - HSC - 10255

Meridia Recruitment is proud to partner with Halifax Seed in the search for a Distribution Manager to lead its Debert distribution operations and play a key role in supporting customers across Atlantic Canada and beyond.

Founded in 1866, Halifax Seed is Canada's oldest family-owned seed company. For 160 years, the organization has served home gardeners, market farmers, landscapers, greenhouse growers, retailers, and commercial customers with high-quality seeds, growing supplies, and horticultural products. Through its retail locations, commercial operations, and distribution network, Halifax Seed supports customers across every Canadian province and territory.

As Halifax Seed continues to invest in systems, operational excellence, and continuous improvement, they are seeking a hands-on, data-driven leader to oversee their Debert distribution centre. This is an opportunity to join a well-established and respected Atlantic Canadian organization where you'll play a direct role in driving fulfillment performance, supporting customer satisfaction, and helping ensure the products customers depend on arrive where they need to be, when they need them.

Role Description
Reporting to the Chief Procurement Officer, the Distribution Manager is responsible for leading fulfillment and distribution activities at Halifax Seed's Debert facility while supporting the broader distribution network.

Leading a small team of warehouse employees, you will oversee customer order fulfillment, warehouse operations, safety compliance, and facility-related activities while ensuring exceptional service across a diverse B2B distribution environment. Leveraging ERP systems, operational reporting, and performance metrics, you will translate data into actionable plans that drive efficiency, improve service levels, and support continuous improvement initiatives.

The successful candidate is a hands-on leader who thrives in a fast-paced, seasonal environment and enjoys balancing operational planning with day-to-day execution.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Lead daily distribution and fulfillment operations to ensure timely and accurate order processing and shipment coordination.

• Oversee the execution of customer orders across multiple business segments while maintaining high service standards and operational efficiency.

• Monitor key performance indicators such as order volumes, lines shipped, backlog levels, fulfillment throughput, and service performance, leveraging operational data and reporting to identify issues, develop action plans, and drive continuous improvement.

• Provide leadership, coaching, and direction to warehouse employees while fostering accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

• Prioritize workloads and allocate resources effectively to meet changing customer demands throughout seasonal fluctuations.

• Champion continuous improvement initiatives across distribution, fulfillment, inventory, and warehouse processes.

• Maintain strong visibility on the warehouse floor and provide hands-on support when operational demands require it.

• Utilize ERP systems, reporting tools, and Excel to support operational planning, forecasting, and decision-making.

• Ensure compliance with safety regulations, company policies, and best practices.

• Oversee facility-related activities including contractor coordination, maintenance planning, and building improvement projects.

• Identify operational risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement before they impact business performance.

• Collaborate with internal teams to deliver an exceptional customer experience and ensure successful execution across multiple product segments.

Your Qualifications:
The ideal candidate is a proactive and analytical operations leader who combines strong business acumen with a hands-on leadership style. You are comfortable working with data, systems, and operational reporting while remaining highly engaged with your team and day-to-day warehouse activities.

## Your qualifications will include:

• 5+ years of leadership experience within distribution, wholesale distribution, logistics, fulfillment, or a related operational environment.

• Experience leading and developing employees within a warehouse or distribution setting.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze operational data and translate findings into practical business solutions and operational plans.

• Strong ERP system experience and proficiency with reporting and performance measurement tools.

• Strong Microsoft Excel skills and strong overall systems aptitude.

• Experience managing fulfillment operations, workflow planning, and service-level performance.

• Strong knowledge of workplace safety practices and compliance requirements.

• Customer-focused mindset with a strong understanding of fulfillment performance and service delivery.

• Proven ability to prioritize competing demands and perform effectively in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

• Valid driver's licence.

## Assets include:

• Experience within wholesale distribution, supply chain, logistics, or multi-channel fulfillment environments.

• Experience managing seasonal operations with fluctuating demand volumes.

• Experience with inventory management, inventory control, or cycle-count programs.

• Exposure to facility management, contractor coordination, or building maintenance responsibilities.

• Experience with continuous improvement initiatives and process optimization.

• Knowledge of Syspro ERP or similar enterprise systems.

• Experience developing operational reporting, dashboards, or KPI-driven performance management processes.

Why Join Halifax Seed?
This is an excellent opportunity to join a respected Atlantic Canadian organization where you can make a direct impact on operational performance, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement initiatives.

title: Senior Consultant, Public Affairs (Bilingual)
description:
## ABOUT THE JOB

At CCGoodwin Consulting, we are part management consultancy, part agency. We work strategically with our clients, digging deep into their objectives, pain points and opportunities to design solutions that help them win. Our wheelhouse is in the creation and delivery of marketing communications programs, plans, campaigns and tools, from soup to nuts. We also deliver projects in strategic planning, sustainability, governance, organizational development and change management. In all that we do, we are evidence-based, market-focused, creative and measurement-driven. Our team is composed of hand-picked, top talent. With our distributed and flexible model, we work remotely, but collaborate virtually and in person on a day-to-day basis.

Named by Atlantic Business Magazine as one of Atlantic Canada's Best Places to Work four years in a row, we intentionally keep our operations lean to prioritize investment in our people, nurturing culture, growth and professional development. "Do Good & Be Great" is our purpose, and it's what drives us to continuously improve and contribute to the communities we love. We are a values-driven team, with a focus on building community over competition, empowering people to be great leaders both within and outside the organization, and leading our work with empathy and inclusion.

Since founding the firm in 2019, we have continuously grown the business and client base within Canada. To support our growth, we're looking to hire a Senior Consultant, Public Affairs (Bilingual). This is a remote, permanent full-time role based in Moncton, Fredericton or Saint John, New Brunswick. For the right candidate, we are open to other remote work locations in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia or Prince Edward Island. Travel within the Maritimes is required from time to time, in support of client meetings and team events designed to support culture.

## ROLE SUMMARY

We're on the hunt for a bilingual public affairs practitioner (English and French) who will help manage and deliver client projects, including communications and engagement plans, strategic plans, policy papers, government relations materials and other complex deliverables, working directly with our team, roster of talent and clients. You have a passion for public affairs, you are an exceptional writer in both English and French, and you are resourceful - talents you will bring to bear in all your deliverables. You will help develop fresh, impactful ideas and products, manage schedules and budgets, and write and assemble materials that achieve results. In all the work you do, you will be encouraged to think creatively and be supported by a team of practitioners who have your back.

This role will report to the Director, Public Affairs, as part of our growing Communications & Engagement team.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

## Strategy Development

• Develop - and help others develop - strategic solutions that enable clients to achieve measurable business outcomes. This could include, but is not limited to, organizational communications strategies, project-specific communications and engagement strategies, government relations strategies, strategic plans, governance deliverables, complex policy papers, research reports, issues and crisis management plans, and detailed implementation plans.

## Storytelling, Writing & Editing

• Through crisp, compelling writing, create and help package materials that achieve specific objectives. This could include, but is not limited to, briefing notes, annual reports, website and social media content, video scripts, news releases, key messages, Q&A documents, presentations, facilitator guides and other materials designed for a range of audiences.

• Work with specialists, including in-house and freelance graphic designers, web developers, photographers, videographers, researchers and others to help bring content to life.

• Edit and proof the work of others, contributing to quality delivery and alignment with Canadian Press (CP) Style guidelines.

## Research & Consultation

• Conduct and synthesize secondary research to inform client strategies and decision-making, including materials reviews, jurisdictional and comparator research, environmental scans, stakeholder interviews and surveys.

• Help conduct primary research, including planning and facilitating stakeholder interviews, workshops, focus groups, consultation sessions and simple surveys, and synthesize findings into clear insights and recommendations.

## Project Management & Logistics

• Lead the successful delivery of client projects by managing project plans, schedules, budgets, resources and cross-functional teams to ensure work is delivered on time, on budget and to the highest standard.

• Communicate effectively - in writing, verbally and via Teams and other tools - with project teams and clients.

## Business Development & Culture Contribution

• Help write - and generally support the development of - proposals designed to win new business.

• Contribute to the firm's vision and business plans, and help build a culture of learning, excellence, client-centricity, inclusive leadership and fun.

## QUALIFICATIONS

• Post-secondary education or training with specialization in communications, public relations, journalism, political science or a similar discipline

• Minimum of 7 years' experience working in a fast-paced communications and/or professional services environment, or equivalent, undertaking significant strategic and tactical responsibilities

• Knowledge and experience across a range of communications and public affairs activities, including traditional and social media, stakeholder consultation, and issues and reputation management

• Experience working collaboratively with a range of specialists, including graphic designers, web developers, event planners, researchers and others, to bring communications programs and materials to life

• Exceptional critical thinking, written and verbal communication skills

• Excellent secondary research skills, including experience with the ethical use of AI

• Excellent attention to detail, project management and organizational skills

• Highly proficient in all MS Office programs (including Teams), Generative AI tools and general fluency/comfort with technology

• Fluency in both English and French (written and oral)

• Must have a valid driver's licence

• Assets: general familiarity with the workings of the public service; professional services and/or agency experience; familiarity with design tools (e.g., Canva), SaaS-based project management tools (e.g., Asana) and time-tracking tools

## This role is for you if you are:

• Strategic, analytical and naturally curious

• Comfortable balancing client service and collaboration with hands-on work

• Highly organized and able to manage multiple priorities

• A collaborative team player who enjoys solving problems

• A detail-oriented self-starter committed to delivering high-quality work

• Motivated by continuous learning

• Adaptable and energized by a fast-paced consulting environment

• Able to seek and provide constructive feedback in a clear and kind way

• Energetic and fun-loving, but serious about the work

## BENEFITS & COMPENSATION

The hiring salary range is $80,000 to $90,000, pending experience. The top end of the salary range is $105,000. Benefits include an incentive program (up to 10% of salary), four weeks' vacation and other PTO, health and dental benefits (50% covered by the firm), GRRSP matched at 5% of salary, professional development, a biennial tech subsidy of $1,500, a monthly equipment allowance, flexibility and other fun perks. Our team works from home and connects in person a few times per year at beautifully curated events within the Maritimes, fully paid for by the firm.

Aligned with our values of creating a diverse and inclusive work environment, we welcome and strongly encourage individuals from communities that have experienced, and continue to experience, structural inequities to apply. Our firm adheres to the ISO 26000 guidelines for social responsibility, and we are taking steps to understand and apply the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada's Call to Action #92 (Business and Reconciliation).

## HOW TO APPLY

To apply, please submit your cover letter and resume to hr@ccgoodwin.ca by 5 pm AT on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. Applications received on LinkedIn and Indeed will not be assessed. Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

For more information about our firm, please explore our website or find us on LinkedIn or Facebook.

Due to the nature of the duties associated with this position, including responsibilities involving female persons in custody, being female is a bona fide occupational requirement of the position. Therefore, only applicants who meet this requirement will be considered.

About Us
The Correctional Services division of the Department of Justice is responsible for the administration and operation of community and custody-based programs and services for adults and young persons. Within the Correctional Services core business area there are two programs: community corrections & correctional facilities. Each of these program areas is broken down into closely related activities that have a specific impact on the program's target group.
Community Corrections has 22 offices across the province from Yarmouth to Sydney and is responsible for the supervision of both adult and young persons serving community-based sentences. The sentences include probation, conditional sentence, custody and supervision, conditional supervision and Intensive Rehabilitative Custody and Supervision. Probation officers also supervise those released from custody on conditional releases and prepare pre-sentence investigations to assist the Courts in the sentencing process. Evidence based Program facilitation and supports to specialized courts in areas of domestic violence, mental health and wellness are also part of the role of a Probation Officer as well as Restorative Justice casework and collaboration with community justice agencies.
Four (4) adult correctional facilities and one (1) youth centre provide the safety and security of person in custody while providing programs that address dynamic criminogenic factors to assist with their successful, reintegration back into the community.
Nova Scotia Correctional Services utilizes an evidence-based approach in both Community Corrections and custodial facilities. Core Correctional Practices (CCP) is the foundational practice that drives reintegration and rehabilitation practices deployed within Correctional Services. Utilizing CCP, Correctional Services staff can effectively interact, manage behavior, and help facilitate change, within target populations.
For more information on the Department of Justice Correctional Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Corrections/

About Our Opportunity
As the Captain, you are responsible for supervising Correctional Workers/Officer and ensuring the custody, care and control of individuals in custody. Your responsibilities include regular security and maintenance inspections of the facility to ensure that proper cleanliness and security standards are being maintained. The incumbent is responsible for the development and evaluation of subordinate staff. This includes implementing necessary correction and developmental action, attendance management, shift scheduling, participation in the recruitment process and correctional programming. As the Captain you will conduct special projects, investigations and fine calculations, working regularly with Correctional Services policies and procedures, standing orders, and directives.

Primary Accountabilities
• Maintain the administration and operation of a provincial correctional facility including the safety of individuals in custody, staff and the public

• Maintain the daily facility schedule and ensure these are delivered consistent with schedules (i.e. cleaning, group program activities, etc.)

• Manages the admission and discharge of individuals in custody ensuring the validity of warrants produced

• Ensures the effective management of human and financial resources

• Assigns and delegates work assignments, workloads and directives as well as participates in the recruitment, selection, placement and retention of staff

• Chair of the Unit Review Boards for transfers of individuals in custody in accordance with the Corrections Act and Policy and Procedures

• Investigate and gather information linked to disciplinary levels for the Provincial Adjudicator

• Participate in the Institutional Review Board for participation of individuals in custody in programs and Temporary Leaves of Absence in the community

• Supervises the operation of mechanical and electrical systems

Qualifications and Experience
You will have a High school diploma, completion of a Correctional Officer certificate program and several years of experience as a Correctional Officer or Corrections Youth Worker. You will have previous supervisory experience and a university degree from a recognized institution. An acceptable equivalent combination of education, training and experience in other areas of Corrections, Criminal Justice, Policing, or Court Services may be considered. Experience keyboarding and working in a computerized environment would be an asset.
During the interview, you as the successful candidate will demonstrate knowledge and understanding of currently accepted correctional strategies and philosophies all in the aspects of correctional facility operations. You understand custody management, crisis management and prevention, safety and security, administrative routines and allocation of human and material resources. You as the incumbent will also have effective communication and interpersonal skills with strong leadership abilities to support the development of rapport with institutional staff and individuals in custody. Sound decision-making and problem-solving abilities are also a requirement.
You as the successful candidate will demonstrate an attitude towards individuals in custody and the criminal justice system that is compatible with the objectives the Department of Justice, the Correctional Services Division and the goals of the Correctional Facility.
The Government of Nova Scotia has adopted the LEADS Leadership Framework. During the interview, candidates will be expected to express how they have demonstrated the key behaviours and capabilities required to effectively lead in a caring and inclusive environment. description:
Position Type:
Permanent
*

2026-11-10

Medavie Health Services New Brunswick (MHSNB) is the subsidiary of Medavie Health Services responsible for the optimal operation and management of EM/ANB, an integrated organization specializing in the delivery of primary health care services with the goal of facilitating access to quality care so that patients can achieve better health outcomes. MHSNB is fortunate to be able to count on the expertise of its employees who work passionately to build a healthier province.

Our company is currently looking for new team members to support its mission of providing excellence in emergency and community care within our various programs, namely Ambulance New Brunswick, the Extra-Mural Program and NB Health Link. Each advocates for a highly coordinated, quality service offering guided by a goal of continuous improvement across primary health care.

Medavie Health Services is part of Medavie, a health services organization. Together with Medavie Blue Cross, we are committed to providing innovative solutions that will improve the health of all Canadians.

As a not-for-profit organization, Medavie is proud to commit an annual social dividend to the Medavie Health Foundation to support programs and initiatives aimed at addressing some of our country's most pressing physical and mental health care challenges.

We are looking for a Coordinator, Clinical Education, to help support our growing operation which provides exemplary, highly coordinated primary health care in the right place, from the right provider, at the right time.

The Coordinator, Clinical Education maintains and continually updates the design, development and implementation of the Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) program focusing particularly on the areas of clinical excellence and patient and community satisfaction; participates in internal clinical investigations; develops and undertakes reviews and audits to ensure policies, procedures and standards are adhered to; undertakes research and collaborates with internal and external colleagues to make recommendations to Operations.

The Coordinator, Clinical Education is crucial to the development and maintenance of a systematic clinical care review program. It includes the responsibility of conducting random and targeted audits to assess compliance with approved patient care guidelines, documentation standards and service performance targets to identify deficiencies, anomalies, risks and gaps; and to identify, and recommend, corrective action that could be at the individual (e.g. training interventions) or system (e.g. policy changes) levels.

As employees of MHSNB, we are accountable to our patients and co-workers by participating in and supporting all safety related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

## Roles and Responsibilities:

• Design and implement education around clinical service delivery and patient care equipment aspects of paramedic services;

• Train and assign Field Training Paramedics and monitor performance based on contract agreement;

• Complete PCP and/or ACP audits, field assessments, as well as feedback to employees. Ongoing assessment of service rendered against established procedures, protocols and standards to identify areas of deficiency and non-compliance. Using these findings, make recommendations for emerging training needs for ACPs and PCPs.

• Provide input on new employee/probationary evaluations, recommend extensions or remediation, and ensure issues/concerns are addressed.

• Undertake research and work collaboratively with ANB Operations, the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) and provincial paramedic organizations to identify, recommend and assess clinical and professional standards and protocols appropriate to New Brunswick;

• Complete scheduled and ad hoc reports as required;

• Assist in identifying professional development priorities and/or prepare and deliver presentations as a result of trends identified during audits or investigations;

• Identify, recommend, and support the development of new employee orientations, procedures and policies;

• Gather, and analyze clinical and operational data and statistics

• Audit and review for compliance policies and procedures

• Collaborate on investigations of clinical complaints, occurrences and incidents; and submit reports to Quality and Risk and ANB Operations

• Represent the TQA department on committees, public events and task forces etc.;

• Participate in the provincial monthly reconciliation of controlled pharmaceuticals as required;

• Travel within New Brunswick may be required

Qualifications & Requirements

Education/Experience:

• Post-secondary education, plus successful completion of an approved Primary Care Paramedic or Advanced Care Paramedic program;

• Registered with PANB as a Primary Care Paramedic or Advanced Care Paramedic-(Asset).

• Proven experience with adult learning concepts and facilitation is an asset.

• Minimum five years of paramedic field experience, Experience in quality assurance/improvement-(Asset)

## Knowledge/Skills :

• Ability to analyze data from a variety of sources;

• Innovative and creative in developing quality assurance and improvement programs;

• Work with a variety of software applications to support data collection, analysis and presentation;

• Written and verbal communication skills, including presentation skills;

• Project management skills; (asset)

• Able to work as part of a team;

• Minimum two years experience leading development initiatives, projects or teams would be considered an asset.

• Bilingualism is an asset.

The Base Pay range may vary depending on the successful candidate or other relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience and education/training. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Medavie employees may participate in various performance-based incentive programs. Payments under these programs are discretionary and subject to both individual and organizational results.

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

Information Access & Privacy (IAP) Services is an integrated unit that provides access and privacy services to government departments. In addition to providing client departments with operational advice and guidance on access and privacy issues, the Unit also promotes a culture that supports openness and transparency.

About Our Opportunity
As the IAP Administrator, you are responsible for the administration of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy (FOIPOP) Act process, as well as other information access and privacy (IAP) processes, for the assigned client department(s).

Primary Accountabilities
Specifically, you'll manage the processes as outlined in the Act, will make recommendations on FOIPOP applications and will represent the client department(s) on requests for reviews of departmental decisions by the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner (OIPC) of Nova Scotia. You are also responsible for managing requests under departmental Routine Access policies, as well as facilitating pro-active disclosure where appropriate.

You will provide operational advice and guidance, including training and education, to client departments in matters regarding access and privacy and also promote a culture that supports openness and transparency. As a member of a corporate team, you contribute to the overall operations of the Unit and will keep abreast of current trends in other jurisdictions. Awareness of privacy processes, for example management of privacy breaches or complaints, is also needed in this position. You will require an ability to research, analyze and synthesize the NS Information and Privacy Commissioner's recommendations, those of Commissioners in other jurisdictions, as well as orders and decisions of the Courts on matters related to access and privacy.

You must be able to build relationships with applicants and staff in client departments, as well as negotiate, mediate, and resolve conflicts.
