title: Access Support Worker (Counsellor 2(A))
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50289

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: TRURO

Type of Employment: Temporary

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 04-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
Access Support Workers help children and youth maintain safe contact with parents, family members, and other important people in their lives. The role includes transportation, supervised family access, support during appointments, observation, documentation, and communication with social workers.

This role is not just about driving clients to visits. You will work directly with children, youth, parents, and caregivers, sometimes during emotional, tense, or unpredictable situations. You may need to explain expectations, coach parent-child interactions, set clear limits, redirect behaviour, and intervene when safety or appropriate conduct becomes a concern.

You will often work independently. Success requires calm, professional communication, careful observation, sound judgement, appropriate boundaries, and the ability to follow established procedures while responding to the situation in front of you.

Primary Accountabilities
In this role, you will:

• Transport children, youth, and family members to and from family access visits, appointments, and other approved activities.

• Support the safety and wellbeing of children and youth while they are in your care.

• Supervise family interactions and remain attentive to verbal, non-verbal, and environmental cues.

• Support and coach appropriate parent-child interactions.

• Model respectful behaviour and communication.

• Set clear, professional boundaries and firmer limits when required.

• Recognize when a situation is escalating and intervene when necessary to address safety or inappropriate behaviour in accordance with established procedures.

• Seek direction or escalate concerns to the social worker, supervisor, or Manager.

• Observe and document observations with social workers to support case planning.

• Maintain transportation and mileage records.

• Participate in supervision, staff meetings, case conferences, and required training.

• Maintain confidential and sensitive client and case information.

• Attend Family Court and provide evidence about your recorded observations when requested.

Qualifications and Experience
You have completed an approved child and youth care worker diploma from a provincially approved post-secondary institution, or you have at least two years of related experience supporting children, youth, and/or families. Equivalent combinations of education, training and experience will be considered.

You must have a valid class 5 driver's licence, the ability to travel, and access to a reliable, properly insured personal vehicle suitable for transporting infants and children.

Experience in child welfare or other social services, including daycare or youth services, is desirable.

You demonstrate the ability to:

• Communicate clearly and respectfully with children, youth, parents, caregivers, social workers, and service providers, including when conversations are sensitive or emotionally charged.

• Use sound judgement, remain calm in challenging situations and de-escalate challenging and complex situations.

• Build supportive relationships while maintaining professional boundaries, setting clear expectations and limits when needed.

• Listen actively and manage conflict constructively, balancing the needs of children and youth with safety, service expectations, and the circumstances of the family.

• Observe and document interactions to support case planning.

• Work independently and adapt to changing circumstances, while staying connected with supervisors, social workers, and colleagues.

• Work respectfully with diverse families, recognizing that communication styles, experiences, cultures, and family dynamics may differ.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• a completed diploma or bachelor's degree in a related field such as early childhood education, social sciences, social work, child and youth studies, human services, or disability support services.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Hours of work are between 8:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. across a seven-day operation. Assignments may include weekdays, evenings, and weekends, and start and end times may vary.

You will spend a considerable amount of time driving your personal vehicle. Travel may occur in changing or adverse weather.

Work may take place in client homes, offices, vehicles, parks, playgrounds, and other community locations. You may work with children, youth, parents, or caregivers who are distressed or behaving in a challenging manner.

The role requires sustained attention while driving and while supervising family interactions. Some visits may be emotionally difficult, and you may hear about or witness circumstances involving trauma.

Physical activities may include lifting young children or car seats, carrying children's belongings, using stairs, and walking for extended periods in community settings. You may also encounter common environmental or communicable concerns associated with work in private homes and community settings.

About Us
The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court and Bankruptcy Court. As a Justice Officer, you will provide a broad range of administrative support, as well as being the first point of contact for the public and clients of the Court system. You will receive and balance monies paid into the court and enter and retrieve data from automated systems. You will also record and process documentation, adhere to policies and processes and maintain filing systems—all while working as a team player.
In the role of Justice Officer, you may be required to attend Court to call cases and swear or affirm witnesses, interpreters, and translators. The incumbent will also perform quasi-judicial duties as a Staff Justice of the Peace as assigned and appointed under the Justice of the Peace Act.

You'll have the opportunity to work with a diverse group of students across various grade levels, requiring flexibility in meeting the needs of individual learners, along with practical knowledge of elementary, junior, and high school curricula.

Joining Wood Street's Interdisciplinary Team means working collaboratively to provide diagnostic, assessment, and treatment services, as well as programming for children with complex emotional and/or behavioural needs. title: Solutions Architect
description:
Position Type:
Permanent

If you're looking for a fulfilling career that can make a real difference in your life, and the lives of others, you've come to the right place.

As a national health solutions partner, we put people first in everything we do - and that begins with our team of 8,000+ professionals who bring a cross-section of diverse life experiences and career expertise to Medavie. By collaborating and innovating together, our employees are creating industry-leading solutions in insurance, primary care and emergency medical services that impact millions of lives in Canada each year.

Our mission is to improve the wellbeing of Canadians so that every life can be lived to the fullest - and it's reflected in our award-winning culture. We celebrate individuality and value the diverse perspectives and skills our employees contribute. We go beyond providing competitive pay and comprehensive benefits to offer opportunities for personal and professional growth, flexible work options, meaningful experiences, and supportive leadership. Medavie is where employees can be their best selves, feel they belong, and achieve their full potential. Be part of it by applying for a position with us today.

## Job Summary

The Solution Architect, Clinical Technologies is the primary solution architecture and design authority for technology solutions supporting the Medavie Clinic Division.

The role translates clinical, business, operational, security, privacy, and regulatory requirements into secure, reliable, scalable, and supportable technology solutions that align with enterprise standards and strategic objectives. The Solution Architect leads requirements analysis, solution evaluation, architecture development, technical design, implementation planning, and operational readiness activities across clinic technologies.

Working within a federated delivery model, the position is accountable for the overall solution design and integration of technologies supporting clinic operations, while partnering with Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Privacy, Infrastructure, Identity, Networking, Service Delivery, and other specialist teams who retain ownership of their respective standards, governance processes, and operational services.

The Solution Architect develops and maintains architecture deliverables including current-state and target-state architectures, transition roadmaps, architecture decision records, solution designs, implementation standards, and supporting documentation. The role ensures traceability from business and clinical requirements through design, testing, governance review, implementation, operational acceptance, and lifecycle management.

Architecturally significant solutions are coordinated through appropriate enterprise governance processes including Enterprise Architecture, Technology Review Board (TRB), Cyber Security, Privacy, and operational review forums. The Solution Architect is responsible for incorporating approved recommendations, standards, controls, and required exceptions into solution designs.

This is a highly hands-on architecture role that combines broad technical knowledge with practical implementation experience. While not expected to be the deepest technical specialist in every domain, the architect must possess sufficient breadth, judgment, and leadership to design integrated solutions, coordinate specialist resources, and ensure solutions are secure, supportable, and operationally ready.

## Key Responsibilities

## Solution Architecture and Technical Design

• Lead requirements clarification, options analysis, and the development of current-state, target-state, and transition architectures for clinic technology solutions.

• Engage clinicians, clinic operators, business leaders, IT teams, and vendors to define functional requirements, non-functional requirements, integration requirements, dependencies, operational constraints, and support expectations.

• Produce architecture views, technical designs, architecture decision records, implementation diagrams, and supporting documentation that clearly document options, trade-offs, assumptions, risks, costs, and recommendations.

• Design integrated solutions spanning cloud services, infrastructure, networks, security, identity, endpoint management, business applications, clinical applications, databases, websites, and vendor-hosted platforms in alignment with clinic objectives and enterprise standards.

• Apply approved enterprise architecture principles, security controls, privacy requirements, and reusable technology patterns while identifying and documenting required exceptions.

• Coordinate solution reviews with Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Privacy, Infrastructure, and other governance bodies, incorporating required controls and recommendations into the final design.

• Maintain traceability from business and clinical requirements through design, testing, operational readiness, implementation, and support transition activities.

## Technical Implementation, Testing and Troubleshooting

• Perform hands-on configuration, deployment, integration, testing, validation, cutover, stabilization, and troubleshooting for clinic technology solutions.

• Lead or support implementations for new clinics, acquisitions, migrations, upgrades, technology replacements, and patient-facing services.

• Validate performance, availability, resiliency, backup, recovery, monitoring, security, privacy, remote access, and operational support requirements.

• Coordinate vendors and internal teams during implementation while resolving technical dependencies and escalations.

• Participate in major incident response, problem management, root-cause analysis, and complex troubleshooting when architecture or specialized solution knowledge is required.

## Technical Standards, Documentation and Operational Transition

• Develop and maintain reusable clinic technology standards and patterns, including standard clinic network designs, new-clinic blueprints, acquisition integration patterns, remote-access architecture, endpoint standards, and EMR or patient-application integration patterns.

• Produce complete and current architecture records, configuration documentation, inventories, support procedures, runbooks, recovery procedures, and knowledge articles.

• Define operational readiness and support acceptance criteria before production transition.

• Provide knowledge transfer and practical training to downstream service desk, infrastructure, network, endpoint, application, and clinic support teams.

• Transition stabilized solutions to the appropriate operational owner with documented responsibilities, escalation paths, and support dependencies.

## Business, Clinical and Enterprise Collaboration

• Act as the primary solution architecture resource for Clinical Technologies while working within enterprise technology, security, privacy, and service-management governance.

• Translate clinic workflows and business objectives into practical technology design without losing operational or clinical context.

• Understand how clinic solutions integrate with ERP, HRMS, finance, identity, data, ITSM, and other enterprise platforms.

• Participate in technology and vendor selection and, where appropriate, lead implementation within the clinic division.

• Communicate recommendations, risks, decisions, status, and technical concepts clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

## Lifecycle Management, Governance and Continuous Improvement

• Maintain solution roadmaps and lifecycle plans covering capacity, currency, support status, technical debt, security, availability, continuity, and eventual replacement.

• Ensure implementations follow ITSM practices, ITIL change control, configuration management, release planning, and formal production change processes.

• Identify opportunities to standardize, simplify, automate, consolidate, and improve the reliability and supportability of clinic technologies.

• Support acquisition due diligence, integration planning, clinic onboarding, business continuity planning, and technology risk assessment.

• Evaluate emerging technologies and proof-of-concept opportunities where they address a defined clinic or business need.

## Innovation

• Identify opportunities to standardize clinic technology and create repeatable designs for new clinics, acquisitions, integrations, and remote access.

• Evaluate cloud, automation, security, patient-facing, clinical, and infrastructure technologies against defined business and clinical needs.

• Develop proofs of concept where required to validate feasibility, usability, integration, supportability, security, and cost.

• Recommend modernization opportunities that reduce technical debt, improve resiliency, strengthen security and privacy, simplify support, or improve clinical operations.

• Improve documentation, implementation, transition, and training practices based on lessons learned and operational feedback.

## Working Conditions

• Primarily remote or office-based work with extensive computer and collaboration requirements.

• Requires sustained concentration, independent judgment, and coordination across concurrent operational and project priorities.

• Occasional after-hours work may be required for implementations, maintenance, clinic cutovers, major incidents, or recovery activities.

• Minor national travel to clinic locations, corporate offices, data centres, or vendor sites may be required.

• Occasional physical activity may be required to inspect, install, connect, or troubleshoot technology and network equipment.

## Required Qualifications:

Experience: Minimum 5 years of relevant IT experience, including experience designing and implementing integrated technology solutions. Demonstrated hands-on experience with configuration, deployment, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, and transition to support.

Education: Post-secondary diploma or degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

## Other Qualifications:

• Demonstrated ability to design, document, and implement technology solutions spanning multiple domains including infrastructure, cloud services, networking, identity and access management, business applications, clinical applications, endpoint management, and cybersecurity.

• Strong understanding of architecture principles, solution design methodologies, systems integration, technology lifecycle management, operational readiness, and service transition.

• Ability to evaluate business, clinical, operational, security, privacy, supportability, and cost considerations when developing solution recommendations.

• Experience producing architecture documentation, technical standards, implementation plans, diagrams, decision records, operational procedures, and support documentation.

• Working knowledge of cloud and on-premises environments, network architecture, server infrastructure, endpoint management, application integrations, databases, websites, and IT service management practices.

• Understanding of security-by-design principles, privacy requirements, business continuity, disaster recovery, data residency considerations, and vendor risk management.

• Strong analytical, communication, facilitation, documentation, stakeholder engagement, and training skills.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with Enterprise Architecture, Cyber Security, Infrastructure, Privacy, Service Delivery, vendors, and business stakeholders.

• Demonstrated ability to lead complex technology initiatives from requirements gathering through implementation, operational transition, and lifecycle management.

• Experience with clinical technologies, EMRs, patient-facing applications, healthcare integrations, clinic websites, or multi-site healthcare environments is an asset.

• Lead, mentor, and guide less experienced team member in best practices

## What we're looking for:

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to write for a technical audience

• Robust analytical and problem-solving skills

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and consistently produce results within timelines

• Ability to develop and maintain positive working relationships team members and others

• A highly motivated and dynamic professional

• A problem-solving mindset and ability to translate business requirements into secure and scalable code

• A friendly willingness to collaborate and play nice with others

• Someone with a love for project-based work and staying on top of your technical game

• Open-minded and willing to adapt to existing development standards and structure

• Ability to work independently in a rapidly evolving environment

Language Skills: Fully bilingual (French/English): English proficiency is required to perform the duties of the role, which include daily collaboration with teams and partners outside Québec who operate primarily in English.

Security Clearance Requirement: In conjunction with our contract with the Federal Government, you will be required to have Reliability Status Clearance (Enhanced Level B). This includes Fingerprinting, Criminal Record Check, Credit Check and you must have resided in Canada for at least 5 years and hold Permanent Resident or Citizenship Status.

## What's in it for you?

What makes us a different kind of employer? Our award-winning culture, a team who really cares, unmatched training and support are all dedicated to ensuring you are set up for success.

title: Senior Medical Laboratory Technologist
description:
## Senior Medical Laboratory Technologist (MLT)

MedNexus Health - Private Integrated Health Clinic
Moncton, New Brunswick
Part-Time or Full-Time | Permanent

Join MedNexus Health and bring your laboratory experience to a collaborative team helping shape our multidisciplinary health clinic and diagnostic laboratory.

## Position Overview

MedNexus Health Laboratory is looking for an experienced Medical Laboratory Technologist (MLT) to join our growing team in a part-time or full-time, permanent senior role. This role offers the opportunity to combine hands-on testing with technical problem-solving and quality improvement, while contributing your ideas as our laboratory continues to develop and grow.

As a Senior MLT, you will perform day-to-day laboratory work while supporting the team with workflow coordination, equipment performance, and quality control. You will collaborate closely with the Clinic & Lab Manager and laboratory colleagues and will receive support in carrying out your technical and quality-management responsibilities. You will be supported by an experienced team and external laboratory advisors who are available to provide one-on-one guidance as our services continue to grow. Our collaborative environment will give you opportunities to share your expertise, develop your skills, and help shape a high-quality laboratory service.

## Key Responsibilities

## Laboratory Operations & Workflow

• Perform routine and specialized laboratory testing, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and timely results.

• Coordinate daily laboratory workflow, identify challenges, and recommend improvements.

• Support the implementation of new testing, instrumentation, and diagnostic services.

• Collaborate with laboratory and clinical staff to ensure quality patient care.

## Quality Control, Calibration & Equipment Management

• Lead equipment calibration activities, including scheduling, performance, verification, and documentation.

• Perform, review, and approve quality control (QC) results in accordance with established procedures.

• Investigate QC failures, troubleshoot equipment issues, and implement corrective actions.

• Perform routine equipment maintenance and participate in method verification and equipment validation.

• Escalate significant or unresolved technical concerns to the Clinic/Lab Manager.

## Quality Assurance, Policies & Compliance

• Support the laboratory's Quality Management System and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Provide technical input into laboratory policies, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and work instructions.

• Maintain accurate QC, calibration, maintenance, and testing records.

• Participate in quality assurance activities, audits, and accreditation preparation.

• Ensure compliance with applicable laboratory safety and regulatory standards.

## Inventory & Supply Management

• Monitor inventory, reagent levels, expiration dates, and supply requirements.

• Provide input into purchasing and ordering decisions based on laboratory needs.

• Identify opportunities to reduce waste, manage costs, and improve inventory efficiency.

## Technical Support & Collaboration

• Provide technical guidance and support to laboratory colleagues.

• Assist with orientation and technical training of new laboratory personnel.

• Collaborate with the Clinic & Lab Manager to improve laboratory operations and maintain high quality standards.

• Promote teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

## Experience & Education

• Graduate of an accredited Medical Laboratory Technology program.

• Must be registered and in good standing with the New Brunswick Society of Medical Laboratory Technologists (NBSMLT).

• Minimum of three (3) years of experience as a Medical Laboratory Technologist.

• Experience in hematology and clinical chemistry is considered a strong asset.

• Demonstrated experience with laboratory equipment calibration, maintenance, troubleshooting, and quality control evaluation.

• Experience in supporting reviewing QC trends, investigating failures, and documenting corrective actions is highly desirable.

• Familiarity with laboratory quality management systems, SOPs, and regulatory requirements.

• Experience with Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), and Microsoft Office is considered an asset.

• Experience with inventory management and laboratory supply coordination is considered an asset.

## Qualifications

• An experienced Medical Laboratory Technologist who brings care, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to their work.

• Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

• Experience in quality control principles, laboratory calibration, and equipment performance.

• Ability to organize daily workflow, prioritize competing demands, and adapt to changing laboratory needs.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, particularly regarding documentation and quality assurance.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to work independently, collaborate with colleagues and management, and seek guidance when needed.

• Comfortable taking initiative and contributing ideas in a developing laboratory environment.

• Adaptable, resourceful, and committed to continuous learning and process improvement.

• Strong commitment to patient safety, accuracy, confidentiality, and quality laboratory services.

• Proficiency in English is essential due to operational requirements.

## Schedule & Location

• Flexible part-time or full-time hours are available. The schedule is generally Monday to Friday, with occasional evening shifts as required. No statutory holiday shifts are required.

• The schedule will be determined in collaboration with the employer, taking operational requirements into consideration.

• The successful applicant will work primarily in person in Moncton, New Brunswick, with some flexibility for occasional remote work to support the team's needs.

## Why You Should Join Our Team

• Be part of a growing laboratory and multidisciplinary clinic where your experience, ideas, and contributions are valued.

• Help shape laboratory services in collaboration with the Clinic & Lab Manager and laboratory team.

• Work in a supportive, collaborative environment alongside a multidisciplinary healthcare team.

• Enjoy a schedule with no statutory holiday shifts.

• Receive health and dental benefits and participate in an RRSP program.

If you are passionate about hands-on laboratory work, enjoy sharing your knowledge, and want to contribute to high-quality patient care, we encourage you to apply. We welcome candidates who bring diverse strengths and experience, a willingness to learn, and a desire to make a meaningful contribution to our team.

## Compensation

We offer a competitive compensation package within the range of $41.26-$51.42 per hour. Placement within the range will be determined based on the successful candidate's experience, qualifications, and relevant skills.

Anticipated Start Date: To be discussed with the successful candidate.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Reports to: Josée Levesque, Clinic & Laboratory Manager

At the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (EECD),
we are dedicated to fulfilling New Brunswick`s educational mission.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

## What you will do:

Reporting to the Director, Assessment and Analysis Services, the Research and Insights Advisor supports evidence-informed decision-making across EECD by leading the development, coordination, and delivery of research, analytics, and insight-generating activities. The role oversees the intake, prioritization, design, and execution of research and analytical projects aligned with departmental priorities, including the EECD Education Plan and other strategic initiatives. title: Electrical Maintenance Planner
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking an Electrical Maintenance Planner to join our Utilities Maintenance Integrated Planning Team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

The role is a permanent on-site position, working a 2 weeks on, 2 weeks off rotational schedule.

As an Electrical Maintenance Planner, you will be responsible providing comprehensive planning and scheduling support to the Maintenance Teams at the Voisey's Bay Operations while working collaboratively with operations and other departments to ensure optimal utilization of labour, materials, and equipment. This position develops detailed maintenance and construction plans for electrical infrastructure across the site. Your experience and skills will play a key part in supporting both short?term and long?term maintenance strategies and contribute to the overall reliability and performance of assets.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Ensure that all work packages are in accordance with established safety policies and procedures and adhere to all Vale quality control standards where required.

• Track work package estimates against actual values with respect to resources, materials, and cost for continuous improvement purposes and ensure that all costs are allocated properly.

• Continuously improve material selection, work practices, and planning processes through effective use of established procedures to improve the efficiency and quality of planned work packages.

• Provide guidance and instruction as appropriate when working with the Material Coordinators to requisition parts, follow-up with procurement, and prepare job kits for planned jobs.

• Attend and contribute to the weekly business routines defined within the planning and scheduling work management process which would include the weekly pre-scheduled meeting as well as the 7-21 work order form log priority setting meetings.

• Contribute to Maintenance Shutdown planning strategies identifying and prioritizing future maintenance requirements, tracking the project and cost controls, and working with operations, engineering, maintenance and outside contractors to ensure successful and safe execution.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Education:

• An Interprovincial Red Seal in Industrial Electrician or Instrumentation & Control Technician is preferred.

• A college diploma in Industrial Electrician, Instrumentation & Control Technician, or another applicable post secondary education with an electrical focus is required.

## Experience:

• Minimum of 5 years of work experience in Maintenance Planning, Maintenance Supervision, and/or a closely related discipline in a heavy industrial or mining environment.

• Previous experience coordinating major maintenance activities or shutdowns would be considered an asset.

• Previous experience with project controls, tracking, costing, budgeting, etc. would be considered an asset.

• Familiarity with Voisey's Bay Operations or similar concentrator facilities would be an asset.

## Skills:

• Proficient in SAP, MS office, and Power BI.

• A strong understanding of RCAs and of industrial electrical systems, including low? and medium?voltage distribution, protection systems, motors, drives, and control circuits.

• Analytical, problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.

• Flexible and adaptable, able to respond to changing roles and environment in a positive and constructive manner while managing multiple priorities.

• Able to build and maintain strong positive relationships across multiple work groups.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

title: Sr Manager, Enterprise Architecture
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is growing?

## Who We Are

We are a global mining company dedicated to safely delivering nickel, copper, cobalt, and platinum group metals essential for the world's energy transition.

Our mission is to improve lives and shape a better future together.

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Enterprise Architecture, to join our Information Technology organization, based in Toronto/Sudbury, ON.

This is a permanent, hybrid position, operating in a complex, global, and industrial environment, where enterprise IT, operational technology (OT), and industrial systems must work seamlessly together.

This role is execution-focused and works directly with operational sites, capital projects, and delivery teams. It is not a strategy-only or purely governance role—you will shape and deliver practical, resilient, and fit-for-purpose architectures that support how work truly happens across our business.

You will report to the Head – Governance and Architecture and act as a key technology partner to business leaders, engineering teams, cybersecurity, data & analytics, and operational stakeholders across the organization.

## About You

You are a senior, hands-on architecture leader with deep experience in industrial or asset?intensive environments. You understand how enterprise platforms, industrial systems, and operational technologies intersect, and you are comfortable navigating complexity, safety-critical operations, and global delivery models.

You bring strong systems thinking, practical problem-solving skills, and the ability to influence outcomes without direct authority. You are respected for your ability to translate business and operational needs into architectures that are realistic, secure, and scalable.

## In This Role, You Will:

## Enterprise & Business Process Architecture

• Own and evolve end?to?end business process architectures aligned with the company's operating model

• Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and risks across processes that span corporate IT and operational environments

• Ensure architecture reflects real site conditions, safety constraints, and regulatory requirements

## IT, OT & Industrial Systems Architecture

• Design how enterprise IT systems (ERP, EAM, Finance, HR), OT systems (SCADA, DCS, PLCs), and industrial applications (MES, historians, LIMS) work together

• Define pragmatic integration patterns, reference architectures, and interaction models

• Ensure secure, reliable data flows from field systems to enterprise analytics and decision platforms

## Site & Capital Project Engagement

• Engage directly with mine sites, processing facilities, and operational teams

• Embed within capital projects and modernization initiatives to influence design decisions early

• Support OT modernization and brownfield integration while minimizing operational disruption

## Architecture Delivery & Enablement

• Produce practical architectural deliverables (system diagrams, integration designs, reference implementations)

• Work closely with cybersecurity, data & analytics, automation, and ERP teams to co-design solutions

• Support delivery teams throughout build, testing, commissioning, and transition to operations

## Risk, Safety & Operational Resilience

• Incorporate safety, cybersecurity, and regulatory considerations into architecture designs

• Support segmentation, redundancy, fail-safe designs, and operational resilience across IT/OT boundaries

## Continuous Improvement & Standardization

• Identify recurring challenges and establish repeatable architectural patterns

• Capture lessons learned from incidents and projects to continuously improve designs

• Influence solution selection and procurement decisions aligned with target-state architecture.

## Experience & Education:

• 11–15 years of progressive experience in enterprise, solution, or systems architecture

• Significant experience in industrial, mining, manufacturing, utilities, or other asset?intensive environments

• Proven experience designing and integrating IT, OT, and industrial systems

• Experience working across global, distributed, and site-based teams

• Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

• College Diploma considered with equivalent experience

## Skills:

• Strong understanding of enterprise platforms (ERP, EAM, finance, supply chain, HR)

• Working knowledge of OT systems (SCADA, DCS, PLCs) and industrial applications

• Experience with IT/OT integration, industrial networking, data architectures, and cybersecurity principles

• Ability to think end?to?end across business processes, systems, and data

• Comfortable creating detailed architectural documentation and working hands?on with engineers and vendors

• Strong stakeholder engagement and influence skills

• Pragmatic, execution-oriented, and outcomes-focused mindset

• Strong safety awareness and disciplined approach to risk management

## What We Offer You:

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## Why Toronto

Toronto, Canada's largest city and financial hub, is a center of innovation, commerce, and culture. Known for its diverse economy and vibrant urban environment, Toronto offers unparalleled access to talent, technology, and global connectivity.

Our Toronto office serves as a strategic hub for corporate functions, technology development, and business operations. Here, we drive initiatives that support Vale Base Metals' global operations, leveraging advanced analytics, digital transformation, and strategic planning to ensure operational excellence across all regions.

Toronto's dynamic ecosystem enables collaboration with leading technology partners, universities, and research institutions, fostering innovation in mining and metals processing. This location is integral to shaping the future of sustainable mining and advancing our commitment to responsible resource development.

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are needed for the green economy. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. Vale encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all.

We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: GRF

About Our Opportunity
As a Family Support Worker, you will provide support to the children, youth and families connected to the Child and Family Wellbeing program. You will have an in-depth involvement and will play an active role in working with children, youth and families to build resilience and inspire change. While working collaboratively with the social worker, you will develop and deliver a plan to provide service, education, support and advocacy to the families, children & youth in care.

If you are looking for an opportunity to make positive impacts on the lives of children and families, establish positive connections and build everlasting relationships within your community, we welcome you to apply!

Primary Accountabilities
As an integral part of the Child and Family Wellbeing program, some of your key responsibilities include:

• Developing strategies and providing knowledge, tools and guidance to families and youth to support independent living and meeting their physical/emotional, social and learning needs.

• Building positive relationships with diverse clients (families, children & youth), ensuring respect, empathy and an understanding of the impact of their trauma.

• Advocating for clients and helping them connect to community supports and resources.

• Assisting with income and social supports, affordable housing and life skills.

• Making independent visits to clients in their homes/communities and attending court sessions.

• Comprehensive and timely evaluation of ongoing services to clients with an intent to find solutions and improve services.

Qualifications and Experience
You have an approved Child & Youth Care Worker diploma from a provincially approved post-secondary institution. An undergraduate degree in Social Sciences is considered an asset.

You are compassionate, empathetic and resilient with a focus on inclusivity and understanding the needs of diverse clients. You must demonstrate:

• Knowledge of child development, family dynamics and community resources along with an understanding of physical, psychological, and emotional needs of children and youth in a family setting as well as in care.

• Knowledge of financial management and healthy child development & life skills

• Understanding and experience with working towards the objectives of the established case plans.

• Ability to work independently and in a team environment, to strengthen and improve the support provided to children and families.

• Ability to work collaboratively and build relationships & networks with diverse individuals, groups and communities.

• Effective interactive communication skills (written and verbal) to engage collaborations and navigate diverse client environments with tact and empathy.

• Ability to adapt to the changing/unpredictable client circumstances, exercise timely judgement and make decisions to provide a culturally responsive service to clients.

• Knowledge of various software packages, such as Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams).

Following are the assets for this role:

• previous experience in child welfare or other social services,

• experience with the department case management systems (ICM/CCM)

Scripting and automation experience (e.g., PowerShell, Python) to streamline operational tasks and reporting.

• Knowledge and understanding of networking and protocols.

• Working knowledge of IAM concepts including identity lifecycle, least privilege, rolebased access control (RBAC), and segregation of duties.

• Experience with Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), including users, groups, and access assignments.

• Experience working in a ticketing/ITSM environment, including following change control and documenting work performed.

• You must be a strong team player with excellent interpersonal skills, a strong computer aptitude and the ability to deal with multiple tasks and demands. Leadership skills, self-motivation and demonstrated ability to work independently are essential.

• Previous experience with Underground Transmission / Distribution systems would be an asset.

• You must hold a valid Nova Scotia Driver's license with a minimum of 2 years driving experience and provide a driver's abstract satisfactory to NSPI.

• If you hold a valid Class 3 Nova Scotia Driver's License with trailer endorsement, it would also be considered an asset.

• You are a detailed-oriented individual, working to a high standard.

• You possess strong customer service and interpersonal skills. You are extremely organized, with a strong ability to multi-task. Strong communication skills (oral, written and computer) are required.

• You must demonstrate your commitment to personal development.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Please Note: This is a bargaining unit position. External applicants will only be considered if there are no qualified bargaining unit candidates.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers. If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by November 4, 2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching & volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: A comprehensive benefits plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

If you have any questions about this opportunity or if you are experiencing any technical difficulty with the application process, please email careers@nspower.ca

title: Maintenance Person - NOR 26062
description:
## Maintenance Person

## The Opportunity

Under the direction of the Maintenance Supervisor, the Maintenance Person is responsible for carrying out material and equipment installations, renovations, repairs, and servicing in the following areas - carpentry, plumbing, heating, basic electrical, painting, ventilation, on properties, under the jurisdiction of Nova Scotia Provincial Housing Agency. The incumbent is also required to carry out preventative maintenance to all assigned NSPHA buildings, appliances, fixtures, utilities, and equipment in accordance with established standards, policies, and procedures; assist with maintaining buildings and grounds in clean and proper order; monitoring contractors engaged to carry out maintenance contracts; and providing recommendations regarding the replacement and acquisition of materials and equipment.

Qualifications

## Must Have

• Grade 12 or equivalent, plus five years' experience in building and property maintenance or a related field. Must be able to perform basic tasks in carpentry, plumbing, heating, electrical, painting, and drywall.

• Knowledge of residential building technology, basic knowledge of the National Building Code and Occupational Health and Safety Act.

• Possess current Emergency First Aid and WHMIS certifications.

• Ability to operate electrical and mechanical tools and equipment.

• Ability to perform physical tasks using good body mechanics.

## Nice to have

• Knowledge of Yardi.

An equivalent combination of training, education and experience may be considered.

This position requires a valid driver's license and access to a reliable vehicle. Regular travel within Northern District is required.

Responsibilities
• Maintain properties including maintenance and repairs of walks, driveways, parking areas, drainage systems, curbs and gutters, swales, culverts, manholes, and catch basins.

• Repair foundation including crack repairs, parging, flashing, and related mortar installations.

• Professional development and career growth opportunities

title: Executive Director
description:
We are seeking our next Executive Director at the Murphy Centre.

This is an exciting full-time, permanent position that reports to the Board of Directors.

## About Us

Since 1986, The Murphy Centre has empowered individuals to create positive change in their lives. As a registered non-profit community organization, we acknowledge the immeasurable worth of every individual and believe in their ability to make meaningful and lasting changes in their lives. Through educational opportunities, career and personal development programs, and employment support services, we provide the guidance, resources, and encouragement to help people build confidence, achieve success, and reach their full potential.

The Murphy Centre is governed by a dedicated volunteer Board of Directors and provides an inclusive, alternative learning environment for adults pursuing successful completion of secondary school or equivalency through the High School Credit program (HSC), the Adult Basic Education program (ABE), and the Canadian Adult Education Credential (CAEC).

The Murphy Centre is a recognized leader in career and personal growth programming, helping individuals throughout the community discover new possibilities, strengthen their resilience, and create lasting pathways to success.

As The Murphy Centre continues to build on its legacy of empowering individuals and strengthening communities through education and career development, we are seeking a passionate and dynamic Executive Director to provide visionary leadership, champion our mission, and guide the organization into its next chapter of growth, innovation, and positive impact.

## Position Summary

The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, financial stewardship, and community engagement. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the ED ensures the successful execution of the organization's mission, goals, and strategic priorities while maintaining strong relationships with stakeholders, funders, staff, volunteers, and community partners.

## Key Responsibilities include:

## Leadership & Strategy

• Provide visionary leadership and direction aligned with the organization's philosophy, mission and strategic plan

• Work collaboratively with the Board of Directors to develop and implement strategic initiatives

• Identify opportunities for growth, partnerships, and program development

• Foster a positive, inclusive, and collaborative organizational culture

## Administrative and Operations Management

• Oversee day-to-day operations and ensure efficient delivery of programs and services

• Develop and implement policies, procedures, and organizational best practices

• Create an open, collaborative, and respectful working environment that fosters innovative solutions that address the diverse educational and career development needs of clients

• Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, provincial, and regulatory requirements

• Responsible for the overall administration of the organization, including payroll, human resources, facilities, information management, and office operations

## Financial Management

• Develop and manage annual and project budgets in collaboration with the Board

• Monitor financial performance and ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources

• Oversee financial reporting, audits, and risk management processes

• Ensure compliance with funding agreements and reporting requirements

• Oversees payroll operations, including processing, reporting, and legislative compliance

## Partner and Revenue Development

• Build and maintain relationships with partners, funders, foundations, government agencies, and corporate partners

• Lead fundraising efforts, including grant applications, donor relations, sponsorships, and special events

• Identify and pursue new funding opportunities to support organizational sustainability

## Human Resources

• Provide leadership, coaching and guidance to staff engaged in the delivery and administration of various programs

• Promote employee engagement, professional development, and workplace wellbeing

• Recruit, lead, mentor, and evaluate staff and volunteers

• Ensure compliance with employment legislation and organizational policies

## Community Relations & Advocacy

• Act as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for the organization

• Build strong relationships with community stakeholders, partners, and government representatives

• Promote awareness of the organization's mission, programs, and impact

## Qualifications Required

• Bachelor's degree in social sciences, Business Administration, Finance, Education, Non-Profit Management, Public Administration, or a related field

• Minimum 5 years of senior leadership experience, preferably within the non-profit sector

• Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant writing, and financial management

• Strong understanding of governance and working effectively with a Board of Directors

• Exceptional leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills

• Knowledge of Canadian non-profit regulations and reporting requirements

• Demonstrates a strong commitment to continuous improvement

• A combination of relevant experience and qualifications will be considered

• The successful candidate must provide a satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check as a condition of employment.

## Preferred Qualifications

• Master's degree in a related field.

• Experience working with diverse communities and stakeholders

## What We Offer

• Starting salary of $104,000 annually, with consideration given to experience and qualifications

• Competitive benefits package

• Employer RRSP matching program

• Generous paid leave

• Professional development opportunities

• Meaningful work that makes a positive impact in the community

• Collaborative and supportive work environment

## How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit the following:

• Cover Letter

• Resume

Applications should be sent to hr@murphycentre.ca with the subject line "Executive Director Application" by November 16th, 2026.

The Murphy Centre is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment process upon request. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted, we thank you for your interest in the Murphy Centre.

title: Chief Technology Officer
description:
BE AT THE FOREFRONT OF CANADA'S CLEAN ENERGY TRANSFORMATION.

Salient Energy Inc. is advancing the next generation of safe, sustainable energy storage technology. Our zinc-ion batteries are designed to accelerate the global shift toward renewable power, providing a safer, more cost-effective, and scalable alternative to lithium-ion.

We're looking for a results-driven, technically savvy Chief Technology Officer who understands the pace, complexity, and challenges of a startup environment and brings a genuine passion for clean tech energy. As we move into the heart of commercialization, this leader will drive the continued advancement of our zinc-ion battery platform, aligning technology, execution, and team leadership to support scale, market readiness, and commercial success.

## THE ROLE

Reporting to the CEO, the Chief Technology Officer will provide strategic and hands-on leadership across Salient Energy's technology function at a critical stage in the company's growth, balancing deep technical expertise with the operational and commercial oversight needed to advance through commercialization.

Leading the RCD, Cell Development, and Quality teams, the CTO will align technical direction, cross-functional execution, and team capability to support scale, certification, market readiness, and accelerated commercial success. As a member of the executive team, this leader will foster a strong, accountable, and collaborative culture while also serving as a trusted technical voice with the Board, investors, and external partners.

## WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Lead Salient's technology function by providing strategic and technical leadership across RCD, Cell Development, and Quality.

• Define and deliver product specifications, technical priorities, and performance metrics aligned with Salient's technology roadmap and TRL targets.

• Support the successful advancement of Salient's battery platform through commercialization, including readiness for scale, certification, and market adoption.

• Ensure required product and process certifications, including UL and CSA standards, are achieved.

• Represent Salient externally as a credible technical leader with the Board, investors, partners, and at relevant industry and technical forums.

## YOUR SKILLS, EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE

## Education & Technical Depth

• PhD in Chemistry, Chemical or Mechanical Engineering, or Materials Science/Engineering.

• Deep expertise in battery chemistry, electrochemistry, and testing processes, supported by 10+ years in a chemistry lab environment.

• Experience with advanced battery materials and ion transport mechanisms is considered an asset.

## Product Development & Commercialization

• 8-10 years leading development projects, with demonstrated experience bringing new products to market.

• Proven ability to align technical priorities with commercialization milestones, performance goals, and market needs.

## Leadership Profile

• Strategic & Commercial Acumen - able to connect technical direction to commercialization, scale, and business goals.

• Technical & Operational Leadership - brings rigor, focus, and accountability across complex technical programs.

• People & Stakeholder Influence - builds strong teams and communicates credibly with employees, executives, investors, and partners.

## THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate brings the technical depth and scientific credibility expected of a CTO, along with the leadership, operational oversight, and commercial mindset needed to advance Salient's technology through commercialization. While technical capability is essential, success in this role will depend on the ability to translate innovation into practical commercial application, aligning technical priorities with business objectives, supporting teams with clarity and accountability, and sustaining momentum toward scale, market readiness, and performance. This leader will understand how to balance thoughtful refinement and continuous innovation with the urgency required to meet business goals and move the product forward.

Excellent communication skills, with the ability to mentor teams and translate complex technical concepts into clear business value.

## WHY SALIENT?

At Salient, you'll work alongside a team of scientists, engineers, and innovators who are deeply committed to building a safer, cleaner energy future. We believe the best ideas come from curiosity, collaboration, and continuous learning. As CTO, you will play a defining leadership role in shaping our technology strategy, strengthening our technical organization, and advancing our products toward market adoption. Your work will directly influence how Salient scales its zinc-ion platform and delivers meaningful impact in one of the world's most important sectors: clean energy storage.

We offer a competitive salary and a collegiate, supportive, and diverse team environment. Here, you'll have the opportunity to lead meaningful innovation, develop exceptional teams, and help build a technology company positioned to make a real difference.

## TO APPLY

If you're ready to lead the advancement of future-defining battery technology, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a compelling cover letter outlining your fit for this role for an initial review.

We embrace inclusion and diversity and welcome applicants to self-identify. Please feel free to indicate if you belong or self-identify. Please note this is an on-site position and requires the successful candidate be in, or relocate to HRM. All applications will be reviewed, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Accounting Coordinator
description:
## Accounting Coordinator

Company: Breton Brewing Co.
Location: Sydney, Nova Scotia
Reports To: Chief Financial Officer
Position: Full-Time
Compensation: $55,000-$60,000 based on experience and qualifications

## About Breton Brewing Co.

Breton Brewing Co. is a growing craft brewery and hospitality company based in Sydney, Nova Scotia. Our operations include brewery production, wholesale distribution, retail and taproom operations, Breton Crafthouse, and related business and real estate interests.

As our operations have grown, so have the accounting, reporting and financial systems required to support the business. We are seeking an experienced, organized and detail-oriented Accounting Coordinator to join our finance team and work closely with our CFO and operational leaders.

## Position Summary

The Accounting Coordinator will be a key member of Breton Brewing Co.'s finance team and will take primary responsibility for the day-to-day coordination, completion and accuracy of the company's accounting activities.

The position will be responsible for maintaining and reconciling various areas of accounting while supporting the CFO and other admin staff.

The successful candidate will be comfortable taking ownership of recurring accounting responsibilities, investigating discrepancies, working across multiple business systems and ensuring the CFO has accurate and timely financial information.

## Key Responsibilities

• Accounts Payable & Vendor Management
• Manage the day-to-day accounts payable process from invoice receipt through payment with assistance from admin support staff.

• Review invoices for accuracy, coding, appropriate authorization, supporting documentation, and proper cutoff.

• Maintain vendor accounts and reconcile supplier statements.

• Prepare regular payment runs for CFO review and approval.

• Work with managers to ensure purchasing and invoice-approval procedures are followed.

• Accounts Receivable, Credit & Collections
• Manage the accounts receivable process, including invoicing, payment application and account reconciliation.

• Maintain accurate accounts receivable aging reports.

• Proactively follow up on outstanding and overdue customer accounts.

• Provide regular accounts receivable and collections reporting to the CFO and sales team.

• Payroll Administration
• Coordinate and process regular payroll for Breton Brewing Co. and related entities.

• Review employee hours, salary information, deductions, vacation pay and other payroll inputs for accuracy.

• Coordinate payroll information relating to new employees, departures, compensation changes and other adjustments.

• Maintain accurate and confidential payroll records.

• Reconcile payroll-related accounts and investigate discrepancies.

• Prepare payroll reports for CFO review.

• Support year-end payroll requirements, including T4 preparation and related reconciliations.

• Inventory & Cost Accounting
• Reconcile brewery, warehouse, retail and hospitality inventory to accounting records.

• Investigate unusual inventory variances, losses or costing discrepancies.

• Accounting Systems & Process Improvement
• Develop a strong working knowledge of QuickBooks Online, Dext, EKOS, WHISK, Toast, Order Desk and other systems used throughout the company.

• Help ensure information flows accurately between operational systems and accounting records.

• Reconcile accounting information to inventory, POS, sales and operational platforms.

• Bookkeeping & General Accounting
• Maintain accurate and timely accounting records in QuickBooks Online.

• Review and record financial transactions across company operations.

• Prepare and maintain reconciliations for key balance-sheet accounts.

• Ensure transactions are appropriately classified by business, department and location.

• Maintain organized supporting documentation.

• Assist CFO with month-end close and reporting processes.

• Assist CFO with timely and accurate budgeting and forecasting.

• Assist CFO with year-end reporting schedules for external accountants.

## Qualifications

• 5 years of hands-on accounting, bookkeeping, or related experience.

• Direct experience with accounts payable and accounts receivable.

• Experience processing or administering payroll.

• Experience completing bank, credit-card and balance-sheet reconciliations.

• Experience supporting month-end accounting processes.

• Strong practical understanding of bookkeeping and accounting principles.

• Proficiency with QuickBooks Online or comparable accounting software.

• Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Experience with inventory, manufacturing, POS or operational systems is considered an asset.

• Experience in manufacturing, beverage alcohol, hospitality, retail or another multi-location environment is considered an asset.

• Bachelor of Business Administration with a major in accounting or equivalent diploma/degree is required; equivalent practical experience will also be considered.

## Skills & Attributes

• Highly accurate and detail-oriented.

• Organized and capable of managing multiple recurring deadlines.

• Comfortable taking ownership of accounting processes.

• Able to identify discrepancies and investigate their underlying causes.

• Self-directed and comfortable working with limited supervision.

• Professional when communicating with customers, vendors and employees.

• Discreet when handling confidential financial and payroll information.

• Strong at documenting processes and maintaining organized records.

• Interested in systems, technology and continuous improvement.

• Comfortable working in a growing organization where processes continue to evolve.

• Collaborative and able to work effectively across multiple departments/companies.

## Schedule & Expectations

This is a full-time position with standard business hours. However, peak operational periods-particularly around month-end closes, financial reporting deadlines, and year-end audit/CRA reporting requirements-may require additional time and flexibility to ensure deadlines are met accurately.

## Perks & Benefits

• Access to Medical & Dental benefits (effective after 90 days).

• Annual Healthy Living Stipend.

• Employee Discounts.

• Annual Staff Party.

• Professional development opportunities.

• Use of company equipment / communication support as needed.

## Equal Opportunity Employer

Breton Brewing Co. and related companies are an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive environment that celebrates diversity and embraces the unique perspectives and experiences of our team members. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and excellence in everything we do.

## How to Apply

Please submit your resume and cover letter to careers@bretonbrewing.ca with "Accounting Coordinator" in the subject line.

Please indicate in your cover letter and/or resume, clearly and concisely, how you meet each qualification requirement with the skills/attributes identified above.

We thank all candidates for their applications to this role however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

• Patient and empathetic,

title: Customer Service Representative

• The ability to fluently speak both English and French would be considered an asset.

description:
The Opportunity

Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Energy Delivery, Underground

Type of Employment: Regular, Full Time

Reporting to the Underground Supervisor, you will become a member of a team of professionals at our location in Sackville and you will perform all aspects of installation, commissioning, maintenance and repair of electrical underground plant on the Transmission/Distribution System throughout the Territory.

Key elements of this role include:

## As an Electrician (Industrial):

• You may be temporarily assigned to other locations to assist other areas when required and will be expected to travel throughout the province.

• This position is considered a safety sensitive position. As such, the successful candidate must comply with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Policy which requires a confidential pre-employment alcohol and drug test in accordance with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Procedure.

• Your primary residence must be located within 30 minutes of the work location depot, and you will be required to take on call rotation and work other than normal hours and/or in extreme conditions. You will have 90 days to provide proof of primary residence.

These skills will make you successful:

• Certification as a Journeyman Industrial Electrician with a minimum of two years' experience with troubleshooting electrical equipment is required. If no qualified candidates apply, consideration may be given to those individuals who hold Certification as a Construction Electrician.

• You have proven problem resolution skills and the flexibility and ability to adapt to rescheduled assignments.

• You must be a strong team player with excellent interpersonal skills, a strong computer aptitude and the ability to deal with multiple tasks and demands.

• You must have the skills and physical capabilities to perform all duties, including working at considerable heights and within confined spaces.

• You must hold a valid Nova Scotia Driver's License with a minimum of two years driving experience and provide a driver's abstract satisfactory to NSPI.

Trailer endorsement would also be considered an asset. Consideration may be given to members of an Industrial Electrician Apprenticeship program if no qualified candidates apply.

• Able to push and pull 50 lbs. with whole body strength and be able to push and pull 100 lbs. with upper body strength on an occasional basis.

• Perform sitting, squatting, kneeling, crouching, climbing, bending, stooping, and forward flexional movements on a minimal basis.
