title: Forestry Summer Student
description:
## Forestry Summer Student Opportunities

Flexible Work term: May 3 to August 27, 2027 (18 weeks)

If you have a passion for forestry, then Port Hawkesbury Paper has an opportunity for you! We are looking for motivated TEAM players with a strong work ethic to fill our 4-month summer positions assisting with various projects within our Woodlands unit.

Port Hawkesbury Paper holds several environmental certifications and is the largest Crown license manager in Nova Scotia. The PHP Woodlands team is directly responsible for the forest management and sustainability of more than 500,000 hectares of forested lands in the seven Eastern counties, from the eastern tip of Cape Breton Island to the Eastern Mainland. We also play a significant role in private land forest management.

## What we offer

A competitive salary, relocation assistance, field gear, work vehicle, retailer shopping discount and a place to apply the skills and knowledge gained from your education. As part of our team, you will gain new skills through a variety of experiences in Silviculture and Harvesting such as:

• Silviculture

• Regeneration & plantation surveys

• Plantation quality assessments

• Pre-harvest assessments

• Sampling spacing and manual weeding sites

• Harvesting

• Harvesting supervision audits

• Road construction

• Bridge installation

As a part of the team, you will be involved in a combination of fieldwork where you stay challenged, getting your boots dirty and keeping your mind active. Combine this with the office side where you learn how to use programs required to run a Woodland department. You will have the opportunity to work with experienced professionals who will provide you with training as well as other students with whom to apply your new skills and share experiences.

## What you bring

• A high focus on safety

• Attention to detail

• Level 1 First Aid

• Ability to work alone in the woods

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• Valid driver's license

## Things to do in your spare time

In your free time there is lots to do! You can hike and bike on many trails, kayak or canoe waterways, swim at the many sandy beaches, visit several historic sites like Louisbourg, go camping in the many provincial parks or the Cape Breton Highlands National Park, or drive the scenic Cape Breton Trail. Enjoy the many festivals and events unique to each of the small communities in the area and larger centers like New Glasgow, Antigonish, Sydney and Port Hawkesbury. Check out https://novascotia.com for things to do!

Qualified applicants should email their resume and cover letter to Human Resources at HR@porthawkesburypaper.com on or before November 13th, 2026. We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those considered for an interview will be contacted.

At Port Hawkesbury Paper, diversity means understanding, recognizing, and valuing the differences that make each person unique. We see inclusion as an essential part of our productivity, creativity, innovation, and competitive advantage. We strive for a fair and equitable recruitment process, where hiring decisions are based on the qualifications and experience of each applicant.

Follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook and our Website (www.porthawkesburypaper.com) for news, and career opportunities.

title: Mail Service Agent
description:
The Mail Service Agent is responsible for managing the Company's mail services. This includes processing, sorting, distributing, and scanning incoming and outgoing mail, as well as coordinating regular and special mailings. They ensure the quality and efficiency of mail services while maintaining established budgets. In addition, they provide administrative support to the Finance Department, including activities related to vendor management and other administrative tasks. They also ensures the proper operation of mailroom equipment and contributes to delivering professional, high-quality service across the organization.

Qualifications
• On-Site Presence: This position requires on-site work.

• Bilingualism: Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both French and English.

• Technical Skills: Ability to operate mail processing equipment, including inserting, postage, and scanning machines.

• Attention to Detail and Organization: Ability to ensure accuracy and quality in mail processing and document scanning while effectively managing multiple priorities and daily tasks.

• Customer Service and Teamwork: Ability to work collaboratively with others and provide courteous, professional, and accurate service.

• Microsoft Office Proficiency: Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.

• Experience: Experience in a similar role or within an administrative environment would be considered an asset.

If this opportunity interests you, we invite you to submit your application before November 04, 2026.

Responsibilities
• Mail Processing and Distribution: Receive, sort, and distribute mail on a daily basis, ensuring documents are scanned and electronically distributed in accordance with established policies.

• Mail Coordination and Administration: Ensure the quality of correspondence, respond to inquiries from employees and the sales force, and monitor budgets related to regular and expedited mail services.

• Fax and Email Processing: Process daily incoming faxes and emails and ensure they are routed appropriately.

• Administrative Support to Finance: Reconcile various general ledger accounts, assist with vendor administration within Accounts Payable, and perform other administrative duties under the responsibility of the Finance Department.

• The chance to be part of a dynamic, high-performing team that adheres to the following ethical values: leadership, collaboration, trust and commitment;

• Training and development opportunities;

• A comprehensive benefits package including a competitive salary, bonus, pension and benefits;

• A dynamic location in downtown Moncton;

• A paid volunteer day;

• Time off to care for family members and pets.

title: Court Officer 1-2 - Judicial Support (Pictou)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50238

Department: Justice

Location: PICTOU

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 02-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Court Services Division of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice is dedicated to excellent service and the provision of fair and accessible administration of justice, including court administration and security.
The Division provides administrative support to the courts listed: Nova Scotia Court of Appeal, Supreme Court of Nova Scotia (including Family Division), Provincial Court, Small Claims Court, Probate Court, and Bankruptcy Court. The courts act independently from the government to address individual cases.
For more information on the Department of Justice Court Services please visit our website: https://novascotia.ca/just/Court_Services/

About Our Opportunity
As the Court Officer (Judicial Support), you may coordinate and manage court hearings held in all levels of Court, provide support to the Judiciary, and act as the liaison between the Court, and members of law enforcement agencies, the legal profession, and the public. You will also act in the role of the clerk of the Court in all courts, including jury sittings and perform quasi-judicial duties assigned as a Staff Justice of the Peace as appointed under the Justice of the Peace Act. You will perform your duties in accordance with, and as assigned under, the Court Officials Act.

Primary Accountabilities
The Judicial Support responsibilities include:

• Communicate with legal professionals and self-represented individuals to co-ordinate and manage court hearings held at all levels of court.

• Provide confidential administrative and organizational support to the Judiciary.

• Act in the role of the clerk in all courts, including jury sitting and performing quasi- judicial duties as a Staff Justice of the Peace.

• Train and mentor new staff in day-to-day operational activities.

• Under the Judge's direction, draft and prepare complex orders and decisions arising from court hearings, review and apply relevant acts, statutes, policies, and procedures to all court documentation.

• Record and transcribe court proceedings by means of electronic recording equipment.

• Facilitate all aspects of court hearings from opening court, calling cases, swear or affirm witnesses or interpreters and translators, while simultaneously operating all required technology that may be required to support virtual court or hybrid models of court or appearances.

• Exercise care and control of exhibits, including transportation, until transferred to the Exhibit Custodian.

• You may be required to perform duties in Court Administration.

Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate must have two years of post-secondary education in a related discipline plus one-year related experience, ideally in a legal environment, or an acceptable equivalent.
The successful candidate must also:

• Have experience and competency in keyboarding (combination of speed and accuracy), data entry, transcribing, and other standard computer applications including MS Office products.

• Have experience with virtual platforms such as MS Teams and video conferencing.

• Possess excellent proofreading, spelling, and grammar skills.

• Have superior organizational abilities and strong prioritization skills

• Have excellent attention to detail

• Have the ability to meet tight deadlines.

• Work independently and as part of a team.

• Have tact and discretion.

• Demonstrate an understanding and knowledge of the Rules and Statutes that govern the courts as well as a sound working knowledge of legal documents, forms, court procedures and legal terminology.

• Demonstrate a high level of initiative and problem-solving abilities and readily accept responsibilities. Errors can result in significant impacts for justice system participants.

• Be fair and impartial to all clients using a high degree of confidentiality while exercising your excellent interpersonal and communication skills, particularly listening skills, when dealing with difficult people in complex, sensitive and stressful situations.

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: written examination, typing test, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.
Legal research skills and bilingualism, with oral and written skills in English and French, would be considered assets.

Equivalency
Include, but not limited to:

• A 1-year certificate/diploma in a related discipline plus 2 years of related experience

• 3 years of related experience with exposure to the justice system

PLEASE NOTE: Candidates will not be considered for an interview if applications are incomplete or are missing information. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
• Normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day (typically the hours are 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, this may vary depending on operational needs).

• Your personal resiliency is essential to meet the emotional demands of this position. You may be immersed in high stress situations and encounter distraught and difficult individuals.

• Handling of some exhibits may be mentally or physically disconcerting.

• May involve extensive keyboarding as well as long hours sitting in a formal courtroom environment.

Additional Information
This is a permanent employment opportunity, located in Pictou, NS.
Candidates may be required to obtain training in Firearms Safety in relation to handling evidence and may be required to successfully complete the Nova Scotia Certified Transcribers qualification. This position will require an enhanced level of security screening for an external application.
Some travel and overtime may be required.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless career paths.

description:
Competition # : 50108

Department: Public Prosecution Service

Location: SYDNEY

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: NSCAA

Closing Date: 02-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
The Public Prosecution Service (PPS) offers a unique and meaningful opportunity to contribute to justice and public safety. Established in 1990 as the first statutorily based independent prosecution service in Canada, the mandate of the PPS is rooted in its commitment to ensuring fair and equal treatment in the prosecution of criminal and provincial offences.
We are looking for the brightest legal minds, who also reflect the rich diversity of our province! We don't just accept difference – we celebrate a supportive culture of diversity and belonging. We strive to create an environment where different perspectives and experiences are welcomed and valued. We encourage applications from those that equally value and champion equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility (EDIA).

Why Choose Us?
A career with the Public Prosecution Service in Nova Scotia provides a unique opportunity to contribute to justice, public safety, and the overall well-being of the community while working in a professional, inclusive, and ethical environment.
We are a dedicated and passionate team with a determination to make a difference in the society we serve, utilizing our expertise and recognizing and applying an equity and inclusion lens to our work, in our training and development, workplace culture, communications, partnering and engagement to ensure we protect and reflect the communities we live in and serve.

What We Offer
1. Commitment to Justice and Public Interest:
This is achieved by performing prosecution duties with fairness, professionalism, and integrity. Employees actively contribute to upholding the principles of justice in Nova Scotia.
2. Mission and Goals:
Aligning with the Government of Nova Scotia's priority of fulfilling social responsibility for public safety, the PPS' mission and goals include providing excellence in public service, identifying, and managing resources effectively, applying best business practices, and fostering an environment for independent prosecutorial discretion that recognizes the importance of diversity and inclusion in ensuring representation reflective of the community.
3. Core Business Functions:
Employees at the PPS engage in core business functions that play a crucial role in the legal landscape of Nova Scotia. These functions include representing the Crown in criminal and quasi-criminal matters at all levels of court, handling appeals, providing legal advice and assistance to law enforcement, and actively participating in the development of criminal law and prosecutions policy.
4. Professional Development and High Ethical Standards:
The PPS is committed to maintaining a diverse team that reflects excellence, dedication to public service, and high ethical standards. Employees have the opportunity for professional development in a welcoming environment that values continuous improvement and recognizes diversity and inclusion contributes to a healthy and thriving workplace culture that allows team members to be their full selves at work, while upholding the highest ethical principles.
5. Community Engagement:
The PPS is focused on providing a service that is reflective of the community it serves. By fostering diversity and inclusivity, employees contribute to building a legal system that understands and respects the needs and perspectives of the broader community.
6. Impactful Contribution to Society:
Working for the PPS allows individuals to make a direct and meaningful impact on society by upholding the rule of law, protecting the safety and well-being of the community, and ensuring the fair treatment of those accused of prohibited conduct.
For more information on the Public Prosecution Service please visit the following link: https://novascotia.ca/pps/

About Our Opportunity
These positions are based in Cape Breton Region will report to the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton Region, to whom the incumbent is accountable for the provision of competent prosecution services. The Crown Attorney will advise law enforcement agencies when requested. Other key responsibilities include conducting the prosecution of charges resulting from matters within the Public Prosecution Service mandate that result from law enforcement agency investigations and other prosecutions and duties as directed by the Chief Crown Attorney, Cape Breton Region.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a practicing member of the Nova Scotia Barristers' Society (or eligible to become so) and have a thorough understanding of the prosecution process, and competence in the areas of criminal procedures, evidence, and substantive criminal law. You must have at least one year of criminal prosecution or relevant criminal law experience.
You may be required to travel throughout the province to prosecute cases and may be required to do so for extended periods of time.
Successful applicants may be required to provide a current Certificate of Standing from their law society, including all jurisdictions of which they are members, whether non-practicing or practicing.
The above qualifications will be assessed using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Additional Information
This is a permanent full-time employment opportunity, located in Sydney, NS.
Must have access to reliable transportation as travel throughout the region and across the province is required.

title: Lead Brewer
description:
Jump Recruitment, on behalf of our client, Boomstick Brewing Co., is currently seeking an energetic and highly motivated Lead Brewer to join their team in Corner Brook, NL.

## ABOUT BOOMSTICK BREWING CO.:

Located in downtown Corner Brook, Boomstick Brewing Co. is a proud Newfoundland craft brewery and alehouse with a passion for great beer, great food, and bringing people together. With a beer program inspired by craft brewing traditions from around the world and the stories and character of Newfoundland and Labrador, Boomstick has established itself as a destination for locals and visitors alike.

At Boomstick, brewing is about more than making beer. It's about quality, creativity, consistency, and having fun with the craft, and sharing that spirit with the community. From our core beers and seasonal releases to new recipes and experiments, we make beer for people to enjoy together and feel proud to call their own.

On West Street, the brewery is part of a lively gathering place where good beer, food, events, and a seasonal beer garden bring neighbors and visitors together.

## WHAT YOU'LL DO:

This is an exciting opportunity for a Lead Brewer to play a key role in the continued growth of Boomstick's brewing program. Working alongside a passionate team, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to bring their technical expertise, creativity, and love of craft beer to a brewery that takes its product seriously, while keeping the culture fun.

## Your key responsibilities will be:

• Oversee the daily operations of the brewery, including brewing, cellar operations, packaging, reporting, and recipe development.

• Maintain a comprehensive Quality Program for Boomstick Brewing Company, including defined and measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

• Work closely with the Sales & Distribution Manager and brew team daily to ensure production and operational targets are achieved effectively and efficiently.

• Maintain a clean, safe, organized, and fully functional brewing facility always.

• Complete and/or supervise inventory counts of finished beer, grain, hops, and other raw materials, maintaining accurate records.

• Monitor inventory levels and follow established procedures for raw materials, chemicals, beer, cooperage, small parts, packaging, and other supplies; place orders as required.

• Collaborate with the brewery team and management to maintain the quality and consistency of our established core and seasonal products, while developing new recipes and planning future products, production timelines, and packaging goals.

• In coordination with the Sales & Distribution Manager, plan and execute the internal movement of packaged products, including small-batch rotation, and update batch logs as required.

• Schedule and coordinate preventative and reactive maintenance for brewery equipment to ensure reliable and efficient operations.

• Coordinate additional staffing requirements during peak periods, including packaging and other production needs.

• Oversee the development, production, and continued growth of Boomstick's diverse beverage portfolio-including beer, cider, ready-to-drink beverages, and non-alcoholic beer, while identifying and pursuing opportunities to further diversify the product line and make effective use of the brewery's space and equipment.

• Represent Boomstick Brewing Co. at events, festivals, and promotional activities, helping to build the brand and maintain positive relationships within the community.

• Address customer concerns and complaints professionally and appropriately when required.

• Identify and participate in professional development opportunities to stay current with industry trends, brewing practices, and technical knowledge.

## WHAT YOU BRING:

• 10 years' proven experience in a leadership role within the beverage manufacturing industry, preferably in brewing or beverage production.

• Education in Brewing, Food Science, Chemistry or Microbiology is an asset.

• Familiarity with sanitation standards, food safety regulations, and quality assurance practices.

• Basic math skills for measuring ingredients, adjusting recipes, and managing inventory accurately.

• Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while maintaining attention to detail.

• Excellent communication skills for team leadership and cross-department collaboration.

## WHAT WE OFFER:

• A competitive compensation package

• A flexible, supportive, and collaborative work environment.

• The opportunity to grow your career within a larger, hospitality focused group of companies.

• Access to a management incentive program with perks across all company owned businesses.

• The opportunity to be a part of a passionate and fun team!

If you're an experienced brewer who wants to put your stamp on a growing Newfoundland brewery and be part of something unique in Western Newfoundland, we'd love to hear from you!!

title: Senior Business Analyst (Program Admin Officer 4)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49975

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: HALIFAX

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 02-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
As a Senior Business Analyst with the Innovation Team in the Strategic Operations & Innovation division, you will help improve programs and service delivery for clients and staff.

This is not a role where every problem arrives neatly defined. We are looking for someone who can see the big picture and the details, ask the questions others may not yet be asking, create clarity from ambiguity, and help turn ambitious ideas into practical, lasting improvements.

As a Senior Business Analyst, you will help shape how Nova Scotia's social services evolve. You will work across programs, operations, policy, and technology to define complex problems, identify opportunities, and translate strategic priorities into practical improvements. This may include improving client journeys, redesigning provincial service-delivery models, modernizing policies and processes, exploring responsible uses of automation and artificial intelligence, and helping teams address intersecting program, operational, and technical needs.

Reporting to a Project Executive, you will lead complex analysis and discovery work, develop evidence-based recommendations, and support initiatives from discovery through implementation. You will collaborate with Product Managers, Project Managers, internal divisions, external partners, and subject-matter experts. You will also mentor junior staff, assign tasks, and evaluate their work.

Primary Accountabilities
SD is in the midst of a multi-year journey to dramatically improve client and system outcomes and we're counting on your expertise to help us achieve this. In this role, you will:

• Analyze complex service-delivery challenges and identify improvement opportunities.

• Connect client and staff experience, policy, operations, data, technology, and departmental priorities to develop a whole-system view.

• Lead research, current-state analysis, and collaborative discovery with internal and external partners.

• Clarify root causes, challenge assumptions constructively, and establish shared problem definitions.

• Design practical future-state services, processes, policies, and digital solutions.

• Develop business cases, options, and evidence-based recommendations for decision-makers.

• Work with project, product, program, and technology teams to turn recommendations into achievable plans and implemented changes.

• Identify dependencies, risks, and unintended consequences across programs and service channels.

• Define outcomes and measures, using evidence and feedback to refine implemented solutions.

• Mentor analysts and introduce methods, tools, and approaches that strengthen the team's analytical and delivery capacity.

Qualifications and Experience
We're seeking a strategic and collaborative professional with experience in both planning and execution of business process improvement and digital transformation. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in cross-functional environments and is passionate about improving public services and supporting the successful delivery of departmental and government priorities. If you're committed to meaningful change and improving outcomes for Nova Scotians, we'd love to hear from you.

We value diverse educational and professional journeys and welcome applicants with experience across sectors who bring fresh approaches to social innovation. You have a university degree from a recognized school plus at least six (6) years of related experience, or an equivalent combination of school, volunteering, training and experience.

You also have experience:

• Leading or supporting service redesign, policy development, business process improvement, strategic planning, or digital transformation.

• Conducting analysis and preparing clear deliverables, such as business cases, policy briefs, process maps, service-improvement plans, or outcome-measurement frameworks.

• Managing organizational change and moving complex work from analysis to implementation.

• Building trusted relationships, facilitating collaboration, and influencing decisions through evidence and sound judgement.

• Managing competing priorities and deadlines in a changing environment.

• Using Microsoft 365 and Power Platform tools, including Excel, PowerPoint, Power Automate, Outlook, and SharePoint.

You can bring structure to ambiguous work, recognize connections and risks across systems, challenge assumptions constructively, and balance strategic goals with practical implementation.

The following are considered assets:

• Certification or training in business analysis, project management, Lean Six Sigma, or change management.

• Experience with service design or human-centred design.

• Knowledge of government processes, regulatory requirements, or departmental programs and services.

• Experience with data visualization, Microsoft Power Apps, Power BI, Power Automate, or the development of artificial intelligence tools to improve business processes

We will assess the above qualifications using one or more of the following tools: oral presentations, written assignments, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include, but are not limited to:

• A related master's degree and four (4) years related experience

• Completion of a 2-year college diploma program and eight (8) years related experience

• Ten (10) years total related experience

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
This role is based in a comfortable office environment and you may be working at your computer for extended periods of time. You may be required to travel to worksite locations.

Your normal work week is 35 hours/week, 7 hours/day.

Additional Information
One (1) full-time term position is available with an anticipated end date of December 31, 2028. The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

What We Offer
• Ownership of complex initiatives with meaningful, province-wide impact.

• Influence at the intersection of policy, operations, service design, and technology.

• Work across multiple social programs rather than within a narrow functional area.

• Experiment with practical approaches to digital services, automation, data and responsible AI.

• A welcoming, multidisciplinary team that values curiosity, thoughtful challenge, collaboration, and implementation.

• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies

Pay Grade: PR 17

Salary Range: $3,410.48 - $4,005.58 Bi-Weekly

Employment Equity Statement: Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative, at all job levels, of the citizens we serve. The Government of Nova Scotia has an Employment Equity Policy, and we welcome applications from Indigenous People, African Nova Scotians, Persons of African Descent, Racialized Persons, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ Persons and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. title: Senior Commercial Relationship Manager, Commercial Real Estate Lending
description:
League Savings & Mortgage (LSM) is currently accepting applications for a Senior Commercial Relationship Manager.

## Why join LSM?

At LSM, we're more than a financial institution. We're a purpose-driven organization helping strengthen communities across Atlantic Canada.

As a federally regulated, credit union-owned organization based in Nova Scotia, we combine the stability and expertise of a financial institution with the collaborative culture of a values-based organization.

When you join LSM, you'll have the opportunity to work on complex and meaningful transactions, build strong industry relationships, and contribute directly to the growth of Atlantic Canada's communities and business.

You'll also enjoy:

• Flexible work options, including remote arrangements

• A strong focus on work-life balance; with personal, volunteer days, and even your birthday off

• A collaborative and inclusive environment where your ideas are encouraged and valued

• Professional growth and development opportunities

• A Nova Scotia-based financial institution with deep community roots

• The chance to be part of a Certified B Corporation making a positive impact

Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in finance, business, or a related field.

• Minimum of eight years of commercial lending experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong expertise in commercial and residential mortgage financing, including underwriting, credit analysis, loan origination, servicing, and commercial real estate lending.

• Proven ability to analyze financial statements, assess credit risk, structure financing solutions, and exercise sound lending judgment.

• Advanced knowledge of CMHC financing programs, multi-residential lending requirements, and commercial real estate valuation and appraisal practices.

• Strong communication, relationship management, negotiation, and business development skills.

• Experience delivering training, educational programs, or presentations to adult learners.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Responsibilities
As a Senior Commercial Relationship Manager, you will lead the development and management of a complex commercial real estate lending portfolio while contributing to business development, credit adjudication, strategic planning, and industry engagement.

## Business Development & Strategic Growth

• Develop and maintain strong relationships with credit unions, borrowers, brokers, accountants, developers, investors, and other referral sources to generate new business opportunities.

• Proactively identify and pursue lending opportunities through market research, networking, cold outreach, and industry events.

• Contribute to business growth strategies by identifying emerging market opportunities, referral channels, and new lending initiatives.

• Participate in the development and execution of annual business plans and strategic priorities.

• Monitor industry trends, competitor activity, and evolving market conditions to support informed business decisions.

• Represent the organization at industry associations, conferences, and stakeholder events to strengthen partnerships and enhance market presence.

• Recommend enhancements to existing lending solutions and identify opportunities for new products and services.

## Relationship & Portfolio Management

• Manage and grow a portfolio of complex commercial real estate lending relationships.

• Maintain regular contact with borrowers to understand financing needs, identify opportunities, and address emerging risks.

• Conduct ongoing portfolio reviews and relationship assessments to ensure portfolio quality and performance.

• Monitor borrower and portfolio performance, identify potential credit concerns, and recommend appropriate risk mitigation strategies.

• Stay informed on market and industry developments that may impact borrowers or portfolio performance.

## Credit Adjudication & Transaction Management

• Conduct thorough due diligence and financial analysis on complex commercial lending opportunities.

• Assess financial statements, cash flow, business performance, profitability, and shareholder net worth to evaluate creditworthiness.

• Structure financing solutions, negotiate terms and conditions, and prepare term sheets and lending recommendations.

• Analyze collateral and security arrangements and assess industry and market factors impacting credit risk.

• Prepare comprehensive credit submissions and recommendations in compliance with commercial lending policies and guidelines.

• Complete applications for CMHC Certificate of Insurance.

• Prepare commitment letters, ensure all financing conditions are satisfied, and coordinate loan funding with internal partners.

• Participate in credit committee reviews and provide adjudication support for lending applications across Atlantic Central, League Savings and Mortgage, and regional credit unions.

## Canada Mortgage Bonds (CMB) Analysis

• Analyze potential CMB transactions and prepare credit recommendations for Executive Committee review and approval.

## Training, Advisory & Subject Matter Expertise

• Support the development and delivery of training and information sessions for credit union partners on lending products, services, and industry best practices.

• Provide expert advice and guidance on commercial lending solutions and complex transaction structures.

• Act as a resource to Commercial Relationship Managers by sharing best practices in business development, credit structuring, and risk assessment.

• Mentor and coach team members while contributing technical expertise on complex lending matters.

## Department and Company Support

• Conduct research and market analysis to support business development efforts, lending opportunities, and portfolio management activities.

• Collaborate with Treasury and Securitization teams to support loan funding and securitization activities, including cash flow forecasting and advance planning.

• Contribute to departmental initiatives, cross-functional projects, and organizational priorities.

• Lead or participate in special projects and perform other related duties as assigned.

## Compensation & Benefits

This is a permanent full-time position and is rated a Career Level P5 with a salary range of $111,594 to $131,288. LSM offers a competitive benefits package as well as the opportunity to participate in the Performance Sharing Incentive Plan.

## Location & Flexibility

Based in our Halifax, NS office, this role offers flexibility for remote work.

## Ready to apply?

If you're looking to make an impact on a collaborative, purpose-driven organization, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today.

## Applications Closes: October 30, 2026.

description:
## Employment Opportunity

## Natoaganeg First Nation

Position Title: Resident Support Worker
Program: Nignen Women's Shelter
Salary: Starting at $23.69/hour
Hours of Work: 12-hour shifts - Days, nights, evenings, and weekends
Status: Casual

Nignen Women's Shelter provides emergency shelter, services, and supports to women, their children and the 2SLGBTQQIA+ community, who are experiencing or have recently experienced intimate partner violence in Indigenous communities in New Brunswick. Nignen strives to be a center of excellence in providing the highest level of trauma-informed, culturally sensitive support. The shelter is recruiting a team of full-time and casual crisis support staff to become part of this essential work. Employees will be provided with training and orientation upon commencement of their employment.

## Suitability

The ideal candidate for this role is empathetic and compassionate. They are a confident decision-maker with the ability to build trust and resolve conflict. A solid understanding of First Nations history and culture is essential. Lived experience related to the position is a definite asset. Female applicants of indigenous ancestry preferred.

## Responsibilities

• Responding to calls on the 24-hour crisis line

• Providing care and support to residents

• Aiding with assessment and intake

• Providing safety and security of residents

• Fostering healthy relationships among residents and staff

• Facilitating supports from external social service agencies

• Maintaining exceptional documentation standards and data collection

• Provide updates to colleagues and escalate issues as appropriate

• Housekeeping and food preparation

• Monitor and ensure household standards and policies are upheld

• Adhering to strict confidentiality

• Perform additional duties as requested

## Qualifications and Experience

• Post secondary education in social sciences such as human service worker, social service community worker (an equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered)

• Experience working within First Nation communities and knowledge of culture and traditions

• Demonstrated understanding of the barriers, challenges, and the dynamics of violence against women, children and the 2SLGBTQQIA+ community

• Must be trained or willing to obtain training in CPR/ First Aid, and Non-violent crisis intervention

• Demonstrated ability to collaborate with the community, staff, and partner agencies

• Demonstrated commitment to strict client confidentiality

• Ability to meet the physical demands of the position

• Ability to speak the Mi'kmaq language is an asset

• Successful Criminal Record/Vulnerable Sector Checks

• Proven ability to work within a team environment with respect to professionalism, cooperation, sensitivity and cultural awareness

Those interested in applying are asked to submit a resume demonstrating the required qualifications and competencies for the position. Please clearly reference competition 2026-WS-03 and forward your application to Careers@NatoaganegFirstNation.ca on or before October 30th, 2026.

While we thank all who have applied, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities, and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Justice and Public Safety is dedicated to the rule of law, the promotion of the public interest, and the impartial administration of justice and works to improve the safety, security and resiliency of communities and citizens.

The Office of the Chief Legal Officer in the Department of Justice and Public Safety provides support to the Chief Justice and the Justices of the Court of King`s Bench, as well as court staff, in the legal operations of the Court of King`s Bench, Small Claims Court and Probate Court. The Office has a full-time employment opportunity available for a lawyer to fulfil judicial, quasi-judicial and legal functions necessary for the effective operation of the Court of King`s Bench of New Brunswick.

## What you will do

The Court of King`s Bench is responsible for a wide array of legal proceedings, including civil actions, judicial reviews, family matters, and serious criminal matters. As a legal officer, you will work extensively with the judiciary and court administration to modernize the Rules of Court, identify the impact of legislative and jurisprudential developments, and develop best practices. Background and experience in family, civil and criminal proceedings is preferred.

The legal officer is responsible for providing legal direction to Clerks and Administrators in the discharge of their duties, and giving procedural interpretation regarding the Rules of Court, Criminal Code, and other acts and regulations, to lawyers and the public. The legal officer may also be assigned other duties by the Chief Legal Officer.

This is a legislated position pursuant to the Judicature Act requiring the exercise of all duties, powers and authority of a Deputy Registrar of the Court of King`s Bench prescribed by any Act, Regulation, or the Rules of Court. This includes conducting various hearings and adjudicating matters pursuant to the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act, Support Enforcement Act, Small Claims Act, Enforcement of Money Judgments Act and Rules of Court.

## Who you are

You are a collaborative and adaptable professional with strong communication and problem-solving skills. You can think on your feet, exercise sound judgment, and explain complex legal and procedural matters clearly and effectively. You treat others with professionalism, courtesy, and kindness, and are committed to fairness, consistency, and excellent public service. You enjoy finding practical solutions, contributing to meaningful improvements, and working with colleagues, justice system participants, and members of the public to support the fair and efficient administration of justice for New Brunswickers.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

If the competition is awarded to a PCP as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

## OVERVIEW

Memorial University of Newfoundland (Memorial) is one of Canada's top 10 comprehensive universities, with programs across Newfoundland and Labrador and online. Consistently placing in the top 10 comprehensive universities in Canada and the top 20 overall, Memorial is built on a real commitment to students, to learning, and to making a difference. Our students, researchers, staff, and community partners are tackling some of the world's most pressing challenges. From personalized stroke rehabilitation robotics to discovering new cold-water reefs near the Galapagos Islands, our work has local relevance and global impact.

Memorial's Office of Internal Audit serves as an independent, objective assurance and advisory function for University operations. It helps Memorial achieve its strategic objectives by working with management, the Executive, and the Board of Regents to solve challenges and mitigate risks.

The Senior Internal Auditor applies a systematic and disciplined approach to evaluating risk management, control, and governance processes.

## DUTIES

Under the guidance and direction of the Director of Internal Audit, the Senior Internal Auditor conducts assurance and advisory engagements across organizational and functional units in accordance with the Office of Internal Audit's risk-based annual engagement plan. Key responsibilities include:

## BACKGROUND

Memorial University is one of the largest universities in Atlantic Canada. As the province's only university, Memorial plays an integral role in the education and cultural life of Newfoundland and Labrador, offering diverse undergraduate and graduate programs to nearly 18,000 students. The Faculty of Engineering and Applied Science (FEAS) Student Design Hub (SDH) is a cornerstone of Memorial's innovation ecosystem. It serves students from every discipline through an inclusive, interdisciplinary program designed to help them bring bold, impactful ideas to life. The mission of the SDH is to foster creative builders, and its vision is to develop and sustain a diverse and internationally recognized network of student innovators.

Success in the role will be reflected in stronger project delivery, improved competition readiness, and the development of highly capable student engineers and future technical leaders.

Experience (minimum 2 years) working on student design teams, leading students, and managing technical projects; completion of a bachelor's degree in engineering or a related field is required; or an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered. title: Campus Social Worker
description:
Employment Opportunity: Campus Social Worker - full-time permanent (35 hours per week) position | Subject to probationary period.

Established in 1789, the University of King's College is Canada's oldest chartered university and is associated with Dalhousie University. A small and extraordinarily lively academic community located in Halifax (Kjipuktuk), Nova Scotia, King's is known nationally and internationally for its interdisciplinary programs in the humanities, including its first-year Foundation Year Program, its professional programs in journalism and its fine arts programs in creative writing. King's is a community in which students, faculty, alumni, and staff work to bring greater understanding, creativity, and compassion to the world.

At King's, we believe that students thrive in a campus culture that is safe, inclusive, equitable and responsive to the diverse needs of our community. Through our Office of Equity & Community Supports, this belief is translated in our work that leads the implementation of multiple strategies & policies that strengthen student wellbeing, safety, and community care. We are advancing a university community where Indigenization, equity, safety, accessibility, student wellbeing, and belonging are embedded in how we learn, work, interact and support one another.

## Position Summary

Reporting to the Director of Equity and Community Supports, the Campus Social Worker provides direct social work support, stabilization support, case management, advocacy and systems navigation to King's students experiencing mental health, personal, social, academic or other challenges that may affect their wellbeing and ability to participate fully in university life.

Working from a combination of trauma-informed, strengths-based, anti-oppressive, culturally responsive and harm-reduction approaches, the Campus Social Worker conducts biopsychosocial assessments, develops individualized support plans, coordinates care, responds to students experiencing crisis, and connects students with appropriate university, healthcare and community-based resources. As a member of the Office of Equity & Community Supports, the Campus Social Worker contributes to a coordinated model of student support that recognizes the relationships between mental health, disability, identity, belonging, safety, academic participation and the broader social determinants of wellbeing.

## Key Responsibilities

• Participate in shared planning and coordinated service delivery by contributing social-work expertise to portfolio priorities and lead projects that strengthen student wellbeing, access, belonging and institutional responsiveness.

• Provide direct social work support to students through assessment, short-term intervention, case management and wellbeing plans, client-centred advocacy, psychoeducation, resource navigation, referral and follow-up.

• Assess urgent wellbeing concerns, provide stabilization and safety planning, support transitions to and from hospital or community care, and coordinate post-crisis follow-up.

title: Senior Geologist
description:
Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Senior Geologist to join our Mines Technical Services team in Sudbury. This is a permanent position covered under the Collective Agreement between Vale and the Local 2020-05 United Steelworkers. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

The Senior Geologist will support underground and near mine exploration programs, providing technical leadership in drill planning, geological interpretation, and resource conversion. This role requires strong collaboration with Mine Operations, Mine Technical Services and Brownfield Exploration teams to design, execute, and deliver exploration programs that support the site's 5 Year Exploration Budget Cycle. The In-Mine Exploration team supports all underground and near mine exploration activities focusing on converting Exploration Potential and Exploration Targets into mineral resource for future extraction.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Champion and adhere to departmental safety policies, actively supporting a strong safety culture.

• Collaborate with Mine Operations and Brownfield Exploration to develop annual and 5?year exploration plans; generate and evaluate exploration targets, wireframes, and block models.

• Lead planning and execution of underground exploration drilling, including drill layout design (Datamine/Deswik), progress tracking, and invoice review.

• Perform geological work such as core logging, sampling, QA/QC, and physical handling of drill core (300'–1000' per day); conduct periodic underground inspections.

• Communicate updated ore interpretations, prepare technical inputs for MRMR reporting, and ensure data quality meets internal and industry standards.

• Identify performance improvements and provide mentorship and technical guidance to junior geologists and technicians, along with completing additional tasks assigned by the Chief Geologist.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

## About You

## Education:

• Undergraduate Degree in Geology or Geological Engineering or Geological College Diploma.

• Must be registered with the Professional Geoscientists of Ontario with a P.Geo.

## Experience:

• The ideal candidate will possess a minimum of five years of progressive relevant experience in an underground mining environment.

## Skills:

• Advanced understanding and knowledge of Geological Systems including: MEBS (Mines Exploration Bore Hole System), MRM (Mineral Resource Management database and reporting system including Mineability and Dilution), AMGC (All Mines Grade Control), Diamond Drill Hole Layouts.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office products to include Word, Excel, Access, and Outlook. Demonstrated competency in industry software including: DatamineR StudioRM and Deswik CAD.

## Why Sudbury

Greater Sudbury is a vibrant city in northeastern Ontario, renowned for its rich mining history and significant role in Canada's mineral production. The city sits atop one of the world's largest and oldest meteorite impact sites, the Sudbury Basin, which is exceptionally rich in nickel, copper, and other critical minerals that are required for modern technologies such as AI and defence. The mining sector is a cornerstone of Sudbury's economy, driving both employment and economic growth, and Vale Base Metals plays a pivotal role in this regard. Our commitment to the community is as deep as our mines.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Employees engaged by the Company must be lawfully able to work for the Company in the country where the role is located. The Company does not provide immigration, work permit, or permanent residence sponsorship or assistance.

Vale uses artificial intelligence to screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position.

Pay Grade: K

Minimum Starting Salary: $94,059.05

Apply by: November 2, 2026

title: Product Owner
description:
Halifax Harbour Bridges (HHB), a division of Link Nova Scotia, operates and maintains the Angus L. Macdonald and A. Murray MacKay Bridges, supporting over 38 million crossings every year. We're committed to providing safe, efficient, and cost-effective cross-harbour transportation and safety is at the centre of everything we do. It's a shared responsibility across our entire team.

Reporting to the Integrated Technology and Electronic Services Manager, the Product Owner will shape and deliver software products and applications that support HHB's business and operational needs. As the voice of internal and external customers, you will work with business units, technical teams, and vendors to set product direction, translate needs into priorities, and guide solutions from discovery through delivery and continuous improvement.

## Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

• Develop and maintain product vision, strategy, roadmaps, priorities, and success measures aligned with organizational objectives.

• Gather, analyze, and document business and product requirements through user stories, use cases, process flows, acceptance criteria, and other supporting documentation.

• Manage and prioritize product backlogs based on business value, customer needs, risk, regulatory requirements, dependencies, and available resources.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders, development teams, UX/UI resources, vendors, and subject matter experts throughout the product lifecycle.

• Participate in agile delivery activities, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, reviews, retrospectives, and release planning.

• Coordinate user acceptance testing, release readiness, change management, training, and knowledge-transfer activities.

• Monitor product performance, customer feedback, usage data, service levels, and other key performance indicators to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Manage product-related vendor relationships and support procurement activities, including defining requirements, evaluating solutions, monitoring service performance, and escalating issues as appropriate.

• Ensure product requirements and delivery consider security, privacy, accessibility, integration, operational support, organizational policies, and applicable standards.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

## Requirements:

• Post-secondary degree or diploma in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Minimum of five years of relevant experience in business analysis, product ownership, or product management, delivering technology solutions within an enterprise environment.

• Demonstrated experience delivering IT solutions that address organizational and business needs.

• Experience with agile delivery practices, backlog management, requirements gathering, and requirements-management tools.

• Working knowledge of business modelling techniques such as use cases, cross-functional process flows, and wireframes.

• Knowledge of enterprise business and operational platforms, such as financial, customer-facing, reporting, or other systems that support organizational services and operations.

• Strong analytical, critical-thinking, problem-solving, documentation, and decision-making abilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, consultation, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate technical concepts to varied audiences.

• Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Excel, Word, Visio, and Project.

• Assets include a product ownership or product management certification, such as Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), and experience applying UX/UI principles in product delivery.

• Legally eligible to work in Canada

• A valid Class 5 Driver's Licence is required.

We recognize that strong candidates bring different combinations of education, experience, and perspective. If your background aligns closely with this opportunity but you do not meet every listed qualification, we encourage you to apply and explain how your experience would help you succeed in the role.

## Position details:

• This is one full-time, permanent, non-union position working 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday.

• Occasional on-call response and planned or unplanned work outside regular hours may be required to support operational needs. This work will be compensated in accordance with HHB policy.

• The annual salary range for this position is $73,376 - $91,720.

## What HHB Offers:

• Competitive salary and a comprehensive total rewards package.

• Comprehensive benefits package such as Group Health, Dental, and Disability benefits.

• A fantastic defined-benefit pension plan

• Professional development and learning opportunities

• Employee and Family Assistance Program

• A collaborative and supportive work environment

• Opportunities to contribute to meaningful projects and organizational initiatives

• Commitment to employee well-being, accessibility, equity, diversity, and inclusion

## Working conditions:

This position is primarily based in an HHB office environment and involves minimal physical effort. The work requires sustained attention when gathering and documenting requirements, reviewing product and procurement materials, analyzing performance information, facilitating meetings, conducting testing, and preparing reports and recommendations. At times, the role must manage competing priorities, stakeholder or vendor issues, and complex or time-sensitive matters. Periodic work outside regular business hours may be required to support product releases, implementations, or issue resolution.

## How to Apply:

Interested candidates must submit a resume and complete all pre-screening questions by 4:00 p.m. on Friday, November 6, 2026. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and shortlisted candidates may be contacted and interviewed before the closing date; however, no hiring decision will be made until the posting has closed.

If you require an accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact recruitment@hdbc.ns.ca.

HHB is committed to fostering an equitable, diverse, inclusive, and accessible workplace where employees feel respected, valued, and able to contribute. We welcome applications from qualified candidates with diverse backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and identities. Accommodation is available throughout the recruitment and selection process upon request.

Employment is conditional upon satisfactory reference checks, background checks, and confirmation of eligibility to work in Canada. description:
## Learning Specialist for Professional Learning

## Department of Education and Early Childhood Development

## Contract

## Open

## Fredericton

Interested in making a difference in our province? We encourage you to Choose GNB!

## Who we are:

The work we do has a positive impact on our communities and helps improve the everyday lives of New Brunswickers. Together, we are over 45,000 New Brunswickers who are passionate problem-solvers, who make a difference and are proud to call New Brunswick home.

The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is seeking a Learning Specialist for Professional Learning to join the Digital Learning and System Excellence Branch. The Learning Specialist provides provincial leadership in designing, coordinating, and advancing teacher-centred professional learning that aligns educator growth with student learning needs and improved student outcomes.

The position plays a key role in advancing Education Plan Action A.5- Professional Learning Framework and supporting the New Brunswick Standards of Practice for Teachers, working closely with districts, schools, the NBTA, post-secondary institutions, the Learning Specialist responsible for leadership development and NB Lead, and other partners, while recognizing the distinct roles and responsibilities of partners across the education system.

## What you will do:

• Lead implementation and ongoing development of Education Plan Action A.5 - Professional Learning Framework, including defining provincial expectations for ongoing professional learning, aligning it with student outcomes and Education Plan priorities, and monitoring participation and impact.

• Coordinate with districts, schools, the NBTA, post-secondary institutions, and professional learning providers to strengthen coherence across professional learning priorities, resources, and supports, and serve as a provincial liaison to identify emerging needs.

• Collaborate with district professional learning leads and coordinators to share effective practices, and with the Learning Specialist responsible for leadership development and NB Lead to align teacher professional learning with school leadership development.

• Promote evidence-informed professional learning that is teacher-centred, collaborative, sustained, and connected to student learning, including job-embedded and inquiry-based approaches such as the Cycle of Inquiry and professional learning communities.

• Guide departmental and district teams in designing and evaluating professional learning using principles of adult learning and instructional design, and develop practical approaches to monitoring participation and impact on educator practice and, where appropriate, student outcomes.

• Support the integration of the New Brunswick Standards of Practice for Teachers into professional learning and early career supports.

• Manage the Professional Learning Hub and coordinate provincial professional learning planning and calendars to align efforts and reduce duplication across the Department and districts.

• Advise departmental teams on the professional learning and training needs of provincial initiatives (such as digital literacy and AI), including in-person, virtual, blended, and job-embedded approaches.

• Coordinate provincial supports for early career teachers, including induction, mentorship, and coaching, in partnership with districts and educational partners.

• Support the development of classroom management training and classroom readiness expectations with post-secondary institutions, and the alignment of teacher preparation with classroom realities.

• Advise the educator recruitment and retention team, and contribute to retention strategies through effective early career supports.

• Manage budgets and resources for provincial professional learning initiatives, develop communication strategies to promote opportunities and supports, and contribute to branch and departmental planning.

• Travel within the province, including occasional work in schools with teachers and, at times, in the presence of students.

## Who you are:

You are a collaborative leader who is passionate about professional learning and its impact on teaching and student learning. You are skilled at bringing people and ideas together, building strong relationships, and turning priorities into practical approaches that support educators. You are comfortable working across schools, districts, and provincial teams and can balance system-wide direction with the needs and realities of educators. You are organized, reflective, and confident leading initiatives in a complex education environment.

Your attitude, skills and interests are just as important as your area of study. We are looking for diverse backgrounds that bring a combination of the following:

## Required Competencies:

• A master's degree in education.

• A minimum of seven (7) years of teaching experience within an inclusive K-12 public education system.

• Experience designing, coordinating, facilitating, or supporting professional learning with educators and school or district leaders.

• Experience coordinating projects or initiatives involving multiple partners.

• Experience using digital technologies to support project coordination, communication, collaboration, and learning.

• Written and spoken competence in English.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Please state your language capability on your application.

## Nice to have:

• Written and spoken competence in French.

• Demonstrated knowledge of effective professional learning, adult learning, instructional practice, and approaches to supporting educator growth.

• Experience with job-embedded, inquiry-based professional learning, including the Cycle of Inquiry and professional learning communities.

• Knowledge or experience with New Brunswick's provincial K-12 education system and the New Brunswick Standards of Practice for Teachers.

• Experience supporting early career teachers through induction, mentorship, or coaching.

• Experience developing educational resources or managing digital professional learning platforms.

• Experience analyzing and communicating program participation and outcomes.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

## Behavioural Competencies:

• Effective Interactive Communication

• Initiative

• Collaboration and Teamwork

• Creativity and Innovation

## Technical Competencies:

• Planning and Results Orientation

• Partnership Development

## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context: The Eastern Region maintains and supports approximately 3,500 NL Housing rental properties on the Avalon and Burin Peninsulas through offices in St. John's (Avalon) and Marystown. The region provides a wide range of services, including receiving and processing rental applications; administering rental accounts and lease compliance provisions; providing various client services and tenant relations including eviction prevention, and monitoring, facilitating and administering property maintenance. A variety of programs designed to support low to moderate income households and homeowners are also delivered. Regional staff members are involved in the delivery of the Provincial Home Repair, Home Modification, Home Energy Savings, Partner Managed Housing, and Rent Supplement Programs.

title: Bilingual (French & English languages) Member Service Representative
