CAA Atlantic (https://atlantic.caa.ca/) is a member-based organization serving over 320,000 members across Atlantic Canada, with headquarters in Saint John, New Brunswick.

CAA Atlantic is part of the national CAA federation with almost 7 million members across the country! CAA is one of the largest, most trusted and respected consumer-based organizations in Canada. We provide emergency roadside assistance, travel services, and exclusive savings and rewards for our members. We're deeply focused on helping Atlantic Canadians travel safely and confidently, whether they are on the road close to home or planning trips around the world. We are also proud to be recognized as one of Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures by Waterstone Human Capital (https://waterstonehc.com/canadas-most-admired/canadas-most-admired-corporate-cultures/corporate-culture-winners/).

"It's so fun to work with CAA Atlantic!" - Linda Landry, Travel Advisor

To learn more about the CAA Atlantic employee experience visit us online:

Careers CAA Atlantic- Work With Us - https://atlantic.caa.ca/about/careers/work-with-us

Careers CAA Atlantic- Team Member Stories - https://atlantic.caa.ca/about/careers/team-member-stories

Are you someone who enjoys interacting with people? Are you someone whose natural motive is to help others? Are you savvy with digital mapping technologies? Do you easily adapt to using new technologies and processes?

In this position you will play a critical role in supporting CAA Atlantic members when they need us most. Working in a fast‑paced, people‑first environment, you'll be the first point of contact for members requesting roadside assistance across Atlantic Canada.

This is a hybrid role with work required on site at our Contact Centre, as well as the ability to work virtually some of the time.

This position will provide you with full time hours within our Roadside Contact Centre where you will interact and support thousands of members traveling throughout Atlantic Canada needing immediate roadside help.

As a Bilingual (French & English languages) Member Service Representative , located at our office in Saint John, New Brunswick, you'll provide calm, clear, and compassionate support by answering inbound calls, responding to call‑back requests, and ensuring members feel reassured and cared for during stressful situations. This role offers meaningful, real‑world customer service experience while working at one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers organization known for helping people travel safely and confidently.

Acadia University is seeking an innovative, technically skilled, and collaborative Simulation and Clinical Skills Technician to support simulation-based healthcare education within the School of Nursing.

The role provides expertise in high-fidelity simulators, clinical equipment, audio-visual technology, simulation software, and other technologies that enhance student learning and clinical competence.

This position is responsible for ensuring that clinical skills laboratories and simulation spaces are organized, properly maintained, appropriately stocked, and ready for teaching.

• Provide training to faculty and student assistants involved in simulated learning.

• Monitor, maintain, calibrate, and coordinate updates for simulation and clinical equipment, including simulators, IV pumps, vital signs machines, computers, and laptops.

• Ensure equipment is charged, functional, clean, and ready for teaching.

• Maintain accurate inventories of clinical skills supplies and identify procurement needs.

• Troubleshoot equipment, technology, space, and supply issues before, during, and after educational activities.

• Coordinate repairs, maintenance, deliveries, work orders, linens, and waste management related to clinical teaching spaces.

• Assist with the setup and teardown of clinical skills and simulation environments.

• Work with faculty and NPEs before each academic term to plan simulation and clinical skills activities and schedules.

• Coordinate bookings for simulation and clinical laboratory spaces.

• Support clinical skills components of School of Nursing tours, orientations, and events.

• Coordinate equipment training for faculty and support staff.

• Maintain term schedules for clinical skills training spaces.

title: IT Security Analyst
description:
Are you passionate about safeguarding IT systems and ensuring robust cybersecurity measures? We are seeking a detail-oriented IT Security Analyst to join our team and strengthen our defenses against cyber threats. If you have a keen eye for vulnerabilities and a commitment to protecting sensitive information, we invite you to be a key player in our cybersecurity initiatives.

Position Type: Regular

Location: Any NBCC campus location

Salary Range: $81,146 to $98,046 per annum

Qualifications

## Education/Experience:

• Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field. A two (2) year diploma in a related Information Technology discipline and four (4) years of related experience.

## Technical Skills:

• Experience in security, systems, endpoint, and/or network analysis is an asset.

• Industry standard Cybersecurity certification such as CISSP, CRISC, CISM an asset, or willing to work toward obtaining.

• Strong knowledge of cybersecurity principles, risk management, and compliance requirements.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to convey complex security concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Professional Skills:

• Must be able to work independently or as part of a team.

• Flexibility in working hours, including participation in occasional after-hours support and time shifting.

• Participation in after-hours emergency response.

• Ability to prioritize work, apply departmental standards, and meet deadlines.

• Ability to adapt to changes in work environment.

• Adapts easily to and welcomes technological changes.

• Exercises initiative to independently learn new technologies.

• Team Collaboration: Should have a proven track record of working effectively in a team environment, contributing positively to team operations, and working relationships.

• Empathy and Emotional Intelligence: Demonstrated ability to understand and empathize with others, showing sensitivity to their perspectives and needs.

Candidates must clearly demonstrate how they meet these qualifications on their resumes.

Other combinations of education and experience may be considered as equivalent. Subject to competition response, the minimum qualifications may be raised.

Responsibilities
Reporting to the Manager of Infrastructure and Cybersecurity, the IT Security Analyst advances cybersecurity incident prevention and response across NBCC by promoting cybersecurity awareness and best practices among staff. The incumbent also plays a pivotal role in safeguarding NBCC's digital assets by assessing and strengthening its security posture through close collaboration with NBCC staff and partner institutions on incident and vulnerability prevention, monitoring, detection, and response.

In this role, you will:

• Threat Detection and Mitigation: Leverage tools and technologies to monitor network traffic, identify anomalies, and promptly respond to potential security incidents. Implement and sustain security measures aimed at safeguarding against cyber threats, malware, and unauthorized access, while also collaborating with vendors to ensure comprehensive protection.

• Incident Response: Develop and execute incident response plans, ensuring a rapid and effective response to cybersecurity incidents. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to contain and remediate security breaches while minimizing potential damage.

• Vulnerability Monitoring and Management: Conduct regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing to identify and address weaknesses in the institution's systems and infrastructure. Identify and suggest proactive measures to mitigate vulnerabilities and enhance the institution's overall security posture.

• Security Awareness: Design and implement cybersecurity awareness training programs for NBCC staff, faculty, and students to raise awareness about common cyber threats, social engineering tactics, and best practices for maintaining a secure digital environment.

• Policy Development and Compliance: Create and revise cybersecurity policies, protocols, and standards, guaranteeing they adhere to industry standards and regulatory requirements.

• Collaboration and Communication: Collaborate with IT teams, management, and end-users to foster a culture of cybersecurity awareness. Communicate effectively about security risks, best practices, and updates, aiming to create a collective understanding of the importance of cybersecurity.

At NBCC, you will join a purpose-driven organization that is shaping the future of New Brunswick through education, workforce development, and community impact. In addition to meaningful work, we offer:

• An inclusive culture where people feel valued, supported, and connected.

• Opportunities to grow as a leader through continuous learning and development.

• Membership in the New Brunswick Public Service Pension Plan.

• Competitive vacation, sick leave, and volunteer leave provisions.

• Tuition support programs for employees and tuition benefits for eligible family members.

• The opportunity to work alongside engaged colleagues who are committed to student success and organizational excellence.

Curious to learn more about the benefits NBCC has to offer? Visit our Careers Page.

## Director, Food Programs & Volunteering

## Full-time, Regular

## This posting is open to internal and external candidates.

The North Grove strives for a staff composition that is diverse and reflective of the community of Dartmouth North. Individuals who identify as Indigenous, African Nova Scotian, Black and/or from another group that is under-represented in workplaces are encouraged to apply and self-identify.

## Priority will be given to applicants from these equity-deserving groups.

## About The North Grove:

The North Grove (www.thenorthgrove.ca) is a dynamic community hub, situated in the diverse community of Dartmouth North. We offer services, programs, and space for people to learn and connect through family support, food, and friendship. We also partner with more than 25 organizations to help improve health, reduce social isolation and strengthen connections in this community.

The North Grove team is made up of 35 staff. We work with a dedicated Board of Directors, and more than 170 community volunteers. Collaboration, creativity, and community-centered decision making are important to us.

Diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB) are central to our work and as a team we have committed to a DEIB framework that includes ongoing learning opportunities, policy development, and partnership work.

Learn more about our DEIB commitment here: https://www.thenorthgrove.ca/deib

Our approach is rooted in strengths-based practice. This practice sees all members of the community as having resourceful and resilient qualities and strives to support individual self-determination. We seek applicants who share our commitment to working within this model.

## The Opportunity:

As a Right to Food Partner and the first Community Food Centre in Atlantic Canada, we have spent the last eleven years growing the roots of our food programming and creating opportunities for people of all ages to come together around food. From our flourishing community farm to our lively community meals, cooking classes, and subsidized market, we are committed to dignified access to food. And we believe in the power of facing life's challenges together - that's why 170+ volunteers, many of whom are program participants, share their time with us every week to drive change in this community.

We are now excited to be embarking on a search for a Director, Food Programs & Volunteering to join our leadership team and guide the next stage of our work in Dartmouth North.

This role oversees program design, delivery, and evaluation across all our Community Food Center programming: community meals, food skills, farm, market, and volunteering programs, ensuring alignment with the organization's mission and strategic plan. The Director builds and fosters strong partnerships and positive participant experiences, supports staff development, and ensures programs meet the objectives of the strategic plan and the evolving needs of the community.

If you thrive in roles that connect big picture strategy with operational details, have experience leading teams, and love working in community, we want to hear from you!

Hours: 37.5 hours per week Monday to Friday, with some evenings and weekends as required
Reporting structure: This position reports to the Executive Director
Works closely with: Director, Family Programs & Community Navigation; Director, Strategic Initiatives & Engagement; Manager, Operations

## The Director, Food Programs & Volunteering will:

• Provide strategic leadership for programs in the following areas: Volunteering, Community Meals, Food Skills, Farm, Market, aligning initiatives with the organization's mission, vision, and strategic plan.

• Supervise and mentor program coordinators offering coaching, professional development, and performance communication to ensure strong collaboration, growth and success.

• Collaborate closely with the Director, Family Programs & Navigation to lead organization-wide initiatives including annual program planning, program evaluation, and staff development.

• Design strategies and provide leadership in supporting volunteers, with a focus on engaging community members, providing an inclusive, strengths-based experience, and mentoring staff to maximize the impact of volunteers.

• Work with the leadership team to ensure implementation of The North Grove's DEIB strategy, and model the principles of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in all aspects of their work.

• Work with the Executive Director and program coordinators to develop and oversee program budgets, ensuring fiscal responsibility, alignment with funding requirements, and efficient use of resources.

• Develop, oversee and maintain community partnerships with organizations including Right to Food, Feed Nova Scotia, and others, to strengthen collaboration with other food security and volunteer-based organizations.

• Ensure program compliance and reporting, including funder deliverables, outcome tracking, and evaluation metrics.

• Support a culture of continuous learning, embedding staff feedback, participant perspectives, and best practices into program improvement.

• Act as a senior leader within the organization and external spokesperson, supporting organization-wide planning, decision-making, and representing food & volunteering program staff on the leadership team

• Monitor and support day-to-day operations to ensure staff and participants are well-supported and that responses to emerging needs are timely and appropriate.

What you will bring:
The North Grove is seeking to build a diverse team and values lived experience and non-traditional ways of learning. If you don't meet all the criteria below but you are excited about the job description and believe you bring unique experience and perspective, please apply!

• Post-secondary education in social work, public administration, nutrition, food systems, community development, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training and demonstrated experience.

• Demonstrated progressive experience supervising managers and staff, acting as a role model and providing mentorship, coaching, and performance management to grow and develop staff.

• A minimum of 5 years of experience in program design, delivery, and evaluation, preferably within a non-profit, community-based or food-related setting.

• Experience leading a team in a food-based setting (restaurant, kitchen, farm, food bank, youth cooking, etc.) is strongly preferred.

• Proven track record of developing and managing budgets, ensuring financial accountability and alignment with strategic priorities.

• Experience building and maintaining partnerships with funders, government agencies, and community organizations.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing reports, funding proposals, and presentations.

• Strong interpersonal skills, including the ability to give and receive constructive feedback, navigate nuanced and difficult conversations with objectivity and sensitivity, and address challenges with clarity, fairness and respect.

• Demonstrated ability to integrate equity, diversity, and inclusion principles into program design and organizational leadership.

• Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, and drive innovation.

• Experience working with people who face significant barriers, with an understanding of root causes of community issues, particularly those affecting equity-deserving communities.

• Excellent organizational skills and proven experience managing complex projects and balancing multiple priorities effectively.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and comfort with database or program evaluation tools.

• Flexibility to work occasional evenings or weekends to attend community events or represent the organization.

• Ability to work collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team environment

• A sense of fun and a commitment to kindness and empathy

What We Offer:
The North Grove is a caring and high-energy work environment. Staff wellbeing is prioritized, and we provide training opportunities, employer-paid medical/dental benefits from day one, 4% employer-paid RRSP contribution after probation, 4 weeks of paid vacation, all statutory holidays, paid sick time and 4 personal days. A computer is provided as well as a telephone stipend.

Salary hiring range: $72,100-$80,000 annually*

*Compensation will be determined based on candidate skills, experience, and internal equity.
Future earning potential for this role is currently $92,700

## The Selection Process:

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short initial phone screening call to go over the basics of the position, get a high-level understanding of your experience, and answer any questions you may have.

Following the phone screening calls, a handful of candidates will be invited to an in-person interview at The North Grove, followed by a second interview if required. Candidates are encouraged to submit any accommodation requests to the email below.

Everyone who applies for this position will receive an email update from The North Grove within one month of the application deadline.

## How to Apply:

To apply, please send a cover letter and resume in one document by email to Naomi Samela, Operations Manager, at careers@thenorthgrove.ca under the subject line: Application for Director, Food Programs & Volunteering, by Monday, November 2nd at 9am.

description:

From utensils to cellphones to satellites, our operations simplify daily life and enhance connectivity. Our metals are integral to life-saving medical equipment and the electric vehicles driving the fight against climate change – our work truly matters.

Join our diverse team of 15,000 talented individuals committed to transforming critical minerals into prosperity and sustainable development in countries like Canada, Brazil, Indonesia, the United Kingdom, and Japan. We invite you to use your skills with us and contribute to something meaningful and enduring.

## The Opportunity

We are seeking a Specialist – Project Planning & Integration - to join our VBM / CTO / Studies / Project Controls team at Sudbury, Ontario.

This is a permanent position reporting to the Sr. Manager, Project Controls - Canada and supporting Vale Base Metals' Canadian studies portfolio. The role is responsible for planning and scheduling across multiple studies and projects, ensuring the development, integration, and governance of study schedules and project execution schedules throughout the project lifecycle. As the planning discipline lead for the Canadian studies portfolio, the successful candidate will ensure that project schedules are fully integrated with estimating, risk management, cost control, change management, and performance management processes. This role also serves as a key planning advisor to Canadian Operations by providing independent schedule reviews, technical support, and planning capability development across the organization.

## About You

You are an experienced planning and scheduling professional with a strong background supporting complex capital projects within mining, metals, energy, infrastructure, or other asset-intensive industries. You are skilled at translating technical scope, execution strategies, procurement requirements, construction sequencing, and operational readiness activities into realistic and achievable schedules.

You thrive in environments where schedule integrity, project governance, and effective decision-making are critical to success. Your ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, challenge assumptions constructively, and provide schedule-driven insights allows you to influence project outcomes and improve delivery certainty.

## In this role, you will:

## Planning and Scheduling for Studies

• Develop, maintain, and govern integrated study schedules for Canadian PEA, PFS, and FS projects.

• Establish schedule frameworks, work breakdown structures (WBS), milestones, logic networks, schedule assumptions, and critical path methodologies aligned with Vale standards.

• Validate schedules prepared by engineering consultants and EPCM contractors to ensure logic integrity, realistic durations, resource assumptions, and alignment with project execution strategies.

• Perform schedule quality assessments, critical path analysis, float analysis, scenario planning, and schedule optimization reviews.

• Develop Basis of Schedule documentation and maintain schedule governance throughout study lifecycles.

• Lead schedule reviews and provide schedule recommendations supporting phase-gate and investment decision processes.

## Development of Project Execution Schedules

• Develop and maintain project execution schedules covering engineering, procurement, contracting, construction, commissioning, and ramp-up phases.

• Collaborate closely with engineering, procurement, contracts, construction, HSE, permitting, operations readiness, and commissioning teams to create credible and executable schedules.

• Integrate execution strategies, contracting approaches, long-lead procurement requirements, construction sequencing, and site constraints within schedule logic.

• Evaluate alternative execution scenarios and scheduling strategies to support study recommendations and project planning decisions.

• Establish Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 schedule hierarchies and milestone frameworks supporting project governance and execution readiness.

## Progress Measurement and Performance Reporting

• Establish project progress measurement systems and reporting methodologies.

• Monitor schedule performance, update schedules regularly, identify variances, and forecast project completion dates.

• Develop schedule dashboards, milestone reports, portfolio summaries, resource demand forecasts, and schedule performance analyses.

• Identify emerging schedule risks and opportunities and recommend mitigation or recovery actions.

• Maintain auditable records of schedule baselines, updates, assumptions, forecasts, and revisions

## Integrated Project Controls

• Ensure schedules are fully integrated with estimating, risk management, cost control, change management, and performance management disciplines.

• Partner with the Sr. Specialist, Estimating & Cost Control to develop integrated project baselines, cost-loaded schedules, and cash flow forecasts.

• Support schedule risk analysis activities by working closely with the Sr. Specialist, Project Risk Management to identify schedule uncertainty, model risk events, and establish schedule contingencies.

• Ensure approved scope, cost, schedule, and risk changes are appropriately reflected within project baselines.

• Support integrated reporting of schedule, cost, and risk performance to provide a consistent project controls framework.

## Standards and Continuous Improvement

• Maintain planning standards, templates, procedures, and Primavera P6 governance structures for Canadian projects.

• Develop and maintain schedule benchmarking databases and historical planning information to improve future project planning.

• Support implementation of digital tools, automation initiatives, Power BI reporting solutions, and emerging technologies that improve planning effectiveness.

• Collaborate with global project controls teams to align planning methodologies, standards, and best practices.

• Manage external planning consultants and support providers, ensuring quality, consistency, and value delivery.

## Experience

• Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in project planning, scheduling, project controls, or capital project delivery.

• Extensive experience supporting large and complex capital projects within mining, metals, energy, infrastructure, industrial, or construction environments.

• Proven experience supporting studies and project development phases including PEA, PFS, FS, detailed engineering, construction, and commissioning.

• Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining integrated project schedules using Primavera P6.

• Experience conducting schedule quality reviews, critical path analysis, scenario planning, schedule recovery analysis, and forecasting.

• Experience supporting project governance reviews, investment decisions, and stage-gate processes.

• Experience working with engineering consultants, EPCM contractors, owners' teams, and operations stakeholders.

## Education

• Undergraduate Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, or a related technical discipline.

• Postgraduate qualification in Project Management, Engineering, Construction Management, or related discipline is considered an asset.

## Skills & Competencies

• Expert proficiency in project planning, including schedule development, WBS structures, coding systems, resource and cost loading, baselining, reporting, and contractor schedule integration.

• Strong knowledge of project controls disciplines, including planning, estimating, cost control, risk management, performance management, and change control.

• Understanding of AACE planning and scheduling recommended practices, PMI methodologies, and capital project governance frameworks.

• Experience performing schedule quality assessments, critical path analysis, float analysis, and schedule risk assessments.

• Strong understanding of engineering, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness processes.

• Knowledge of mining, processing, infrastructure, and brownfield project environments.

• Proficiency in Primavera P6, Power BI, Excel, and project reporting tools.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-support capabilities.

• Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.

• Ability to challenge assumptions constructively while maintaining collaborative working relationships.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to support multiple concurrent studies and projects.

• Familiarity with automation, data analytics, and AI-enabled project controls solutions is considered an asset.

## What We Offer You

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans, and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

Sudbury is one of Canada's premier mining centres and a global leader in mining innovation, technology, and sustainability. Home to world-class mining operations and a highly skilled workforce, Sudbury provides unique opportunities to work on industry-leading projects that support the growing demand for critical minerals worldwide. Working in Sudbury offers access to excellent outdoor recreation, strong community connections, and a high quality of life while contributing to the future of responsible resource development and the global energy transition.

This permanent position reports to the Sr. Manager, Project Controls – Canada and provides senior functional leadership for Project Risk Management across Vale Base Metals' Canadian studies and project portfolio. The role establishes and continuously improves the framework, governance, standards and tools applied throughout the project lifecycle, leads major risk assessments, and serves as the primary interface with Enterprise Risk Management (ERM). As a trusted advisor to project teams and senior leadership, it provides independent challenge and insight on threats, opportunities and uncertainties, ensuring these inform planning, execution and investment decisions across all disciplines and functions.

## About You

You are a strategic and collaborative risk management professional with extensive experience supporting large, complex capital projects within mining industry. You are highly skilled at facilitating discussions, challenging assumptions, and helping project teams proactively manage uncertainty. You possess strong leadership and influencing abilities, enabling you to build credibility with project teams, senior management, and key stakeholders.

You thrive in complex environments where balancing technical, commercial, schedule, cost, organizational, and external risks is critical to project success. Your ability to translate risk insights into practical business decisions allows you to drive value and improve project outcomes.

title: Senior Finance Analyst - EM Domestic Relief
description:
Title: Senior Finance Analyst - EM Domestic Relief

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The incumbent will be reporting to the Finance Manager, Emergency Domestic Relief Finance Services, the Senior Finance Analyst will provide finance support services to programs managed through Domestic Relief Operations. The incumbent will provide both financial and analytical reporting to ensure the effective management of the administrative and financial aspects of government and non-government funded projects, maintenance, and analysis of monthly reporting and compliance with the CRC accounting policies and procedures. They will contribute to the achievement of the Emergency Domestic Relief Finance Services mandate: establish, modernize and maintain effective, efficient finance systems, processes, procedures, frameworks and work practices to coordinate financial monitoring and ensure the provision of timely reports, analysis and advice to operations and/or management.

## In this role, you will:

• Lead the month-end process for the EM - Domestic Relief Finance Services team ensuring all deadlines are met.

• Prepare monthly budget/variance report to budget holders.

• Prepare commitment schedules in order to assist program areas in revising project budgets and forecasts.

• Assist and support the annual budgetary preparation and monitoring progress.

• Identify financial risks the projects and/or departments may be exposed to and discuss possible scenarios with Finance Manager and Program Manager to mitigate (or eliminate) these risks.

• Oversee cash flow and cost control measures; accounts receivable and payable, data entry, month-end closure, reconciliations, etc.

• Provide financial and statistical analysis, reports, advice, and recommendations to the Finance Manager and/or Director, Finance Services on a regular basis and in a timely and accurate manner.

• Develop reporting standards, emphasizing key financial and non-financial metrics to inform decision making.

• Validate financial transactions for general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable and trust modules before posting batches.

• Evaluate field systems and controls to ensure reporting of accurate, complete, and timely financial information that accounts for the funds used on the field.

## What we are looking for:

• Post secondary level education in finance, business administration, accounting or a related discipline or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

• A professional accounting designation (CPA) and background in audit and assurance is preferred.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

• Knowledge of other languages from countries in which International Operations works will also be of added value.

• Minimum 5 years of progressive, relevant experience in financial management, preferably in project/program management.

• Knowledge of financial and management accounting, GAAP.

• Computer literacy is essential. Knowledge of current word processing and spreadsheet (advanced level in Excel) applications and accounting software (i.e., D) is required.

• Experience working directly with program managers to provide financial advice.

• Customer focus with the ability to explain complex issues in plain language to non-experts.

• Excellent budgeting and financial management skills.

• Proactive approach with strong critical thinking, business acumen and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast paced, ambiguous, global environment with multiple conflicting demands and changing circumstances and demonstrated positive experience working in a cross-cultural environment.

## Working conditions:

• The majority of the work will be performed in a clean and comfortable environment.

At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services(ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Are you seeking a career where you have endless opportunities to positively impact the lives of vulnerable children and families?

We are hiring Social Workers across Nova Scotia in our Adoption, Foster Care, Disclosure Program, Screening and Regional Resource programs. Under the provisions of the Children and Family Services Act (CFSA) and An Act respecting First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Children, Youth, and Families (FNIM), your role will actively work towards providing ongoing services to parents and children, and collaborate with program areas to assess families for the placement of children. You will join an interdisciplinary team and have an opportunity to positively bring about change.

Primary Accountabilities
Social Workers ensure the health, safety, and well-being of children in the care of the Minister and those who remain in the care of their parents where concerns exist about their health and safety. Daily, you actively work to engage people and communities to build resilience, address challenges and trauma, and create change. Every day is different, and you will encounter unique challenges with responsibilities ranging from:

• Collaborating with individuals, families and communities

• Planning, developing, and monitoring case plans with birth families kinship caregivers, foster parents, adopting parents, childcare staff

• Working closely with the community and advocating for connections to community resources

• Participating in risk assessments, court testimonies, and evaluations

• Planning with and supervising children in care of the Minister

• Recruiting, preparing, assessing, and supporting foster and adoptive parents

A completed Bachelor of Social Work or Master of Social Work is required as well as a valid drivers license. You must be eligible for registration with the Nova Scotia College of Social Workers (NSCSW).

You are also:

• A strong team player

• Empowered to impact change

• Compassionate, reliable, and resourceful.

You are understanding of child development, family dynamics, trauma-informed care, counselling, community resources, and are well versed in effective intervention strategies. Your problem-solving skills and experience, combined with your creative thinking, work to strengthen, and improve support while working with children and families.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Working Conditions
Most of your work involves meeting with clients in their homes or with service providers. This necessitates considerable driving time, sometimes in adverse weather conditions.

On a rotating schedule, you may be required to provide child and family wellbeing services for your designated area, after regular business hours. This will include working on weekends and reporting to the provincial after-hours response team. You may be required to work beyond regular business hours on short notice.

Your resiliency is essential to meet the physical and emotional demands of this position. You will be immersed in high-stress and crises, with plenty of support and resources accessible to you. You must be able to work under pressure and be personally and professionally committed to inclusively working with culturally diverse individuals.

This posting will be used to fill opportunities in either the Foster Care or Adoption Program areas.

description:

Type of Employment: Permanent

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and Disability Support Program(DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong dedicated network of supports and staff, to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity
Wood Street Campus (WSC) is a cornerstone in providing specialized treatment services for children and youth in the care of the Minister. Operating 24/7, we are dedicated to supporting young people and helping them develop the skills, resilience, and confidence to thrive in their communities. The work is deeply rewarding, offering the chance to make a meaningful difference in the lives of children who need it most.

Our campus offers two (2) programs: a secure treatment program and a long-term treatment program. You may work in either or both.

As Unit Supervisor, you will provide steady, consistent leadership that fosters positive relationships among staff and youth, builds morale, and ensures a safe and supportive environment. You will play a key role in both day-to-day operations and long-term outcomes by supporting the safety, security, and well-being of youth and staff. You will also maintain dynamic and static security measures in both secure and long-term treatment settings and provid direct supervision, guidance, and development for Youth Workers who deliver treatment and case management services

Primary Accountabilities
As the Unit Supervisor, we count on your effective and consistent leadership to ensure and maintain positive relationships with staff, youth, and community partners, along with high morale and safety. A few of your key responsibilities will include:

• Scheduling and managing the daily operations, including treatment plan strategies, the application of case management, and overseeing the delivery of emotional and social programming for youth.

• Supervising, coaching and assigning work to Youth Workers, student placements and volunteers.

• Supporting recruitment, performance management, attendance management, payroll reporting, employee development and workplace health and safety processes.

• Ensuring the safety and security of youth and employees through facilitating, monitoring, and maintaining both dynamic and static security on campus.

• Providing appropriate interventions in response to managing acting-out/pain-based youth behaviour.

You may occasionally, in the absence of the Program Manager, assume responsibility for the daily operations and may issue Secure Treatment Certificates and Leaves of Absence under the authority of the Children and Family Services Act.

Qualifications and Experience
You have completed a related degree and several years of experience in child and youth care treatment programs, including demonstrated success in a leadership role.

You bring:

• Proven ability to provide both individual and group supervision, offering direction, coaching, and modelling of effective youth care interventions.

• Familiarity with culturally responsive care for diverse populations.

• Strong understanding of short-term crisis programs, youth-in-care treatment, and group care dynamics.

• Solid working knowledge of safety, security, program operations, and staffing in a treatment setting.

• Exceptional verbal and written communication abilities, with the interpersonal skills needed to build trust, maintain positive relationships, and work collaboratively.

• Ability to lead, motivate, and support a team of Youth Workers in an intensive, high-demand environment, while fostering a positive and professional workplace culture.

• Skills in assessing situations quickly, making sound decisions under pressure, and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Assets include:

• Certification in Non-Violent Crisis Intervention (NVCI), Therapeutic Crisis Intervention (TCI), or similar de-escalation and intervention training.

• Training or certification in trauma-informed care and attachment-based approaches

• Experience supervising in a unionized environment.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
You will work in a treatment facility that operates 24 hours a day, seven (7) days a week and rotating shift work is required. Working hours are from 7 a.m.- 7 p.m. and 7 p.m.- 7 a.m., as assigned. You will work every second weekend.

Components of the treatment program/campus may be secured. You will facilitate and maintain both dynamic and static security to provide safety and security for youth, visitors, staff, and the public. While we take precautions, children and youth may demonstrate harmful/aggressive behaviours and Nonviolent Crisis Intervention (NCI) techniques are utilized to manage these behaviours; you must be able to perform these techniques.

Personal resiliency is essential to meet the physical and emotional demands of this position. You will be subjected to a high degree of stress and must be able to work under pressure and in crises.

Additional Information
We may use this competition to fill additional Unit Supervisor opportunities within 1 year of the closing date of the competition.

• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Engaging workplace. Our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in. We have forward-thinking policies and strategies.

• Countless Career Paths.

The Justice Supports and Services Division of the Department of Justice consists of three programs: each providing Nova Scotians access to critical programming and support. Victim Services offers support to victims of crime as their case moves through the justice system.
The Maintenance Enforcement Program (MEP) is a free service of the Nova Scotia Department of Justice that helps you make or receive court-ordered maintenance payments when your court order is enrolled with the program and can take steps to enforce maintenance orders when payments are not made. The MEP operates under the laws set out in the Maintenance Enforcement Act. Benefits of enrolling in the MEP include: we keep an accurate record of all payments made and received; we protect your personal information; we act as a buffer between payors and recipients; we work with the MEPs in other provinces if the payor or recipient lives outside Nova Scotia; and we can take enforcement action if payments are not made. • Design and develop standard and non-standard repairs.

• Conduct and/or peer review/check structural analyses of repairs and modifications.

• Conduct effective communications and act as liaison on technical matters with representatives from MOBs, Department of National Defense (DND), Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), Design Support Network (DSN) elements, and Design Authorities.

• Conduct and support the assessment of airworthiness risk on the aircraft structure including preparation and review of Airworthiness Impart Assessment (AWIAs) and Records of Airworthiness Risks Management (RARMs).

• Manage tasks related to implementing and monitoring corrective actions for structural systems. This includes addressing in-service difficulty reports, flight safety reports, special inspections, service bulletins, and airworthiness directives.

• Prepare and review engineering reports, technical memoranda and technical directions.

• Provide support to the configuration management and data management activities of the department.

• Perform airworthiness functions as a recognized Design Engineer (DE) when authorized.

• Review and approve engineering data within assigned scope of approval.

• Support engineering special projects and initiatives as requested.

• Support the activities of the department in respect to maintenance program monitoring, maintenance rationalization, and maintenance requirements analysis.

• Support identification of performance criteria/objectives for CH149 aircraft structures, in-service performance monitoring to these criteria, and technical investigations to identify and correct deficiencies or reduce life-cycle cost.

• In extraordinary circumstances and when required by operational necessity, provide weekend and after-hours support to SAR Ops.

• Other tasks as assigned.

What You Will Bring:
• B.Eng. or B.Sc. (Eng.), or CET (Diploma in Engineering Technology), or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Eligibility for registration as a Professional Engineer is desirable.

• Possess clear and effective written and oral communication skills.

• Knowledge of CH149 airframe, systems, drawing system, technical publications and Electronic Record Keeping System (ERKS) is consider an assest.

• Knowledge of airworthiness regulations and standards, and military aircraft modification processes.

• Current or past authority to approve engineering data is considered an asset.

• Current or past airworthiness authority for aircraft design change certification is considered an asset.

• 2 or more years experience in an aircraft engineering environment will be considered an asset.

• Ability to manage multiple projects and tasks.

• Sound interpersonal skills and an ability to work effectively with people at all levels, both within the organization and those in outside agencies.

• Must be self-motivated and possess good self-discipline with an ability to work independently when required.

• Must possess an ability to logically assimilate information and identify related causal factors, as well as to effectively prioritize multiple tasks.

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program, and Transport Canada RAIC clearance.

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) to join our healthcare team at Rosecrest Under the direction or supervision of the Director of Care, the LPN is responsible for creating a human habitat and providing care and services to meet the needs of the elders in the cottages. Join our team to make a meaningful difference in the lives of patients through compassionate nursing practice.

title: Immigration Paralegal
description:
Are you a detail-oriented legal professional who enjoys managing complex files, building strong client relationships, and helping people navigate significant life and business transitions?

McInnes Cooper is seeking an Immigration Paralegal to join our national Immigration Practice. This position may be based in any McInnes Cooper office and offers a hybrid work arrangement. Working closely with immigration lawyers and legal professionals across the firm, you will play a key role in delivering exceptional service to both corporate and individual clients. You will manage immigration matters from intake through filing, helping clients navigate Canada's immigration system while ensuring applications are prepared accurately, efficiently, and on time.

Qualifications

## What You Bring to the Team

The ideal candidate will possess:

• A Paralegal, Legal Administration, or related diploma, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Experience supporting immigration matters or working in a legal, regulatory, professional services, or client-service environment.

• Knowledge of Canadian immigration processes and documentation requirements, or the ability to develop this expertise quickly.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Exceptional attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling sensitive information.

• A client-focused mindset and the ability to build positive working relationships with clients and colleagues.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 and an aptitude for learning new technology and case management systems.

Immigration experience is considered an asset; however, we welcome applications from candidates with strong legal, regulatory, professional services, or client-service backgrounds who are eager to develop expertise in this growing area of practice.

## Compensation & Benefits

The anticipated salary range for this position is $47,000 to $70,500 annually. Individual compensation is determined based on the successful candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and other relevant factors.

Responsibilities

## What You'll Do

As an Immigration Paralegal, you will:

• Manage immigration files from initial intake through completion, ensuring deadlines, requirements, and client expectations are met.

• Prepare, review, and coordinate immigration applications and supporting documentation, including:
• Work permits

• Intra-Company Transfers (ICTs)

• Labour Market Impact Assessments (LMIAs)

• CUSMA applications

• Business visitor and visitor visa applications

• Permanent residence applications

• Citizenship-related matters

• Draft forms, submission letters, correspondence, and supporting materials for lawyer review.

• Communicate directly with clients to gather information, obtain supporting documentation, provide updates, and guide them through application processes.

• Liaise with government agencies, including Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

• Maintain accurate records using immigration case management technology and firm systems.

• Conduct immigration-related legal and procedural research to support client matters.

• Collaborate with lawyers and team members across offices to deliver timely, high-quality legal support and client service.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, knowledge sharing, and best practices within the Immigration Practice.

## Why Join McInnes Cooper?

McInnes Cooper is one of Canada's leading business law firms, known for innovative legal solutions and a collaborative, inclusive, and genuinely supportive culture. When you join McInnes Cooper, you'll benefit from:

• Meaningful work with experienced lawyers and legal professionals at a nationally respected firm.

• A collaborative environment where your contributions and ideas are valued.

• A flexible, modern workplace that supports well-being, learning, and professional growth.

• Opportunities to collaborate across offices and practice groups.

• A Great Place to Work® committed to inclusion, wellness, and community engagement.

At McInnes Cooper, you'll find more than a job. You'll find challenging and rewarding work, opportunities to grow, and a community of people who genuinely care about each other, our clients, and the communities we serve.

## Our team members enjoy access to:

• Hybrid and flexible work options for many team members;

• Diversity, equity and inclusion programs, with community and volunteer opportunities

title: Production Support Manager
description:
Job Title: Production Support Manager
Location: New Glasgow, Nova Scotia
TP - JMC - 9636

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to partner with MacKay Meters in search of a Production Support Manager to join their team in New Glasgow, Nova Scotia.

For over 50 years, MacKay Meters has been an industry leader in the design, manufacturing, and delivery of innovative parking technology solutions. Headquartered in Nova Scotia, the company serves municipal and private-sector clients across Canada, the United States, and international markets. Known for its commitment to quality, innovation, and continuous improvement, MacKay Meters offers employees the opportunity to work on sophisticated electronic products within a collaborative and technically driven environment.

## Role Description:

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the Production Support Manager will serve as a key technical resource supporting MacKay's electronics manufacturing operations. Acting as a bridge between Engineering, R&D, and Production, this role is responsible for ensuring products are effectively built, tested, validated, documented, and continuously improved throughout their lifecycle.

This is a hands-on position suited to an individual with a strong electronics manufacturing background who enjoys troubleshooting complex technical issues, supporting production teams, and contributing to ongoing product improvement initiatives. The successful candidate will become deeply familiar with MacKay's products and manufacturing processes while helping ensure production teams have the tools, documentation, and technical support required to consistently deliver high-quality products.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Support production operations through technical troubleshooting, issue investigation, and problem resolution.

• Develop, maintain, and improve manufacturing documentation, work instructions, bills of materials, and production procedures.

• Maintain and enhance testing equipment, fixtures, and test jigs used throughout the manufacturing process.

• Investigate product, process, and manufacturing issues and implement practical corrective actions.

• Collaborate with subcontractors and suppliers to support production requirements and product quality.

• Serve as the primary liaison between Production and Engineering teams to facilitate effective communication and issue resolution.

• Review and evaluate new products, technologies, and design changes prior to production implementation.

• Ensure manufacturing documentation, build instructions, and production records remain accurate and up to date.

• Test and validate hardware components, circuit boards, radios, card readers, firmware updates, and related technologies.

• Support the introduction of new products, manufacturing tools, and production technologies.

• Participate in product change management, issue tracking, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Develop a thorough understanding of MacKay's products, systems, and manufacturing processes to support operational excellence.

## Your Qualifications:

The ideal candidate is a technically strong and practical problem solver with experience supporting electronics manufacturing environments. You possess a strong understanding of circuit board assembly, manufacturing processes, and production troubleshooting, along with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

## Key qualifications include:

• Diploma or degree in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electronics Technician, or a related technical discipline.

• Experience working within an electronics manufacturing environment.

• Strong understanding of printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing and assembly processes.

• Ability to read and interpret electrical and electronic schematics.

• Hands-on troubleshooting experience involving electronic products and manufacturing processes.

• Experience with product testing, validation, and quality assurance activities.

• Experience supporting production operations, manufacturing activities, or industrial electronics environments.

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across technical and operational teams.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and technical documentation management.

• Valid driver's license with the ability to travel occasionally as required.

## Assets include:

• Familiarity with electronics test equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, and related diagnostic tools.

• Experience supporting subcontract manufacturers, suppliers, or external production partners.

• Knowledge of PCB design tools, manufacturing standards, or certification requirements.

• Experience with industrial electronic products and systems.

• High-reliability soldering training or experience.

• Experience supporting new product introductions within a manufacturing environment.

• Residence in or proximity to the New Glasgow area.

The Centre for Research in Integrated Care (CRIC) is based out of UNB Saint John. CRIC is a living laboratory that develops and evaluates integrated patient-centred models of care for individuals with complex care needs, their families, and members of the care team.

• Develop and implement knowledge translation (KT) strategies for CRIC's research projects and partner initiatives, identifying key audiences and opportunities to share findings and support their use in practice and policy.

Ready to build a rewarding career in an industry that is transforming the future?

## Who We Are

We are Vale Base Metals – a global supplier of the critical minerals transforming the future.

With industry-leading reserves of copper and nickel in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia, and state-of-the-art infrastructure in the U.K., Canada, and Japan, VBM delivers a secure and responsible supply of high-quality products to customers across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.

Global demand for critical minerals is growing exponentially. From energy to aerospace, batteries to magnets, robotics to artificial intelligence, a secure and responsible supply of critical minerals is fundamental to power modern technologies. And at Vale Base Metals, we are transforming our business to provide a secure and responsible supply of these minerals.

Join our diverse team of 13,000 talented individuals committed to providing mineral security to a world in transition. We invite you to put your skills to work, driving meaningful and enduring change while enjoying a rewarding career.

## The Opportunity

We are currently seeking a Surveyor to join our Mine Technical Services team in Voisey's Bay, Labrador, a fly-in fly-out operation.

The role is a permanent on-site position, working 2 week on/2 week off schedule at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site.

As a Surveyor, you will be responsible for providing intermediate level technical support within the mine (open pit/underground) on a daily execution schedule. The surveyor works collaterally with their peers within the mining and technical services team and cross functionally with all other areas of the mine to complete tasks in their area of accountability.

Additionally, in this position you will:

• Conduct underground and surface mine surveying activities to support mine development, production, construction, and excavation projects.

• Collect, process, and maintain survey data, drawings, sections, and digital mine plans in accordance with established standards.

• Prepare and issue development, production, and excavation layouts, ensuring compliance with design specifications, line, grade, and short-term mine plans.

• Perform month-end surveys, reconciliation activities, and reporting to support operational and business requirements.

• Maintain survey equipment, software, and related technologies, including Total Navigation Systems and drone-based surveying applications.

• Opportunity to support mine ventilation programs by conducting ventilation surveys, maintaining ventilation plans and emergency drawings, and assisting with ventilation monitoring and analysis.

• Monitor mine performance and conditions, identify non-conformances, and provide recommendations to improve safety, productivity, quality, and cost performance.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives through data collection, KPI tracking, operational analysis, and collaboration with technical and operational teams.

## What We Offer You

• Competitive compensation including a variable annual incentive plan

• Participation in a competitive Defined Contribution Pension package

• Comprehensive benefits package (company paid core coverage, flex health and dental coverage, flex accounts, disability plans and optional insurances)

• Leave for all of life's reasons (vacation, personal, sick, parental)

• Work culture dedicated to safety, diversity & inclusion, and career growth

• Employee Family Assistance Program

• Virtual Healthcare online

• Online training and career development opportunities

• Relocation Assistance

• Chartered flights within Newfoundland & Labrador

• 24/7 access to a fully stocked cafeteria with balanced meals prepared by our culinary team

• Access to recreational facilities and social activities (cardio/weight room, gymnasium, music room, movie theatre, etc.)

• Accommodations are equipped with cable TV, internet, and unlimited long-distance calling

• All Personal Protective Equipment is provided upon hire. Employees are given a safety boot allowance and receive a 100% reimbursement for prescription safety glasses

## About You

## Education:

• A post-secondary diploma in Geomatics/Surveying, Engineering Technology, or Mining Engineering Technology is required. A related technical diploma may also be considered.

## Experience:

• A minimum of 3 years' experience with a focus on surveying.

• Experience in a mining environment would be considered an asset.

## Skills:

• Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

• Knowledge of mine surveying, ventilation, and ground control principles.

• Proficiency with survey equipment, drone technology, and surveying software.

• Experience with Deswik and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

• Ability to interpret technical drawings, mine plans, and survey data.

• Strong analytical skills with attention to detail and accuracy.

• Commitment to safety, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

• Ability to work effectively in a dynamic underground mining environment.

## Why Newfoundland and Labrador

Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada's easternmost province, is known for its rugged coastline, rich cultural heritage, and significant natural resources. The province's economy is bolstered by a robust mining sector, where Vale Base Metals' integrated operations play a crucial role.

At Long Harbour, we operate a state-of-the-art processing plant, which refines nickel concentrate from Vale Base Metals' Voisey's Bay mine, located in Labrador, into nickel, copper, and cobalt products. This plant is a cornerstone of our commitment to value-added processing in Canada. Meanwhile, the Voisey's Bay mine is one of the world's most substantial nickel deposits. It provides high-quality nickel, copper, and cobalt, essential for the 21st century economy.

## Include to Transform

At Vale Base Metals, we are committed to ensuring an inclusive work environment where people can act like owners, being their authentic selves and empowering them to deliver results. Vale Base Metals encourages everyone to express their ideas and opinions and values the plurality of individual profiles. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are critical to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or any other personal consideration that makes us different.

Vale is an equal opportunity employer seeking to increase diversity across our operations and improve equal opportunity at Vale and in the mining industry.

Vale recognizes the Impacts and Benefits Agreements with the Innu Nation and the Nunatsiavut Government in which Innu and Inuit workers have first preference for employment at the Voisey's Bay Mine Site. This is guided by an adjacency principle that first gives preference to those who live on the coast of Labrador, followed by those residing in the rest of Labrador, those residing on the island of the province, followed by the rest of Canada.

Next, priority will be given to Newfoundland and Labrador residents. We also welcome those who are willing to relocate back home and those looking to make NL their permanent home.

Accommodation is available throughout our recruitment process for applicants with disabilities.

Innu Nation members and Nunatsiavut beneficiaries can submit their application to their Vale Indigenous Employment Coordinator.

Pay Grade: H02

## Apply by: Sunday, November 1st, 2026.

## #ValeBaseMetals

Interested applicants must submit their application online at https://vale.eightfold.ai/careers.

• Minimum of one to three years' experience in payroll/benefits/human resources with a medium to large organization

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills with a customer service orientation

title: Senior System Analyst
description:
Service New Brunswick

Senior System Analyst

Open Competition

Permanent Opportunities

R2026/27-496

Pay Band 5

Flexible Work Location Within New Brunswick

Working at Service New Brunswick is more than just a job — it's an opportunity to build a meaningful career. Guided by our vision of "Excellence in Service Delivery", our teams provide high-quality, innovative public services for customers with a focus on value for all New Brunswickers.

Known for our people-oriented workplace culture, we foster an environment where innovation, inclusivity, and teamwork are celebrated. We are proud to be recognized as one of Atlantic Canada's Top Employers for 2026!

What We Offer:

At SNB, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We are:

Human-Centered: We prioritize well-being and flexibility for our employees.
Driven by Growth: We invest in your professional development and career advancement.
Celebrating Excellence: We recognize and reward outstanding contributions.
United by Purpose: Every project you work on makes a real difference for New Brunswickers.
Empowered to Decide: We trust our teams to make decisions and innovate boldly.

With offices and locations in most New Brunswick cities and a wide variety of positions and job roles, SNB offers unmatched opportunities for growth and impact, including an employee recognition program, a mentoring program, training & development opportunities, employee townhalls and ongoing leadership development.

SNB also offers a comprehensive employee benefits package.

Service New Brunswick's Technology Services Division is seeking to create a list of qualified candidates to fill current and future Senior System Analyst roles. The SNB Technology Services Division provides technology services to all Government of New Brunswick departments and Regional Health Authorities. With over 800 employees, we form one of the largest IT employers in the province with office locations in most cities and regions. We are mandated to deliver an extensive range of IT Services across various information technology disciplines. Members of our team have the opportunity drive innovation and excellence across government using technology.

The Government of New Brunswick (GNB) is committed to transforming how it manages its operational business units and finances. GNB's goal is to modernize its business processes through the implementation and operation of an Oracle Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Cloud Software as a Service (SaaS) solution over the next 10+ years. The Senior System Analysts will play a role in the efficient and effective delivery of technology and business solutions needed to meet GNB's evolving business requirements and improvement of processes. This position is part of a multi-disciplinary and highly skilled DEV/OPS team assigned to creating and supporting innovative strategies to help transform GNB service delivery through the ERP Cloud platform.

Who are you?

You are client-centric and passionate about delivering exceptional service
You demonstrate initiative and are adaptable, organized and solution-oriented
You are self-motivated with strong teamwork skills
You are an effective communicator and collaborator
You have strong problem solving and analytical skills
You have knowledge of best practices to guide your efforts to deliver high-quality solutions

What will you be doing?

The Senior System Analyst's responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Analyzing, designing, configuring, and supporting Oracle Fusion HCM solutions, including Core HR, Payroll, Benefits, Absence Management, Time and Labor, Talent Management, and Workforce Structures, to meet business requirements and strategic objectives.

Working closely with Human Resources, Payroll, Finance, and technical teams to gather requirements, assess impacts, and develop scalable solutions that align with organizational policies, best practices, and Oracle Fusion standards.

Developing and maintaining reports, dashboards, and analytics using Oracle Transactional Business Intelligence (OTBI), HCM Extracts, BI Publisher, and Financial Reporting tools to support operational and regulatory reporting requirements.

Evaluating and implementing Oracle quarterly releases, new features, legislative updates, and payroll-related enhancements, including impact assessments, testing coordination, and stakeholder communication.

Providing operational support for Oracle Fusion HCM and Payroll, including troubleshooting production issues, resolving system defects, supporting payroll processing activities, and ensuring service levels are maintained.

Designing, testing, and supporting integrations between Oracle Fusion HCM, payroll, benefits providers, time collection systems, financial systems, and other internal or external applications.

Supporting the integrity, accuracy, security, and confidentiality of employee and payroll data through effective configuration, validation, and adherence to data governance standards.

Collaborating with other teams (Integration, Infrastructure, etc.) within Technology Services to investigate and ensure implementation of effective solutions.

Conducting system analysis and recommending improvements to HR and payroll business processes, system functionality, and user experience.

Providing technical leadership, guidance, and mentorship to business analysts, systems analysts, and other team members regarding Oracle Fusion HCM functionality, configuration standards, support processes, and best practices.

Developing and maintaining system documentation, including solution designs, process flows, configuration specifications, test plans, and operational procedures.

Supporting testing activities, including system integration testing, user acceptance testing, payroll parallel testing, and regression testing associated with system changes and Oracle quarterly updates.

Ensuring all design, development, maintenance, and support activities comply with organizational policies, security standards, audit requirements, and payroll legislative obligations.

Contributing to the continuous improvement of incident, problem, change, release, and risk management processes within the Oracle Fusion ERP support environment.

Managing multiple priorities, projects, and operational support activities in a fast-paced environment while maintaining a high level of service to HR and payroll stakeholders.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

A university degree in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of five (5) years related experience in System Development and support OR a two (2) year college diploma in Information Technology with a minimum of seven (7) years related experience.

Experience with one or more Core HR, Payroll, Benefits, Absence Management, Time and Labor, Talent Management, and Workforce Structures in Oracle Fusion Cloud or other related HRM systems.

Subject to the response to this competition, an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

Written and spoken competence in English and French is required for some positions. Other positions will require written and spoken competence in English only.

Please state your language capability on your application and ensure that preferred language for assessment is clearly identified.

Applicants must clearly demonstrate the essential qualifications to be given further consideration.

ASSET QUALIFICATIONS: Preference may be given to candidates who demonstrate they have training or experience in one or more of the following areas:

Experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud in areas such as Human Resources, Procurement or Finance
Experience with a large Enterprise Resource Planning Solution in areas such as Human Resources, Procurement or Finance
Experience with Oracle Cloud Enterprise Performance Management (EPM)
Experience with Oracle Maintenance Cloud (OMC)
Experience with SaaS or PaaS solutions or technologies
Experience with SQL, Oracle PL/SQL
Experience with planning and managing software releases
Experience in assessing the impacts and risks of customization and configuration to support long term system and business process sustainability within a SaaS application.
Knowledgeable in Data Conversion/Migrations, Inbound/Outbound interfaces, and Reports with 3rd party applications.

Subject to the response to this competition, candidates may be required to demonstrate on their application one or more of the asset qualifications in addition to the essential qualifications in order to be given further consideration.

OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Some weekday evening and weekend work hours may be required on occasion.
Some travel throughout the province may be required, and you must possess a valid driver's license.
Candidates will be required to undergo Criminal History Clearance prior to appointment.

BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following behavioral competencies:

Client Service Orientation
Results Orientation
Teamwork and Cooperation
Relationship / Network Building
Strategic Thinking
Creative Thinking/Innovation

TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES: The successful candidate will possess the following technical competencies:

Consulting Skills
Specialized Subject Matter Expertise and Knowledge
Planning and Organizing Skills

Resumes should be in chronological order specifying education and employment in months and years including part-time and full-time employment.

Salary: $ 68,614 - $ 95,810 annually – Pay Band 5 - Management and Non-Union Pay Plan

We strongly encourage you to submit your application via the online portal, by using the "Apply Online" button, to increase the efficiency and maintain a consistent candidate experience. Please ensure your application is complete by 16 November, 2026 and indicate competition number R85-2026/27-496. In the unlikely event that you experience technical difficulties or are unable to complete your application online, contact pc@snb.ca.

This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level.

We thank all those who apply, however only those selected for further consideration will be contacted. This competition may be used to fill future vacancies at the same level within the same work location.

Veterans, who demonstrate they are among the most qualified, shall be given preference at the time of appointment.

title: Electrician
description:
