Company, Department: Nova Scotia Power, Energy Delivery, System Maintenance

Type of Employment: Regular, Full Time

Salary: $49.43 per hour as per IBEW Collective Agreement Local 1928

Closing Date: October 30, 2026

## Location: Coldbrook

We are looking for an Electrician (Industrial) to join our System Maintenance Team in a permanent position.

Reporting to the System Maintenance Supervisor, you will become a member of a team of professionals at our location in Coldbrook and you will perform all aspects of routine electrical maintenance and repair work on equipment throughout the Territory.

Key elements of this role include:

## As an Electrician (Industrial):

• You must be able to work effectively as a member of the Substation Operations team and be capable of functioning in a planned work environment.

• You may be temporarily assigned to other locations to assist other areas when required and will be expected to travel throughout the province.

• You will be required to assist with emergency / storm related power restoration.

• You will be required to participate in regulatory training and be willing to participate in on-the-job training or training programs that support the development of additional skills.

• You will be responsible for your personal safety and that of your co-workers by observing all Occupational Health and Safety Rules and Regulations.

• You will be accountable for environmental performance as it relates to the environmental management system processes and initiatives.

• This position is considered a safety sensitive position. As such, the successful candidate must comply with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Policy which requires a confidential pre-employment alcohol and drug test in accordance with the Emera Alcohol and Drug Procedure.

• Your primary residence must be located within 30 minutes of the work location depot, and you will be required to take on call rotation and work other than normal hours and/or in extreme conditions. You will have 90 days to provide proof of primary residence.

These skills will make you successful:

• Certification as a Journeyman Industrial Electrician with a minimum of two years' experience with troubleshooting electrical equipment is required. If no qualified candidates apply, consideration may be given to those individuals who hold Certification as a Construction Electrician, with the expectation they will complete their Industrial Electrician Certification within an agreed timeframe.

• You have proven problem resolution skills and the flexibility and ability to adapt to rescheduled assignments.

• You must be a strong team player with excellent interpersonal skills, a strong computer aptitude and the ability to deal with multiple tasks and demands.

• You must have the skills and physical capabilities to perform all duties, including working at considerable heights and within watercourses.

• You must hold a valid Nova Scotia Driver's License with a minimum of two years driving experience and provide a driver's abstract satisfactory to NSPI.

• Operation and maintenance experience associated with Substations would be considered an asset. Class 3 Drivers license would be considered an asset. Trailer endorsement would also be considered an asset. Consideration may be given to members of an Industrial Electrician Apprenticeship program if no qualified candidates apply.

Please Note: This is a bargaining unit position. External applicants will only be considered if there are no qualified bargaining unit candidates.

Work Conditions and Physical Capabilities

• Must be able to lift 70 lbs. from the floor to waist level on an occasional basis and 70 lbs. from shoulder to overhead level on a minimal basis. Able to carry 70 lbs. with both hands on a minimal basis, with the overall ability to carry 30 lbs. on an occasional basis.

• Able to push and pull 50 lbs. with whole body strength and be able to push and pull 100 lbs. with upper body strength on an occasional basis.

• Perform static reaching at waist to above shoulder level on a frequent basis and from below waist level on an occasional basis.

• Perform frequent standing and twisting. Perform occasional walking and neck flexion and rotation movements.

• Perform sitting, squatting, kneeling, crouching, climbing, bending, stooping, and forward flexional movements on a minimal basis.

• Ability to perform fine finger manipulation and possess a simple to firm grasp while performing turning and pinching motions.

We understand that experience comes in many forms, and we're dedicated to adding new perspectives to the team. So, if your experience is close to what we've listed above, please consider applying.

Learn more about our culture and values

At the Emera Group of Companies, you'll be part of an inclusive, respectful workplace where everyone is welcomed and supported. Come build a career as unique as you are: making an impact from Atlantic Canada to the world. Your experience and perspective will help us to safely deliver cleaner, more reliable energy to our customers. If working in an innovative environment, challenging yourself, and shaping a cleaner energy future inspires you, we want to hear from you. Apply by October 30,2026 and let us know why this role is right for you.

The perks of joining our team? We offer:

• Health & Wellbeing: A comprehensive benefits plan, 24/7 access to virtual health care services for you and your family through Dialogue, access to a free on-site fitness centre, Employee and Family Assistance Program, parental leave top-up plan and wellness benefits.

• Grow Your Career: Opportunities to advance within and between our affiliate companies, a focus on employee development and available sponsored education programs.

• Community Engagement & Care: Corporate investments in the places where our people live and work, mentoring opportunities, fundraising-matching & volunteer programs, various committees and employee resource groups, and scholarships for children of employees.

• Competitive Compensation: A comprehensive benefits plan and a Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion at Emera

As one of Atlantic Canada's largest publicly traded companies, we are ranked one of Canada's Top 100 Employers, Top Employers for Young People and Top Diversity Employers. We know our success is driven by our dedicated teams and we strongly encourage applications from all qualified candidates, including persons who identify as racially visible, Indigenous, persons with disabilities, women in underrepresented roles and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community.
Applicants from these equity groups may self-identify through the online application process. We support candidates and employees with access and accommodation needs and encourage you to let us know when you require accommodation.

Recruitment & Promotion Policy

The success of the Emera Company is driven by its people: a strong team with a shared commitment to support the Emera Company mission and values. The purpose of our recruitment policy is to provide a consistent framework to support fair and equitable attraction, hiring, and retention of the best talent for vacant positions. We are dedicated to maintaining a fair hiring process that provides equitable opportunities to all our applicants and is guided by our company values.

title: Collector - COR 26093
description:
## Collector

## Corporate Services

Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia
Type of Employment: Full Time, Permanent
Union Status: NSGEU Local 47
Competition # COR 26093
Closing Date: October 30, 2026

## The Opportunity

Under the direction of the Client Service Manager, the Collector is responsible for the collection
of rental arrears and tenant charges. The Collector provides financial counseling to tenants
regarding arrears with the goal of maintaining tenancy and reducing the volume of arrears and
write-offs.

Qualifications

## Must Have

• Degree or diploma in Commerce or Business Administration plus five years' collections experience.

• General knowledge that the source/amount of income and NSPHA Policy may change lease charges and tenant balances.

• Knowledge of Residential Tenancies Program and Small Claims Court procedures.

• Intermediate to advanced knowledge of desktop software, including Microsoft Office.

• Ability to balance persistent collection efforts with strong personal skills, judgment, and an understanding of the limited income base of most NSPHA tenants.

• Ability to remain calm when provoked or when placed in stressful or emotional situations.

## Nice to have

• Working knowledge Yardi Property Management software.

• Emergency First Aid and WHMIS certifications.

## The Fine Print

An equivalent combination of training, education and experience may be considered.

This position requires a valid driver's license and access to a reliable vehicle. Occasional travel within the Metro District is required.

Responsibilities

title: Senior Logistics and Trade Compliance Coordinator
description:
## About the Role

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Senior Logistics and Trade Compliance Coordinator to join our Operations team. In this role, you will coordinate domestic and international shipments, manage shipping and customs documentation, and ensure the smooth, compliant, and cost-effective movement of goods. You will work closely with internal teams, customers, carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers to support on-time delivery and exceptional customer service. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with transportation, logistics, or international shipping experience who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys solving problems, building relationships, and driving operational excellence.

Qualifications

## Education

• High School Diploma required.

• Post-secondary education in Supply Chain, Logistics, International Trade, Business, or a related field is considered an asset.

## Experience

• Experience in transportation, logistics, shipping coordination, or supply chain operations.

• Experience preparing shipping and customs documentation is an asset.

• Experience working with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and international shipments is preferred.

• Strong knowledge of import/export processes, customs regulations, international shipping documentation, and trade compliance requirements.

• Knowledge of import/export processes, customs regulations, and trade compliance requirements is considered an asset.

• Experience in an electrical manufacturing would be an asset.

• Experience mentoring, or supervising team members would be considered an asset.

## Skills & Competencies

• Strong organizational and multitasking abilities.

• Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

• Effective problem-solving and decision-making skills.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively across departments.

• Customer-focused mindset with strong relationship-building skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines.

• Demonstrates accountability, initiative, and sound judgment.

• Commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

• Strong negotiation, vendor management, and relationship management skills.

• Ability to assess logistics provider performance and identify opportunities for cost savings and service improvements.

Working Conditions

• Frequent use of computers, spreadsheets, databases, and planning tools.

• Visits to production areas may be required.

• Safety shoes are required when entering production areas.

Additional Requirements

• Must successfully complete Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) Training.

• Must be eligible to obtain and maintain Transport Canada security clearance.

Responsibilities

## Transportation & Logistics

• Manage end-to-end domestic and international logistics operations, including inbound materials, outbound finished goods, and intercompany shipments, ensuring on-time delivery and compliance with customer and regulatory requirements.

• Own relationships with carriers, freight forwarders, customs brokers, and logistics service providers, ensuring high service levels and reliable transportation solutions.

• Monitor and track shipments to ensure delivery commitments and customer expectations are met.

• Investigate and resolve shipping issues, delays, discrepancies, and freight claims.

• Obtain transportation quotes and evaluate shipping options to support cost-effective decision-making.

• Collaborate with Customer Service, Operations, and Sales teams to develop shipping solutions that meet customer requirements.

• Negotiate transportation rates, service agreements, and logistics arrangements to optimize cost, service, and operational efficiency.

• Monitor provider performance, address service issues, and maintain qualified alternative logistics providers to support business continuity and risk mitigation.

## Customs & Trade Compliance

• Manage end-to-end customs documentation, including HTS classification, commercial invoices, and country-of-origin certificates to eliminate border delays.

• Maintain strict adherence to international trade laws, customs regulations, and global trade compliance programs.

• Manage customs clearance activities and ensure all documentation is accurate and complete.

• Ensure compliance with customs regulations, international trade requirements, transportation legislation, and company policies.

• Act as the primary liaison with customs brokers and regulatory agencies to facilitate efficient cross-border movement of goods.

• Maintain comprehensive transportation and import/export records, ensuring documentation accuracy, regulatory compliance, and audit readiness.

## Continuous Improvement and Risk Mitigation

• Conduct regular internal freight audits and compliance checks, reducing customs penalties and clearing backlog risks.

• Identify opportunities to improve transportation processes, documentation accuracy, and operational efficiency.

• Support ISO requirements, continuous improvement initiatives, and departmental objectives.

• Contribute to KPI achievement, on-time delivery performance, and overall customer satisfaction.

description:
Title: Lead Humanitarian Research Specialist

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Lead Research Specialist is responsible for the development and integration of complex research initiatives within Enablement. Working in alignment with organizational priorities and the broader external environment, they generate humanitarian research findings, analysis, and evidence to inform and influence strategic decision-making internally and externally. Through deep research and collaboration with internal teams and external stakeholders, they produce actionable and sharable products-such as briefs, research reports, evidence-based insights and strategic recommendations-that support the organization's demonstration of expertise, service delivery, advocacy efforts, and long-term planning.

## In this role, you will:

• Provide strategic leadership by developing, integrating, and implementing research approaches that align with organizational priorities and external policy environments.

• Act as a technical advisor to senior leadership on a range of issues, offering expert analysis, evidence-based insights, information synthesis, and strategic recommendations.

• Support Service Lines in integration of research findings into organizational programs, services, and initiatives to ensure alignment with evidence-based practices and stakeholder expectations.

• Develop informed content, reports, guidance materials, and resources that support internal decision-making and external engagement.

• Design and implement planning processes and methodologies, which may include procedural requirements for service delivery, advocacy, or regulatory compliance.

• Conduct and oversee research, literature reviews, policy and legislative scans, and impact assessments within area of accountability to inform the development and refinement of organizational positions.

• Prepare high-level briefings, reports, documents, and presentations for senior leadership and external partners.

• Lead internal and external research and knowledge-sharing and capacity-building initiatives to enhance organizational profile and recognized expertise.

• Build and maintain strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including academic institutions, partner organizations, and relevant communities to advance shared objectives.

• Ensure that diverse perspectives and considerations-such as equity, accessibility, and community impact-are embedded in development, design, and decision-making processes.

• Participate in related coordination structures, working groups, and advisory forums at the local, national, or international level.

• Leverage experience within operational teams to integrate real world experience and examples into research approaches and findings.

• Publish research based and expert reports and other materials on behalf of the Canadian Red Cross.

• Collaborate with internal teams and research counterparts to ensure coherence, alignment, and responsiveness across initiatives.

## What we are looking for:

• Qualifications include a minimum of 8-12 years of related experience and relevant advanced university degree (including a master's degree and/or PhD) in a field relevant to disaster and humanitarian work, and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Requires relevant expertise within the research and analysis domain area.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint) and SharePoint is required.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex research files and advising senior executives.

• Proven experience working with diverse communities or in areas requiring cultural competency and inclusive practices.

• Strong understanding of research methodologies and evidence-based practices.

• Ability to identify complex problems, conduct deep analysis in unfamiliar areas, predict outcomes, and develop innovative, collaborative solutions by balancing technical inputs with strategic objectives.

• Communication and influencing skills to synthesize diverse and sometimes conflicting perspectives and find mutually beneficial solutions, often in sensitive or complex situations.

• Exceptional writing skills to develop a wide range of knowledge products for internal and external audiences, including senior leadership.

• Demonstrated leadership and project management capabilities.

• Fluency in English is required; French is an asset.

## Working Conditions:

• Work will be conducted in an office-like setting.

• May require travel to safe locations.

• Requires significant attention to detail and concentration and ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• Ability to adapt to frequent and often urgent changes in priorities, and make decisions under pressure, work at an unpredictable pace.

• Work requires the ability to work to multiple, conflicting deadlines.

• In a large-scale emergency, you may be asked to support emergency operational needs.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, clients/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Case Manager
description:
Title: Case Manager

Employee Working Location: Mainly In-Person/On-Site - (Preference for candidates based in Okanagan region; Vernon/Kamloops/Kelowna/Summerland/Penticton)

Employment Status: Temporary Full Time (12 months)

The Canadian Red Cross (CRC) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Case Manager is responsible for providing support to individuals affected by emergencies, crises, or other challenging events by actively listening to and understanding their needs, strengths, and barriers to recovery. The Case Manager will assess identified needs and connect individuals with available services and resources, both internally through the Canadian Red Cross (CRC) and externally through community supports, in alignment with operational requirements.

## In this role you will:

• Work with affected clients by listening and documenting what they have experienced, what needs have arisen and what gaps or barriers they may be experiencing.

• Gather client's needs, strengths, risks and capacities and work with them to identify a plan that supports their overall recovery.

• Document immediate, medium and long-term needs and assesses what relevant services are available against pre-defined options.

• Provide recommendations on assistance to be provided to supervisor based on assessment of case files.

• Gather information from client and identify and recommend services and solutions for basic needs, financial assistance, recovering planning and referrals from a pre-defined list of options. Conduct authentication of clients where necessary; gather documents required per available programs.

• Support clients in actively participating in their own recovery by providing information, guidance, and resources; assisting with service navigation and goal setting; and ensuring they remain engaged in decision-making and problem-solving throughout the recovery process.

• Book appointments, complete outbound and follow-up calls.

• Develop and maintain a professional and trusting relationship with clients.

• Document thoroughly all interactions to ensure the completeness of case files at all times and in alignment with data governance policy.

• Ensure case file information is complete, accurate and continually updated within applicable system.

• Participate in and contribute to planned internal briefings/debriefings and meetings.

• Collaborate with other team members to ensure that impacted persons' needs are always at the forefront.

• Identify emerging trends related to identified needs and capacity and share with team.

• Adheres to established processes and procedures, including recognizing and escalating complex case file to the appropriate experts for further assessment and action, and adhering to procedures for incident reporting and risk management.

• Lived and/or has professional experience with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Nations or communities.

• Demonstrated experience working directly with Indigenous communities, organizations, or governments in a culturally safe, respectful, and reciprocal manner.

## What we are looking for:

• The ideal candidate has professional experience with First Nations, Inuit and/or Métis Nations or communities.

• Qualifications include a minimum of 3 years' experience and a 1-2-year post-secondary certification/diploma in social work, psychology, human services, social services, community or health studies or related field and/or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite), client database software and comfortable to navigate multiple systems.

• Ability to identify and resolve issues, by applying standard procedures and functional or organizational knowledge.

• Communication skills, diplomacy and empathy to interpret information and deliver advice, clarify client or stakeholder needs, offer solutions, and resolve escalations in new or somewhat sensitive situations.

• Skilled in active listening and customer service by being able to conduct comprehensive assessments of clients' needs, strengths, and challenges and be able to identify problems, develop action plans, and implement strategies to address client issues effectively while being receptive, sensitive and aware of their situation.

• Experience working with Indigenous communities.

• High degree of attention to detail, and ability to simultaneously listen and type to ensure client information is accurately captured and aligns to CRC requirements.

• Valid driver's license from a Canadian province or territory required.

## Working Conditions:

• This is a field-based role.

• Occasional lifting of up to 5 kg.

• Periods of prolonged sitting or standing with limited breaks.

• Fast-paced and often unpredictable, with competing and time-sensitive priorities.

• Requires adaptability to frequent changes and the ability to make decisions under pressure.

• Involves managing multiple, business-critical deadlines simultaneously.

• Requires sustained concentration, attention to detail, and accuracy, including working with non-routine information and data entry.

• Involves exposure to emotionally charged situations and supporting individuals experiencing trauma.

• As we work with and support people (colleagues, those impacted by disasters, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Policy and Procedures

title: Molecular Biology Laboratory Technician
description:
Kelly Cove Salmon Ltd., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing East Coast family company, with Platinum Member status in Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is offering a unique opportunity for a highly motivated individual to join the Company's team in Bay Fortune, PEI as Molecular Biology Laboratory Technician for our Atlantic Canada on land aquaculture facilities.

Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, and South America. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

## The Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented and motivated Molecular Biology Laboratory Technician to join our team. The successful candidate will assist with laboratory experiments, maintain equipment, and support researchers in conducting molecular biology studies. This role requires strong laboratory skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced research environment.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Perform molecular biology techniques such as DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, qPCR, and gel electrophoresis.

• Prepare reagents, buffers, and culture media for laboratory experiments.

• Maintain, calibrate, and troubleshoot laboratory equipment while ensuring overall lab organization.

• Record and analyze experimental data using laboratory software and spreadsheets.

• Assist in sample preparation and processing for downstream analyses.

• Follow laboratory safety protocols and maintain compliance with regulatory and company standards.

• Manage inventory, order supplies, and maintain laboratory documentation.

• Support researchers with experimental design, optimization, and troubleshooting when required.

## Qualifications:

Required

• Diploma or bachelor's degree in molecular biology, Biotechnology, or a related field.

• Experience with basic molecular biology laboratory techniques and aseptic techniques.

• Strong organizational and documentation skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented laboratory environment.

Preferred

• Previous experience in a research laboratory or biotech company.

• Familiarity with cell culture, bacterial culture, or CRISPR techniques.

• Experience using laboratory data management systems.

Skills

• High attention to detail and accuracy in laboratory work.

• Strong problem-solving abilities.

• Effective communication and collaboration skills.

• Strong time-management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple experiments.

## Working Conditions:

• Requires the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as lab coats, gloves, and boots.

• May involve standing for extended periods, repetitive pipetting, and handling temperature-controlled equipment (e.g., freezers, incubators).

• Occasional lifting of up to 25 lbs (e.g., lab supplies, equipment).

• Work hours may vary depending on experimental schedules; some flexibility may be required.

• Adherence to all company safety protocols, biosafety regulations, and laboratory best practices is mandatory.

## Benefits

• Competitive salary

• Health and dental benefits

• Opportunities for professional development

• Access to advanced laboratory equipment and training

## The Opportunity

The role description is just one part of the story. This is an opportunity to grow, to stretch, to work within the parameters of the role but stretch to your fullest potential. We are a team that counts performance, we reward contribution, and we recognize talent. It is about being at the center of the fastest-growing company in Atlantic Canada and knowing you are part of that growth. The ability to bring your passion for learning, desire for growth, and energy for moving your career forward is what we offer.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethics. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

title: Nutrition Registered Dietitian
description:
Job Description

Reporting to the Manager of Cancer Support, the Program Leader of Nutrition is responsible for developing, facilitating, and leading nutrition-focused Cancer Support programming for individuals with lived cancer experience and their support persons.

Working in collaboration with multidisciplinary team members, community partners, and clinical teams, the Program Leader of Nutrition promotes healthy eating habits and lifestyle practices that support overall well-being throughout the cancer journey.

The Program Leader of Nutrition will conduct research to create content and deliver engaging educational presentations on a variety of nutrition topics related to cancer prevention, treatment, recovery, and survivorship, as well as conduct hands-on food demonstrations that encourage practical application of healthy eating principles.

This role includes researching emerging evidence and best practices to develop new and update current, program topics, presentations, resources, and handouts that meet the evolving needs of those impacted by cancer. The Program Leader of Nutrition will also collaborate with other Program Leaders and teams to create integrated, participant-centered programming and support services.

In this role, you will be critical to Chalmers Foundation Cancer Support's ability to provide exceptional care and support to participants at any stage of their cancer journey. You will contribute to the overall well-being and quality of life of individuals with lived cancer experience and their loved ones in our community by delivering evidence-informed education and support, adhering to professional practice standards and Chalmers Foundation and Chalmers Foundation Cancer Support policies and procedures, and ensuring quality, safety, respect, compassion, and dignity in all interactions.

Responsibilities

Researching, preparing, and presenting education sessions and information to individuals with lived cancer experience and their support persons.

Participate in developing, maintaining, and evaluating policies and procedures for nutrition programming.

Participate in developing and sharing information related to clinical skill sets, best practices, clinical guidelines and programming specific to supportive community care for cancer.

Adhere to Chalmers Foundation Cancer Support agreements/standards of care.

Be a program ambassador and community-based cancer support champion.

Qualifications

A Bachelor of Science degree in Nutrition or Dietetics and successful completion of an accredited internship program.

Must be registered and a member in good standing with the New Brunswick Association of Dietitians.

Certified Diabetes Educator (CDE) and completion of the Certification Program for Insulin Dose Adjustment considered an asset.

Written and spoken competence in English is required. Written and spoken competence in French is an asset.

Oncology and/or Chronic Health Experience is an asset.

Requirements

· Standard First Aid Certification for the Workplace

· Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Check (issued within the past two years)

Work Location and Program Environment

This position is based at the Chalmers Foundation Care & Support Centre, located at 25 Alison Boulevard, Suite 2, Fredericton, New Brunswick. The successful candidate is expected to perform their regular work duties on-site at the Centre and will be responsible for delivering nutrition education sessions, presentations, and food demonstrations within the Centre's Wellness Kitchen.

As part of the Centre's interdisciplinary approach to cancer support, the Program Leader will engage directly with individuals living with and beyond cancer, as well as their support persons, in a welcoming and supportive environment that promotes health, wellness, and quality of life throughout the cancer journey.

Who We Are

Chalmers Foundation Cancer Support is dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for people affected by cancer through the delivery of comprehensive whole-person care and support at every stage of their cancer journey.

The goal of Chalmers Foundation Cancer support is to help enhance the well-being of our participants through education, physical wellness, emotional support, and creative expression. Our programs provide practical tools and strategies to manage symptoms, rebuild strength, connect with others who have a shared experience, and explore creative ways to express and cope.

The Chalmers Foundation Care & Support Centre provides a dedicated space for those in our community impacted by cancer. The Centre serves as a sanctuary of care and connection, offering comfort and community through shared experience. No one should walk the cancer journey alone.

Chalmers Foundation Cancer Support is made possible through the generosity of donors whose support helps fund innovative programs and services for individuals and families affected by cancer. Donor contributions play a vital role in enabling positions such as this one and in ensuring participants have access to evidence-informed education, wellness programming, and supportive care services.

To Apply

Must provide a cover letter and résumé via email to: AMorellKennedy@ChalmersFoundation.com.

title: Maintenance Operations Analyst
description:
## The opportunity: drive maintenance excellence through analytics

The Maintenance Operations Analyst will specialize in supporting Maintenance and Engineering operations by analyzing data related to aircraft maintenance: on-time performance, efficiency, safety, and quality. You will focus on optimizing processes, reducing downtime, improving on-time performance, enhancing safety and quality standards, and ensuring compliance with regulatory policies and procedures. You will specialize in query and data model development and optimization, business intelligence reporting, and the use of other analytics and optimization tools. This is a unique opportunity to transform complex data into strategies that keep Canada’s largest regional airline operating at peak performance.

If you are naturally analytical, thrive on problem-solving, and want to make aviation safer and more efficient, we want you on our team!

## Key responsibilities

• Maintenance Operations Analyses
• Identify trends and patterns, recurring issues, potential corrective actions, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

• Develop and monitor aircraft maintenance performance metrics.

• Identify inefficiencies in operational processes, deviations from standards or plans, and factors impacting delays.

• Conduct post- and root-cause analysis, including case studies focused on understanding operational issues.

• Business Intelligence Report Development
• Design, develop, administer, and maintain business intelligence reports that visualize maintenance data, present actionable insights, support data-driven decision-making, and drive operational improvement.

• Document report builds, methodologies, best practices, user guides, processes, and procedures.

• Create dashboards to track KPI’s to easily spot trends, problems, and opportunities.

• Provide tutorials and training on using existing and new BI reports.

• Advance BI reports to proactively send alerts and information directly to identified users.

• Query and Data Model Optimization
• Collaboration with internal IT Solution Architect for Data & Analytics.

• Focus on enhancing the efficiency of the data analytics stack.

• Improve query performance, minimizing resource usage, and ensuring data accuracy.

• Business Intelligence and Analytics
• Respond to Integrated Analytics requests, as assigned (ex. Access, Data Export).

• Query writing and optimization.

• Report building, inclusive of Excel, Power BI, PowerPoint, etc.

• Amending or adding data or features to existing reports.

• Perform duties in accordance with established policies and procedures while giving primary consideration to personal safety, and the safety of co-workers and customers.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

## Required qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, or Data Analytics.

• Proficient in Business Intelligence and Visualization techniques, specifically in Power BI, DAX, Advanced Power Query, Visualization, and KPI development;

• Strong command of Data Platforms & SQL techniques, including MS SQL Server and T SQL.

• Skilled in Data Modeling.

• Familiar with Statistical Modeling and programming for Data, using Python and R.

• Proficient in MS Office 365 applications (Excel, Word, Outlook).

• Skilled at collaborating effectively or working autonomously, being proactive, building strong relationships, and translating business requirements into technical solutions.

• Strong project management abilities, including administration, priority setting, and adapting to changing priorities.

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, including presentation creation and delivery.

## Preferred qualifications

• Master's degree in Data Analytics.

• One to three years’ experience in data analysis and/or analysis; Open to a new grad.

• Aviation maintenance-related experience.

## Benefits of joining our award-winning team

• Enjoy exclusive employee travel programs across the Air Canada network, giving you and your family access to incredible destinations.

• Secure your long-term financial well-being with our competitive, employer-supported retirement savings programs (defined contribution pension plan or voluntary group RRSP) for permanent employees.

• Benefit from a comprehensive health and wellness package, including health, dental, life, and accident insurance to keep you and your loved ones protected.

## About Jazz Aviation LP

Jazz Aviation LP (Jazz) is Canada’s largest regional airline and Air Canada’s primary Air Canada Express operator, connecting people and communities to approximately 70 destinations across North America.

With over 4,200 dedicated professionals, Jazz fosters a workplace united by purpose and supported by programs and policies that promote safety, diversity, and wellness. Jazz is proud to be recognized for its strong commitment to people and culture. Visit our Company Awards and Recognition page to learn more about the honours we've earned.

Join our award-winning team and be part of shaping the future of regional aviation!

## Our commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility

We strive to make our workplace accessible and inclusive. To support your success, we can provide accommodations for people with disabilities, such as adjustments or assistive measures to remove barriers during the recruitment process. If you require any accessibility support, please contact us at taleosupport@flyjazz.ca.

Jazz values diversity and we empower our employees to foster an internal culture of inclusion. Jazz is committed to providing equitable opportunities for employment and career advancement and we will continuously work to create inclusive and accessible work environments to maximize individual potential as well as psychological health and safety. Meeting the needs of passengers is critical to our success and we recognize the importance of a workforce that is reflective of the communities we serve.

title: Senior Finance Manager - Domestic Relief & Readiness
description:
Title: Senior Finance Manager - Domestic Relief & Readiness

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will :

• Manage the teams that perform the day-to-day financial planning and analysis for the program's administrative departments and domestic readiness project, including budgeting, proposal writing, transactional reconciliation and review, general ledger journal entries as needed, monthly forecast updates, and monthly and ad hoc financial reporting to operational teams.

• Understand staff related policies and procedures and ensures operational compliance and provide leadership, training, coaching, and advice to staff to facilitate continuous improvement and development.

• Review and analyze program's consolidated budgets ensuring completeness and accuracy and to identify any errors or omissions that may require collaboration with operational and finance teams to resolve.

• Develop program specific monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting timelines with appropriate deadlines to ensure CRC wide reporting deadlines are met and ensure the process occurs as scheduled.

• Review program's consolidated year to date actuals to ensure completeness and accuracy, identify errors or omissions, and collaborate with finance teams to resolve before general ledger close.

• Review program's consolidated annual forecasts to ensure completeness and accuracy, identify errors or omissions, and collaborate with finance teams to resolve before forecast ledger close.

• Collaborate with program finance teams to gather reports to be utilized to develop program's consolidated reporting and narratives for submission to Director of Finance, VP of Finance, CFO, and AFC.

• Identify analysis and reporting process deficiencies and recommends areas of improvement and collaborate with finance systems team to adjust existing reports or develop new reports, as needed.

• Review and/or perform other analysis and reporting as requested by program operational staff or senior management.

• Prepare analysis and reporting for presentation to operational senior management to allow for operational decision making and ultimate approval of the program budget submission.

• Prepare reporting and narrative for submission as part of CRC consolidated budget to VP of Finance, CFO, the Audit and Finance Committee (AFC), and Board of Directors.

## What we are looking for:

• A professional accounting designation (CPA) and a minimum of seven (7) years of job-related experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong knowledge and understanding of accounting theory, techniques, and policies.

• Experience directly working with and reporting to both operational and financial senior management.

• Experience in people management, specifically direct reports.

• Experience working with Microsoft AX Dynamics and/or BI360 systems is considered an asset.

• Strong attention to detail, analytical, and problem-solving skills along with the ability to make sound financial decisions.

• Superior knowledge of Excel is required and knowledge of PowerBI is considered an asset.

• Superior organization and time management skills reflected in the ability to prioritize and multi-task within a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to work both independently with minimal supervision, and collaboratively within a team in a matrix structure.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate and report effectively to operations and senior management. French is considered an asset.

• The commitment to the Fundamental Principles of the Red Cross Movement and model the core competencies of the CRCS: team excellence, service excellence, accountability and results focused.

• A satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

## Working Conditions :

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume.

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP or PCP;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Get Stuff Built - Engineer
description:
DESCRIPTION
You make things that work, and you make them fast. You take rough ideas and turn them into repeatable, data-collecting prototypes. You own the full prototype cycle, iterate quickly, learn from failure, and trade perfection for results when it matters. You like being hands-on, you enjoy rapid cycles of build-test-learn, and you get energized by shipping messy systems that actually collect useful data in the field.

Above all we value speed, practical judgment, and a relentless bias toward building. If you are the sort of maker or coder who would put a 3D printer on wheels, make a Pringles can fly, or build a gasoline scooter because electric scooters weren't allowed on your campus, you will feel at home at Marble. If you are someone who would aspire to work at SpaceX if you lived in the US, then this is your moment. We are looking for people who thrive at a workbench, breaking down a problem and building it back up, people who aren't satisfied until they've pushed a prototype to its literal breaking point to see how it fails. If you bring that mindset in hardware, electronics, software or embedded systems, we want to hear from you!

REQUIREMENTS
We are hiring both junior and senior people who fit the above and below descriptions:

• Junior hires should show clear, recent hands-on projects and a demonstrated ability to iterate quickly.
• Senior hires should show they have led shipping prototypes, shortened cycle time, made systems more repeatable, and mentored others.

Don't see a role that fits? We will hire as many amazing people as we can find. If reading about how we work makes you feel genuinely excited, understood, and at home, tell us who you are, what you have built, and where you think you can push Marble forward.

TIMELINE
We will be reviewing applications immediately and interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis until the position(s) are filled.

title: General Manager
description:
## General Manager

Miawpukek First Nation - Conne River, NL

Who we are

Miawpukek First Nation (MFN) is a vibrant Mi'kmaq community located at the mouth of the Conne River on the south coast of Newfoundland. At the heart of MFN is a strong sense of community, culture and connection, and a commitment to providing quality programs and services while continuing to build for the future.

We're looking for an experienced, community minded leader to join us as General Manager. This is a senior leadership role, reporting directly to Chief and Council and working closely with MFN's Directors and Managers. You'll have overall responsibility for the administration and operations of the organization. But just as importantly, you'll be part of a community where relationships matter and where the work you do has a very real impact.

What we're looking for

Leading with the Miawpukek First Nation means understanding both the organization and the community it serves. We're looking for someone who brings strong business and leadership experience, while recognizing that good leadership here is also built on relationships, trust and connection to community. You're someone who can see the big picture while still understanding what's happening on the ground. You're comfortable working with Chief and Council, supporting and challenging a leadership team, making difficult decisions when needed and building strong relationships along the way.

You also know how to actively listen, ask good questions, bring people together and move things forward. An understanding and appreciation of Mi'kmaq culture, traditions and values and experience working within First Nations or Indigenous communities would be a strong asset. Equally important is a genuine willingness to learn, build an understanding of the community and its culture and bring that understanding into how you lead and work with others.

What you'll be doing

As General Manager, you'll provide leadership and oversight across MFN's programs, services and administrative operations. That includes:

• Working closely with Chief and Council to turn strategic priorities and decisions into action.

• Leading, coaching and supporting MFN's Directors and Managers.

• Overseeing financial planning, budgets, organizational resources, risk and performance.

• Helping strengthen systems, accountability and organizational capacity.

• Leading strategic and operational planning, policy development and continuous improvement.

• Building a workplace culture that is respectful, collaborative and accountable.

• Developing strong relationships with community members, governments, Indigenous organizations, funding partners and other stakeholders.

• Identifying opportunities for funding, partnerships and development that support MFN's priorities and future growth.

What you bring

There are different paths that could prepare someone for this role, and we're open to hearing about yours. Ideally, you'll bring:

Significant progressive leadership experience, typically 10 years or more, including experience at a senior management or executive level.

Relevant post secondary education in business, public administration, finance, Indigenous governance, a technical discipline or a related area. A Masters or professional designation is an asset.

Experience working with elected leadership and an understanding of the different roles of governance and administration.

Strong financial, organizational and business judgment.

Experience leading people, navigating change and strengthening organizations.

The ability to communicate clearly, build trust and handle challenging situations with good judgment.

An understanding and appreciation of Mi'kmaq culture, traditions, values and community practices.

A valid driver's licence and flexibility to travel or work outside regular hours when needed.

Equivalent combinations of education, leadership experience and relevant community or professional experience will also be considered.

What we offer

MFN offers a competitive compensation package in accordance with its wage structure. Depending on the successful candidate's circumstances, additional allowances and/or relocation related supports may also be available.

Beyond compensation, this is an opportunity to take on a meaningful senior leadership role in a community with a strong identity, an important history and ambitious plans for its future.

If you're an experienced leader who values community, relationships, accountability and getting things done, we'd like to hear from you. Recruitment for this position will also reflect MFN's established hiring policies and its commitment to employment opportunities within the community.

Application deadline: October 30, 2026

Interested candidates are invited to submit a resume and cover letter through the platform where this position is advertised or by email to nicole@nbconsultingnl.com.

Fredericton, New Brunswick

York Care Centre (YCC) is seeking an experienced, values-driven leader to serve as its next President & CEO, following the upcoming retirement of the current CEO. YCC is a not-for-profit long-term care organization providing 218 long-term care beds alongside a 31 unit assisted living, 72 independent living apartments, and an Adult Day Program for seniors living with dementia. The York Care group of companies includes York Care Centre, York County Properties Inc., York Developments Inc., and the Centre for Innovation and Research on Aging.

In this rewarding role, you will provide in-home early intervention programming and family support services for children from birth to eight years of age who have moderate to significant developmental delays or who may be at risk due to family circumstances. Working collaboratively with families, you will build on their strengths, support their capacity to meet their child's developmental needs, and promote positive outcomes for children.

We are a non-profit organization governed by a volunteer Board of Directors and funded by the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.

## QUALIFICATIONS

Applicants must possess either:

• A university degree in Early Childhood Education or a related field from a recognized post-secondary institution; additional training/experience in ECE is an asset; or

• A 2-year diploma in Early Childhood Education or a related field from a recognized post-secondary institution, combined with a minimum of three (3) years of related experience.

Candidates must demonstrate knowledge of:

• Early childhood growth and development;

• Infant and preschool development;

• Developmental delays and disabilities;

• Family-centered practice; and

• Child and family support services.

Pedagogical Knowledge

• Strong understanding of early childhood development and current research related to brain development, emotional resilience, self-regulation, attachment, and relationships.

• Commitment to ongoing professional learning in areas such as speech and language development, infant mental health, trauma-informed practice, and developmental disabilities.

Observation and Assessment Skills

• Ability to observe, document, and analyze child development and family interactions.

• Ability to connect observations to developmental theory and identify when additional assessment or support may be beneficial.

• Confidence discussing developmental concerns with families in a respectful and supportive manner.

Communication and Relationship Building

• Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills.

• Ability to establish positive working relationships with children, families, colleagues, and community partners.

• Professional, objective, and strength-based documentation practices.

Family Support and Coaching

• Ability to nurture, guide, and support children and caregivers.

• Capacity to model effective teaching, caregiving, and parenting strategies.

• Strong reflective and active listening skills.

Collaboration and Professional Practice

• Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of an interdisciplinary team.

• Experience collaborating with community partners and stakeholders, including Social Development.

## WORKING CONDITIONS

Be part of an organization committed to fostering growth and empowering individuals on our team and in our East Coast community.

East Coast Credit Union is looking for a Project Manager to join our team! The Project Manager leads projects from initiation through completion, ensuring effective planning, governance, risk management, reporting, and successful delivery. The role fosters collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement while ensuring compliance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements. As a champion of project management best practices, the Project Manager supports innovation, strengthens project delivery outcomes, and contributes to the Credit Union's strategic objectives and community initiatives.

## We offer…

An outstanding culture and opportunity to join an engaged and community-focused team.

Competitive compensation ($83,503.62 - $99,192.95) and performance-based incentives.

Generous benefit package including a Flexible Health and Dental Plan (paid 100% by employer) and up to 9% contribution with employer match in the Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

Tuition reimbursement, training, and personal development.

Employee perks such as annual wellness credit; reduced rates on employee loans/mortgages and paid volunteer time.

## You would…

Lead the full project lifecycle, including planning, initiation, execution, and closure, ensuring alignment with change management principles and consulting with the Change Management Committee as required.

Provide guidance to internal and external partners on defining project goals, objectives, risks, assumptions, resources, roles, and responsibilities, including work breakdown structures, milestones, and deliverables.

Facilitate the identification and alignment of partner expectations, ensuring clear, effective communication throughout the project lifecycle.

Drive the successful delivery of projects that support the Credit Union's strategic initiatives within agreed timelines and objectives.

Assist with Enterprise Intake meetings and maintain visibility into the project pipeline.

Maintain and update the corporate project roadmap, providing timely progress updates to the broader organization.

Leverage data and insights to inform leadership decisions regarding project performance, productivity, capacity, cost, quality, risk, and ROI.

Design and deliver training on project management methodologies and best practices for both groups and individuals.

Actively support and participate in community initiatives, representing the Credit Union at events, system conferences, and professional meetings.

## You have…

Successfully completed a bachelor's degree in business, Finance, or a related field.

A minimum of five years of experience in project management, ideally within a structured Project Management Office.

## You are…

Knowledgeable in project lifecycle methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid) and change management practices, with proven ability to plan, execute, and manage complex projects and risks.

Skilled in developing dashboards, scorecards, and reporting tools to monitor progress and inform leadership decisions.

Experienced in leading, coaching, and guiding cross-functional teams, fostering collaboration, accountability, and professional development.

Please note that all offers of employment are conditional upon the acceptance of an Individual Fidelity Bond Application which includes a criminal check and a credit check.

Creating Homes Where Life is Worth Living http://www.edenalt.org/

The Eden Alternative shows how companionship, the opportunity to give meaningful care to other living things, and the variety and spontaneity that mark an enlivened environment, can succeed where pills and therapies often fail. Places that have adopted the Eden Alternative typically are filled with plants, animals, and are regularly visited by children.

The Eden Alternative is also about changing the culture of long-term care organizations.
