title: Education & Engagement Coordinator
description:
## EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITYEducation & Engagement Coordinator

Join Our Team
The North Shore Mi'kmaq Tribal Council (NSMTC) is seeking an Education & Engagement Coordinator to join our Support Services Department.

Position Title: Education & Engagement Coordinator (One year term)
Report To: Data Governance Lead
Location: Hybrid (Remote & in person)
Anticipated Start Date: November 16, 2026
Application Deadline: October 28, 2026

NSMTC Member Communities
Ugpi'ganjig (Eel River Bar), Oinpegitjoig (Pabineau), Natoaganeg (Eel Ground), Metepenagiag (Red Bank), L'nui Menikuk (Indian Island), Tjipõgtõtjg (Buctouche), and Amlamgog (Fort Folly).

The Opportunity
The North Shore Mi'kmaq Tribal Council (NSMTC) is seeking an Education & Engagement Coordinator for a one year term to support digital education, organizational learning, youth programming, and engagement across our member communities. This role is ideal for someone with an education background who enjoys teaching, facilitating, developing learning resources, and building relationships. Technical expertise in Data Governance, OCAP®, privacy, cybersecurity, or AI is not required, as comprehensive training and mentorship will be provided.

What You'll Do
The purpose of this role is to support the operational needs of managers and staff as NSMTC continues to adopt OCAP®, Indigenous Data Sovereignty, and responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) ethics across the organization and within our member communities. Working alongside the Data Governance team, the successful candidate will help translate complex concepts into practical, accessible learning opportunities through education, engagement, and relationship-building.

Education & Resource Development:

• Develop, update, and maintain training materials, presentations, facilitator guides, curriculum, handouts, and educational resources.

• Assist with the design and continuous improvement of learning materials for staff, youth, leadership, and community members.

Administrative Support & Project Coordination:

• Provide administrative support for grant-funded initiatives, project coordination, reporting, tracking, scheduling, and documentation.

• Assist managers with operational priorities by organizing educational initiatives, maintaining project records, and supporting program implementation.

Delivery & Engagement:

• Deliver educational sessions, workshops, Lunch & Learns, and presentations.

• Facilitate monthly community engagement sessions and roundtable discussions.

• Support youth programming, including the Little Teacher (Nujikina'muet-jij) initiative, and deliver programming within community schools.

• Build relationships by attending events, engaging with community members, and helping share knowledge where it is needed most.

## What You Bring

• A background in education with experience teaching, facilitating, coaching, mentoring, or presenting.

• Strong communication, organization, and relationship-building skills.

• Confidence presenting to small and large groups.

• Creativity in developing educational materials and learning experiences.

• Strong cultural understanding and awareness is considered an asset.

• Willingness to learn and champion OCAP®, Indigenous Data Sovereignty, AI ethics, and digital best practices.

• Ability to travel throughout NSMTC member communities.

• Experience working with First Nation communities and/or Indigenous organizations would be considered a strong asset.

• An equivalent combination of education, training, professional experience and demonstrated leadership may be considered.

Working at NSMTC
Our employees are expected to contribute beyond their individual roles. They understand how their work supports NSMTC's broader strategic direction, communicate effectively, use good judgment in their day-to-day work, manage their responsibilities reliably, work collaboratively across the organization, and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Above all, we are looking for someone who understands how their work contributes to strong teams, programs, and services for First Nation communities.

Interested in Joining NSMTC?
If you are passionate about directly supporting First Nation communities and are motivated, collaborative, innovative, and possess excellent communication skills, we encourage you to apply for this position.

What We Offer:

• A work culture that supports employee wellbeing, diversity, engagement, and a sense of belonging.

• Competitive salary

• Collaboration with a team of passionate professionals working towards contributing to the growth and success of First Nations communities.

Additional Information:

The NSMTC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all interested parties. However, if there are applicants of equal education, skills, and experience, preference may be given to members of our seven member communities.

Application Deadline:
Please submit your resume and cover letter to Tammy Scott, Human Resources Manager at careers@nsmtc.ca by October 28, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.

We thank those who apply, but only individuals selected for further consideration will be contacted. Applicants are responsible for the timely submission of applications.

title: Director, Product Marketing
description:
## About Dash Social

Dash Social is brand-intelligent AI for social growth. By bringing brand, creative, social performance and workflows together in one connected system, Dash helps marketing teams create content, act on recommendations, report on results and know what to do next. Global brands rely on Dash to move faster without losing control of their brand. Learn more at dashsocial.com.

At Dash Social, you'll have the opportunity to take risks, learn and grow your career alongside a talented, hardworking team. Our policies and practices have earned us recognition as a top employer in Canada.

## Overview

We're looking for a Director of Product Marketing to set product marketing strategy and lead the PMM team at Dash Social. This is a highly visible, strategic role. You'll be Marketing's main counterpart, the voice of the product in company positioning, and the leader of the releases that create our biggest market moments. Reporting to the VP of Customer Success, you'll work closely with Product, Marketing, Enablement, and Revenue teams. Together, you'll make sure our products, both new and existing, are clearly differentiated, well-enabled in the field, and resonate with our buyers and users, leading to adoption and growth.

The role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution. You'll build an efficient, repeatable, AI-enabled system that turns the continuous flow of new capabilities into easily digestible, value-based narratives for the field. You'll also measure whether that work is moving pipeline and win rate.

Qualifications

## Desired Qualifications

• 7+ years of experience in product marketing, product management, or related GTM roles, with at least 5 years in B2B SaaS product marketing.

• Experience managing and developing a team of product marketers.

• Proven track record developing product positioning, messaging, personas, and GTM strategies that drive adoption and growth.

• Experience leading major launches end-to-end, ideally including designing a tiered launch framework.

• Experience running a competitive intelligence program with recurring outputs that Sales and leadership rely on.

• Comfort with data, including measuring content usage and its impact on pipeline or win rate using tools like SalesHood, Gong, and Hubspot.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, or AI features in your GTM stack) in your day-to-day work, with examples of workflows you've built or streamlined.

• Ability to translate technical capabilities into compelling, value-based narratives.

• Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence across the organization.

• Experience working closely with Product teams and understanding product development lifecycles.

## Nice to Have

• Experience in social media, martech, or creator economy SaaS.

• Background in building product marketing functions from the ground up.

Responsibilities

## What You'll Do

• Set product marketing strategy and priorities for the PMM team, and serve as Marketing's primary counterpart on product narrative, launches, and go-to-market planning.

• Own Dash's product pillars, use cases, and buyer and user personas. Build a value-first messaging framework from them that equips Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success.

• Lead our largest (tier-1) releases end to end: narrative, audience, cross-functional readiness, enablement, and measurable success criteria. Define the launch tiering model that governs how every release is handled.

• Own win/loss reviews, competitive and market intelligence, including a recurring quarterly competitive report and battlecards. Turn these insights into input for product, positioning, and deal strategy.

• Bring the PMM perspective to company positioning, ICP, analyst relations, and the GTM calendar in partnership with Marketing leadership.

• Track how PMM content is used in the field and measure its influence on pipeline and win rate. Use those insights to decide what to build, refine, or retire.

• Define how PMM works with Product, Enablement, and the field, including intake, launch planning, feedback loops, and shared rituals.

• Continuously find efficiencies in how PMM works, using AI tools and automation to speed up research, competitive monitoring, content creation, and launch execution so the team can focus on high-judgment work.

• Lead and develop the Product Marketing team, setting the standard for PMM excellence at Dash.

## Why Dash Social

• Opportunity to lead product marketing at a fast-growing company with an industry-leading platform.

• Collaborative, innovative environment with high-calibre teammates.

• Chance to make a visible impact on our GTM success and company growth.

Don't meet every qualification? Research shows that equity-deserving groups are 20% less likely to apply to jobs if they don't check every box. If this role excites you and you think you have what it takes, we encourage you to still apply. You may be the best candidate for this role.

## Work With Us

Dash Social is a social media management platform that equips brands with intelligence and speed to stay ahead of the curve. We're building a team of smart, curious, and driven people who care about doing great work. It's the people at Dash that propel us forward.

We believe that great ideas come from different places. We're proud of the team we've built so far and are always looking for people who bring new ideas, experiences, and dedication as we continue to grow. If you are collaborative, thoughtful, eager to learn and grow, and are a hard worker, you'll fit right in here.

Dash Social's hiring practices are based on skills, potential and character, regardless of race, religion, colour, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law.

## Employee Benefits

At Dash Social, our team is our competitive advantage. We are committed to supporting one another and work hard to ensure everyone has the support they need. In addition to health and dental benefits for you and your family, you can also expect:

• Vacation, personal days and sick time

• RRSP/401k matching

• Annual mental health benefit

• Quarterly wellness benefit

• Donation matching program

• Parental leave top-up plan

• Work-from-home benefit

• Flexible working hours and location

• Departmental and team-wide bonding activities

title: Manager, Risk Management and Compliance
description:
## Manager, Risk Management and Compliance
Halifax, NS
Reference # HL-CUD-10233

The role of the Nova Scotia Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation (NSCUDIC) is to provide deposit insurance for credit unions and caisses populaires in Nova Scotia, Canada. Working with Atlantic Central and the Nova Scotia Department of Finance, NSCUDIC provides the most comprehensive deposit insurance and stabilization programs of any financial institution in Nova Scotia. We are pleased to be partnered with them to bring an experienced Manager, Risk Management and Compliance to their Halifax, NS team.

The Manager, Risk Management and Compliance (Manager) will keep abreast of all changes of the Nova Scotia Credit Union Act and Regulations which affect the administration of deposit insurance and stabilization activities for credit unions. Reporting to the CEO, the Manager will be responsible for leading the Internal Control and Governance Review Program for all 18 Nova Scotia Credit Unions.

## The key functions of this role are to:

• Act as primary contact and relationship manager for a group of credit unions and work with other Managers/Senior Analysts as required in risk managing the Nova Scotia Credit Union system.

• Identify and analyse problem areas in credit union operations to ensure credit unions develop and implement plans to address issues of non-compliance, loan risk exposure, operating risk exposure and financial performance which fall below minimum operating standards.

• Ensure the implementation of operational systems, procedures and standards aimed at improving the operational and financial performance of credit unions.

• Ensure action plans with clear time frames are developed and implemented and monitored regularly for effective progress in resolving credit union performance deficiencies and other issues.

• Supervise the financial performance and operation of credit unions placed under supervision of NSCUDIC and to plan and initiate any corrective action that is considered necessary.

• Communicate with Atlantic Central staff on a timely basis about activities undertaken by NSCUDIC.

## The key responsibilities in this role will be to:

• To conduct periodic reviews of Internal Control and Governance Reviews in assigned credit unions as well as working with system partners on Anti-Money Laundering risk management.

• Follow-up trends identified by the monitoring system within a group of assigned credit unions or within an individual credit union.

• Respond to identified issues of non-compliance and risk exposure for credit unions assigned to him/her.

• Maintain a working relationship with the provincial government, Atlantic Central, NSCUDIC's Board of Directors and Management, and Credit Union Management.

• Prepare reports on the status of credit unions as required.

• Maintain an efficient and timely monitoring system that effectively identifies and detects problems or deviations from standards. This includes monthly regulatory reports such as Overdraft Reports, Delinquency Reports, Allowance for Doubtful accounts, etc.

• To carry out the duties of the supervisor, for those credit unions directly under NSCUDIC's supervision.

• Provide emergency, short term, interim management in credit unions under supervision when required.

• Attend Board meetings of credit unions on Intervention as required.

• Work with Directors and Management of Credit Unions, as required, to provide consultation on rehabilitation direction in order to improve financial performance.

• Provide input and recommendations into the development of Policies, Standards of Sound Business Practices, Directives and Guidelines.

• Conduct information seminars at Manager meetings, relating to interpretations of policies, procedures, guidelines and standards issued by CUDIC.

• Review and forward to CEO/Manager//Superintendent/ Atlantic Central CEO Monthly/Quarterly Delinquency Reports.

• Credit Union Loan Limits: Lead the review of assigned Credit Union Loan Limits.

• Understand and be available to explain the NSCUDIC deposit coverage to Credit Unions and inquiries from the public.

• Operate as a portal for "best practices" of credit information acquired from the various credit unions and share that with the System.

• Complete Quarterly Credit Union Reports provided to NSCUDIC Board.

## The ideal candidate will possess:

• Post secondary degree with 10-15 years of related experience in risk management and compliance.

• Progressively senior audit, risk management and compliance experience and a history of providing strategic oversight in complex and highly accountable environments.

• Demonstrated knowledge of regulatory compliance frameworks and risk management practices, with the ability to interpret legislation, regulations, standards, and guidelines and apply them in a practical business environment.

• Knowledge of enterprise risk management, anti-money laundering practices, and emerging regulatory trends within the financial services sector.

• Familiarity with credit union operations, financial institution supervision, or cooperative business models.

• Strong commercial and financial acumen, and a demonstrated ability to contribute to organizational growth, resilience, and long-term sustainability.

• Ability to build productive relationships with leadership teams, regulators, industry partners, and community stakeholders.

• Collaborative approach, strong interpersonal skills, and the ability to navigate diverse viewpoints while helping organizations achieve their strategic objectives.

This is an amazing opportunity for a professional who has focused their career in risk management and compliance. NSCUDIC offers a hybrid working schedule. This isn't an opportunity to be missed!

To express interest in this opportunity please apply online at: https://meridiarecruitment.ca/Career/17913952554220000008cio

For more information about this exciting opportunity please contact Heather Labucki, Partner, or Sara Morey, Senior Consultant, at smorey@kbrs.ca. If you require accommodation to participate in the recruitment process, please let Sara Morey know.

title: Special Patient Program Lead
description:
Position Type:
Permanent
*

## Closing date:

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## Nature and Scope

Reporting to the Manager of Interprofessional Practice & Learning, the Special Patient Program (SPP) Lead shall be responsible for oversight of the EHS SPP, supporting the promotion of safe and effective person-centred care.

The incumbent will be responsible for, but not limited to, processing, amending and approving SPP applications, promoting the program within and outside of EMCI, overseeing revisions to the SPP process, developing care plans, and collaborating with patients, families, and healthcare providers. The SPP Lead shall work in close collaboration with Interprofessional Practice & Learning, Risk and Patient Safety, and Operations Divisions to ensure the success and sustainability of the SPP.

The incumbent will work directly with ground operations, the Medical Communications Centre, EHS physicians, Nova Scotia Health, and other partners to proactively identify patients requiring care and/or response plans and develop appropriate plans accordingly. The SPP Lead will also collaborate with EHS physicians to identify the need for, and development of, care plans.

The SPP Lead must have good organizational and computer skills and are able to work on their own with little supervision.

As an employee of EMC, the SPP Lead will be accountable to our patients and coworkers by participating in and supporting all safety related initiatives, as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture that focuses on patient safety and a safe workplace.

Though the position is listed as being in Dartmouth, it may be possible to work from anywhere within the province.

## Duties and Responsibilities

## Special Patient Program Care Plan Coordination and Management

Responsible for the review, development, implementation, and ongoing management of SPP enrolments and care plans. This includes, but is not limited to:

• Reviewing and processing enrolment requests, including approvals and denials.

• Developing, revising, and maintaining clinical and operational care plans.

• Analyzing call and patient data to identify opportunities for care plan

• enhancements.

• Collaborating with healthcare providers, EHS Clinical Teams, EMC leadership, and external partners to ensure care plans are accurate, complete, and responsive to patient needs.

• Supporting program reporting and monitoring enrolment trends and outcomes.

## Communication, Collaboration and Education

Act as a key liaison for internal and external partners regarding SPP activities and initiatives. This includes, but is not limited to:

• Communicating with healthcare providers, patients, families, partner organizations, and EMC teams.

• Providing education, guidance, and support related to the SPP for internal staff.

• Providing education, outreach, guidance and support related to the SPP for external partners and communities.

• Collaborating with EHS physicians, Nova Scotia Health, and other partners on complex care planning.

• Working directly with ground operations and the Medical Communications Centre to proactively identify patients requiring response plans and developing appropriate plans.

• Participating in committees, working groups, and program-related initiatives.

• Keeping leadership informed of program activities, issues, risks, and opportunities.

## Program Administration and Operational Support

Oversee and coordinate the administrative and operational functions required to support the effective delivery of the SPP. This includes, but is not limited to:

• Providing direction and guidance to the SPP Administrator.

• Maintaining accurate enrolment records and tracking patients through the care plan lifecycle.

• Entering, updating, validating, and maintaining program data and documentation.

• Developing, maintaining, and updating program processes, procedures, work

• instructions, and related documentation to support consistent program delivery.

• Monitoring inventory levels and coordinating the ordering of required program materials in a timely manner.

• Performing and overseeing program administration functions, including coverage during employee absences. This work includes:
• Preparing and distributing correspondence, mailings, and program materials.

• Maintaining organized electronic records and shared filing systems, ensuring they are up to date, clearly titled and free of unnecessary documents.

• Supporting operational efficiencies and ensuring administrative practices align with established program processes and standards.

• Assisting in the creation and dissemination of faxes and mailouts, which includes template completion, printing, packaging, mailing and faxing of material.

## QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

## Education / Experience:

• Regulated Healthcare Professional within Nova Scotia required; Paramedic or Registered Nurse preferred

• Experience working in a healthcare setting and with sensitive information is required

• Computer applications experience is required

• Previous quality assurance experience is an asset

• Experience with public speaking is an asset

• Familiarity in working with confidential information is an asset

• Participation in committees and/or working groups is an asset

• Working as part of a collaborative care team involving multiple disciplines is an asset

## Knowledge & Skills:

• Leadership skills

• Strong analytical, problem solving and organizational abilities are required

• Demonstrated ability to work independently and with others to achieve program goals

• Able to maintain a positive, supportive and inclusive attitude

• Understanding of medical terminology is required

• Ability to handle confidential and sensitive issues with tact and discretion

• Understanding of the EHS CPGs, protocols, and policies is a strong asset

• Understanding of EMC policies and directives is a strong asset

• Proficiency in the use of computers and information systems, including Microsoft Office applications, particularly MS Word, PowerPoint and Excel is required. Familiarity with using Access or other databases is an asset.

• Exercises a significant degree of discretion in the decision-making process.

• Engages team members in decision-making and for collaborative solutions.

• Proficient time management skills to meet deadlines

• Exemplary customer service and communication abilities, including written, oral, and presentation skills are required

• Strong interpersonal skills to build good working relationships with internal and external partners

• Candidates must recognize their own personal development requirements and demonstrate tangible efforts to continuously improve

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the citizens we serve. We are committed to building an inclusive team that represents a variety of backgrounds, cultures, races, perspectives and skills. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities. Candidates who identify as being from any of these groups are encouraged to voluntarily self-identify.

## Job Summary

The position of Medical Communications Officer (MCO) works within the Medical Communications Centre (MCC) with accountability to ensure coordination and balanced ambulance coverage to all communities within the designated coverage area. The MCO provides rapid response to requests for Routine, Emergency, and Non-Emergent Ambulance service, as well as coordinating the Flight Team and the Provincial Air Ambulance program. The MCO will work independently under the policies and guidelines of NLHS, reporting directly to the Operations Supervisor.

## Job Demands

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Occasionally lifts or moves objects weighing less than 25 lbs.

• Regularly required to sit at a work station for extended periods of time.

• Constantly uses fine finger precision work while working on a computer.

• Auditory demands include multiple phone lines ringing, listening for radio transmissions from ambulances, which have to be time stamped and entered into the computer, and background talking from other dispatchers and staff.

• Alertness and concentration are required when performing emergency medical dispatch work. Higher than normal levels of attentiveness or alertness for the health and safety of others is required at all times.

• Time pressures, interruptions, deadlines and lack of control over work pace are experienced when dealing with medical emergency dispatching and responding to 911 calls, listening to radio transmissions from ambulances and entering information into the computer.

## Job Qualifications

• Completion of an Emergency Medical Dispatcher (EMD) certificate with the International Academy of Emergency Medical Dispatchers (IAED) is required and must be valid when applying.?

• Completion of a recognized/approved Standard First Aid and BLS - CPR certification is required and must be valid when applying.?

• Completion of a recognized/approved Medical Terminology course is required*

• Successful completion of CritiCall aptitude testing is required. Testing will be administered by the Human Resources.?

• Computer literacy in a Windows environment with strong comprehensive computer skills required. A Windows skills test score of 70% is required. A Windows skills test will be administered by Human Resources.

• Knowledge of the geography of the province of Newfoundland Labrador, including major streets, highways, communities, regions, hospitals, and primary medical facilities, is required.?

• Knowledge of Microsoft Windows in a multi-screen computer environment is required.

• Demonstrated ability and dexterity in handling call-taking and dispatching functions using computer aided - dispatch, multi-line telephone, and radio communications systems is required.

• Demonstrated ability to define and carry out priorities as identified.

• Demonstrated ability work efficiently and effectively in a multi-tasking high stress environment is required.

• Demonstrated sound and rapid decision-making ability under stressful conditions is required.

• Demonstrated effective interpersonal communications and customer service skills to deal with the public and co-workers is required.

• Demonstrated strong critical thinking, decision making and problem-solving skills is required.

• Demonstrated excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively in English is required.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

*If medical terminology isn't current, a medical terminology test may be administered by the Human Resources Client Services Department.

This Occupational Therapist in this position practices independently and is an integral member of the interprofessional team. Regularly stands and walks and drives to and from sites/homes within the region.

Graduate of a school or program of occupational therapy recognized by the board.
Current licensure with the Newfoundland and Labrador Occupational Therapy Board.

Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, with interprofessional team members, patients/residents/clients and their families in a one-to-one and group environment.
Demonstrated effective written communication skills required for client documentation, report writing and professional communications
Demonstrated ability to effectively translate and communicate knowledge in the specialized area of occupational therapy practice to others.
Proven supervisory and leadership skills.
Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor and train Clinical Occupational Therapists, Occupational Therapist Support Workers and students.
Proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships as a member of an interprofessional team.
Proven ability to assume professional responsibility for safe, ethical and effective practice.
Proven ability to develop positive working relationships with external stakeholders.

A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required.

If there are no Primary Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Primary Care Paramedic, then Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to an EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Primary Care Paramedic (or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to persons suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as a PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

Position Summary
Morse Machining, in partnership with the Scotia Investments Family of Companies, is a progressive and growing company based in Hantsport, Nova Scotia. The Shop and Field Service Supervisor is responsible for overseeing day-to-day shop and field service operations, supporting workflow planning and scheduling, assisting with estimating and quoting, and ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, accurately, and on time.

Reporting to the General Manager, this role requires a dependable, hands-on leader who can support skilled trades teams, maintain strong customer service standards, and contribute to continuous improvement across machining, millwright, fabrication and field service.

## Key Responsibilities

• Lead day-to-day operations for shop and field service teams, including machinists, millwrights, mechanics, apprentices, and other skilled trades employees.

• Plan, schedule, and prioritize work to meet customer requirements, production timelines, and project deadlines.

• Monitor workflow, job progress, and resource allocation to ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, accurately, and on time.

• Support estimating and quoting by reviewing job requirements, labour needs, materials, timelines, specifications, and customer expectations.

• Oversee inventory management for parts, materials, tools, supplies, and equipment required to support shop and service operations.

• Support quality control by ensuring work meets specifications, drawings, customer requirements, and internal standards.

• Coordinate deliveries, including CKF-related deliveries and other customer or supplier requirements.

• Maintain accurate records related to work orders, estimates, schedules, inventory, quality, safety, and customer communication.

## Leadership, Safety, and Continuous Improvement

• Provide coaching, guidance, and day-to-day supervision to employees, including supporting apprentices and helping develop team capability.

• Promote and support a strong safety culture through safe work practices, hazard identification, housekeeping, and compliance with company policies and regulatory requirements.

• Identify and implement practical process improvements that enhance efficiency, communication, safety, productivity, quality, and customer service.

• Work collaboratively with trades employees, customers, suppliers, leadership, and other stakeholders to keep work moving and resolve issues effectively.

## Qualifications and Experience

• Previous supervisory, operations, or project coordination experience in a skilled trades, industrial, manufacturing, service, maintenance, machining, millwright, fabrication, or equipment repair environment.

• Experience leading or supervising skilled trades employees is preferred.

• Strong understanding of estimating, quoting, scheduling, inventory management, quality control, and process improvement.

• Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, work orders, and customer requirements.

• Knowledge of machining, welding, fabrication, industrial maintenance, mobile equipment, hydraulics, pneumatics, mechanical systems, and related shop or field service work is considered an asset.

• Comfort using technology, including email, scheduling tools, work order systems, spreadsheets, and other business software.

## Skills and Competencies

• Practical, hands-on leadership style with the ability to support employees, solve problems, and maintain operational momentum.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities, deadlines, and changing customer needs.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to work effectively with internal teams, customers, suppliers, and leadership.

• Commitment to safety, quality, accuracy, customer service, and continuous improvement.

• Sound judgment, reliability, accountability, and the ability to work well in a deadline-driven, fast-paced environment.

## Required and Preferred Certifications

• Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

• Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) Certificate preferred.

• First Aid Certificate preferred.

• Basic security clearance may be required.

Working Conditions
This is a full-time, permanent position based in Hantsport, Nova Scotia. Regular hours are expected to include Monday to Friday daytime hours, with flexibility required to support operational needs, customer requirements, on-call situations, and special projects. The role involves time in both office and shop environments and may include exposure to manufacturing or industrial conditions such as noise, dust, odours, moving equipment, and active work areas.

## Total Compensation

• Comprehensive group insurance.

• Company pension plan.

• Company events, training opportunities, and free on-site parking.

To apply, please send your resume to recruitment@morsemachining.com

title: Senior Legal Counsel
description:
The Financial and Consumer Services Commission (Commission) is a leader in integrated financial and consumer services regulation. The Commission's mandate is to protect consumers and enhance public confidence in the financial and consumer marketplace through the provision of regulatory and educational services. With offices in both Fredericton and Saint John, it is responsible for the administration and enforcement of provincial legislation regulating mortgage brokers, payday lenders, real estate, securities, insurance, pensions, credit unions, trust and loan companies, cooperatives, unclaimed property, and a wide range of consumer legislation. The Commission is a self funded Crown corporation responsible for the administration and enforcement of financial consumer services legislation.

We offer opportunities for dedicated professionals to play a vital role in carrying out our mandate.

## Senior Legal Counsel, Enforcement Division (Saint John or Fredericton Office)

We're looking for an experienced Senior Legal Counsel to join our Enforcement Division, where you'll work at the centre of complex regulatory matters, partnering with investigators to identify and assess misconduct, determine appropriate enforcement action and build strong cases. You'll manage matters from investigation through resolution or hearing, providing trusted legal advice and representing the Commission before the Tribunal (the Energy and Utilities Board) and courts.

As Senior Legal Counsel, you'll use your legal expertise, sound judgement and strategic thinking to focus on:

• Reviewing investigations: Collaborate with investigators to disrupt misconduct, build cases and assess evidence. Provide legal advice and interpretations of legislation under the Commission's jurisdiction, including determining whether regulatory or criminal laws have been breached and preparing related legal analyses and reports.

• Hearings and applications: Conduct legal research, draft pleadings and prepare witnesses. Prepare for and conduct hearings and applications before the Tribunal, as well as judicial reviews and interim applications before the courts, as required.

• Disclosure and settlements: Prepare and conduct disclosure in accordance with legal standards and negotiate settlement agreements, where appropriate.

• Legal opinions and advice: Provide legal opinions and day-to-day advice to Commission staff on administrative, procedural and policy issues related to enforcement.

• Monitoring enforcement: Monitor enforcement actions in other jurisdictions and liaise with regulatory counterparts.

• Appeals: Represent regulators before the Tribunal in appeals of administrative decisions.

## What you Bring

• Law degree;

• Membership in Law Society of New Brunswick;

• 7+ years' litigation experience;

• A strong ability to analyze complex legal issues that arise during investigations and enforcement actions;

• An ability to play a lead role and manage complex projects;

• An ability to write clearly and concisely;

• Exceptional listening, interviewing, questioning and probing skills;

## Additional Strengths

• Bilingualism is an asset

The Financial and Consumer Services Commission offers a competitive salary and benefit package as well as excellent opportunities for personal growth and challenge. Salary will be commensurate with experience. If you are interested in being a key part of this team, please forward your résumé and covering letter.

Salary Range: $106,401 to $146,301 (annual compensation)

As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a pre-employment background check in accordance with the Commission's Pre-Employment Background Checks Directive. This may include criminal record checks, credential verification, and reference checks.

For more information about this position please visit our website at www.fcnb.ca or call the Talent Acquisition Specialist at (506) 643-7790.

Please note that only candidates selected for further evaluation will be contacted.

title: Project Manager
description:
## Job Title: Project Manager
Location: Antigonish, Nova Scotia
TP - TOA - 10223

The Town of Antigonish is committed to building and maintaining the infrastructure that supports a vibrant, sustainable, and connected community. Through strategic investments in municipal services, public facilities, transportation networks, and community development initiatives, the Town of Antigonish continues to enhance quality of life for residents while supporting long-term growth and prosperity.

Meridia Recruitment has partnered with the Town of Antigonish to recruit a Project Manager to join their Infrastructure and Engineering team.

## Role Description

Reporting to the Director of Infrastructure and Engineering, the Project Manager will play a key role in the planning, coordination, and delivery of municipal infrastructure and operational projects. This position is responsible for providing project management and technical support across a diverse portfolio of capital initiatives, ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with municipal, provincial, and federal standards.

Working closely with contractors, consultants, municipal staff, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders, the Project Manager will oversee projects from planning and procurement through execution and close-out. This is an excellent opportunity for a collaborative and solutions-focused professional who enjoys balancing technical project delivery with stakeholder engagement and operational leadership.

## Your responsibilities will include:

• Lead the planning, coordination, and delivery of municipal capital and operational projects.

• Develop project plans, schedules, budgets, and timelines while monitoring progress against established milestones.

• Prepare, review, administer, and manage tenders, Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and Requests for Quotations (RFQs).

• Coordinate consultants, contractors, internal departments, and external stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.

• Conduct site inspections and oversee project activities to ensure compliance with applicable standards, regulations, and project requirements.

• Monitor project budgets, evaluate invoices, support financial forecasting, and contribute to annual budgeting processes.

• Identify project risks and implement mitigation strategies to support successful project outcomes.

• Manage stakeholder engagement and communication plans, ensuring clear and timely project updates.

• Assist with the preparation of drawings, quantity calculations, tender documentation, and construction-related specifications.

• Support funding applications and reporting requirements for provincial and federal infrastructure programs.

• Review contractor safety submissions and promote compliance with workplace health and safety legislation and policies.

• Respond to public inquiries, complaints, and requests while maintaining positive relationships with community stakeholders.

The Family Practice Nurse Practitioner will work in close collaboration with physicians and other interdisciplinary health professionals in a community-based collaborative care clinic. As a vital member of the team, the Nurse Practitioner is responsible for delivering high-quality comprehensive primary care to patients with a focus on the assessment and management across the full spectrum of primary care presentations in all populations, as well as health education, disease prevention, and chronic disease management.

## About Us

The clinic is a new collaborative care practice established to provide primary care to the community. The clinic will work collaboratively with health authorities and community partners to enhance local patient care and improve professional satisfaction for all health care team members. At the clinic, we will strive to create a welcoming space for staff and patients. We will maintain a culture of improvement, with all team members contributing to better health care systems. We believe primary care should be accessible to all New Brunswickers and will work hard to provide continuity and access to our patients.

## Why work with us?

• Competitive salary.

• Experienced, multi-disciplinary team.

• Career development - continuous education/advancement encouraged.

• Comprehensive benefits package available. Additional pay in lieu of benefits negotiable.

• Cross-coverage of your practice while you are absent.

• Heavily clinical- and patient-focused role as part of an innovative team!

## Key Responsibilities

• Independently manage a family practice roster.

• Cross-coverage of parallel practices while other providers are absent.

• Focused engagement in quality improvement initiatives and performance tracking to improve delivery of care.

• In collaboration with other providers:
• Create and maintain up-to-date patient charts.

• Review incoming investigations.

• Primary care acute/urgent issues assessment and management.

• Chronic disease management and surveillance.

• Opportunities for engagement on patient panels of interest, including (but not limited to) acute care, sexual health, mental health, perinatal health, pediatric medicine, etc.

## Working Conditions

The NP position requires availability to work in the clinic during regular working hours from Monday to Friday. Cross-coverage expectations, after-hours clinics, virtual care/work from home clinics, and/or occasional meeting attendance outside of office hours are negotiable.

## Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in nursing and successful completion of a postgraduate Nurse Practitioner program in Primary Health Care.

• Current CPR or Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS) Registration.

• Current formalized physician consultant role (note: employer can provide same).

• Medical expert with in-depth knowledge of patient care.

• Excellent organizational and time-management skills.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently and efficiently, while maintaining accuracy, critical thinking, and proper judgement.

• Dedication to professional improvement.

• Adherence to professional ethical principles.

• Previous experience with an electronic medical record (EMR) program is an asset.

• Knowledge of the NB primary health care system is an asset.

• Bilingualism is an asset.

Email your CV to Dr.Matthew.Piamonte@horizonnb.ca.

The Senior Data Analyst, reporting the Lead, Data and Analytics, in Humanitarian Services plays a critical role in driving data-informed decision-making by performing advanced data analysis, developing reports, and optimizing data processes. This position works with large datasets, designs dashboards and other visualizations, and provides analytics results to support business strategies. ## In this role, you will:

business objectives

• Lead and coordinate data analysis, reporting, and audit activities for assigned clients or projects

• Apply advanced analytical techniques to identify trends, insights, and areas for improvement.

• Collaborate to rationalize and standardize cross-platform data analysis.

• Develop reports and presentations to communicate findings and insights to partners and leadership.

including support to testing.

privacy.

• Identify emerging trends and opportunities in the data analytics field and provide recommendations on how to leverage these to enhance the organization's data analytics capabilities.

title: Policy Opportunities (Future Opportunity Stream)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49448

Department: Government of Nova Scotia

Location: Multiple Locations

Type of Employment: Permanent

Union Status: Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date: 30-Jun-27 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Help Shape Public Policy in Nova Scotia
Policy work helps government make better decisions. It turns research, evidence, public needs, operational realities, legislation, data and stakeholder perspectives into clear advice and practical next steps.

Across the Government of Nova Scotia, policy professionals work on issues that affect people, communities, programs, services and systems. Some roles focus on research and analysis. Others focus on legislation, regulations, Cabinet submissions, program policy, corporate reporting, data, service delivery, stakeholder engagement evaluation or implementation planning.

This Future Opportunity Stream offers a one-application pathway to be considered for future policy opportunities across government.

What this Future Opportunity Stream Is
This is not a posting for one specific vacancy.

By applying to this stream, you are expressing interest in being considered for future policy work opportunities across the Government of Nova Scotia.

Opportunities may vary by department, job classification, union status, location, level of responsibility, and area of policy work. These will include bargaining unit (unionized) policy roles as well as excluded classification (non-unionized) positions. Positions could be Permanent, Term or Temporary.

Being part of this stream does not guarantee an interview or job offer. Candidates must still meet the qualifications and assessment requirements for each specific opportunity.

Why Apply to This Stream
This stream makes it easier to be considered for future policy roles across the Government of Nova Scotia.

Instead of applying separately every time a policy vacancy becomes available, you can submit one application and complete one Policy Candidate Profile. Talent Acquisition may then use your information to consider you for multiple future opportunities where your background appears to be a strong fit.

This helps us better understand not only whether you have policy experience, but what kind of policy work you have done, what products you have worked on, how much responsibility you carried and which roles may be a strong fit.

How it Works
To be considered through this stream, you must complete both:

• the online application, including your resume and required information

• the Policy Candidate Profile questionnaire

The Policy Candidate Questionnaire is required, and the link will be emailed to you within 14 days of us receiving your application. This information helps Talent Acquisition understand your preferences and experience in more detail, along with reviewing your application, resume and cover letter.

As vacancies arise, Talent Acquisition may review candidates in the stream and identify those whose application and Policy Candidate Profile appear to align with a specific role.

If you are identified as a potential match, Talent Acquisition will contact you before your application is forwarded for review. You will be provided with a description of the specific job opportunity and will have the chance to confirm whether you are still interested in being considered.
Click here for more information on Future Opportunity Streams.

Policy Analyst & Senior Policy Analyst Roles
This stream will support Policy Analyst and Senior Policy Analyst opportunities across government.

Policy Analyst roles may involve research and analysis, drafting, coordination and reporting, program or service delivery policy, legislative or regulatory support, stakeholder engagement and the preparation of advice, recommendations or briefing materials.

Senior Policy Analyst roles generally involve greater independence and responsibility for more complex files, including developing strategic advice and recommendations and working with senior leaders, decision-makers, partners and colleagues across government.

The exact duties, classification, union status, qualifications and assessment requirements will vary by opportunity. Role-specific details will be provided if you are considered for a particular opportunity through this stream.

Click here for more information about the general expectations, responsibilities, and scope of work associated with Policy Analyst and Senior Policy Analyst roles.Qualifications
Specific qualifications vary between each unique role.

Policy Analyst and Senior Policy Analyst positions may have different requirements based on the classification, department, level of responsibility and nature of the work. Some roles, including bargaining unit positions, may have defined requirements related to education, training and years of related experience.

If you are considered for a specific opportunity, your application will be reviewed against the qualifications and assessment requirements for that role.

We are looking for candidates with education, training and/or experience related to policy, research, analysis, program development, evaluation, legislation, regulation, corporate reporting, data analysis, stakeholder engagement, service delivery or decision support.

Equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience may be considered where applicable. This means you may still be considered if you do not meet the exact education path listed for a specific role, but you have a related mix of education, courses, professional training and practical experience that demonstrates the required knowledge, skills, and abilities. Candidates relying on equivalencies must clearly demonstrate in their application how their education and/or experience meets the requirements of the role.

Assets That May Help Us Match You
Assets will vary by role. Some examples include experience with:

• Briefing notes, briefing binders, reports, presentations or decision materials

• Cabinet, Executive Council, Treasury and Policy Board or other senior approval processes

• Legislation, regulations, bylaws, governance or compliance

• Jurisdictional scans, literature reviews, research reports or policy options papers

• Data analysis, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, dashboards or data visualization

title: Production Supervisor
description:
Requisition ID: 2664

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
To plan, organize and direct the activities of assigned personnel to meet safety, productivity, schedule, quality and administrative objectives and standards of the department. To ensure these activities are performed in accordance with the approved applicable standard plant procedures (SPPs) and with current technical data.

The Production Supervisor will report to Electronic Systems in Hammonds Plains.

What You Will Do:
• Supervise all cable and wire harness manufacturing activities, including wire cutting, stripping and marking, crimping, soldering, connector and backshell assembly, shielding and braiding, potting and electrical testing, to ensure work is completed safely, to required quality standards, and within productivity objectives and schedule

• Plan, prioritize and assign work orders and personnel based on the production schedule, material availability and labour capacity, adjusting priorities as required to meet customer delivery commitments

• Ensure work is performed to the current revision of drawings, wiring diagrams, specifications and work instructions, and that any changes, rework or supplemental work are recorded and initiated correctly

• Ensure workmanship meets IPC/WHMA-A-620 (Class 3), IPC J-STD-001 and customer-specific requirements (e.g., NASA-STD-8739.4), and that assemblers hold current certifications for the work they perform

• Ensure work order travelers, process records and labour transactions are completed accurately and in a timely manner

• Review daily clocking and productivity reports for accuracy and initiate action to correct errors

• Monitor work-in-progress, shortages and bottlenecks, and work with Planning, Purchasing and Stores to resolve material and kitting issues

• Ensure cleanroom and controlled-environment protocols, FOD prevention and a high standard of housekeeping, safety and workplace hygiene are achieved and sustained

• Ensure supervisory obligations of the AS9100 Quality System are met, including reporting non-conformances, containment, root cause analysis and corrective action; support MRB, customer source inspections and MIPs

• Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to resolve technical issues and drawing discrepancies, and to improve processes, methods and cycle times

• Maintain a high standard of discipline and conduct within the workplace, managing attendance, performance and employee relations in accordance with the collective agreement and company policy

• Maintain and review department employment and training records, including the skills matrix and workmanship certifications

• Supervise overtime and off-shift crews

• Support Continuous Improvement, Lean and 5S activities in the area

• Stand in for the Production Manager and provide status and production briefing response at program meetings when required

• Other duties as required

What You Will Bring:
• A minimum of six years experience in cable and wire harness or electrical/electronic assembly manufacturing (aerospace, defence or space preferred), including a minimum of three years in a supervisory role, or a suitable combination of education, training, civil/military experience and record of achievement

• Current or previous IPC/WHMA-A-620 certification is strongly preferred; IPC J-STD-001 and/or NASA workmanship certification is an asset

• Strong working knowledge of harness fabrication processes, including wire preparation, crimp and solder terminations, connector and backshell assembly, shielding and electrical testing

• Must be capable of reading and interpreting engineering drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics, connector pinouts, Bills of Material, specifications, Work Orders (WOs) and work instructions

• Working knowledge of AS9100 quality system requirements, including non-conformance reporting, root cause and corrective action, and First Article Inspection (AS9102)

• Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling and capacity planning

• Strong communication, interpersonal and computer skills are a must, including proficiency with the MS Office suite (Excel in particular)

• Must be able to manage multiple priorities and support multiple tasks on a consistent basis

• Must have the ability to organize, schedule and plan daily activities while supporting staff with technical knowledge

• Knowledge of Labour Relations and Union environments

• Must be flexible with work hours and willing to work irregular hours, overtime and rotating shifts (730am to 4pm, 330pm to 12am) when needed

• Must have a mature and professional appearance & behavior and lead by example at all times

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies

• Participate in Continuous Improvement, Lean & 5S activities in your area

• Must be eligible to meet requirements for Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP), and Secret Level II Security Clearance through PSPC- Contract Security Program

What We Will Do For You:
• All IMP's benefits become effective on your first day of work, regardless of your position.

• Employees are entitled to 3 paid personal days and 12 statutory holidays per year.

• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RRSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

IMP is committed to Employment Equity and our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative at all job levels. We welcome applicants from Indigenous People, Visible Minority Groups, Persons with Disabilities and Women in occupations or positions where they are under-represented. If you are a member of one of these equity groups, you are encouraged to self identify on either your cover letter or resume.

description:

Imagine a career where, at the end of every day, you know you've made a positive difference in the lives of people who need your help.

NB Health Link (NBHL) leverages technological solutions and innovative clinical delivery models to provide access to care for New Brunswickers who don't have a family doctor or nurse practitioner. The program provides patients who are registered with the program access to a network of family doctors, physician assistants and nurse practitioners throughout the province - offering in-person, telephone and online appointments in both official languages.

As part of NBHL, your role is vital in our province's overall health. Join an integrated team of health care professionals, dedicated to providing New Brunswickers with outstanding, highly coordinated primary health care.

## JOB SUMMARY

The Nurse Practitioner (NP) is a generalist who offers quality and relevant care across the health continuum and throughout the patient's lifespan, including health promotion, disease and injury, prevention, curative, supportive, rehabilitative, and palliative care within an interdisciplinary team of health providers.

The service model is based on the principles of primary health care with the goal of supporting communities in meeting their health care needs.

As a key member of the NB Health Link team, the NP is responsible and accountable for their practice and professional conduct while working in collaboration with physicians to ensure quality and relevant care.

As an EM/ANB employee, the NPs are accountable to our patients and families and co-workers by participating in and supporting safety related initiatives as well as acting in a manner that fosters a culture of learning.Safety for patients, caregivers, and workplace are kept the priority.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Integrates a broad knowledge base and critical appraisal in determining and communicating the diagnosis and the patient's needs.

• Applies advanced assessment techniques, critical thinking and clinical decision-making skills when assessing patients.

• Systematically collects documents and critically analyzes health data by performing a holistic health assessment using multiple tools and sources of data.

• Completes a prescription accurately and completely according to relevant legislation, standards, and policies.

• Orders diagnostic imaging tests, laboratory and other tests when clinically indicated and in accordance with the Nurse Practitioner Schedules and program guidelines for Ordering.

• Promotes health and reduces the risk of complications, illness, and injury for patients.

• Ensures that diagnostic tests are interpreted, and results are acted upon in an appropriate and timely manner.

• Monitor the ongoing therapy of patients with chronic stable illnesses.

• Screen for the presence of chronic illnesses and works in collaboration with physicians who identified presence of chronic illness in patients.

• Monitors the effectiveness of interventions.

• Facilitates the patient's transition within and between health care settings, e.g., admitting,

transferring, and discharging patients.

• Ability to work independently and as part of the interdisciplinary team including making appropriate referrals.

• Documents clinical data, assessment findings, diagnosis, plan of care, therapeutic intervention (including consent), patients' response and clinical rationale in a timely and accurate manner in the patient health record.

• Maintain a positive working relationship with the interdisciplinary team.

• Help build protocols and templates in prevention medicine for the program.

• Responsibilities to support the core provincial program will be the primary task.

• Other responsibilities may be assigned to support the program.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND OTHER JOB REQUIREMENTS:

• Bachelor's Degree in Nursing and successful completion of a postgraduate Nurse Practitioner program in Primary Health Care.

• Registered as a Nurse Practitioner with the College of Nursing of New Brunswick (CNNB)

• Current Basic Life Saving certificate and maintain certification.

• At least 2 years' experience in primary health care setting in Community Health Centre or Collaborative Practice. ;

• Excellent interpersonal, oral and written communication skills;

• Demonstrated organizational and leadership skills;

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with other members of a team toward common goals;

• Demonstrated ability to function independently in the role with recognized decision-making and problem-solving skills;

• Demonstrated ability to critically analyze theory and research literature and apply to practice;

• Demonstrated ability to integrate a determinants of health approach into care delivery;

• Actively participates as a team member to provide comprehensive care to all patients;

• Must be able to work all shifts as assigned, maintaining a good attendance record;

• Adherence to professional ethical principles.

• Skillful use of computer tools and Microsoft Office Programs.

All interested applicants are encouraged to apply as an equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

We would like to thank all candidates for expressing interest. Please note only those selected for interviews will be contacted.

NBHL is committed to the principle of equal opportunity in its employment practices and to providing an environment free from discrimination and harassment for all employees.

title: Payroll, Pension & Benefits Service Coordinator
description:
## Purpose of position

The Payroll, Pension & Benefits Coordinator is the frontline contact with employees regarding payroll, pension and benefits services.

Under the direction of the Payroll, Pensions and Benefits Services Manager, the coordinators are responsible to ensure the accuracy of employee data for all facets of the payroll, pensions & benefits transactional business processing. Responsible for entering all master file changes, payroll transactions and ensuring employees are registered in all benefit and pension plans as soon as they are first eligible, as well as liaising between employees and the plan providers. PPB Coordinators play an important role in all Leave of Absence (LOA) processes; ensuring benefit and pension continuation is communicated and carried out for the duration of an employee's leave.

## Key responsibilities

• Provide guidance and advice to employees regarding payroll, pension and benefits, utilizing exceptional interpersonal skills and knowledge of each union group and their respective Collective Agreements and company policies.

• Establish employee benefits eligibility, coverages, effective dates and payroll premium deduction set-up in accordance with union contracts and benefit policy agreements.

• Serve as intermediary between employees and Canada Life, Sun Life and payroll third parties.

• Ensures all payroll, pension and benefits documents, booklets and information brochures are accurate and current for dissemination.

• Deliver benefits & pension orientation to new employees by providing a summary overview of plan-specific benefits.

## Data Input and Payroll, Pension & Benefits (PP&Bs) Processing

• Process initial new hire payroll documents to ensure all necessary information is received and entered accurately in Ultimate Kronos Group (UKG); follow up as required. Create new hire files and file accordingly.

• Update employee earnings and deductions in accordance with the payroll checklists and specific events processing.

• Ensure that procedures including events processing checklists are current at all times.

• Process benefit enrollment forms and coordinate any required paperwork to be sent internally or to third party.

• Enter payroll employee data and status changes with existing employees in the system. Update payroll, pensions and benefits workflows as required from employee or manager notifications (new hires, terminations, leaves, returns, rehires, status changes).

• Audit and review for accuracy.

• Audit all payroll entries using pay period files, registers and the daily audit reports to ensure accuracy.

• Process payroll adjustments for employee refunds/collecting premiums as appropriate.

• Update beneficiary & dependent information in system (send pension & RRSP forms to Sun Life if applicable).

• Review & action insurance carrier correspondence for issuing waiver of premium entitlements under the group life insurance benefits.

• Return to Work Audit - audit payroll to ensure all premium payments are up to date for returning employees.

• Review termination notices and calculate final pay including lieu of notice, severance etc.; Review details for effective dates and potential continuation of pay and or benefits (Involuntary Separation Packages (ISPs) or retirees).

• Issue Records of Employment (ROEs) for terminating employees in the current pay.

• Issuing letters and entering year to date transactions for employees on leave that are set up with direct debit (formerly manual cheque processing).

• Work with the reporting and control team members investigating and correcting variances as required.

## Issuance of Letters & Correspondence

• Benefit & Pension Continuation Letters; maintain election forms & banking info.

• Termination of benefits letter (if no response received to Benefit Continuation Letter). Shut off benefits in system for employees who decline or who do not respond to Benefit Continuation letter.

• Employment termination letter (option of continuing benefits).

• Confirmation of eligible dependants.

• Provide amounts of premiums paid for income tax purposes.

• Direct Debit and Cheque Processing for Employees on Leave.

• Enter direct withdrawal benefit continuation data into Ulti-pro system (monthly).

• Enter Canada Life/Manulife-paid pension data (pilot group).

• Cross Reference Benefit Deduction File and Initial Cheque Report and forward to Pension Specialist for pension approval.

• Perform duties in accordance with established policies and procedures while giving primary consideration to personal safety, and the safety of co-workers and customer.

• Perform other related duties, as assigned.

## Required qualifications

• Knowledge and experience of processing payroll and benefits.

• Strong attention to detail.

• Ability to carry out multiple tasks in accordance with strict deadline.

• Strong knowledge of Microsoft Outlook, word and excel.

• Strong interpersonal skills.

• English language fluency, both written and verbal. (Must be able to communicate with English internal and external customers across the country).

## Preferred qualifications

• Undergraduate Degree or College Diploma.

• PCP (Payroll Compliance Practitioner) designation.

• CEBS (Certified Employee Benefits Specialist).

• French language fluency or working knowledge.

## Benefits of joining our award-winning team

• Enjoy exclusive employee travel programs across the Air Canada network, giving you and your family access to incredible destinations.

• Secure your long-term financial well-being with our competitive, employer-supported retirement savings programs (defined contribution pension plan or voluntary group RRSP) for permanent employees.

• Benefit from a comprehensive health and wellness package, including health, dental, life, and accident insurance to keep you and your loved ones protected.

## About Jazz Aviation LP

Jazz Aviation LP (Jazz) is Canada’s largest regional airline and Air Canada’s primary Air Canada Express operator, connecting people and communities to approximately 70 destinations across North America.

With over 4,200 dedicated professionals, Jazz fosters a workplace united by purpose and supported by programs and policies that promote safety, diversity, and wellness. Jazz is proud to be recognized for its strong commitment to people and culture. Visit our Company Awards and Recognition page to learn more about the honours we've earned.

Join our award-winning team and be part of shaping the future of regional aviation!

## Our commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility

We strive to make our workplace accessible and inclusive. To support your success, we can provide accommodations for people with disabilities, such as adjustments or assistive measures to remove barriers during the recruitment process. If you require any accessibility support, please contact us at taleosupport@flyjazz.ca.

Jazz values diversity and we empower our employees to foster an internal culture of inclusion. Jazz is committed to providing equitable opportunities for employment and career advancement and we will continuously work to create inclusive and accessible work environments to maximize individual potential as well as psychological health and safety. Meeting the needs of passengers is critical to our success and we recognize the importance of a workforce that is reflective of the communities we serve.
