Definition of Work:
Work involves providing nursing care and treatment services for the physically ill, disabled and/or cognitively impaired clients under the direction of a Registered Nurse. The successful candidate must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements.

Physical Demands:
By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):
• Constantly moves/lifts up to 10-15lbs, regularly moves/lifts up to 50lbs; required to restrain/reposition/move/lift up to, or above, 50lbs with co-worker assistance and repetitively required to complete pushing/pulling with medium force (22-44lbsF).
• Constantly stands/walks. May work in awkward or cramped positions to assist with care. Work repetitively involves reaching/stretching, bending/twisting and repeated bouts of low-level postures such as squatting, crouching or stooping.
• Potential for exposure to blood, bodily fluids and/or other contagion. May be exposed to patients/residents with potential risk for aggressive behavior.
• Work Environments present potential for exposure to scented/chemical products and/or other allergens within publicly accessible areas.

Required qualifications:
• Graduation from a practical nursing program approved by Central Health.
• Current BLS certification.
• Current registration with the College of Licensed Practical Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador.
• Demonstrated effective interpersonal and communication skills.
• Demonstrated competency in working to the full scope of practice (as per the CLPNNL and Central Health’s policies and procedures) and standards of care relevant to designated client population.
• Completion of other skills and post basic competencies as required.

title: Care Coordinator (Intensive Planning Support Coordinator) (Designated)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 50039

Department: Opportunities and Social Development

Location: SYDNEY

Type of Employment: Term

Union Status: NSGEU - NSPG

Closing Date: 01-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Designation Status
This opportunity is designated to applicants who identify as Indigenous.

See the Nova Scotia Government's Employment Equity Policy for more information, including additional details on the designated groups.

About Us
At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Employment Support Services (ESS), Income Assistance (IA), Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

The Disability Support Program (DSP) is committed to fostering innovative ways to empower individuals with disabilities to pursue their vision of a fulfilling life. We are on a journey to implement international best practices that uphold human rights and choice to enhance the way people engage with their communities. We envision Nova Scotia as a place where people with disabilities can choose the life they want to live, in communities that are welcoming, inclusive, and supportive. A life where individuals can build authentic relationships, explore their interests, and achieve their full potential as valued citizens in their community.

About Our Opportunity
We are looking for passionate, values-driven people to join our team as Intensive Planning and Support Coordinators (IPSCs), a vital new role helping bring to life the Human Rights Remedy and create real change in the lives of people with disabilities.

As an IPSC, you'll work alongside individuals at the speed of trust, specifically those transitioning from institutional settings or with complex support needs, helping them shape their own futures. You'll build strong, trusting relationships, focus on each person's unique strengths, and support them to live full, inclusive lives as active citizens in their communities.

This is a transformative, human-rights-based role. You'll work closely with clinical and allied health professionals, mainstream services, and local communities, building partnerships that strengthen the support around each person. You'll be a key advocate for the individuals you support, ensuring their voices are heard and their choices respected.

We're looking for people who are compassionate, adaptable, and committed to a strengths-based, trauma-informed approach. You'll need to be comfortable working independently and tailoring your support to each person's communication style, creating a safe, respectful space where people can express themselves and make their own decisions.

Primary Accountabilities
As an Intensive Planning and Support Coordinator (IPSC), you will play a key role in providing intensive, personalized support and planning. You'll work alongside individuals with disabilities to create, implement, and continuously refine support plans that reflect their unique needs, aspirations, and rights.

You'll build strong, respectful relationships with individuals and their support networks. By gathering and assessing information together, you'll support informed decision-making and help connect people with the services and professionals that best fit their goals.

A big part of your work will involve supporting individuals as they move from institutional settings into community life. You'll coordinate these transitions thoughtfully, making sure each step is supported and centred on the person's vision for their future.

In this dynamic role, you'll balance multiple priorities while maintaining strong relationships with service providers, government agencies, healthcare professionals, and community organizations.

You'll use your knowledge of multidisciplinary services to build partnerships and strengthen community capacity. This includes helping individuals access the right resources while also working to improve the systems around them.

Creating inclusive, person-centred plans means bringing the right people together. You'll help build connections to natural support networks, peer supports, and community relationships that reflect each individual's culture, values, and preferences.

Throughout your work, you'll be guided by a deep commitment to person-directed planning, supportive decision-making, and the rights of people with disabilities, as outlined in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. This is a role where your compassion, creativity, and advocacy can help create meaningful, lasting change in people's lives.

Qualifications and Experience
You are a Licensed Professional in Nursing (RN or LPN), Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy or Nutritional Studies, plus five (5) years of related experience. You must be currently registered, or eligible for registration, with your applicable professional association.

A valid driver's license and access to reliable transportation are required (as an inclusive employer, we are committed to considering accommodations in accordance with the Human Rights Act). In addition, you have:

• Ability to develop, implement, and evaluate comprehensive support plans tailored to individual needs and aspirations.

• Skills in facilitating and promoting supportive decision-making practices.

• An understanding of trauma and its impact, with the ability to adapt support approaches.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information in an accessible manner.

• Proven ability to establish and maintain trusting relationships with individuals, families, support networks, and professional partners.

• Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, capable of mediating complex personal and environmental dynamics to develop innovative solutions.

• Experience in collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, including healthcare professionals, service providers, and community organizations.

• Strong advocacy skills, cultural competence, and an understanding of Disability Rights and Legislation as well as community resources and services

Assets include:

• A completed related Master's degree

• Additional certifications or training in trauma-informed care, disability rights, or community engagement.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Equivalencies include:

• a Master's degree in either Nursing, Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy or Nutritional Studies plus three (3)years of related experience.

Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
The IPSC will travel to various locations including homes, facilities, and hospitals, supporting individuals with disabilities, including those with complex needs. The role involves extensive driving, entering private residences, and occasional lifting. Travel is required throughout the region or province, under varying weather conditions. The role requires resilience in handling emotional situations, potential aggression, and navigating diverse family dynamics. IPSCs must make professional judgments in complex situations and work inclusively with culturally diverse individuals. This environment underscores the importance of adaptability and emotional resilience.

Additional Information
This is a TERM employment opportunity with an anticipated end date of August 1, 2027. The appointment status ('term', 'temporary' or 'casual') is dependent on the start date of the successful candidate.

We may use this posting to fill additional IPSC roles within 4 months of the closing date of this competition.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career

• Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies

• Countless career paths

title: Category Lead, Procurement
description:
Job Title: Category Lead, Procurement
Location: Halifax, Nova Scotia
TP - DAL - 10237

Dalhousie University is Atlantic Canada's leading research-intensive university and a driver of the region's intellectual, social and economic development. Located in the heart of Halifax, Nova Scotia, with an Agricultural Campus in Truro/Bible Hill, Dalhousie is a truly national and international university, with more than half of our almost 21,000 students coming from outside of the province. Our 6,000 faculty and staff foster a vibrant, purpose-driven community, that celebrated 200 years of academic excellence in 2018.

As the University continues to invest in modernization and operational excellence, procurement has become an increasingly strategic function supporting teaching, research, technology, and campus operations across a diverse and complex institution.
Meridia Recruitment is pleased to partner with Dalhousie University in recruiting a Category Lead, Procurement to join their Strategic Procurement team during an exciting period of transformation and growth.

## Role Description:

• Reporting to the Manager, Strategic Procurement, the Category Lead, Procurement will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of procurement at Dalhousie University. As the University's first Category Lead, you will help establish strategic category management practices, support procurement modernization efforts, and influence purchasing decisions across a diverse and complex institutional environment.

• Over the past several years, Dalhousie has embarked on a significant procurement transformation journey, implementing a new procurement platform and advancing a more centralized procurement model. This newly created role is a critical next step in that evolution, helping move procurement beyond transactional purchasing toward a strategic, value-driven function.

• Working closely with stakeholders across faculties, research groups, and administrative departments, you will develop category strategies, analyze organizational spend, identify opportunities for optimization, and lead sourcing initiatives that deliver measurable value. While initially supporting technology-related procurement categories, including software, hardware, and IT services, this position offers a rare opportunity to build category management capability from the ground up while leaving a lasting impact on one of Canada's leading universities.

## Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Sourcing & Category Management:

• Develop and implement category strategies aligned with institutional priorities and stakeholder needs.

• Conduct spend analysis, supplier reviews, and market assessments to identify opportunities for value creation, risk mitigation, standardization, and cost optimization.

• Develop annual category procurement plans informed by demand forecasting, market analysis, and stakeholder priorities, and support long-term sourcing initiatives.

• Build business cases and recommendations that support informed procurement decisions.

Procurement Leadership:

• Lead complex and high-value sourcing and competitive procurement initiatives from planning through contract award.

• Develop sourcing strategies, facilitate supplier engagement, oversee evaluations, and negotiate commercial agreements.

• Ensure compliance with University policies, public sector procurement standards, and applicable trade agreements.

• Promote procurement best practices related to fairness, transparency, sustainability, and supplier diversity.

Stakeholder Engagement & Change Leadership:

• Build trusted relationships with academic, research, and administrative stakeholders across the University.

• Act as a strategic advisor, helping departments navigate procurement decisions and planning activities.

• Influence purchasing practices and support the University's transition toward a more centralized procurement model.

• Drive change management efforts by promoting procurement best practices and encouraging early engagement.

Supplier Relationship Management & Continuous Improvement:

• Lead supplier relationship and contract performance management activities.

• Identify opportunities for innovation, service improvements, supplier rationalization, and ongoing value creation.

• Provide mentorship and guidance to Buyers and procurement colleagues.

• Champion continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen procurement processes, tools, systems, and category management practices.

## Your Qualifications:

• Undergraduate degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Public Administration, or a related discipline, preferably in a public-sector or higher-education environment (or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience).

• Professional procurement designation (SCMP, CIPS, CPPB, CPPO, PSPP, or equivalent), or active progress toward completion.

• 7+ years of progressive procurement experience with increasing levels of strategic responsibility.

• Demonstrated experience developing sourcing strategies, conducting spend analysis, and leading category planning initiatives.

• Proven success leading complex procurement projects, formal RFx processes, supplier negotiations, and contract management activities.

• Strong analytical and business acumen with the ability to translate data into actionable recommendations.

• Exceptional communication, relationship-building, and influence skills.

• Experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

## Assets include:

• Experience working within government, higher education, healthcare, broader public sector, or other large institutional environments.

• Knowledge of public procurement legislation and trade agreements.

• Experience supporting procurement transformation, modernization, or change initiatives.

• Exposure to technology-related procurement categories.

## Why Join Dalhousie University?

This is a rare opportunity to help build something new.

As Dalhousie continues its procurement transformation journey, the Category Lead, Procurement will play a foundational role in establishing category management practices and shaping the future of strategic procurement across the University. You will have the opportunity to influence major procurement decisions, work with stakeholders across a highly diverse institution, and contribute to initiatives that support teaching, research, and innovation.

Dalhousie also offers a competitive total rewards package including:

• Defined benefit pension plan

• Comprehensive health and dental benefits

• Health spending account

• Generous mental health coverage

• Tuition assistance for employees dependent children

• Strong commitment to work-life balance and employee well-being

Reporting to the Supervisor, Business Solutions Specialist, you will be responsible for improving the financial well-being of business and non-personal members and improving the member experience through provision of holistic advice and business solutions. Through collaboration with the Business Services team and branch staff, the Business Solutions Specialist identifies and delivers cash management solutions for new small business members and meets the needs of existing members.

## We offer…

• Outstanding culture and opportunity to join an engaged and community-focused team.

• Competitive compensation ($67,795.23-$79,759.41 annually) and benefits with performance-based incentives.

• Potential for flexible work arrangements including Flex Time, Telework and compressed work week.

• Generous benefit package including a Flexible Health and Dental Plan (paid 100% by employer) and up to 9% contribution with employer match in the Defined Contribution Pension Plan.

• Tuition reimbursement, training, and personal development.

• Additional employee perks include but not limited to annual wellness credit; reduced rates on employee loans/mortgages and paid volunteer time.

## You would…

• Provide exceptional member service by proactively engaging and following up with borrowing and nonborrowing small business and non-personal members; follows the Credit Union's Experience Map while adhering to the company's policies, procedures, and service standards.

• Provide support and training to the Business Services Team, and the retail branch staff, in the sale and fulfilment of all cash management solutions in a timely and professional manner.

• Conduct detailed analysis and evaluation and recommend cash management solutions and digital offerings to business members; prepare and deliver on-site and off-site presentations; provide virtual or in-person training and ongoing technical support regarding members' cash management services.

• Respond to member inquiries regarding, but not limited to, research, system capabilities, password resets, online banking, Payment stream limit increases, wire payment processing, and other banking features that would support members' business and financial transactions.

• Proactively identify and respond to members' needs such as account opening, changing signing authorities, updating contact information, email addresses, etc.

• Complete custom pricing packages and monitor/review each account annually.

• Proactively plan and prepare weekly contact strategy; track weekly status and volume reports and provide progress updates to management.

• Act in a consultative capacity internally and externally and acts as subject matter expert in all cash management services offerings.

• Ensure all documentation in relation to Cash Management services are completed in an accurate and timely manner in accordance and compliance with all policies, procedures, and legislative requirements as appropriate.

• Complete other duties as assigned.

## You have…

• Completed a certificate or diploma in Business or Commerce.

• A minimum of three years of experience in business/commercial banking in a financial institution; or an equivalent combination of training and experience.

• A valid drivers license and access to a relaible vehicle.

• Knowledge of cash management products and services.

• Strong negotiation, interpersonal and communication skills.

• Demonstrated ability to establish trust and identify opportunities to expand and deepen member relationships.

• Experience drafting RFPs and preparing reports.

## You are…

• Able to work independently with confidence while prioritizing and planning workload to meet deadlines.

• Equipped with strong presentation skills and the ability to engage with others authentically.

• Proficient in Microsoft Office and using various technologies and digital platforms.

St. John's, NL

Meridia Recruitment is pleased to partner with the Teachers' Pension Plan Corporation (TPPC) in the search for a Director of IT and Risk Management.

This role is responsible for the leadership and operational execution of the organization's information technology, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence (AI), and enterprise risk management (ERM) functions. You will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering an integrated IT, AI, and risk management strategy aligned with organizational priorities and the strategic plan, ensuring that these capabilities support operational resilience, best practices, and fiduciary responsibilities.

The Director establishes, maintains, and advances governance, priorities, and direction across the organization's technology and risk management functions while leading the implementation and delivery of the initiatives, controls, and programs that support those objectives. Working closely with internal stakeholders, external service providers, and the executive team, the Director ensures systems are secure, reliable, and efficient, proactively manages organizational risk, and supports informed decision-making. Fostering a culture of risk awareness, accountability, and continuous improvement across TPPC is key to the role.

## What You Will Do

• Lead the organization's IT strategy, digital transformation, cybersecurity, and enterprise risk management program.

• Develop and execute a technology roadmap that supports modernization, business continuity, and long-term organizational goals.

• Oversee enterprise technology architecture, infrastructure, systems, data management, and cloud-based solutions.

• Manage IT operations, budgets, vendors, contracts, and service delivery to ensure reliable, scalable, and cost-effective technology services.

• Drive AI strategy and governance, promoting responsible adoption while managing AI-related risks and emerging regulatory requirements.

• Lead cybersecurity and information security programs, including threat management, incident response, privacy, and regulatory compliance.

• Establish and maintain technology policies, governance frameworks, standards, and internal controls.

• Lead the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program, including risk identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, and reporting.

• Advise senior leadership on technology, cybersecurity, and enterprise risk matters.

• Oversee business continuity and disaster recovery planning, testing, and organizational readiness.

• Ensure technology solutions effectively support pension administration, investment management, and operational excellence.

• Monitor emerging technology, cybersecurity, and risk trends to strengthen organizational resilience and performance.

## What You Bring

• Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Risk Management, or related field; a Master's degree and/or professional certification (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CRISC), completed or in progress, is considered an asset.

• 10+ years of progressive experience in IT strategy, operations, cybersecurity, and enterprise risk management.

• Experience working with executive leadership.

• Proven leader recognized for building trusted relationships, inspiring high performance, and ability to influence across the organization.

title: Purchasing & Inventory Specialist
description:
Job Title: Purchasing & Inventory Specialist
Location: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia
TP-10240

Our client is a well-established Atlantic Canadian industrial services organization with many years of experience supporting commercial, industrial, and infrastructure operations across the region. With expertise spanning mechanical services, heavy equipment support, fabrication, machining, and specialized field services, the company has built a strong reputation for delivering reliable solutions to complex operational challenges.

Known for its skilled workforce, practical problem-solving approach, and commitment to safety and customer service, the organization plays a critical role in supporting clients whose operations depend on responsiveness, technical expertise, and operational excellence. As the business continues to grow and invest in its people, processes, and systems, it is seeking a Purchasing & Inventory Specialist to help strengthen procurement and inventory management practices across the organization.

Meridia Recruitment Solutions is pleased to be partnering with our client on a confidential search for a Purchasing & Inventory Specialist based in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia.

Role Description
Reporting to operational leadership, the Purchasing & Inventory Specialist plays a key role in supporting purchasing, inventory control, and operational efficiency across the organization. This position is responsible for coordinating the procurement of materials, supplies, equipment, and services while ensuring inventory records remain accurate and inventory levels effectively support operational needs.

Working closely with operations teams, department managers, suppliers, and Accounts Payable, the successful candidate will help ensure purchasing activities are executed efficiently, inventory is effectively managed, and critical materials are available when required.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organized and detail-oriented professional who enjoys working in a fast-paced operational environment. The role offers the opportunity to expand responsibilities over time and become a trusted resource for purchasing processes, inventory controls, cost-management initiatives, and continuous improvement efforts across the business.

## Key Responsibilities:

• Process purchase requisitions and prepare purchase orders for materials, supplies, equipment, and services.

• Source products and services through established and prospective suppliers.

• Obtain and evaluate quotations based on pricing, quality, availability, delivery requirements, and service levels.

• Monitor open purchase orders and follow up with suppliers regarding delivery schedules and outstanding orders.

• Coordinate shipping, freight, and delivery requirements as needed.

• Maintain accurate purchasing records, supplier information, pricing data, and supporting documentation.

• Communicate purchasing updates, shortages, delays, and supply concerns to internal stakeholders.

• Develop and maintain positive working relationships with suppliers and service providers.

• Work closely with Accounts Payable to resolve purchasing, receiving, and invoicing discrepancies.

• Maintain accurate inventory records within the organization's ERP system.

• Monitor inventory levels and support replenishment activities while minimizing excess inventory and maintaining inventory accuracy.

• Conduct cycle counts and assist with physical inventory activities.

• Investigate inventory discrepancies and support corrective actions.

• Assist with developing and improving purchasing procedures, inventory controls, and operational processes.

• Support cost-control initiatives, evaluate supplier performance, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

## Qualifications

You are a highly organized and proactive professional who takes ownership of your work and prides yourself on accuracy, follow-through, and strong communication. You enjoy solving problems, managing competing priorities, and building positive relationships with both internal stakeholders and external suppliers. You are comfortable working in a fast-paced operational environment where priorities can shift quickly, and urgent purchasing requirements regularly arise.

## Your qualifications include:

• 2+ years of experience in purchasing, procurement, inventory control, supply chain, materials management, or a related position.

• Experience processing purchase orders, obtaining supplier quotations, and tracking orders through completion.

• Knowledge of purchasing and inventory management principles.

• Experience using ERP, purchasing, or inventory management systems.

• Strong computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.

• Excellent organizational, prioritization, and time-management skills.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• Effective communication and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities within a fast-paced operational environment.

## Assets include:

• Experience within industrial, manufacturing, construction, mechanical, transportation, or operations-focused environments.

• Experience coordinating freight, shipping, receiving, or logistics activities.

• Experience with inventory planning, cycle counting, and inventory control processes.

• Experience with Sage 300 or similar ERP platforms.

• Exposure to purchasing process improvement, supplier management, or cost-control initiatives.

Why join this opportunity?
This is an opportunity to join a stable and growing organization where purchasing and inventory management are recognized as critical business functions. You'll work closely with operational leaders and key stakeholders across the business while gaining broad exposure to procurement, inventory control, supplier management, and process improvement initiatives.

The organization offers a collaborative work environment, opportunities for professional growth, and the chance to develop into a trusted subject matter expert supporting purchasing and inventory activities across the operation.

The total rewards package includes:

• Competitive pay, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

• Comprehensive medical benefits.

• RRSP program.

• Stable weekday schedule with early start and finish times.

title: Fitter- Assembly/ Bonding
description:
With more than 50 years of Aerospace industry experience, IMP Aerostructures, an Operating Unit of IMP Aerospace and Defence, is a leader in the Aerospace industry providing top quality, structural components and assemblies to clients such as Bombardier, Bell Helicopter, Boeing, Spirit Aerosystems and Lockheed. Located in the quaint town of Amherst, NS, just a short trip from Moncton, NB, you'll enjoy a lifestyle that offers all of the amenities of big city living in a rural setting. Recognized as one of Canada's Best Managed Companies, IMP Group takes enormous pride in the diligence and hard work its employee groups provide. Known for providing its employees with a supportive and challenging atmosphere, fostering growth and personal development, IMP Aerostructures has an immediate opening for a motivated individual to join its winning team!

Position Overview:
Responsible to assemble, fit and install prefabricated detail parts and components to produce, manufacture and/or repair aircraft and aerospace components, sub-assemblies and final assemblies in accordance with customer or engineering specifications, Company procedures, SWIMS, etc.

What You Will Do:
• Interact with Supervisor and/or Charge Hand by communicating and receiving instruction in the transition of the workflow and production work scheduling; to assess current material needs and/or to address any problems accordingly.

• Adhere to workplace safety policies, regulations and the use safety equipment will be the highest priority for you and your co-workers;

• Ensure the efficient movement of production parts identified as priority (AOG or Critical).

• Set-up and efficiently operate the tools and equipment as dictated by the task at hand and the training, knowledge and ability to do so.

• Adhere to, read and interpret drawings, blueprints, mylars and follow procedures (work orders, customers' specifications, engineers' drawings/prints, work instructions, SWIMs, company specifications)

• Locate and mark reference points/holes, etc. for installation of parts and components using jigs, templates and measuring instruments.

• Assemble and fit pre-fabricated parts to form sub-assemblies according to blueprints, specifications, Company workplace instructions, SWIMS, manuals, etc. using hand and/or power tools working at benches or directly on aircraft structures.

• Disassemble or assemble aircraft and/or aerospace components for overhaul or repair.

• Position and align sub-assemblies in jigs or fixtures using measuring instruments, following blueprint, customer specifications, engineering drawings, SWIMS, shop drawings, etc.

• Drill, scribe/trim and fit parts, components and sub-assemblies, bolt, screw or rivet accessories to fasten, support or hang components and sub-assemblies prior to fastening with adhesives or bonding.

• Mix and apply sealant and/or adhesives to parts, components and/or assemblies as required.

• Perform routine maintenance on work equipment; keep tools, equipment and immediate work area(s) in a clean, orderly and safe condition.

What You Will Bring:
• Completion of High School (Grade 12), equivalent experience and/or training.

• Demonstrated experience operating machines and measuring components;

• Completion of an aircraft blueprint course or have demonstrated 'tested' ability to read aircraft blueprints;

• Must possess mechanical aptitude, high attention to detail, a high level of manual dexterity and a strong interest in aircraft assembly and/or repair.

• Completion of Global Harmonized System (WHMIS) course.

• Must be able to work with others co-operatively and follow directives precisely.

• Knowledge of processes, products and equipment and ability to read blueprints and engineering documentation will be considered an asset.

• Must meet physical requirements of the position including but not limited to: walking, static standing and leg/foot movement for extended periods, bending, stooping, squatting, twisting/trunk rotation, weight bearing / lifting, carrying, pushing & pulling heavy objects; hand/wrist gripping, grasping, pinching, vibration depend on tasks/tools, neck & back flexion.

• Adhere to, and demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment Policies. Continually focusing on your individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by your work and to fully comply with all Nova Scotia Provincial Health, Safety and Environment Legislation.

• Must be eligible to meet the requirements of the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and the Canadian Security Clearances – Secret Level II

What We Will Do For You:
• We offer a comprehensive Benefits Package, including RSP Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Long Service Awards, Volunteer Grant Program, Scholarship Program, and more!

title: Project Manager, Youth & Manufacturing Engagement - NB/Gestionnaire de projet Jeunesse et mobilisation manufacturiere- NB
description:
Are you a natural relationship builder who loves connecting people, managing impactful projects, and creating opportunities for youth? Excellence in Manufacturing Consortium (EMC) is looking for an energetic Project Manager to lead our Youth in Manufacturing and Enhanced Co-op initiatives across New Brunswick.

In this role, you will bridge the gap between high school students, educators, and local manufacturers-helping young people discover rewarding manufacturing careers while supporting the province's growing industrial workforce.

The Excellence in Manufacturing Consortium (EMC) is expanding its youth workforce development activities in New Brunswick through two complementary initiatives: the New Brunswick Youth in Manufacturing initiative in partnership with WorkingNB and the Enhanced Co-op Program, developed in partnership with the New Brunswick Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (EECD).Together, these initiatives are designed to strengthen New Brunswick's manufacturing talent pipeline by introducing youth to manufacturing careers and creating clearer pathways from high school into summer employment, full-time work, skilled trades and other career opportunities.

The Project Manager, Youth & Manufacturing Engagement will lead the delivery of EMC's New Brunswick Youth in Manufacturing initiative and support the continued development and delivery of the Enhanced Co-op Program. The Project Manager will also work closely alongside EMC's New Brunswick Manufacturing Consortium Manager, leveraging existing relationships with manufacturers across the province and coordinating employer outreach and engagement activities.

This is a hands-on role combining project management, employer engagement, education and community partnerships, and youth workforce development. The successful candidate will serve as a key EMC representative in New Brunswick, working directly with manufacturers, schools, government, employment service providers and community partners to create meaningful employment and work-integrated learning opportunities for youth.
The ideal candidate will be an energetic relationship builder who is equally comfortable visiting a manufacturing facility, working with educators and students, engaging government partners, and managing the day-to-day requirements of government-funded projects.

This opportunity offers:
• Combination of home-office work and in-the-field activities, including onsite meetings, school and manufacturer visits, event facilitation and stakeholder meetings.
• Home office must be based within New Brunswick.
• Regular travel throughout the province is required.
• Flexible schedule, including occasional evenings and weekends.
• Valid driver's licence and reliable vehicle required.
• Occasional travel outside New Brunswick for EMC meetings, events or training may be required.

## Responsibilities

Relationship Building & Community Outreach

•Build strong relationships with New Brunswick manufacturers, educators, government agencies, and community groups to promote and expand participation in EMC youth programs.
• Engage with schools, teachers, and youth to raise awareness of manufacturing pathways and match students' career goals with hands-on workplace opportunities.
• Represent EMC at career fairs, school activities, and employer events to showcase program successes and attract new partners.

Program Delivery & Student Support
• Support the full recruitment lifecycle including screening, matching, onboarding, and supporting youth within participating manufacturing sites.
• Conduct site visits and maintain active communication with students, employers, and schools to ensure successful, safe placement experiences.
• Coordinate student completion of EMC learning modules (e.g., Manufacturing Foundations, Lean Fundamentals, Introduction to AI in Manufacturing) prior to their workplace terms.

Project Management & Administration
• Oversee project timelines, budgets, performance targets, and participant outcomes, ensuring accurate tracking in EMC's CRM and project management systems.
• Other related duties may be assigned as required to support successful program delivery.

Education and Experience:
• Proven ability to build trust and communicate confidently in both French and English across diverse groups, including students and educators, manufacturing executives, and government partners.
• 2-5 years of experience coordinating projects or workforce development initiatives (ideally within education, employment services, or manufacturing)
• A proactive problem-solver who can handle multiple priorities, track program targets, and adapt in a dynamic environment.
• Proficient with Microsoft Office 365 and comfortable using CRM or project management platforms for reporting.
• Relevant post-secondary education or equivalent practical experience. Knowledge of youth employment programs, high school co-op pathways, or government-funded initiatives is a strong asset.
• Ability to travel regularly throughout New Brunswick, hold a valid driver's license, and obtain a clear criminal record check. (Must be legally entitled to work in Canada).

How to Apply:
Those interested in applying for this opportunity should submit a resume outlining your experience, skills, and why you feel you are the best fit for this role at EMC. Please submit your resume and cover letter to Lynn Morris, Human Resource Manager, lmorris@emccanada.org

OVERVIEW
Manufacturing is a key component of Canada's output and overall economic well-being. EMC has grown to become Canada's largest manufacturing consortium and, with over one thousand industry events annually, is one of the most active manufacturing organizations in North America.

For more than a quarter-century, EMC has been responsible for contributing significant knowledge, expertise, and resources towards the success of over 18,000 consortium and online member manufacturers, representing every province across Canada. EMC's total manufacturing audience includes 700,000 manufacturing employees. The manufacturing sector provides jobs for over 1.7 million people (9% of the Canadian workforce), comprises more than 10% of Canada's GDP and accounts for 68% of Canada's merchandise exports.

Vous êtes une personne qui crée naturellement des liens, qui aime rapprocher les gens, gérer des projets porteurs et créer des occasions pour les jeunes? Le Consortium pour l'excellence manufacturière (EMC) est à la recherche d'une personne dynamique pour occuper le poste de gestionnaire de projet et diriger ses initiatives Jeunes dans le secteur manufacturier et le programme coopératif bonifié partout au Nouveau-Brunswick.

Dans ce rôle, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les élèves du secondaire, les membres du personnel enseignant et les manufacturiers locaux, afin d'aider les jeunes à découvrir des carrières enrichissantes dans le secteur manufacturier tout en soutenant le développement de la main-d'oeuvre industrielle de la province.

Le Consortium pour l'excellence manufacturière (EMC) élargit ses activités de développement de la main-d'oeuvre jeunesse au Nouveau-Brunswick grâce à deux initiatives complémentaires : l'initiative Jeunes dans le secteur manufacturier du Nouveau-Brunswick, en partenariat avec TravailNB, et le programme coopératif bonifié, développé en partenariat avec le ministère de l'Éducation et du Développement de la petite enfance du Nouveau-Brunswick (EDPE).
Ensemble, ces initiatives visent à renforcer le bassin de talents du secteur manufacturier du Nouveau-Brunswick en faisant découvrir aux jeunes les carrières en milieu manufacturier et en créant des parcours spécifiques entre l'école secondaire et les emplois d'été, les emplois à temps plein, les métiers spécialisés et d'autres possibilités de carrière.

Aperçu du poste
Le ou la gestionnaire de projet, mobilisation des jeunes et secteur manufacturier dirigera la mise en oeuvre de l'initiative Jeunes dans le secteur manufacturier au Nouveau-Brunswick et appuiera la poursuite du développement et de la prestation du programme coopératif bonifié. Cette personne travaillera également en étroite collaboration avec le ou la gestionnaire du consortium manufacturier d'EMC au Nouveau-Brunswick, en tirant parti des relations déjà établies avec les manufacturiers de la province et en coordonnant les activités de sensibilisation et de mobilisation des employeurs.

Il s'agit d'un rôle concret qui combine la gestion de projet, la mobilisation des employeurs, les partenariats avec le milieu de l'éducation et la communauté ainsi que le développement de la main-d'oeuvre jeunesse. La personne retenue agira comme représentante clé d'EMC au Nouveau-Brunswick et travaillera directement avec les manufacturiers, les écoles, les gouvernements, les fournisseurs de services d'emploi et les partenaires communautaires afin de créer des possibilités d'emploi et d'apprentissage intégré au travail significatives pour les jeunes.

La personne idéale sera dynamique et habile à créer des relations. Elle sera tout aussi à l'aise de visiter une installation manufacturière, de travailler avec le personnel enseignant et les étudiants, de collaborer avec des partenaires gouvernementaux et de gérer les exigences quotidiennes de projets financés par le gouvernement.
Ce poste offre :
• Une combinaison de télétravail et d'activités sur le terrain, notamment des réunions sur place, des visites d'écoles et de manufacturiers, l'animation d'événements et des rencontres avec les parties prenantes.
• Le bureau à domicile doit être situé au Nouveau-Brunswick.
• Des déplacements réguliers dans l'ensemble de la province sont requis.
• Un horaire flexible, incluant occasionnellement des soirs et des fins de semaine.
• Un permis de conduire valide et l'accès à un véhicule fiable sont requis.
• Des déplacements occasionnels à l'extérieur du Nouveau-Brunswick pour des réunions, événements ou formations d'EMC peuvent être requis.

Responsabilités
Développement de relations et rayonnement communautaire
• Établir de solides relations avec les manufacturiers du Nouveau-Brunswick, le personnel enseignant, les organismes gouvernementaux et les groupes communautaires afin de promouvoir les programmes d'EMC pour les jeunes et d'accroître la participation.
• Collaborer avec les écoles, les enseignants et les jeunes afin de mieux faire connaître les parcours de carrière dans le secteur manufacturier et de jumeler les objectifs professionnels des élèves à des occasions concrètes d'apprentissage en milieu de travail.
• Représenter EMC lors de salons de l'emploi, d'activités scolaires et d'événements destinés aux employeurs afin de mettre en valeur les réussites des programmes et d'attirer de nouveaux partenaires.

Prestation des programmes et soutien aux élèves
• Appuyer l'ensemble du cycle de recrutement, notamment la présélection, le jumelage, l'intégration et le soutien des jeunes dans les milieux manufacturiers participants.
• Effectuer des visites sur place et maintenir une communication active avec les élèves, les employeurs et les écoles afin d'assurer des expériences de placement réussies et sécuritaires.
• Coordonner la réalisation, par les étudiants, des modules d'apprentissage d'EMC (p. ex. Fondements de la fabrication, Principes fondamentaux du Lean, Introduction à l'IA dans le secteur manufacturier) avant le début de leur période en milieu de travail.

Gestion de projet et administration
• Superviser les échéanciers, les budgets, les cibles de rendement et les résultats des participants, tout en assurant un suivi précis dans le CRM et les systèmes de gestion de projet d'EMC.
• D'autres tâches connexes peuvent être confiées au besoin afin d'assurer la réussite de la prestation des programmes.

Formation et expérience :
• Capacité démontrée à établir un climat de confiance et à communiquer avec aisance en français et en anglais auprès de groupes variés, notamment des élèves et du personnel enseignant, des dirigeants du secteur manufacturier et des partenaires gouvernementaux.
• De 2 à 5 ans d'expérience en coordination de projets ou d'initiatives de développement de la main-d'oeuvre (idéalement dans les domaines de l'éducation, des services d'emploi ou du secteur manufacturier).
• Personne proactive et orientée vers la résolution de problèmes, capable de gérer plusieurs priorités, de suivre les cibles des programmes et de s'adapter dans un environnement dynamique.
• Maîtrise de Microsoft Office 365 et aisance à utiliser un CRM ou des plateformes de gestion de projet à des fins de production de rapports.
• Formation postsecondaire pertinente ou expérience équivalente. La connaissance des programmes d'emploi jeunesse, des parcours coopératifs au secondaire ou des initiatives financées par le gouvernement constitue un atout important.
• Capacité à se déplacer régulièrement dans l'ensemble du Nouveau-Brunswick, à détenir un permis de conduire valide et à obtenir une vérification de casier judiciaire sans antécédents. (La personne doit être légalement autorisée à travailler au Canada.)

Comment postuler :
Les personnes intéressées par ce poste sont invitées à soumettre un curriculum vitæ présentant leur expérience et leurs compétences, ainsi que les raisons pour lesquelles elles estiment correspondre au profil recherché pour ce poste chez EMC. Veuillez faire parvenir votre curriculum vitæ et votre lettre de présentation à Lynn Morris, gestionnaire des ressources humaines, à l'adresse lmorris@emccanada.org.

APERÇU
Le secteur manufacturier est une composante essentielle de la production canadienne et du bien-être économique global du pays. EMC est devenu le plus important consortium manufacturier au Canada et, avec plus de mille événements de l'industrie chaque année, l'une des organisations manufacturières les plus actives en Amérique du Nord.

Depuis plus d'un quart de siècle, EMC contribue de façon importante, par ses connaissances, son expertise et ses ressources, au succès de plus de 18 000 manufacturiers membres du consortium et membres en ligne, représentant toutes les provinces du Canada. L'auditoire total d'EMC représente 700 000 employés du secteur manufacturier.

Le secteur manufacturier fournit des emplois à plus de 1,7 million de personnes (9 ? la main-d'oeuvre canadienne), représente plus de 10 % du PIB du Canada et compte pour 68 ?s exportations canadiennes de marchandises.

Halifax, NS

Reporting to the Director of Finance, the Controller will play a key leadership role in overseeing the firm's financial reporting, treasury management, trust accounting, accounts payable, and financial data governance functions. title: Compliance Officer
description:
The Financial and Consumer Services Commission (Commission) is a leader in integrated financial and consumer services regulation. The Commission's mandate is to protect consumers and enhance public confidence in the financial and consumer marketplace through the provision of regulatory and educational services. With offices in both Fredericton and Saint John, it is responsible for the administration and enforcement of provincial legislation regulating mortgage brokers, payday lenders, real estate, securities, insurance, pensions, credit unions, trust and loan companies, cooperatives, unclaimed property, and a wide range of consumer legislation. The Commission is a self funded Crown corporation responsible for the administration and enforcement of financial consumer services legislation.

We offer opportunities for dedicated professionals to play a vital role in carrying out our mandate.

## Compliance Officer - Securities Division - Saint John Office

We're looking for a Compliance Officer (15-month contract) to join our Securities Division. This is an opportunity to play a meaningful role in protecting investors and maintaining confidence in New Brunswick's capital markets. Working in a dynamic regulatory environment, you will conduct compliance reviews of registered firms and individuals, contribute to national regulatory initiatives through the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA), participate in oversight activities involving self-regulatory organizations, and perform key registration functions. Using your strong analytical, investigative, and communication skills, you'll help ensure market participants meet their regulatory obligations and support a fair and effective securities marketplace.

## Your Focus:

• As a key member of the Securities Division, you will:

• Lead and participate in compliance reviews, examinations, and regulatory initiatives to assess registrants' compliance with securities legislation, regulatory requirements, and firm policies.

• Identify compliance risks and regulatory breaches, recommend appropriate regulatory action, and support enforcement investigations when required.

• Represent the Commission on Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) committees and working groups, contributing to national compliance initiatives, regulatory guidance, and self-regulatory organization (SRO) oversight activities.

• Review and approve registration applications, assess applicant suitability, and make recommendations regarding registration terms, conditions, or refusals.

• Provide guidance and advice to registrants, market participants, regulatory bodies, and Securities Division staff on compliance and registration matters.

• Conduct reviews of Community Economic Development Corporations (CEDCs) and Cooperatives to ensure compliance with ongoing regulatory reporting requirements.

• Monitor industry developments and contribute to regulatory policy work, including the review of proposed amendments, policies, and exemption applications.

## What you Bring

• University degree in business, commerce, public administration or a related discipline;

• 3+ years of relevant industry work experience,

• Understanding of risk and compliance issues in a regulatory environment,

• Completion of, or willingness to complete, the Canadian Securities Course (or equivalent course),

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines,

• Effective communicator in both collegial and adversarial situations,

• Solid interview skills,

• Highly analytical,

• Sound judgment while exercising tact and discretion,

• Takes initiative.

## Additional Strengths

• Bilingualism is an asset

• Experience in conducting audits, examinations and/or compliance with respect to regulated industry participants is an asset,

• Working knowledge of securities legislation is an asset,

The Financial and Consumer Services Commission offers a competitive salary and benefit package as well as excellent opportunities for personal growth and challenge. Salary will be commensurate with experience. If you are interested in being a key part of this team, please forward your résumé and covering letter.

Salary Range: $75,482 to $103,787 (annual compensation)

As a condition of employment, the successful candidate will be required to undergo a pre-employment background check in accordance with the Commission's Pre-Employment Background Checks Directive. This may include criminal record checks, credential verification, and reference checks.

For more information about this position please visit our website at www.fcnb.ca or call the Talent Acquisition Specialist at (506) 643-7790.

Please note that only candidates selected for further evaluation will be contacted.

title: Heavy Equipment Mechanic
Director, School and Child Clinical Psychology Training Clinic
description:
Mount Saint Vincent University invites applications for the position of Director, School and Child Clinical Psychology Training Clinic (the "Director"). This new training clinic is associated with the Doctor of Psychology (PsyD) in School and Child Clinical Psychology program, which emphasizes the practitioner-scientist model of training, and admitted its first cohort of students in September 2026. The position of Director is a full-time position, which reports to the Dean of Education. This position will have a dotted-line reporting relationship to, and will coordinate duties of the clinic in collaboration with, the Director of Training and the training committee for the PsyD program.

The training clinic features heavily in the training model for the PsyD program. The Clinic will host the initial assessment and intervention practicum experiences for all PsyD students. Each annual entry cohort has a capacity of eight students. Additional practicum experiences will be created at the training clinic for upper-level students by the Director and other clinic psychologists in consultation with the Director of Training and the training committee.

The Clinic will employ additional registered psychologists, as well as the Director. The training clinic will also be home to four full-time predoctoral residency positions within the next four years. The successful candidate for the Director position will be involved in the selection process for the registered psychologists and will have the chance to lead these initiatives to shape the clinic's model of care and, with the Director of Training and the training committee for the PsyD program, develop a model of training that supports students' learning about providing clinical services across multiple systems (e.g., schools, health, mental health, justice) that children, adolescents, youth, and their families might be in contact with.

Qualifications
The successful candidate will have earned a doctoral degree in school and/or child-focused clinical psychology from a CPA or APA-accredited, or equivalent program, which will have included a one-year predoctoral residency. If the degree program is equivalent to a CPA or APA-accredited program, the predoctoral residency must be CPA or APA-accredited. Applicants must be registered or eligible for registration with the Nova Scotia Regulator of Psychology (NSRP) and have liability insurance as required for registration. The successful candidate will have a minimum of three years of experience in the provision of psychological services for children, adolescents, and/or youth, and their families.

As the successful candidate, you will be knowledgeable about and/or have experience with multiple systems (e.g., schools, health, mental health, justice) that children, adolescents, youth, and/or their families might be in contact with. Preference will be given to candidates who can demonstrate knowledge of and/or who have some experience working within school systems.

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate their experience conducting psychological assessments for a broad range of concerns related to learning, behaviour, and mental health, as well as providing individual and group intervention to children, adolescents, and/or youth, and their families. The successful candidate will be familiar with a range of assessment and intervention strategies and consultation practices that are evidence-based and aligned with research-informed best practices. Experience providing care to clients from a range of diverse backgrounds and experiences will be considered an asset.

The successful candidate will have experience with supervision of graduate students who are providing psychological services. Experience with supervision in a university setting is preferred. Experience with working with a team to provide training and supervision to students will be considered an asset.

The ideal candidate will be able to demonstrate experience with developing and maintaining relationships with community partners. Experience managing a psychology training and/or outpatient clinic, experience with electronic record keeping and data management, and familiarity with CPA accreditation standards and processes will be considered an asset.

Responsibilities
The Director will oversee the day-to-day operation of the training clinic, including processes related to scheduling, staffing, and record management. They will also manage the clinic budget and acquire necessary materials for the clinic's functioning. The Director will have supervisory responsibility for other psychologists working in the training clinic and for the clinic's administrative assistant. The Director will also have primary responsibility for developing and maintaining relationships with community referral partners.

The Director will support supervision activities for assessment and/or intervention practica. The Director may be called upon to provide some direct assessment and intervention services as required for training purposes and/or continuity of care. The Director will serve on the PsyD program training committee to support the integration of coursework and practical experiences across the curriculum and throughout all years of the program. As the training clinic is publicly funded by the Province of Nova Scotia, the Director will play a key role in required, cyclical government reporting.

Classification: Director Level 1

Salary: $111,355 per annum to start, with 5 steps in the salary range up to $135,480

Start Date: ASAP, ideally by November 1, 2026

## Application Process

Please submit a cover letter briefly describing how you meet the criteria for the position, as well as a current curriculum vitae. Include a statement that outlines your supervision/teaching experience and includes a description of your supervision philosophy and/or a description of your approach to supervision. Please provide the names of 3 references who can speak to your clinical skills and/or supervision experience.

If you require an accommodation at any time during the application process, please let us know.

We will review applications beginning October 22, 2026, and the position will remain open until filled.

title: Director of Business Growth & Trade Development
description:
Halifax Partnership is Halifax's public-private economic development organization. The Partnership drives and accelerates economic growth by selling and marketing Halifax to the world to attract business, talent, and investment, helping businesses reach their full potential, and tracking and reporting Halifax's economic progress.

Reporting to the Vice President, Investment Attraction & Business Development, the Director, Business Growth & Trade Development will lead Business Retention & Expansion (BRE) efforts with a priority focus on supporting growth, overcoming barriers to exporting, labour market development and opportunities for productivity enhancement. This position is 75% externally focused (meeting face-to-face with companies) and 25% internally focused.

This role is key to the Halifax Partnership's focus on driving GDP per capita growth through investment attraction, business expansion, and export growth.

Qualifications

## Education

• Undergraduate degree in business, marketing or other related discipline.

• Economic Development Certification will be considered an asset.

## Experience

• 7+ years' experience in business development, economic development or B2B enterprise sales.

• Experience in delivering a comprehensive BRE program preferred.

• Experience in managing and reporting on publicly funded projects and programs, including budget management.

## Skills

• Strong business acumen.

• Highly motivated and detail-oriented self-starter.

• Proven track record of building and maintaining effective interest-holder relationships.

• Excellent interpersonal, presentation and written communication skills.

• Demonstrated proficiency in statistical analysis.

• Strong critical thinking and analytical skills to resolve high-impact, complex problems.

• Ability to engage/direct others in developing innovative solutions and apply sound decision-making skills to highly complex strategic and operating problems.

Responsibilities

## Leadership

• Provide leadership and direction to the Business Retention & Expansion Account Executives.

• Provide continuous review and evaluation of the teams' work to ensure their deliverables and performance targets are achieved.

• In collaboration with the Research Team, analyze data collected from company interactions to identify company/community-specific and common issues and opportunities and share that competitive intelligence with economic development partner organizations and government.

• Lead the implementation of a revised visitation survey prioritizing key employers in Halifax's target sectors, identifying issues, concerns and potential opportunities and assisting where appropriate.

• Develop and maintain key trade relationships with Trade Commissioners and international partner organizations.

• Track and report on program progress at quarterly intervals for internal and external accountabilities.

## Account Management

• This role will have a strong emphasis on supporting companies with the potential to begin or grow their current exports and connecting them to the resources they need to have a facilitated pathway to success.

• Develop high-level expertise in the strengths, assets, programs, and connections the Halifax ecosystem can provide to help companies enhance their growth strategy. Apply this expertise in developing customized solutions for companies.

• Develop and manage key client accounts and gain an in-depth understanding of each client's unique business needs and service offerings.

• Initiate and conduct targeted interviews with company leader(s) to collect information that will help identify and recommend action plans to respond to threats and opportunities.

• Enter, compile and analyze interview data from company visits.

• Through a structured referral system, connect clients to appropriate referral partners, partner organizations, and/or community interest-holders to respond to and/or support immediate threats and/or opportunities.

• Ensure consistent, timely follow-up and ongoing dialogue with action team members and interest-holders to ensure referrals have been acted upon in a timely manner.

• Meet assigned individual targets for company visitations and connections.

• Develop trusting working relationships with public organizations and private sector companies.

• Support and collaborate on strategic economic development opportunities across all areas of Halifax Regional Municipality, including rural areas.

• This position has a high degree of accountability requiring weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting. This includes inputting data into the corporate database to identify company-specific and common issues and opportunities.

• Work collaboratively with the Partnership's Marketing and Communications team to raise awareness of lessons learned, opportunities, or systemic problems.

• Maintain a high degree of confidentiality.

• A total compensation package that includes a competitive salary and a hybrid workplace (three days working with your colleagues in the office, with the option to work remotely for the other two days).

• A welcoming workplace where everyone belongs. Halifax Partnership is committed to fostering a culture of belonging, grounded in the principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, especially African Nova Scotians, Indigenous peoples (especially Mi'kmaq), women, persons with a disability, racialized persons and 2SLGBTQ+ and/or gender and sexually diverse individuals.

Please submit your cover letter and resume by 5:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, 2026, addressed to Margot Bégin, Vice President, Investment Attraction and Business Development.

Applicant's must meet the following qualifications:

• Successfully completed a bachelor's degree in nursing.

• Hold a masters degree in practical nursing.

• Successfully completed the Canadian nurse practitioner examination (CNPE).

• Self-motivation with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment.

The clinic operates Monday through Thursday and remains closed on weekends, evenings and statutory holidays.

The clinic is located at 66 Brode Rd., Oromocto, NB.

Our clinic invites you to apply for this exciting opportunity to become part of a positive, team oriented environment where you will benefit from:

• A professional, supportive, and inclusive workplace that promotes wellness and work-life balance.

## Compensation:

Hourly rate within the range of $65.00 - $72.00 commensurate with experience and qualifications. Final compensation will be discussed and confirmed with the successful candidate.

Competitive health benefits and employer contributions to your RRSP.

Direct collaboration with ownership and a close-knit team.

The opportunity to take ownership of your work and contribute to a growing local business.

A varied role that combines people, sales, marketing, and organization.

Help people find their next home-and help shape the next stage of Foundation Properties.

title: Building Services Technician
description:
## Drive growth. Fuel innovation. Shape the future of Nova Scotia.

Invest Nova Scotia empowers businesses of all sizes to leverage our province's natural advantages and deliver world-class solutions for Canada and global markets. Through our focus on three key areas of economic growth: start-up and venture capital, scale-up and export, and investment attraction, we're helping Nova Scotia become an economic success story. Together, we turn local potential into lasting prosperity.

As a provincial crown corporation reporting to the Department of Growth and Development, and Defence Industries our team is as innovative and energetic as the clients we serve. We are a client and people-centric organization, and we care deeply about the work we do, guided by our values and our passion to help the companies we work with grow and succeed.

## Job Opportunity: Building Services Technician (Permanent)

Reporting to the Manager, Properties and Incubation, the Building Maintenance Technician is responsible for the janitorial, maintenance, and repair services that keep our facilities safe, functional, and welcoming. This role supports the operation of more than 40,000 square feet of specialized space where innovative startups can grow and succeed.

This role is based at The Labs on the Dalhousie campus, a hub for Nova Scotia's life sciences sector. The Labs is home to startup and growing life sciences companies, offering laboratory and office space, onsite support, and opportunities to connect and collaborate with other businesses. Invest Nova Scotia also operates The Bays in Dartmouth, which provides office and light industrial space for clean technology and other innovative businesses.

## What You'll Do

You'll play a hands-on role in maintaining the cleanliness, safety, and overall appearance of our facilities through daily janitorial duties, minor maintenance activities, preventative maintenance support, and timely responses to facility-related requests. You'll also support the day-to-day operation of the facilities by coordinating building-related activities, assisting with event and meeting room setups, responding to resident client and tenant inquiries, maintaining records and documentation, and working with contractors and service providers to help ensure facility issues are addressed promptly and professionally.

## What We're Looking For

• You hold a high school diploma and have 3-5 years of practical experience, or an equivalent combination of training and experience, working with the public and performing building maintenance duties.

• Training in building maintenance or facility management is an asset.

• Experience with housekeeping, janitorial, and general maintenance practices.

• Knowledge of building maintenance and repairs, including mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems.

• Understanding of Occupational Health & Safety standards and safe work practices.

• Experience coordinating maintenance activities, maintaining records and documentation, and working collaboratively with internal and external partners.

• Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.

• Strong customer service, communication, and relationship-building skills.

• Strong organization, planning, scheduling, problem-solving, decision-making, and troubleshooting abilities.

• Ability to perform physical work, including lifting and carrying materials, tools, and equipment, and working in a hands-on environment that requires bending, kneeling, reaching, and climbing ladders, and working both indoors and outdoors in varying conditions.

## What We Offer

We offer a people-focused rewards package designed to support your wellbeing and work/life balance. Our defined benefit pension plan, robust Blue Cross health and dental coverage, and Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP) provide comprehensive support for you and your family. You'll also have access to professional development opportunities, mentorship, and the chance to work with innovative, emerging companies in Nova Scotia. All to help you build a fulfilling career while maintaining a balanced life.

Explore more: investnovascotia.ca

## We Value Diversity

Invest Nova Scotia is committed to embracing diversity and fostering a workplace that reflects the communities we serve.
