title: Talent Growth Coordinator
employer: Envision Saint John: The Regional Growth Agency
description:
## Seeking Bold, Inspired Leaders

Envision Saint John (Agency) is the Saint John Region's lead economic development and visitor attraction agency, tasked with sustainably growing our economy and population. We are governed by an independent Board of Directors and actively supported by the municipalities that are our key funding partners - Saint John, Quispamsis, Rothesay, Grand Bay-Westfield, Hampton, Fundy-St. Martins, and the Fundy Rural District.

Envision Saint John is a convener, bringing together diverse stakeholders to develop a shared economic vision. We function as an economic intelligence hub, gathering and interpreting economic data that informs strategic decision-making. We work as an innovation accelerator, creating platforms and support mechanisms that help businesses and entrepreneurs start up and scale up. We are storytellers, crafting compelling narratives that attract visitors and new residents and reveal the region's economic potential to local, provincial, national, and international audiences.

## Role Description

As the Talent Growth Coordinator, you will serve as a passionate ambassador for the Saint John Region, engaging young talent at every stage of their journey, from students exploring future possibilities to early-career professionals building their careers, and helping them see the region as a place where they can build their future.

You will build and maintain relationships with educational institutions, youth-serving organizations, community partners, employers, and young professional networks to expand awareness of opportunities and strengthen engagement with young talent across the region.

This position requires frequent travel throughout Atlantic Canada and within the Saint John Region; a valid driver's license is required. You will report to the Director of Population Growth and Workforce Development and collaborate with colleagues across the agency to support talent attraction and retention efforts.

This role is ideally suited to an early-career professional who is passionate about the Saint John Region, enjoys building relationships, and is excited by the opportunity to engage, inspire, and connect the next generation of talent.

## What you will do:

• Serve as an enthusiastic ambassador for the Saint John Region, promoting the region as a place to live, learn, work, and build a future.

• Plan, coordinate, and deliver outreach and engagement activities that showcase career opportunities, educational pathways, and community connections in the Saint John Region.

• Represent the Saint John Region through campus visits, events, activations, and presentations across Atlantic Canada.

• Foster relationships with post-secondary institutions, student organizations, and co-op and career services offices, while identifying new partnership and engagement opportunities that increase awareness of the Saint John Region and support ongoing student engagement.

• Conduct follow-up activities with students and emerging talent to maintain awareness of local opportunities and encourage continued connection with the region.

• Work with young professional organizations, schools, youth-serving organizations, community centres, employers, and community partners to promote opportunities, networks, and experiences that support the attraction and retention of young talent.

• Connect youth, students, and early-career professionals with existing programs, resources, networks, and opportunities that support their educational, career, and community goals.

• Coordinate assigned young talent initiatives, ensuring activities, partnerships, and engagement efforts are delivered effectively and aligned with organizational objectives.

• Track engagement activities, outcomes, and key performance indicators, and provide regular updates and recommendations to the Director of Population Growth and Workforce Development.

• Travel regularly throughout Atlantic Canada and within the Saint John Region to support outreach activities and maintain stakeholder relationships.

• Contribute to other tasks and team efforts as needed.

## Your qualifications:

• You're genuinely passionate about the Saint John Region and bring lived experience or a strong connection that enables you to authentically champion the region and inspire youth, students, and early-career professionals to see a future for themselves here.

• Demonstrated interest or experience in student engagement, recruitment, sales, marketing, community outreach, or event activation (through work, internships, volunteer experience, or extracurricular involvement).

• This entry-level role is best suited for recent graduates or early-career professionals beginning their professional journey.

• A confident relationship-builder who enjoys meeting new people, creating connections, and engaging in diverse audiences.

• Comfortable speaking to individuals and groups in a variety of settings, including presentations, events, and networking activities.

• Proactive and adaptable, with strong critical thinking skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and embrace new challenges.

• Strong communication skills in English (written and verbal); additional languages, especially French, are a definite asset.

• Comfortable working independently, travelling regularly, and representing the organization in a professional manner.

• Valid driver's license and ability to provide a clean driver's abstract.

## Why Envision Saint John?

• A Culture of Inclusivity: We embrace and celebrate individual differences, creating an inclusive environment where every team member's voice is valued. We believe in harnessing the collective power of diverse perspectives to drive creativity and excellence in everything we do.

• Empowerment and Autonomy: We trust our employees to make informed decisions and take ownership of their work. Empowerment and autonomy are the pillars of our work culture, allowing you to unleash your full potential and bring your best ideas to life.

• Collaboration at Its Best: You'll be part of a collaborative ecosystem that encourages open communication and cross-functional collaboration. Together, we create a supportive network that helps each other succeed.

• Work-Life Balance: We understand the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Our flexible work arrangements and generous time-off policies enable you to achieve harmony between your personal and professional life.

• A Welcoming Workspace: Our modern, state-of-the-art office is designed to inspire creativity and productivity. Comfortable breakout areas, well-equipped facilities, and a fun-filled ambiance make it a second home for our employees. Our office is centrally located in beautiful uptown Saint John, New Brunswick, with sweeping views of the region.

## Benefits:

• Salary $51,852 per year less deductions as required by law

• Health and wellness programs

• Retirement savings plans

• Regular team-building activities and social events

• Opportunities for professional development

title: Airframe Mechanic
description:
Requisition ID: 2299

Why Choose IMP Aerospace & Defence:
IMP Aerospace & Defence is not only one of the leading companies in the Aerospace field, but we are also one of the most engaging and equality advocating companies to work for. We believe that regardless of where you work at IMP Aerospace & Defence, you are a part of our ever-growing team. IMP is able to achieve success through this teamwork mindset. That is why at IMP, you are not defined by your role.

Position Overview:
The incumbent is responsible for Servicing, Elementary Work, Modification and Maintenance, and Specialized Maintenance tasks on aircraft airframe structure, airframe and engine systems and components in accordance with the approved maintenance program using technical data that includes technical manuals and drawings.

The Airframe Mechanic will report to the IMP Group Ltd. – Aerospace and Defence location near the Halifax International Airport.

What You Will Do:
• The Airframe Mechanic must achieve a technical level sufficient to be authorized to carry out tasks for both aircraft and R&O, these include:

• The removal, disassembly, survey inspection and work order initiation of mechanical components.

• The disposition and conditioning of removed mechanical components and parts.

• The servicing, repair, modification, reassembly and installation of mechanical components.

• Providing support to Airframe Technicians for both on and off aircraft work.

• The safe operation of support equipment and hand/power tools while adhering to Tool and foreign Object Damage (FOD) control procedures.

• Maintenance of a clean/safe work area utilizing safe work practices and appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

• Performance of corrosion removal; standard and non-standard structural repairs; repair part local manufacture; standard and advanced fastener removals and installations.

• Carrying out primary aircraft structure refurbishment including disassembly, replacement and reassembly.

• The assembly of modification kits, including the manufacture, modification, and identification of parts and components for products manufactured, repaired or overhauled by the company.

• Working with various composites used in the manufacture and repair of aircraft and aircraft components.

• Performs ramp duties including, but not limited to, marshalling, parking, towing, fuelling/defueling, servicing, and post/pre-flight inspections.

• After further training, demonstrated experience and where necessary promotion, perform authorized airworthiness functions of Shop Certification Authority (SCA), Aircraft Certification Authority (ACA), Aircraft Release Authority and Product Conformance Authority (PCA).

• Travel and work on off-site Mobile Repair Parties/Field Teams, and Work Parties.

• Provide on-job-training (OJT) and technical supervision to other Airframe Mechanics.

• Attend trade training and development sessions for qualifications/authorization purposes

• Adhere to policies, procedures and directives as established by the company.

What You Will Bring:
• The Airframe Mechanic must have a minimum of 4 years experience performing aircraft maintenance at an AMO or MRO.

• The Airframe Mechanic must, as a minimum, meet one of the following: be a graduate of recognized aircraft maintenance program or apprenticeship program; hold a current Transport Canada Civil Aviation (TCCA) Aircraft Maintenance Engineering (AME-M or AME-S) license; be qualified as an AVN or ACS with the Canadian Forces; be a graduate of a demonstrably equivalent foreign military/civilian basic trade-training program.

• The Airframe Mechanic shall possess, as a minimum, a basic knowledge of aircraft structures and/or mechanical systems including, but not limited to: flight controls; hydraulic and oil distribution systems; fuel systems; oxygen systems; landing gear systems; engine systems including auxiliary power unit (APU) systems; transmission and drive train systems; propeller and rotor systems; life support and cargo systems and cabin pressurization systems.

• The Airframe Mechanic must be capable of reading and interpreting technical documentation such as technical manuals, drawings, Technical Data Packages (TDPs), technical instructions and Work Orders (WOs).

• The Airframe Mechanic must demonstrate a basic understanding of airworthiness requirements for authorization to perform airworthiness functions. Must demonstrate a compliant and skilled level of task proficiency, which is aided by course/OJT/OJE training and practical experience.

• Must be eligible for authorization for the performance of maintenance (POM) and maintain the ability to carryout instructions and exercise self-verification of work.

• Demonstrate a personal commitment to IMP Occupational Health, Safety and Environment policies. Continually focusing on your individual safety and the safety of others who may be affected by your work and to fully comply with all Federal Health and Safety Legislation.

• Participate in Continuous Improvement, Lean & 5S activities in your area.

Title: Senior Manager, Clinical Services

Employee Working Location: Partially Virtual / Hybrid (Canada)

Employment Status: Permanent Full-time

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

## In this role, you will:

• Provide strategic and operational leadership for clinical services across the Health in Emergencies portfolio, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, humanitarian standards, and health system needs.

• Lead the design, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of clinical services supporting emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and risk reduction.

• Ensure the readiness of clinical personnel, systems, equipment, and processes for domestic and international emergency deployments.

• Oversee clinical governance, quality, compliance, and technical support for emergency health operations, including Humanitarian Health Services and Emergency Response Units.

• Lead programme management activities, including planning, monitoring, quality improvement, budgeting, resource allocation, risk management, and operational reporting.

• Strengthen workforce capacity and strategic partnerships by supporting personnel development, stakeholder engagement, and representation of the Canadian Red Cross in relevant technical and coordination forums.

## What we are looking for:

• University degree in Medicine, Nursing, Public Health, Allied Health Sciences, or another relevant clinical discipline; graduate studies and professional healthcare registration in Canada are assets.

• Significant experience in clinical services, public health, humanitarian health, emergency management, or related health sectors.

• Proven leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams, complex health programmes, and emergency health operations.

• Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and overseeing clinical services in domestic, international, and low-resource settings, including emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and outbreak operations.

• Strong expertise in emergency clinical services, humanitarian health programming, health systems, clinical governance, professional standards, regulatory requirements, and risk management.

• Exceptional analytical, communication, stakeholder engagement, people leadership, and change management skills, with experience managing budgets, resources, and partnerships in complex and rapidly evolving environments.

• Fluency in English is required; French is strongly preferred.

## Working Conditions:

• Hybrid work environment, with regular domestic and international travel.

• Ability and willingness to deploy to emergency operations in Canada and internationally, including disaster-affected, resource-constrained, epidemic, conflict-affected, or insecure environments.

• Candidates must be medically fit for international travel and deployment in accordance with Canadian Red Cross requirements.

• The role may require work outside normal business hours, including extended hours and work on short notice, in support of emergency and humanitarian operations.

• Deployments may involve difficult environmental, physical, and emotional conditions and require adherence to security protocols and effective personal resilience.

• Ability to work under pressure, manage competing priorities, and make sound decisions in rapidly changing situations.

• As we work with and support people (managers, colleagues, beneficiaries/customers, volunteers, donors and external partners) and communities in Canada and around the world, applicants whose first language is not English may be required to perform the responsibilities of the role in English.

• Eligibility to work in Canada: At this time, we welcome applications from candidates eligible to work in Canada. If you are not a citizen or permanent resident of Canada, we encourage you to carefully review your visa to find out whether you are eligible to work in the job you are considering applying for. Refer to our FAQ for more information.

• If you are selected for this role, you will be required to complete a successful pre-employment screening process which includes a satisfactory Enhanced Police Information Check (E-PIC).

title: Director of Technical Services
description:
## EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

## DIRECTOR OF TECHNICAL SERVICES

## Join Our Team

The North Shore Mi'kmaq Tribal Council (NSMTC) is seeking a Director to join our Technical Services team.

Position Title: Director of Technical Services

Report To: General Manager

Location: 47 Church Road, Natoaganeg, NB, E1V 4E6

Anticipated Start Date: November 16, 2026

Application Deadline: October 23, 2026

NSMTC Member Communities: Ugpi'ganjig (Eel River Bar), Oinpegitjoig (Pabineau), Natoaganeg (Eel Ground), Metepenagiag (Red Bank), L'nui Menikuk (Indian Island), Tjipõgtõtjg (Buctouche), and Amlamgog (Fort Folly).

## The Opportunity

Reporting to the General Manager, the Director of Technical Services is a key member of NSMTC's senior leadership team and provides strategic leadership and oversight to a diverse portfolio of technical programs and services supporting our member First Nation communities.

This is an exciting opportunity for a leader who can see the big picture while building strong relationships, developing people, strengthening systems and turning organizational and community priorities into action. The Director provides leadership to Technical Services Program Managers and works across NSMTC to ensure programs are well managed, appropriately resourced and aligned with the organization's strategic direction. The role has broad responsibility for departmental strategy, people leadership, financial and resource stewardship, governance and risk, partnerships, continuous improvement and the development of new opportunities that respond to the evolving needs of NSMTC member communities.

## What You'll Do

• Provide strategic leadership and direction across NSMTC's Technical Services portfolio.

• Lead, mentor and support Program Managers and other assigned employees, establishing clear expectations, accountability and opportunities for development.

• Translate NSMTC's strategic priorities and Board direction into departmental plans, priorities and measurable results.

• Lead the development, implementation and evaluation of the Technical Services strategic plan.

• Provide oversight of departmental budgets, funding, forecasting, resource allocation and financial performance in collaboration with Finance.

• Ensure appropriate oversight of funding agreements, reporting requirements, program commitments and organizational obligations.

• Identify and manage operational, financial, people and reputational risks within the Technical Services portfolio and escalate significant matters appropriately.

• Provide the General Manager and Board with timely information, analysis and recommendations to support effective decision-making.

• Build a respectful, collaborative and accountable workplace culture grounded in NSMTC's values and commitment to serving First Nation communities.

• Develop leadership capacity within the department through coaching, mentorship, professional development and succession planning.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with member communities, Indigenous organizations, government departments, funding agencies, educational institutions, utilities and other strategic partners.

• Support the continued development and expansion of services related to housing, infrastructure, water and wastewater, solid waste management, climate change, energy and other emerging community priorities.

• Monitor emerging trends, policy changes, funding opportunities and service-transfer initiatives that may impact NSMTC and its member communities.

• Identify innovative technologies, partnerships, business opportunities and service-delivery approaches that strengthen Technical Services and create value for communities.

• Work collaboratively with other NSMTC Directors and departments to support organization-wide priorities and effective use of resources.

## What You Bring

You are an experienced leader who is comfortable working in a complex, multidisciplinary environment and balancing strategic priorities with organizational accountability. You bring:

• Post-secondary education in business or public administration, engineering, infrastructure, environmental sciences, project management or another relevant discipline.

• A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible professional experience in technical services, infrastructure, engineering, environmental services, business administration, program management or a related field.

• A minimum of five (5) years of leadership or management experience, including experience leading, mentoring and developing employees and/or managers.

• Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple programs, projects and priorities within a complex organization.

• Strong financial and resource management experience, including budgeting, forecasting, funding proposals, contribution agreements and financial oversight.

• Experience with strategic planning, organizational development, change management and continuous improvement.

• Strong judgment and decision-making skills, with the ability to assess risk, consider organizational impacts and make sound recommendations.

• Demonstrated ability to build strong teams, develop people, navigate challenging workplace issues and foster a respectful and accountable culture.

• Excellent relationship-building, communication, facilitation, negotiation and problem-solving skills.

• The ability to work effectively with First Nation communities, senior leadership, Boards, government, funding partners and other stakeholders.

• Knowledge or experience related to infrastructure, housing, water and wastewater, environmental services, engineering, energy or climate change would be considered an asset.

• Experience working with First Nation communities, Indigenous organizations and/or Indigenous Services Canada programs and funding would be considered a strong asset.

• An equivalent combination of education, training, professional experience and demonstrated leadership may be considered.

## Leadership at NSMTC

Our team leaders are expected to lead beyond their individual departments. They connect the work of their teams to NSMTC's broader strategic direction, exercise sound judgment and decision-making, manage resources responsibly, develop people and leadership capacity, work collaboratively across the organization, and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Leadership & People Management • Communication & Relationship Management • Decision-Making & Problem Solving • Planning & Strategic Execution • Financial & Resource Management • Cultural Competence & Community Engagement • Adaptability & Continuous Improvement

Above all, we are looking for someone who understands that strong leadership is about creating the conditions for people, programs, and communities to succeed.

## Interested in Joining NSMTC?

If you are an experienced leader who is excited about the opportunity to strengthen [Department], develop people, and contribute to meaningful work with First Nation communities, we would welcome your application.

## What We Offer

• A work culture that supports employee wellbeing, diversity, engagement, and a sense of belonging.

• Competitive salary, pension, and benefits package, including access to an Employee and Family Assistance Program.

• Collaboration with a team of passionate professionals working towards contributing to the growth and success of First Nations communities.

## Additional Information

The NSMTC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all interested parties. However, if there are applicants of equal education, skills, and experience, preference may be given to members of our seven member communities.

Application Deadline
Please submit your resume and cover letter to Tammy Scott, Human Resources Manager at careers@nsmtc.ca by October 23, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.

We thank those who apply, but only individuals selected for further consideration will be contacted. Applicants are responsible for the timely submission of applications.

description:

Salary: $131,945.00 - $156,298.00/Year Job Type: Permanent Full Time Closing Date: November 4, 2026 Position Overview:
The Director of Occupational Health, Safety & Organizational Resilience provides enterprise-wide strategic leadership for the transformation, modernization, and continuous improvement of the City's Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) Program. As a key member of the City's leadership team, the Director will shape and execute a forward-looking Corporate Safety Strategy that strengthens organizational resilience, reduces risk, and advances a culture of safety excellence across a diverse municipal workforce.

The Director will lead organizational change and influence leaders at all levels of the organization to embed safety, risk management, prevention, and employee well-being into strategic and operational decision-making. This position will build alignment across departments, engage union and employee partners, and create the conditions necessary for sustainable adoption of new policies, practices, systems, and behaviours.

The Director will provide strategic advice to senior leadership on occupational health and safety, enterprise risk, regulatory compliance, emerging workplace risks, and organizational readiness. The role will balance strategic leadership with operational oversight, translating the City's safety vision into measurable outcomes, strengthened organizational capability, and sustained cultural change.

Success in this role will require a leader who can influence, build trust across diverse stakeholder groups, navigate competing priorities, and create shared accountability for safety outcomes. Formalizing governance mechanisms, notably through a cross-functional team (CFT), which brings together operational, administrative, and safety leaders to provide coordination, consistency and accountability.

As the Director Occupational Health, Safety & Organizational Resilience, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

•Lead the development and execution of the City's Corporate Safety Strategy, establishing strategic priorities, objectives, performance measures, and accountabilities that align occupational health and safety with the City's broader strategic direction.

•Lead the transformation and modernization of the City's OHS Program, redesigning policies, processes, systems, and practices to reflect legislative requirements, leading practices, emerging risks, and the evolving needs of the organization.

•Lead organizational change associated with the transformation of the safety program, developing and executing change management strategies that build awareness, create alignment, address resistance, engage stakeholders, and achieve sustained adoption of new approaches and practices.

•Influence and partner with senior leaders, departmental leadership teams, managers, and employees to embed safety and risk management into strategic planning, operational decision-making, workforce practices, and organizational performance.

•Build organizational alignment and shared accountability for safety, using strong influencing, relationship-building, consultation, negotiation, and communication skills to bring diverse stakeholders together around common objectives.

•Establish and strengthen corporate safety governance, defining clear roles, responsibilities, accountabilities, escalation processes, and decision-making structures to support consistent and effective safety practices across the organization.

•Drive measurable improvements in safety performance, leveraging data, trends, leading and lagging indicators, risk assessments, and organizational insights to identify priorities and evaluate the effectiveness of safety strategies and interventions.

•Provide strategic advice and recommendations to the senior leadership team and Council, as appropriate, on significant health and safety risks, regulatory requirements, organizational exposure, emerging issues, and opportunities to strengthen workplace safety and resilience.

•Develop and maintain trusted relationships with managers, employees, union representatives, and other key stakeholders, fostering collaboration, credibility, transparency, and shared ownership of safety outcomes.

•Lead and develop a high-performing team of safety professionals, building organizational capability, professional expertise, leadership capacity, and a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

•Oversee significant incident investigations and organizational learning, ensuring rigorous root cause analysis, appropriate corrective and preventive actions, and effective follow-through to reduce recurrence and address systemic risks.

•Anticipate and respond to emerging risks, monitoring legislative and regulatory developments, industry trends, workforce trends, and changing operational environments to ensure organizational readiness and compliance.

•Champion continuous improvement and safety innovation, identifying opportunities to improve processes, leverage technology and data, enhance employee engagement, and increase the effectiveness and accessibility of safety programs.

•Lead strategic safety communications and engagement, ensuring employees and leaders understand the City's safety priorities, their individual and collective responsibilities, and the purpose and benefits of organizational change.

•Strengthen organizational resilience and readiness by identifying systemic vulnerabilities, enhancing prevention and response capabilities, and ensuring the City can effectively adapt to emerging occupational health and safety challenges.

•Champion a proactive safety culture and employee well-being, moving the organization beyond compliance toward prevention, learning, accountability, and sustained safety excellence.

Essential Qualifications:
The successful candidate will bring a minimum of ten years of progressive leadership experience in occupational health and safety, operations, public safety, human resources, or a related field, including significant experience leading organizational transformation, change management, continuous improvement, or enterprise-wide initiatives. Experience in a unionized and/or municipal environment would be considered an asset.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

•A university degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Human Resource Management, Occupational Health & Safety, or a related discipline, supplemented by post-secondary education in Occupational Health & Safety or a related field.

•A recognized professional certification in Occupational Health & Safety.

•Comprehensive knowledge of applicable occupational health and safety legislation, regulations, standards, and leading practices.

•Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise-level strategies and transformational programs.

•Proven ability to lead and sustain organizational change, including the ability to build commitment, manage resistance, and translate strategy into practical and sustainable action.

•Exceptional ability to influence, build consensus, navigate competing interests, and create alignment among diverse stakeholders.

•Strong political acumen and the ability to operate effectively within a complex public-sector environment.

•Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and influence senior leaders, managers, employees, union representatives, and external partners.

•Experience using data, performance measures, and risk intelligence to inform strategic decisions and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

•Exceptional communication, presentation, negotiation, consultation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences.

•Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, develop, and engage high-performing professional teams.

•Strategic thinking combined with the ability to translate organizational priorities into practical implementation plans and measurable results.

The Canadian Red Cross (Red Cross) - an inspirational not for profit organization, helps people and communities in Canada and around the world in times of need and supports them in strengthening their resilience. As a Canada's Best Employers 2026, we are committed to having an accessible, diverse, inclusive, and barrier-free work environment.

The Senior Lifecycle Marketing Specialist owns the design, build and optimization of the Canadian Red Cross's always-on donor lifecycle in HubSpot. This role leads the execution of our audience-first, monthly-first fundraising strategy by designing and optimizing automated donor lifecycle journeys. This role oversees the donor experience across acquisition, conversion, retention, upgrade, and reactivation, using donor insights and behavioural data to drive revenue growth, increase retention, and maximize long-term donor value.

As the owner of lifecycle marketing, the successful candidate will ensure donor data, technology, and communication channels work together to deliver timely, personalized engagement and the right next-best action at every stage of the donor journey.
Working within the Digital Marketing portfolio and reporting to the Senior Manager, Digital Marketing, this senior-level role operates with a high degree of autonomy and collaborates across teams to drive strategic marketing initiatives and outcomes - aligning Digital, Sustainer, Stewardship, Direct Mail and Fundraising Operations around one coordinated donor experience in support of the FY28 audience-first transition and an ambitious 2030 goal.

## In this role, you will :

• Lead the development and execution of donor lifecycle marketing strategies, designing and optimizing personalized donor journeys across acquisition, onboarding, retention, upgrade, and reactivation. Leverage donor personas, behavioural insights, and engagement data to drive revenue growth, improve retention, and maximize long-term donor value.

• Own and optimize marketing automation within HubSpot, translating strategy into scalable workflows and trigger-based campaigns. Develop, manage, and continuously improve donor journeys, including welcome, conversion, upgrade, payment recovery, retention, and re-engagement programs, while ensuring the overall health and effectiveness of the automation ecosystem.

• Develop and maintain audience segmentation, lifecycle data models, and performance measurement frameworks. Partner with fundraising, digital, and technology teams to ensure seamless integration across marketing platforms and data sources, enabling accurate targeting, personalized engagement, and effective donor communications.

• Monitor, analyze, and report on lifecycle marketing performance, including acquisition, conversion, retention, reactivation, upgrade, and donor value metrics. Lead testing and optimization initiatives, using data-driven insights to improve campaign effectiveness, donor engagement, and fundraising results.

Marketing Automation, Data & Performance Management

• Build, manage, and optimize HubSpot automation programs, ensuring efficient, scalable donor journeys and continuous improvement of workflows and campaign performance.

• Develop and execute personalized donor journeys, including onboarding, conversion, retention, upgrade, payment recovery, and reactivation campaigns, using testing and insights to improve results.

• Maintain donor segmentation and data frameworks, leveraging behavioural and giving data to support targeted engagement and personalized donor experiences.

• Monitor and report on lifecycle marketing KPIs, including acquisition, conversion, retention, reactivation, upgrade rates, and donor lifetime value, and support audience activation and retargeting strategies.

Collaboration, Vendor Management & Compliance

• Collaborate with fundraising and cross-functional teams to deliver a seamless and coordinated donor experience across channels.

• Provide expertise and guidance on lifecycle marketing, audience segmentation, and marketing automation best practices.

• Manage external vendors and consulting partners, overseeing project delivery, performance, timelines, and stakeholder coordination.

• Ensure compliance with privacy, consent, accessibility, and communication requirements while maintaining donor trust and engagement.

## What we are looking for:

• Minimum 6-9 years of relevant experience and a 3-year college diploma or university degree in marketing, digital marketing, philanthropy/fundraising, business administration or a related field - or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Demonstrated experience designing and building lifecycle / CRM marketing automation and multi-step donor or customer journeys (acquisition, onboarding, conversion, retention, reactivation, upgrade).

• 6-9 years of hands-on expertise with HubSpot (workflows, lists, properties, reporting); experience integrating marketing automation with a CRM and donation/payment platforms is a strong asset (e.g. Unity, Fundraise Up, Salesmsg).

• Strong grasp of audience segmentation, persona modelling, behavioural triggers, propensity and lifecycle/journey strategy.

• Ability to identify complex problems, analyze interrelated data and platform factors, assess and mitigate risk, and develop solutions using specialized skills.

• Analytical fluency - defining KPIs, reading journey and campaign performance, and turning insight into optimization.

• Communication and influence skills to align stakeholders and drive consensus, often in sensitive or cross-team situations.

• Proficiency in standard computer applications (Microsoft Office Suite) and fundraising/marketing databases; bilingual EN/FR an asset.

## Working Conditions :

• No unusual physical requirements; office-like setting.

• Requires significant attention to detail, concentration, and the ability to mentally process large amounts of information.

• Work pace is often unpredictable with significant time pressures, and requires adapting to frequent and sometimes urgent changes in priorities.

• Work is conducted in an office-like setting and requires the ability to work to deadlines.

title: Executive Director, Clean Energy
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:

Department: Energy

About Us
The Department of Energy serves the social, environmental, and economic interests of Nova Scotians by ensuring that energy resources are developed and used in an efficient and sustainable manner. The Department delivers programs and activities related to electricity, renewable energy, energy efficiency, geoscience, petroleum, and industry development.

About Our Opportunity
The Executive Director, Clean Energy is the Department's senior executive lead for electricity, renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable transportation and non-petroleum energy-sector matters. The role leads a team of senior professionals responsible for advancing policy, regulatory, program and implementation work that supports a reliable, affordable and lower-carbon energy system for Nova Scotians.

As Executive Director, you lead the clean energy component of provincial energy strategy and direct the integration of electricity, renewable energy, energy efficiency and sustainable transportation priorities into government-wide planning and decision-making.

You lead the development and delivery of clean energy strategies and initiatives, including electricity policy and planning, renewable energy development, efficiency and demand-side management, sustainable transportation, electricity market design and utility-related regulatory matters. In addition, you contribute sector expertise to integrated provincial energy planning, and support whole-of-department alignment on major priorities. Lastly, you are accountable for setting direction, aligning Branch resources, and supporting the team to deliver clean energy priorities effectively.

Primary Accountabilities
• Provide senior executive leadership for clean energy policy, planning, regulation, programs and implementation across electricity, renewables, efficiency, demand-side management, sustainable transportation and related non-petroleum energy matters.

• Retain lead accountability for clean energy sector substance, including electricity, renewable energy, energy efficiency and sustainable transportation policy development, regulatory approaches, stakeholder relationships, sector-specific strategies and implementation.

• Lead development and implementation of major clean energy strategies, plans, legislation, regulatory frameworks and funding initiatives, ensuring they support affordability, reliability, sustainability, economic development and public confidence.

• Lead the department's position on complex utility-sector, regulatory and electricity market matters, including regulatory proceedings, electricity market design, governance issues, utility accountability and legislative or regulatory approaches that affect Nova Scotia's electricity system.

• Lead renewable energy and energy efficiency policy and delivery, ensuring sector-specific strategies are aligned with the Department's integrated provincial energy strategy.

• Provide expert, timely advice to the Deputy Minister, Minister, Cabinet and central agencies on clean energy issues, risks, trade-offs, legislative proposals, regulatory approaches and implementation considerations.

• Build and maintain constructive relationships with utilities, regulators, Independent Power Producers, industry, other governments, Indigenous peoples, municipalities, communities, non-government organizations, researchers and other partners.

• Act as lead Executive Director or Project Sponsor for assigned major clean energy initiatives, clarifying objectives, milestones, engagement requirements, decision points, risks and barriers.

• Provide strategic management of Branch resources, including human and financial resource oversight, performance management, procurement, budget forecasting, workforce leadership, diversity, healthy workplace practices and team development.

Qualifications and Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, you have a bachelor's degree in a related field (such as science, energy systems, engineering, or business and administration) and substantial (10+ years) senior level strategic related experience, or an equivalent combination of training and experience may also be considered. A graduate (Master's) degree would be an asset.

You have experience leading multidisciplinary teams, as well as experience working with industry, utilities, communities, municipalities, regulators and other governments. Further you have strong understanding in areas such as renewable energy technologies, energy efficiency, climate change and greenhouse-gas reduction, as well as government decision-making.

The role requires innovation in identifying emerging clean energy opportunities and risks, applying sector expertise to policy and regulatory challenges, and developing practical approaches that support responsible clean energy development and implementation within the department's broader direction. As a forward-thinking leader, you anticipate changes in clean energy markets, electricity systems, regulatory models, technology trends, and public expectations. Further, you have significant decision-making authority and accountability for advancing the clean energy priorities within the branch's mandate. Lastly, you have excellent leadership, communication (verbal and written), interpersonal, presentation and consultation skills. You work well independently and engage effectively with senior decision makers.

Leadership competencies required at this level of work are: Decisiveness, Strategic Orientation, Developing Others, Team Leadership, Self-Awareness and Personal Impact, Effective Interactive Communication, Partnering and Relationship Building, and Intercultural and Diversity Proficiency.

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency
Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

• Mostly office-based work with occasional requirements to travel and attend meetings, within Nova Scotia and to other provinces.

• Considerable and sustained pressure from deadlines, conflicting demands and stakeholder opinion, continuous change, and ambiguity.

Additional Information
This is a permanent, full-time position based in Halifax, Nova Scotia.

What We Offer
• Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career.

• Countless career paths.

Location: 103-15 Medicine Trail, Eskasoni, NS Hours: 35 hours per week (8:30AM – 4:30PM)

## What we offer:

## NSECDIS offers a competitive compensation package including:

• Salary: $34.20 per hour ($62,244.00 per year) with annual adjustments up to 8 years

• 105 hours Vacation, 105 hours Sick time

• Group Health Benefits Plan (including Extended Healthcare, Dental and Wellness services)

• Contributory Defined Benefits Pension Plan

• Paid holidays (provincial & federal) as well as a paid winter holiday shutdown

As well as:

• Continuous Professional Development

• A chance to support families and educators in your community

## Who we are:

Nova Scotia Early Childhood Development Intervention Services (NSECDIS) provides province-wide services for families of children, birth to school entry, who may be at risk for, or with a diagnosis of, developmental delay. Our goal to promote improved developmental outcomes for children through consultation, coaching, information sharing, support and services designed to meet the individual needs of the child and family. Services emphasize the enhancement of skills and ability through planned interactions to promote child development and family capacity and are delivered in the child's home and community-based programs.

We also facilitate Early Learning and Child Care program and Early Childhood Educator capacity building through coaching within child care and Pre-primary programs with use of The Pyramid Model for Supporting Social Emotional Competence in Infants and Young Children.

As an employer we offer a supportive environment where staff are encouraged to follow their passion within our field. We believe in continuous Professional Development and growth. Our teams are comprised of compassionate trained professionals who enjoy serving their communities.

## Duties include:

• In home coaching with families and community consultations to establish and implement family led meaningful goals and strategies

• Supporting capacity building in families and educators by providing participatory experiences and opportunities that strengthen knowledge and skills and promote a positive sense of competence and confidence

• Connect families with community partners/resources and support navigation within service systems

• Maintaining positive relationships and continual communication with families and their support teams to facilitate joint programming

• Tracking of child and family progress and goals through timely and accurate documentation of all caseload observations and data within our internal database system and support files

• Other related duties as required

## Qualifications & Skills:

• A minimum Bachelor's Degree in Early Childhood Development or related field

• Experience working with children from birth to school age with developmental disabilities and their families is essential

• Strong planning, organizational and time management abilities are required

• Excellent communication (oral & written)

• Strong interpersonal skills

• Adaptable and dependable

• Valid driver's license and access to own reliable vehicle is required daily

Please apply using our Applicant Tracking System though the link provided via this website with a Resume & Cover Letter

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the families we serve. If you are a member of one or more equity groups, you are encouraged to self-identify on your cover letter or resume.

title: Maintenance Controller
description:
## Purpose of position

To provide direction and support for the entire Maintenance system during IROP situations & daily operations.

## Key responsibilities

• Oversee the Line Maintenance related matters on a system wide basis.

• Monitor and Maintain Technical Dispatch of Fleet.

• Maintain a close working relationship with Dispatch and the Commercial Operations Manager (COM) on issues that will impact operational aircraft.

• Monitor and track ALL rescheduled maintenance items, MELs, CDLs and Deferrals using Trax and MX Control.

• Liaise with the maintenance bases & maintenance planning to ensure timely rectification of MELs, CDLs and Deferrals or other outstanding maintenance discrepancies.

• Liaise with Maintenance Quality, System for authorization of AOG maintenance on company aircraft at non-maintenance stations and authorization of Ferry Flights, test flights, etc. This may include liaison with the Bombardier Help Desk.

• Liaise with Flight Dispatch and provide current and continuous reports of general mechanical status of entire fleet.

• Provide technical or functional guidance to other staff: Flight Crews & Line Stations, Contract maintenance personnel, Line Planning, Base Supervisors, Crew Chiefs, Stores, & Airports.

• Communicate and document status of IROPS, occurrences, and emergencies to appropriate persons.

• Coordinate with the aircraft routers on the routing of aircraft required for specific maintenance functions.

• Coordinate maintenance requirements during irregular operations in an effort to minimize costs and disruptions.

• Liaise with the Material Coordinator to expedite acquisition of required replacement parts in the event of irregular operations or mechanical interruptions.

• Implement action to be taken to protect aircraft during inclement weather at an operating station and determine further action to be taken by appropriate maintenance personnel.

• Participate in Maintenance projects and review Groups as required.

• Coach line/hangar employees for consistent quality completion of responsibilities; Give feedback and support in conjunction with coaching.

• Provide assistance to the bases in acquiring resources and tools for support staff to perform their duties.

• Demonstrate support and commitment to the diverse needs of staff.

• Create an open, honest and supportive work environment.

• Encourage ongoing teamwork through meetings, open dialogue, team challenges and informal collective experiences.

• Perform other related duties as assigned.

• Perform duties in accordance with established policies and procedures while giving primary consideration to personal safety, and the safety of co-workers and customers.

## Required qualifications

• AME License (ACA Holder) with 5 years of experience.

• A minimum of 2 Aircraft Endorsements.

• Good interpersonal and effective communication skills.

• Excellent organizational skills.

• Knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word etc.).

• Good computer literacy skills.

• Good working knowledge of the functions of other departments. E.g. Supply Management, Flight Operations, etc..

• Ability to work under tight time constraints during irregular flight operations.

• Willing and able to work varying shifts.

## Preferred qualifications

• Knowledge of FliteTrac, MXPlan, & Trax .

• Previous Maintenance Control experience.

## Benefits of joining our award-winning team

• Enjoy exclusive employee travel programs across the Air Canada network, giving you and your family access to incredible destinations.

• Secure your long-term financial well-being with our competitive, employer-supported retirement savings programs (defined contribution pension plan or voluntary group RRSP) for permanent employees.

• Benefit from a comprehensive health and wellness package, including health, dental, life, and accident insurance to keep you and your loved ones protected.

Jazz Aviation LP (Jazz) is Canada’s largest regional airline and Air Canada’s primary Air Canada Express operator, connecting people and communities to approximately 70 destinations across North America.

Jazz is proud to be recognized for its strong commitment to people and culture. Visit our Company Awards and Recognition page to learn more about the honours we've earned.

Join our award-winning team and be part of shaping the future of regional aviation!

title: Medical Communications Centre Nurse
description:
Position Type:
Permanent
*

Closing date:
2026-10-15
*

Emergency Medical Care Inc. (EMC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Medavie Health Services (MHS) that manages and operates ground ambulance, air medical transport and the medical communications operations in Nova Scotia through a performance-based contract with the provincial government's Emergency Health Services (EHS) Operations division and the Department of Health and Wellness. As well, EMC operates TeleHealth/811 medical communications for Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island for the Department of Health.

We access all communities in Nova Scotia in a timely and efficient manner with our fleet of more than 180 ambulances and support vehicles operating out of 60+ stations. We respond to 165,000+ calls annually across the province, which are actively managed through the EHS Operations Medical Communications Centre, the hub of all emergency (911) and non-emergency (hospital transfers) medical calls.

The EHS Operations LifeFlight program provides even greater accessibility by responding to patients on scene or through inter-facility transports by our critical care team via helicopter, fixed wing, or ground ambulance.

In addition, paramedics in Nova Scotia participate in various programs both urban and rural such as community-based paramedic programs, collaborative emergency centres, and emergency preparedness and special operations, to name a few.

There are lots of opportunities waiting for you in Nova Scotia. Apply now to learn more about our service and available positions.

## Nature and Scope:

Work within a collaborative, inter-professional team to appropriately manage and support caller access to health care services to meet their non-emergent, non-life-threatening health situations. The MCC-N will perform secondary telephone based medical triage of lower acuity 911 EHS calls, performing patient assessment, formulating treatment plans and assisting patients in arranging appropriate care using information and with the support of evidence -based, computer decision support software, clinical guidelines, protocols and other resources. The MCC-N will use critical thinking, therapeutic communication and clinical decision-making skills to assess, plan, implement, educate and evaluate the patients' health situation and/or informational needs.

## Duties and Responsibilities:

• Demonstrates accountability for own nursing practice by complying with the Canadian Nurses Association (CAN) Code of Ethics, and Nova Scotia College of Nursing Standards for Nursing Practice.

• Delivers appropriate patient care within the RN's scope of practice and the MCC-N scope of employment.

• Provides nursing care within the standards defined by professional nursing body, which has been legislated by the province to regulate and license registered nurses.

• Provides telephone based clinical care advice, alternate care pathway and service referral to individuals through the effective application of registered nursing skills, clinical judgment, computer-based decision support software, appropriate evidence-based clinical guidelines, and other relevant information databases/resources.

• Using in-depth clinical knowledge, applies process to identify patient care needs, risks and safety issues, educational opportunities, and appropriate health care referrals.

• Apply critical analysis to the combination of complex information during the care process to provide accurate advice and health information to patients to empower them.

• Accurately and completely document clinical and other relevant notes within the computer software program in a timely manner throughout and immediately during and after a call.

• Demonstrates compliance with all program specific metrics, participates in the evaluation and or measurement of these metrics and plays an active role in improving personal, team and program performance.

• Provides clinical advice and proactively promotes the use of alternative care pathways to operational staff.

## Qualifications and Requirements:

• Diploma in nursing; Bachelor of Nursing or Bachelor of Science in Nursing preferred

• Clinical nursing experience in an acute care environment (e.g., general medical surgical)

• Emergency or intensive care unit experience

• Experience in general nursing triage experience

• Experience in nursing tele-triage, such as 811 or ECNS

• Minimum three (3) years recent (within the past five years) clinical experience

• An active license and good standing as a Registered Nurse with the Nova Scotia College of Nursing (NSCN) and compliance with all applicable laws pertaining to the practice of nursing in the province

• Current BLS certification

• Ability to obtain and maintain Emergency Medical Dispatch (EMD) and Emergency Communication Nurse System (ECNS) certifications

## Knowledge and Skills:

• Excellent communication, telephone, web and customer relation skills

• Good critical thinking, sound clinical decision-making and problem-solving skills

• Demonstrates a commitment to education and training relating to EHS Medical Communications Centre protocols and processes.

• Solid knowledge and competence in the use of computers and keyboarding

• Fluency in English (oral and written) is required; fluency in English and French (oral and written preferred)

While Medavie may use automated tools, including AI, to support application screening, candidates are expected to complete all recruitment interactions independently-without AI assistance-to ensure a fair and equitable process.

Our goal is to be a diverse workforce that is representative of the citizens we serve. We are committed to building an inclusive team that represents a variety of backgrounds, cultures, races, perspectives and skills. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates including women, persons of any sexual orientations and gender identities and/or expressions, Indigenous persons, African Canadians, other racialized groups, persons with disabilities. Candidates who identify as being from any of these groups are encouraged to voluntarily self-identify.

title: ETO (Electro-Technical Officer)
description:
Since 1982, Norbulk has been a provider of ship management services, providing technical ship management, crew management, technical services and commercial ship management. We are a privately owned company, with a long term focus, investing in our seafarers and shore staff to equip them with the skills and knowledge needed to further their careers and continually improve our marine operations. Norbulk is headquartered in Bermuda, with offices in North America, Europe, The Middle East and Asia. Norbulk carries out ship management for all vessel types. At Norbulk, we are committed to Health and Safety of our seafarers and the protection of the environment.

Our Saint John, New Brunswick office manages two Canadian Oil Tanker Vessels and we are currently recruiting an ETO (Electro-Technical Officer) with Ocean Service Ltd.

EDUCATION:

Diploma in Electrical Engineering or equivalent marine qualification.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Responsible to the Chief Engineer for the maintenance and condition of electrical equipment assigned to his care, in accordance with the instructions issued by the Chief Engineer. Duties include but are not limited to:

· Monthly inspections of the vessel's electrical equipment with special attention being paid to tankship electrical equipment in respect to hazardous areas outside machinery spaces and accommodation areas.

· Providing a monthly report on the serviceability of electrical equipment for the Chief Engineer with special attention to gas tightness and intrinsic integrity of tankship equipment.

· Isolating electrically operated machinery or circuitry to enable maintenance or other work to be carried out safely (See NS HSM - Health and Safety Manual).

· Weekly checks of ship's emergency batteries and GMDSS equipment.

· Assist as necessary during entering/leaving port.

· Assist in the preparation of requisitions for electrical equipment stores and spare parts and submit them to the Chief Engineer for approval.

· Maintain an inventory of the materials on hand and on order to make both the normal routing supplies and specific demands for stores.

· Carry out receipt checks and sign for the materials and goods when delivered, ensuring they are properly labelled, preserved, stowed and secured to avoid loss from damage or deterioration.

· Maintain control over the issuance and usage of tools and materials and other goods in his charge to prevent waste.

· Upon joining the vessel, the Electrical Officer must report to the Master and then the Chief Engineer. He must consult with the Officer he is relieving regarding the machinery and equipment for which he will be responsible. He will then inspect such machinery and equipment, reporting any deficiencies to the Chief Engineer.

· Complete NS PER 006 (Handover Report) & NS SAF 001 (Shipboard Familiarisation Record).

· The Electrical Officer is additionally responsible for the serviceability and cleanliness of the vessel's electrical systems and equipment including but not limited to the following items:

- Main, auxiliary and emergency switchboard;

- Alternators (including the routine testing of the emergency unit);

- Starters and motors;

- Cargo handling equipment (where appropriate);

- Electrical and electronic control equipment for engine, cargo and deck machinery;

- Communications equipment;

- Accommodation, lighting and galley services;

- Refrigerated container power boxes/sockets;

- Maintenance of power sources for GMDSS equipment.

Qualifications:

Certificates: Electrician Certified Marine Advanced First Aid, Marine Emergency Duties, Marine Medical, Passport (must be able to travel to the States), Securities Training with Designated Duties, WHMIS, Confined Space, Basic Oil and Chemical Tanker Familiarization, Seaman's Discharge Book, and Fatigue Management. Marine certification will take priority; however, for a strong candidate we are willing to assist in receiving the proper certification.

Our ideal candidate is solutions oriented, has a strong work ethic, and works well in a team environment. Our full time employees work 40 days on 40 off, and have a competitive benefits package for them and their families. We provide paid travel to and from the vessel; therefore, the position is open to anyone living in Canada.

If you or someone you know in your professional network is interested in this exciting opportunity please send you CV to norbulksjnorbulknb.com

We thank all applicants for their interest, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Medical Office Administrator
description:
Medical Office Administrator

## WHO WE ARE

Our Health Centre is a non-profit community health centre serving the Municipality of the District of Chester and the Tancook Islands. Now approaching our tenth year, we operate a Same Day Clinic five days a week, along with specialty clinics including our new peri/menopause clinic, and programs that reach well beyond the exam room. Our programs and services are shaped by what our community members tell us they need.

We are small enough that every person here influences how care is delivered, and ambitious enough to keep testing new models to bring the best possible services and programming to our community. If you want your work to make a tangible difference in the community you live in and to help build something, this is where you want to be.

## AT A GLANCE

• Location
Onsite: Chester, Nova Scotia

• Term
Permanent. 30 to 40 hours per week over 4 to 5 days, based on the clinic schedule.

• Schedule
Approximately one evening per week (until 8 pm) and occasional Saturday coverage. Schedules are provided one month in advance whenever possible.

• Compensation
$23.00 to $26.00 per hour, based on experience.

## WHAT WE OFFER

• Health and dental coverage, 70% employer-paid

• Employer RRSP contributions of 5%, increasing to 6% as of April 2027

• 12 paid personal and sick leave days per year

• Two weeks of vacation to start, increasing with years of service

• Time in lieu available for hours worked beyond scheduled hours

• Benefits commence after successful completion of a three-month probationary period. Leave entitlements are prorated for scheduled hours.

## ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Medical Office Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day administrative coordination of all clinical services, including the Same Day Clinic and associated programs. This is a front-facing role, working directly with the patients and community members who come through our doors. The Medical Office Administrator works alongside the administrative assistant, and there are regular shifts where this position is the only administrative staff member on site.

The role ensures efficient workflows, accurate medical records and billing, effective scheduling and coverage, and high-quality support for both physicians and community members. It carries a high degree of independence. We are looking for someone who works collaboratively within a small team, takes full ownership of their work, and takes pride in getting things right the first time.

Given the sensitive nature of clinical information and community interactions, this position requires the highest standards of confidentiality, professionalism, accuracy, and sound judgment.

## TO APPLY OR LEARN MORE

To apply, send your resume and cover letter to Roger Bower, Executive Director, at ed@ourhealthcentre.ca. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, with the first review beginning October 16, 2026. The position will remain open until filled.

To learn more about Our Health Centre, visit www.ourhealthcentre.ca. For a full job description, contact Roger Bower directly.

title: Mobile Service Mechanic (Year Round) (Ashfield/Judique)
employer: Public Service Commission, Government of Nova Scotia
description:
Competition # : 49809

Department: Public Works

Location: ASHFIELD/JUDIQUE

Zone: 6

Type of Employment: Year Round

Union Status: CUPE - NSPG

Closing Date: 25-Oct-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

Under Article 13 of the Collective Agreement between the Nova Scotia Department of Public Works and the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Local 1867, the following opportunity is being posted.

Please quote the competition number and the Zone you are applying for as noted above on your application.

About Us
At the Department of Public Works, we are responsible for building and maintaining a sustainable provincial infrastructure for Nova Scotians. From highways and bridges to government buildings and registration of vehicles, safety and quality of life are top of mind. We support Nova Scotia's 23,000 kilometers of roads and highways, 4,100 bridges, and 9 provincial ferries.

Our Fleet Services Division is pivotal in ensuring the Public Works Fleet is running smoothly; ensuring the safety of our provincial road network.

About Our Opportunity
As the Mobile Service Mechanic, you will have the opportunity to work on our wide variety of equipment that maintains our roads and highways. You will be responsible for maintaining Utility Tractors, Rubber Tire Loaders, Graders, Tandem Trucks and all associated attachments including wings, plows, and sweepers.

Primary Accountabilities
You will not only repair, rebuild and make adjustments to our fleet, but also determine the reasoning for equipment malfunctions. To minimize such occurrences, preventative maintenance is a critical component in this role.
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Your coveralls and other personal protective equipment (PPE) are provided. We also have an annual footwear and tool reimbursement allowance as you must bring your own mechanical tools.

Qualifications and Experience
Some high school and an Inter-Provincial Red Seal Certificate of Qualification in Truck and Transport plus a minimum of five (5) years of diversified mechanical experience.

Upon hire, applicants will be required to successfully complete Nova Scotia Motor Vehicle Inspection (MVI) training as part of their probationary requirements.

A valid Class 5 drivers' license is a condition of employment, and an acceptable driver abstract must be submitted before employment begins. Air Brake endorsement is an asset.

Knowledge and experience of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology, electrical schematics, dealer purchased engine programs, online service manuals, and safety inspections are considered assets.

Air Conditioning Certification and a Motor Vehicle Inspection license would also be considered assets.

You consistently demonstrate initiative in your role, remaining up to date in changes to equipment, methods and technology within the mechanical field. Strong communication skills are necessary for the times when you will be helping staff diagnose and resolve equipment issues. You must also be able to work effectively with minimal supervision as most of your time will be spent working independently. Professionalism and a high standard for client and customer service is required.

You will be assessed on the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, interview, and reference checks.

Benefits
Based on the employment status and union agreement, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short and Long Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions
Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.

Additional Information
There is one (1) opportunity in Ashfield/Judique in Zone 6 covering the Antigonish/Judique/Port Hawkesbury Fleet Services area including Zones 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

Normal hours of work are 8:00am - 4:30pm. If equipment breaks down, we will count on you to help things get up and running again. Therefore, you will be on-call outside of your regular work schedule.

This opportunity is for a 52-week Year-Round position – the duties of which are full time and continuous in nature.

You must bring your own mechanical tools.

title: Clinical Therapist (LCT or RSW)-Bilingual (French and English)
description:
## Clinical Therapist (LCT or RSW)-Bilingual (French and English)

Location: New Brunswick
Part-Time (3 Days per Week) | Hybrid/Remote

Our impact is growing, and so is our team! Join us as we expand our programs and take our initiatives to the next level.

Behind every person living with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias are countless individuals dedicated to providing support, education, and hope. The Alzheimer Society is the leading not-for-profit health organization working nationwide to improve the quality of life for Canadians affected by Alzheimer's disease and other dementias while advancing the search for causes, treatments, and cures.

Since 1987, the Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick has been committed to supporting individuals living with dementia and their care partners through education, navigation, advocacy, and support services that help them live well throughout their journey.

## Job Summary

Reporting to the Manager of Support and Navigation, the Clinical Therapist plays a key role in supporting the emotional well-being of individuals living with dementia and their care partners. The successful candidate will provide trauma-informed, person-centred, and culturally responsive counselling services in individual and group settings.

Working collaboratively with clients, families, community partners, and internal teams, the Clinical Therapist will support individuals living with dementia and their care partners as they navigate the emotional, psychological, and practical impacts of the disease. In addition to providing therapeutic services, the successful candidate will lead the development, implementation, and evaluation of a pilot counselling program for people living with dementia, offered in both English and French, helping to expand access to specialized dementia-focused supports across New Brunswick.

This is a part-time position (three days per week). Services may be delivered in person, virtually, or through a hybrid approach based on client needs and program requirements.

## Typical Duties and Responsibilities

• Provide individual, family, and group counselling services to people living with dementia and their care partners.

• Conduct assessments and develop individualized support and treatment plans based on client needs and goals.

• Utilize evidence-informed therapeutic approaches to support client well-being and quality of life.

• Deliver counselling services in person, virtually, or through a hybrid model, as appropriate.

• Develop, implement, pilot, and evaluate a dementia-specific counselling program for people living with dementia in both English and French.

• Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical documentation in accordance with professional and organizational standards.

• Collaborate with clients, families, internal teams, and community partners to support coordinated service delivery.

• Participate in case consultations, team meetings, and interdisciplinary discussions as appropriate.

• Contribute to the development of educational resources, tools, and supports for clients and care partners.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with community partners and stakeholders.

• Represent New Brunswick on national working groups, committees, and collaborative initiatives as requested.

• Participate in ongoing professional development and maintain current knowledge of best practices in dementia care and counselling.

• Uphold ethical and professional standards in accordance with applicable regulatory and professional requirements.

• Assist with administrative duties and organizational initiatives as required.

• Travel within New Brunswick as required.

## Qualifications

• Master's degree in counselling, Counselling Psychology, Social Work, or a related field.

• Current professional registration or licensure, or eligibility for registration, in New Brunswick (e.g., Licensed Counselling Therapist or Registered Social Worker).

• Minimum of two years of counselling experience, preferably within community-based, non-profit, mental health, or social service settings.

• Experience providing counselling services in both virtual and in-person environments.

• Training and experience in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and other evidence-informed therapeutic approaches.

• Demonstrated understanding of the impact of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias on individuals, families, and care partners.

• Experience working with older adults, caregivers, and individuals experiencing significant life transitions is considered an asset.

• Knowledge of trauma-informed, strengths-based, and person-centred practices.

• Strong clinical assessment, communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.

• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and manage sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

• Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.

• Experience facilitating groups, workshops, or educational sessions is considered an asset.

• Strong community awareness and the ability to develop collaborative partnerships.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and experience using electronic documentation systems.

• Must carry, or be eligible to obtain, professional liability insurance in accordance with regulatory requirements.

• Bilingualism in English and French is required.

• Possession of a valid New Brunswick driver's licence and access to reliable transportation.

• Ability to travel within the region and work occasional evenings as required.

• The successful candidate must provide and maintain a satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnerable Sector Check as a condition of employment.

## What We Offer

• A supportive, collaborative, and mission-driven team environment where your work makes a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families affected by dementia.

• The opportunity to design and lead an innovative counselling program that will help shape future dementia support services in New Brunswick.

• Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and ongoing development.

• A comprehensive benefits package and a positive, inclusive workplace culture that values compassion, respect, collaboration, and excellence.

The Alzheimer Society is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion, and welcomes applications from all individuals. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.
