title: First Link Clinic Coordinator
description:
## First Link Clinic Coordinator

Location: Saint John NB
Job Type: Full time/On-Site

Our impact is growing, and so is our team! Join us as we expand programs and take our initiatives to the next level.

Behind every person with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, there are hundreds of people dedicated to helping them. The Alzheimer Society is the leading not-for-profit health organization working nationwide to improve the quality of life for Canadians affected by Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and advance the search for a cause and cure. Active in communities right across Canada, the Society has programs and services near you. Since 1987, we've been dedicated to providing help for people with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias and their caregivers. That help comes in many ways.

## Job Summary:

As the primary point of contact for individuals and families seeking support, information, and guidance related to dementia, the First Link Clinic Coordinator plays a vital role in building trusting relationships and providing person-centred support. Working within a healthcare setting, the First Link Clinic Coordinator collaborates with healthcare providers, clinic staff, community organizations, and support services to connect clients with appro-priate resources and ensure they receive timely, compassionate, and coordinated support throughout their de-mentia journey.

This is a full-time, on-site position based within a clinical setting, and candidates must be available to work in person during regular clinic hours.

## Distinguishing Characteristics:

The ideal candidate is compassionate, organized, and skilled in client support, with the ability to navigate sensi-tive conversations and complex situations. This position serves as a key liaison between individuals living with dementia, their care partners, healthcare professionals, and community resources. The successful candidate will be committed to providing exceptional client service while helping individuals and families access the infor-mation, programs, and supports they need to maintain quality of life.

## Typical Duties and Responsibilities:

• Provide person-centred support, education, and navigation services to individuals living with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, as well as their care partners.

• Receive and respond to referrals from healthcare providers and clinic staff in a timely and professional manner.

• Conduct needs assessments to identify client strengths, challenges, and support requirements.

• Connect clients and families with appropriate community resources, support services, educational op-portunities, and dementia-specific programs.

• Maintain ongoing communication and follow-up with clients and families to ensure changing needs are identified and addressed.

• Build and maintain collaborative relationships with physicians, nurse practitioners, allied health profes-sionals, clinic staff, and community partners.

• Maintain accurate, confidential, and up-to-date client records in accordance with privacy legislation and organizational policies.

• Provide information packages, educational resources, and toolkits to clients and families.

• Participate in case consultations, care planning discussions, and interdisciplinary meetings when appro-priate.

• Deliver presentations and educational sessions to healthcare providers, community organizations, and the public as required.

• Support awareness initiatives that promote understanding of dementia and available supports within the community.

• Maintain the CRM database and ensure timely and accurate data entry for reporting purposes.

• Participate in provincial and national initiatives, meetings, and committees as requested.

• Travel within the region as required.

• Perform other duties related to client service delivery and organizational priorities as assigned.

## Qualifications:

• Post-secondary education in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience.

• Experience working in healthcare, community services, social services, client support, administration, or a related environment.

• Experience working within a healthcare or clinical setting is considered an asset.

• Ability to build positive and collaborative relationships with healthcare professionals, clients, families, and community partners.

• Demonstrated understanding of the impact of Alzheimer's disease and other dementias on individuals, families, and care partners.

• Strong interpersonal, communication, and active listening skills, with the ability to navigate sensitive and emotionally challenging conversations.

• Demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

• Strong organizational, time management, problem-solving, and administrative skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.

• Ability to work independently while contributing positively as part of a team.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and experience using databases, client information systems, or CRM platforms.

• Bilingualism (English and French) is considered a strong asset.

• Possession of a valid New Brunswick driver's licence and access to reliable transportation.

• Ability to travel within the region and work occasional evenings or weekends as required.

• The successful candidate must provide and maintain a satisfactory Criminal Record Check and Vulnera-ble Sector Check as a condition of employment.

## What We Offer:

• A supportive, collaborative, and mission-driven team environment where your work makes a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families affected by dementia.

• Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and ongoing development.

• A comprehensive benefits package, including health and dental coverage, paid time off, wellness initiatives, and retirement contributions.

• A positive and inclusive workplace culture grounded in teamwork, respect, compassion, and innovation.

The Alzheimer Society is committed to equity, diversity, and inclusion, and welcomes applications from all individuals. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates.

Annual Salary: $48,000.00 per year

Qualified candidates are invited to submit their resume to:

The Alzheimer Society of New Brunswick
320 rue Maple Street, Suite 100
Fredericton, N-B E3A 3R4

The MCRT is an Emergency Service responding to unknown clients/unpredictable situations in a variety of community settings as determined by need and coordinating when needed with other services such as police/paramedics. description:
Requisition ID: 1982

Location: Vessels

Marine Atlantic is dedicated to creating an environment which promotes employee growth, career development, and job satisfaction. Our employees embody our core values; they are diverse, safety-oriented team-players who exhibit integrity and commitment, and always strive for excellence.

Marine Atlantic is currently seeking motivated and committed Deckhands who are eager to learn and grow within the Marine Industry. Successful applicants will primarily work as a Deckhand and will receive training to become a Quartermaster, allowing them to step into that role once training is complete and operationally required. These positions are permanent, spare and relief positions that are scheduled across our fleet and each tour based on operational requirements.

Marine Atlantic is committed to a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace. Preference may be given to members of the following equity deserving groups: women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities and 2SLGBTQIA+ community members. If you are a member of one or more of these groups, please state to which group(s) you identify in your application.

Quartermaste main function is helmsman duties, entering and departing port and as required at sea. When not performing helmsman duties at sea this position will act as an additional lookout and assist the OOW as required. In port the Quartermaster will act as gangway or bridge watch.

Deckhand duties have several components; including, but not limited to emergency responsibilities, completion of documentation, fire/security patrol, deck patrol, and lookout.

## Additional Key Areas of Responsibility - Quartermaster

• Follow safe work procedures and work within MOHS regulations.

• Actively participate in all emergency and security drills as per the duties assigned in the Muster list.

• Perform/Switch to Emergency Steering and Autopilot.

• Understand the Emergency Steering Procedures, the location

• of the steering repeaters and magnetic compass.

• Follow helm orders as directed by the Master or OOW.

• Ensure all crew and visitors sign the gangway logbook and verify visitors ID as required.

• Verify and collect passenger tickets as required.

• Ensure gangway and walkways are clear of slip, trip and fall hazards.

• May be called out for mooring operations.

• Fire plan locations for shore fire department's while in port.

• Assist in the accomplishment of company objectives by performing other related duties as required.

## Key Areas of Responsibility- Deckhand

• Daily checklists for fall Protection, Forklifts, Man Lifts, Confined Spaces, manual sign-offs of tools, Occupational Safety & Health manual, International Safety Management reviews and Emergency Procedures

• Daily and routine work which includes painting, cleaning, and securing

• Housekeeping as it relates to the vessel's exterior decks and vehicle decks

• Rectification of Inspection iems as directed by the Bosun and/or the Occupational Safety & Health Committee

• Hourly fire and security patrol rounds of the entire vessel above the vehicle decks as per vessel plan

• Continually patrolling the vehicle decks and direct any unauthorized passengers to the passenger areas

• Inspecting lashings and tightening where required at sea and reporting it to the Officer on watch when in port

• Reporting any cargo shifting, fuel leaks, vehicle damages, fire hazards, lighting issues, and slip trip and fall hazards

• Working diligently to promote a safe working environment.

• Assisting in the accomplishment of vessel functions by performing other related duties as required

## What qualifications do I need to be considered for this opportunity?

## Education Certification and Experience

• Bridge Watch Rating Certificate STCW 95 or Able Seafarer Certificate STCW 95

• Valid STCW 6.1 and STCW 6.2 Certificates

• Transport Canada mandated Marine Medical Examination

## Additional Qualifications

• Ability to work in confined spaces

• Strong desire to learn and develop skills as a Quartermaster

## Asset Qualifications

• MED Refresher Certificate

• Passenger Safety Management

• Confined Space Certification

• Marine Basic First Aid

• Previous experience as a helmsman

We thank all applicants for applying, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of the Marine Atlantic team, you will participate in a variety of ongoing training programs and development opportunities to navigate your career and chart your course for success. There is a monthly tour pattern for regularly assigned positions of 15 days on and 15 days off, normally commencing the 1st and 15th of each month. title: Sous Chef
description:
## Sous Chef

## Fredericton, New Brunswick

## Reference #JL-10216

On behalf of our confidential client, Meridia Recruitment Solutions is currently recruiting for an experienced Sous Chef to join a well-established hospitality operation in Fredericton, New Brunswick.

Reporting to the Executive Chef and working closely with Kitchen Leadership, the Sous Chef will play a key role in the day-to-day success of a high-volume restaurant operation. This position offers an opportunity to mentor and develop junior kitchen staff, support culinary execution, and contribute to the continued growth of a respected food service operation. For an ambitious culinary professional, this role also presents the opportunity to grow into increasingly senior leadership responsibilities over time.

Operating year-round, our client has built a strong reputation within the market and continues to invest in its people, facilities, and guest experience. The successful candidate will join a collaborative team environment focused on quality, consistency, and continuous improvement.

## Responsibilities:

• Assist in overseeing daily kitchen operations and service execution.

• Lead, coach, and mentor line cooks and junior kitchen staff.

• Ensure food quality, consistency, presentation, and portion control standards are maintained.

• Support food preparation, cooking, and service during peak operating periods.

• Coordinate kitchen workflow and assist in directing service flow.

• Foster a positive, respectful workplace culture built on teamwork and communication.

• Ensure compliance with food safety, sanitation, and workplace health and safety standards.

• Train team members on recipes, preparation techniques, and operational standards.

• Maintain inventory controls, food storage standards, and product rotation procedures.

• Assist with kitchen administration functions including ordering, inventory management, scheduling, and cost control as responsibilities evolve.

• Support opening and closing procedures and ensure proper kitchen organization and cleanliness.

• Collaborate effectively with front-of-house leadership to deliver an exceptional guest experience.

• Participate in menu development initiatives and continuous operational improvements.

## Competencies:

• Calm and composed under pressure.

• Strong culinary fundamentals and technical cooking abilities.

• Effective communicator and relationship builder.

• Positive and supportive leadership style.

• Team-oriented with a willingness to coach and develop others.

• Highly organized with strong attention to detail.

• Adaptable and solutions-focused.

• Committed to quality, consistency, and guest satisfaction.

## Characteristics:

title: Director of Recreation and Tourism
description:
Position Title: Director of Recreation and Tourism

Competition Number: 2026-48

Employee Group: Non Union/Management

Salary: $110,822.31 - $147,763.08

Closing Date: This position will remain open until it is filled.

The City of Corner Brook is presently accepting applications for the position of Director of Recreation and Tourism. This senior leadership position is responsible for the strategic planning, development, administration, and continuous improvement of the City's recreation, tourism, cultural, and community programming services. The Director provides organizational leadership for municipal recreation facilities, tourism development initiatives, special events, community programming, parks and recreational assets, the Corner Brook Civic Centre, and the Marina Redmond Centre.

As a member of the City's senior management team, the Director contributes to corporate planning, policy development, budget preparation, long-term capital planning, and community development initiatives. The Director provides professional advice and recommendations to the City Manager and Council and works collaboratively with community organizations, tourism stakeholders, provincial agencies, user groups, staff, and residents to support quality of life, economic development opportunities, and positive recreational and community experiences.

The Director will provide strategic direction and operational oversight for recreation programs, facilities, parks, tourism initiatives, community programming, festivals, celebrations, and major municipal events. The successful candidate will foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement while ensuring exceptional customer service, financial stewardship, effective risk management, and employee engagement. The Director will also oversee departmental operating and capital budgets, identify opportunities for operational efficiencies and revenue generation, and support long-term capital and asset management planning.

The Director will lead, mentor, and develop department managers, supervisors, and staff while supporting recruitment, workforce planning, training, performance management, succession planning, and labour relations matters involving unionized and non-union employees. The Director will establish and maintain productive relationships with community organizations, user groups, tourism operators, government agencies, educational institutions, and private-sector partners and will represent the City on boards, committees, conferences, and regional initiatives. The position will also oversee recreation and tourism-related capital projects and ensure facilities, programs, events, and operations comply with applicable legislation, municipal policies, occupational health and safety requirements, and industry standards.

The City of Corner Brook is looking for an individual with a university degree in Recreation Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, Tourism Management, Community Development, Recreation Leadership, or a related discipline. A Master's degree would be considered an asset. The successful candidate will have a minimum of seven to ten years of progressively responsible management experience in recreation, tourism, community services, facility operations, or municipal administration, including at least five years of senior leadership experience with direct supervisory responsibilities. Experience overseeing large public facilities, events, tourism initiatives, and municipal programs is required. Municipal government experience is strongly preferred, while experience working in a unionized environment would be considered an asset.

The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, strategic planning, organizational, project management, communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills. A sound understanding of municipal governance, public-sector administration, recreation service delivery, tourism development, budget management, financial analysis, capital planning, and asset management is required. The ability to build productive partnerships, manage complex projects and competing priorities, and provide effective solutions to challenging issues will be essential.

The position generally follows a standard administrative work schedule; however, frequent evening and weekend attendance will be required for Council meetings, community events, facility activities, tourism initiatives, and emergencies. Attendance at conferences, trade shows, tourism events, and regional meetings will also be required, with occasional travel throughout the region, province, and other destinations. A valid Class 5 Newfoundland and Labrador driver's licence is required.

The City of Corner Brook will provide support throughout the recruitment process to applicants with disabilities, including accommodation that considers an applicant's accessibility needs. Candidates are encouraged to discuss specific needs with the City's Human Resources division,

Please submit résumés giving complete details of qualifications to the Human Resources Office

The City of Corner Brook thanks all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Service Writer
description:
Fort Equipment is a locally owned and operated Kubota dealership that has served the Amherst area for over 45 years. We're proud of the team we've built-many of our employees have been with us for years, reflecting our commitment to a respectful, supportive, and stable workplace. We provide opportunities to learn and grow, encourage teamwork, and strive to create an environment where employees can build rewarding long-term careers while helping our customers succeed.

We're seeking a Service Writer to join our team and help ensure our Service and Rental Departments continue delivering excellent customer support.

Position Title: Service Writer

Reports To: Service Manager

## Job Summary

The Service Writer (SW) is responsible for providing an exceptional customer experience while supporting the efficient and profitable operation of the dealership's Service Department. Acting as the primary point of contact between customers and the service team, the SW identifies and documents customer service and repair needs, prepares accurate work orders, coordinates with technicians, and keeps customers informed throughout the repair process.

The role ensures that service work is properly scheduled, prioritized, documented, and completed in a timely manner while maintaining high standards of quality and customer satisfaction. The SW also supports the growth of the Service Department by identifying appropriate maintenance and repair opportunities, providing clear estimates, following up with customers, and building long-term relationships based on trust, reliability, and professional service.

## Responsibilities

• Act as the first point of contact for customers with service or rental inquiries, providing professional, friendly, and timely assistance. Gather relevant information, understand customer needs, answer questions, and ensure requests are directed and handled appropriately.

• Assist in the daily coordination of the Service Department to support an organized and efficient workflow. Help prioritize incoming service requests, monitor jobs in progress, coordinate required parts or information, and assist in ensuring customer commitments and service timelines are met.

• Help manage technician schedules and work assignments by coordinating jobs based on technician availability, skill requirements, job priority, and expected completion dates. Monitor workflow throughout the day and communicate changes or priorities as required.

• Prepare and maintain accurate work orders for customer, internal, and warranty jobs, ensuring all required information is clearly documented, including customer concerns, equipment information, requested repairs, technician notes, parts, labour, and other relevant details. Ensure work orders are complete and accurate before closing or submitting for warranty processing.

• Maintain clear and consistent communication with Service Technicians regarding work assignments, customer concerns, repair requirements, priorities, timelines, and changes to the scope of work. Follow up on job progress and help resolve questions or issues that could delay completion.

• Keep customers informed throughout the service process, including providing updates on repair status, estimated costs, additional recommended work, delays, and anticipated completion times. Obtain customer authorization when additional repairs or costs are identified.

• Support a positive customer experience from initial contact through completion, ensuring customers understand the work performed, addressing questions or concerns, and helping build long-term customer relationships through responsive and dependable service.

## Qualifications

Education

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Post-secondary education in business administration, automotive or equipment service, mechanical trades, or a related field is considered an asset.

• Relevant industry experience, training, or a combination of education and practical experience will be considered.

• Manufacturer, dealership, warranty, or equipment-specific training is considered an asset.

Experience

• Previous experience in a service writer, service advisor, customer service, parts, rental, or equipment dealership environment is considered an asset.

• Any other related experience.

• Mechanical aptitude and general knowledge of agricultural, construction, or power equipment.

Skills/Competencies

• Strong customer service and interpersonal skills with the ability to build positive, professional relationships with customers.

• Mechanical aptitude and general knowledge of agricultural, construction, or power equipment is considered an asset; willingness and ability to learn Kubota equipment and products is essential.

• Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple service jobs, priorities, and deadlines.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with customers, technicians, parts personnel, and management.

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy when preparing work orders, documenting repairs, processing warranty information, and maintaining service records.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced service environment and adjust priorities as customer needs and operational demands change.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify issues, gather information, and work collaboratively toward practical solutions.

• Comfortable using computers, dealership management systems, email, and other service-related software.

• Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a team-oriented environment.

• Professional, dependable, and customer-focused with a strong sense of accountability and follow-through.

• Valid driver's licence required.

## Behaviors

• Service Excellence - must be the best at what they do and go the extra mile, needs to be flexible, customer focused, feel the need to constantly improve, provide top quality work.

• Accountability - ability to keep their word, deliver results, be committed to their responsibilities, have strong willpower and act as if the company is their own.

• Teamwork - must have team spirit and be able to work within a team and empower one another.

• Honesty - must be an open communicator, sincere, trustworthy and transparent. Always ethical and behave and act in the best interest of the company and team members.

• Diversity - Respectful and open to different cultures and opinions, have an eye for all stakeholders. "Think Global, Act Local".

## Special Requirements/Training

• A valid NB/NS Driver's License.

## Working Conditions

• Most job duties will be in an office, service desk, and garage environment.

• Monday to Friday work week, day-time hours, 40 hours a week.

## Physical Requirements

• Sitting and standing in an office, counter environment.

• Occasional and light duty lifting may be required.

title: Chief Officer
description:

Location: Vessels

Application Closing Date: Until Filled

Marine Atlantic is dedicated to creating an environment which promotes employee growth, career development, and job satisfaction. Our employees embody our core values; they are diverse, safety-oriented team-players who exhibit integrity and commitment, and always strive for excellence.

Marine Atlantic is currently looking for a Chief Officer to work onboard our vessels that operate from the ports of Port aux Basques NL and North Sydney NS year round; and Argentia NL during the summer season. These positions are permanent full-time spare and relief positions that are scheduled across our fleet and each tour based on operational requirements. Eligible candidates may qualify for a signing incentive, subject to a return of service in the position for a specified period.

Marine Atlantic is committed to a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace. Preference may be given to members of the following equity deserving groups: women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities and 2SLGBTQIA+ community members. If you are a member of one or more of these groups, please state to which group(s) you identify in your application.

Reporting directly to the Master, the Chief Officer is the head of Deck Department and must ensure all functions are performed efficiently by the Deck Department's employees, making this acritical role in leading, managing, and developing their team, ensuring quality results and the safety of all vessel staff and passengers.

## Key Areas of Responsibility

• Plan, direct and monitor the loading and unloading of the vessel as well as the stowage, segregation and securing of dangerous goods.

• Perform routine and preventative deck maintenance inspections; maintain life-saving and fire-fighting equipment; ensure an adequate supply of fresh water is maintained; arrange deck watches and notify the Purser of crew changes.

• Maintain up-to-date Deck Department files and records and attend and actively participate in Ship Safety Meetings as the Ship Safety Officer.

• Incident control and emergency response.

• Application of hazard assessment and job safety analysis.

• Conduct risk assessment, incident investigation, and root cause determination.

• Promote a positive customer experience.

• Have full knowledge of the SOLAS Training Manual under the SMS

• Understand the Safety Management System (SMS) under ISM

• Be aware of all aspects of the ship's operation, so that they are able, if required, to assume command immediately

• Ensure workers under their supervision have proper training and understand their responsibilities under the CLC Part II

• Supervise cargo operations and have full understanding of Dangerous Goods and associated hazards

• Have full familiarity with the International Collision Regulations

• Have full familiarity of the fire control panel, hull opening & water-tight door panel and other indicator panels

• Understand and maintain ship security plan, perform drills, and maintain all ship security equipment.

## What qualifications do I need to be considered for this opportunity?

## Education Certification and Experience

• Valid Master, Near Coastal STCW 2010 Certificate of Competency

• Minimum 5 years of experience as a Deck Officer, 2 of which need to be as a Chief Officer of a large vessel

• Radio Operator Certificate (GMDSS)

## Additional Qualifications

• Knowledge and experience working with vessels certified under the International Safety Management Code

• Valid Transport Canada Marine Medical

• Demonstrated Leadership Abilities

## Assets Qualifications

• Graduate from a recognized marine school program

• MED Refresher

• Previous experience working on large passenger ferries

• Passenger Safety Management or Specialized Passenger Safety Management

• Knowledge of the Canadian Regulations including the Canada Labour Code Part II and MOHS Regulations

We thank all applicants for applying, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

## Why work for the Marine Atlantic team?

As part of the Marine Atlantic team, you will participate in a variety of ongoing training programs and development opportunities to navigate your career and chart your course for success. We provide a positive and inclusive work culture that is dedicated to creating an environment which promotes employee growth, career development, and job satisfaction. Some benefits of working with Marine Atlantic include competitive salaries, defined benefit pension plan, comprehensive health benefit packages, and professional development opportunities. Come experience the pride of working with an organization with newly constructed and revitalized infrastructure that has positioned itself for the future.

## Marine Atlantic's Tour Pattern

There is a monthly tour pattern for regularly assigned positions of 15 days on and 15 days off, normally commencing the 1st and 15th of each month. As a new spare and relief employee, you will be called for work in accordance with operational requirements; therefore, you may be required to work in intervals throughout both tours (i.e. one month) in order to obtain 15 days of work. Please note, you may be called to work fewer than or in excess of 15 days per month should it be operationally required.

## Safety Sensitive Position

This position is designated as a safety sensitive position and is subject to the provisions of Marine Atlantic's Drug and Alcohol Policy which includes, but not limited to pre-employment testing. We have a zero-tolerance policy for alcohol, cannabis, and illicit drugs.

## Additional Information

Marine Atlantic is a Federal Crown Corporation that provides a vital ferry service link between Newfoundland and Labrador and mainland Canada.

At Marine Atlantic, we are dedicated to building and fostering an inclusive and diverse environment, where all employees and customers feel welcomed, valued, and respected.
Marine Atlantic invites applications from all qualified candidates and hires based on merit. We are committed to the principles of equitable employment for all and strongly encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, visible minorities and 2SLGBTQIA+ community members. If you are a member of one or more of these groups, please state to which group(s) you identify in your cover letter, resume or application.
To receive this job poster in an alternative format or to discuss alternate ways of completing the online application, please contact the Marine Atlantic Human Resources Department, in confidence, at careers-carrieres@ma.ca.
We are committed to providing an inclusive and barrier-free work environment, starting with the recruitment process. If you need to be accommodated during any phase of the evaluation process, contact the Marine Atlantic Human Resources Department, in confidence, at careers-carrieres@ma.ca.

Marine Atlantic respectfully acknowledges that we operate in Mi'kma'ki, the ancestral and unceded territory of the Mi'kmaq peoples, and on the island of Ktaqmkuk, the unceded traditional territory of the Beothuk and Mi'kmaq peoples. We also acknowledge Labrador as the traditional ancestral homelands of the Innu of Nitassinan, the Inuit of Nunatsiavut, and the Inuit of NunatuKavut.

title: Research & Data Specialist
employer: Envision Saint John: The Regional Growth Agency
description:
## Research & Data Specialist

Envision Saint John is the Saint John Region's lead economic development and visitor attraction agency, tasked with sustainably growing our economy and population. We are governed by an independent Board of Directors and actively supported by the municipalities that are our key funding partners - Saint John, Quispamsis, Rothesay, Grand Bay-Westfield, Hampton, Fundy-St. Martins, and the Fundy Rural District.

Envision Saint John is a convener, bringing together diverse stakeholders to develop a shared economic vision. We function as an economic intelligence hub, gathering and interpreting economic data that informs strategic decision-making. We work as an innovation accelerator, creating platforms and support mechanisms that help businesses and entrepreneurs start up and scale up. We are storytellers, crafting compelling narratives that attract visitors and new residents and reveal the region's economic potential to local, provincial, national, and international audiences.

## The Opportunity

As Research & Data Specialist, you will report to the Director of Data Services & Project Management and serve as Envision Saint John's internal resource for regional economic, tourism, and organizational performance information by sourcing, organizing, interpreting, and communicating reliable data and research. Working across the agency, you will monitor emerging trends, ask thoughtful questions, and support colleagues in understanding the implications of new information. You will lead research initiatives that support the four pillars of the Agency's strategic plan: Growth Readiness; Talent Attraction and Retention; Business Attraction, Retention and Expansion; and Visitor Attraction.

## What you will do:

• Monitor economic, demographic, tourism, and organizational performance indicators, identify emerging trends, and support the development of evidence-based narratives and public reporting.

• Support and advise research design, data limitations, methodological considerations, and interpretation of statistical information for research initiatives across disciplines such as real estate, industrial development, population growth, workforce development, business growth, and tourism.

• Implement Envision Saint John's internal measurement framework.

• Oversee Envision Saint John's CRM, including reporting optimization and providing guidance on CRM processes and data standards.

• Develop efficient processes and automation opportunities to improve data collection, preparation, reporting, and dashboard maintenance.

• Support the production of the annual State of the Economy report and quarterly insights.

• Respond to ad hoc information requests from internal staff and external partners.

• Leverage data visualization techniques and effectively communicate quality data internally and externally.

• Other administrative and research supports as assigned.

## Your qualifications:

• 3-5 years of experience in research, economic development, or a related field.

• Post-secondary degree in a related discipline.

• Demonstrated ability to synthesize information from multiple sources, identify trends and anomalies, and communicate findings to diverse audiences.

• Demonstrated experience working with Statistics Canada datasets and products.

• Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the use of pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and advanced formulas for data cleaning, transformation, analysis and reporting.

• Experience with data visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau or similar.

• Experience with Customer Relationship Management systems or similar to support business processes and performance measurement.

• Demonstrated ability to manage recurring deadlines, respond to changing information needs, and prioritize competing requests.

• Experience with SQL, Python, GIS, or other analytics tools is considered an asset.

## Why Envision Saint John?

• A Culture of Inclusivity: We embrace and celebrate individual differences, creating an inclusive environment where every team member's voice is valued. We believe in harnessing the collective power of diverse perspectives to drive creativity and excellence in everything we do.

• Empowerment and Autonomy: We trust our employees to make informed decisions and take ownership of their work. Empowerment and autonomy are the pillars of our work culture, allowing you to unleash your full potential and bring your best ideas to life.

• Collaboration at Its Best: You'll be part of a collaborative ecosystem that encourages open communication and cross-functional collaboration. Together, we create a supportive network that helps each other succeed.

• Work-Life Balance: We understand the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Our flexible work arrangements and generous time-off policies enable you to achieve harmony between your personal and professional life.

• A Welcoming Workspace: Our modern, state-of-the-art office is designed to inspire creativity and productivity. Comfortable breakout areas, well-equipped facilities, and a fun-filled ambiance make it a second home for our employees. Our office is centrally located in beautiful uptown Saint John, New Brunswick, with sweeping views of the region.

## Benefits:

• Annual Salary: $69,788 - $73,643

• Health and wellness programs

• Regular team-building activities and social events

• Opportunities for professional development

title: Director of Quality Assurance
description:
Cooke is a global seafood company with operations in North America, Europe, South America and Australia. Our company's success is driven by our dynamic, highly skilled, and innovative management team, supported by dedicated employees who live in coastal communities and contribute to the local area's economy and sense of community.

True North Salmon Partnership Ltd., a division of Cooke Aquaculture Inc., a dynamic and growing east coast family company, with Platinum Member status in the Canada's Best Managed Companies Program, is seeking a results orientated individual to join our Company as Director of Quality Assurance.

## The Role

This role leads the strategic implementation and oversight of corporate quality and traceability programs, with a strong focus on compliance, process control, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration. The position ensures adherence to food safety standards (including HACCP), manages product specifications and certifications, supports new product development, and oversees quality assurance across multiple operations in Eastern Canada and Maine.

## Essential Functions:

## Quality Program Leadership

• Lead the implementation and oversight of the corporate Quality Management and Traceability Programs, including HACCP and related food safety systems.

• Act as the primary quality control resource for issue identification, resolution, loss reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Oversee allergen management programs and ensure that labeling and packaging meet regulatory compliance for all destination markets.

• Design, implement, and maintain procedures for process control, process improvement, testing, and inspection.

• Conduct root cause analyses and implement corrective actions and continuous improvement strategies.

## Laboratory Oversight and Testing

• Oversee in-house laboratory operations for product testing and sample analysis.

• Manage relationships and quality standards with third-party laboratories.

• Ensure timely and accurate testing to support product quality, compliance, and safety.

## Systems and Data Management

• Manage the product specification system and lead the implementation of a new system (Trace Grain).

• Oversee and maintain the corporate Quality Assurance software, ensuring it supports compliance, reporting, and continuous improvement efforts.

• Establish, track, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure the effectiveness of quality systems (e.g., process capability, control charts, measurement quality).

• Report quality issues, trends, and losses to senior management.

## Regulatory Compliance and Agency Interaction

• Serve as the primary point of contact for regulatory bodies including CFIA (Canadian Food Inspection Agency), FDA (U.S. Food and Drug Administration), and other relevant agencies.

• Ensure all products and processes comply with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards.

• Support third-party and customer certification programs, including audit preparation and follow-up.

• Import/export regulatory compliance (certificates, licenses, etc.)

## Cross-functional and Regional Collaboration

• Coordinate cross-functional quality initiatives across diverse East Coast operations, including facilities in Eastern Canada and Maine.

• Provide quality assurance support to other Cooke operations as required.

• Support the corporate New Product Development (NPD) team to ensure quality is integrated from concept to commercialization.

## Leadership and Resource Management

• Oversee performance evaluation systems for the Quality Assurance team, fostering a culture of accountability and development.

• Develop and manage the corporate Quality Assurance budget, ensuring it includes measurable targets and aligns with corporate goals.

• Develop and maintain internal process certification standards and support company-wide audit and certification activities.

## Technical and Industry-Specific Skills

• In-depth knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS) including HACCP, GMP, and traceability systems.

• Strong understanding of food safety regulations and standards (CFIA, FDA, GFSI schemes like SQF or BRC, etc.).

• Experience with lab operations, including oversight of both in-house and third-party laboratory testing protocols.

• Familiarity with product specification systems, especially the implementation and management of platforms like Trace Grain.

• Ability to interpret and apply regulatory requirements in labeling, allergen management, and product claims.

• Knowledge of process control tools such as SPC (Statistical Process Control), control charts, and root cause analysis methods (e.g., Fishbone, 5 Whys, FMEA).

• Audit readiness and certification management, including experience with internal and external audits.

## Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills

• Strong analytical skills to interpret lab results, trend data, and KPIs to identify quality issues and opportunities.

• Process improvement expertise, including Lean or Six Sigma methodologies (certification a plus).

• Critical thinking and decision-making in high-stakes or time-sensitive quality issues.

## Leadership and Management Skills

• Proven leadership experience, ideally managing multi-site QA/QC teams.

• Budgeting and resource planning abilities.

• Experience leading cross-functional teams, particularly across geographically distributed sites.

• Ability to manage performance evaluations, training, and development of quality team staff.

## Communication and Interpersonal Skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills for reporting, policy writing, and audit documentation.

• Strong interpersonal skills to work with internal teams (NPD, Operations, Supply Chain) and external stakeholders (labs, regulators, certifiers).

• Comfortable dealing with government agencies and acting as the face of the organization in regulatory matters.

## Technology and Software Skills

• Proficiency in quality management software, ERP systems, and data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Power BI, or similar).

• Experience with product specification software (such as Trace Grain or similar platforms).

• Competency in digital document control systems for SOPs, quality manuals, audit trails, and test records.

## Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Quality Assurance, or a related field (Master's preferred for senior-level roles).

• Professional certifications (e.g., HACCP, PCQI, SQF Practitioner, ASQ Certified Quality Auditor/Manager).

• 7+ years of progressive experience in food quality assurance, with at least 3 years in a leadership or multi-site role.

Join our team and enjoy the benefits of full-time year-round employment with competitive rates and a comprehensive benefits package tailored to support your well-being and career growth.

## Benefits Package:

• Health Benefits: Includes coverage for dental, vision, and extended medical care.

• Insurance: Life and disability insurance provided for financial security.

• Support Services: Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

• Financial Planning: Opportunity for RRSP matching to support your retirement savings.

• Time Off: Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave for work-life balance.

• Wellness: Wellness programs and access to on-site gym facilities (available in some locations).

• Career Development: Professional growth opportunities and avenues for advancement.

• Perks: Employee discounts on company products or services.

• Convenience: On-site parking or parking allowance.

If you're looking to join a supportive team environment with opportunities for personal and professional development, apply now and become part of our dynamic team.

## The Why

Why Cooke? Simple - because we are a company that rewards initiative, resourcefulness, and work ethic. We will champion your growth and provide you with the platform to create your path, your career, and your future.

NOTE: The recruiter is reviewing and interviewing eligible applicants for this position as they are received. If you are interested in this posting, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

Working within established procedures, this role performs high-volume data entry, batch processing, deposit preparation, and record maintenance within CRC systems (e.g., donor management platforms).

## In this role, you will :

• Support the accurate and timely processing of donations and donor information within CRC systems, ensuring data integrity and adherence to established procedures

• Prepare and reconcile donation batches and bank deposits, validating completeness and accuracy of supporting documentation

• Maintain and update donor records and data files, including supporting large-volume data uploads and data quality checks

• Provide general clerical and administrative support to the finance and philanthropy teams, including reporting and responding to routine inquiries

• Identify and flag discrepancies, ensuring issues are resolved or escalated as appropriate

• Contribute to continuous improvement of processes and documentation to enhance efficiency and accuracy

• Collaborate with team members to support consistent, high-quality service delivery

• Adhere to CRC policies, procedures, and data handling and compliance requirements

• Support broader organizational priorities, including emergency response activities, as required

## What We Are Looking For:

• 1-2 years of experience in a data processing, clerical, or finance support role

• Post-secondary diploma/certificate (1-2 years) or equivalent experience

• Strong data entry skills with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail

• Basic understanding of financial processes and data accuracy controls

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially Excel)

• Ability to follow standardized procedures and resolve routine issues

• Strong organizational and time management skills in a high-volume environment

• Clear communication skills and a collaborative, service-oriented approach

• French proficiency will be seen as an asset

## Working Conditions:

• Work is performed in a clean, office-based environment in Saint John, NB

• Role requires sustained concentration, attention to detail, and meeting time-sensitive deadlines

If there are no Advanced Care Paramedic applicants, we will consider applications from Primary Care Paramedics (PCP) and Ambulance Operators/Attendants (also known as Emergency Medical Responder (EMR)). We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

title: Nurse Practitioner - Primary Care
description:
## Nurse Practitioner - 2 positions

Salary: Starting at $150,000 annually + $20,000 Sign-On Bonus (with 2-year commitment)
Start date will be determined in collaboration with the successful candidate.
Location: Dieppe, New Brunswick (On-site / No weekends)
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Help Shape the Future of Primary Care
At Clinique Médicale Accès, we believe the future of primary care is not about asking healthcare professionals to work harder-it is about building smarter systems that allow every member of the team to practise at the highest level of their training. Our collaborative physician-nurse model has demonstrated that innovation, prevention, and efficient team-based care can dramatically increase access to primary care while preserving the quality of the patient experience. We continue to invest in new ways of delivering care, empowering healthcare professionals, and improving the lives of our patients.

As our clinic continues to grow, we are excited to welcome two bilingual Nurse Practitioners (NP) to join our team with the committed to support both experienced NP's and new graduates through a structured onboarding process that allows time for learning, mentorship, and professional development. We intentionally hope to recruit two Nurse Practitioners together, believing that beginning this journey alongside another NP creates opportunities for collaboration, mentorship, professional support, and long-term job satisfaction. If you are passionate about preventive medicine, collaborative practice, and helping redefine how primary care is delivered, we would love to meet you.

The Opportunity
These positions offer the opportunity to develop a rewarding practice focused primarily on preventive medicine while working alongside an experienced collaborative care team. Your practice will primarily focus on:

• Well-baby care

• Preventive health assessments

• Cancer screening appointments

• Adult preventive care

• Immunizations and vaccination programs

• Health promotion and patient education

You will also collaborate with physicians and nurses in providing comprehensive primary care while practising to the full scope of your Nurse Practitioner licence. One of the unique aspects of our clinic is our commitment to supporting the professional interests of our providers. As our organization continues to grow, there will be opportunities to further develop areas of practice aligned with your expertise and career goals.

## Key Responsibilities

• Perform comprehensive health assessments

• Diagnose and manage acute and chronic medical conditions

• Prescribe medications and therapies within scope of practice

• Order and interpret laboratory investigations and diagnostic imaging

• Provide preventive health screening and counselling

• Provide well-baby care and routine childhood follow-ups for children from 2 weeks to 5 years of age. Approximately two days per week are dedicated to these appointments.

• Administer and oversee vaccination programs

• Educate patients regarding disease prevention and healthy lifestyles

• Maintain accurate EMR documentation

• Review laboratory results, diagnostic reports, electronic consultations and incoming correspondence

• Collaborate closely with physicians, nurses and administrative staff

• Maintain current evidence-based practice standards

Qualifications
Applicants must:

• Hold a Bachelor's Degree in Nursing

• Hold a Master's Degree in Nursing (Nurse Practitioner)

• Have successfully completed the Canadian Nurse Practitioner Examination (CNPE)

• Be registered and in good standing with the Nurses Association of New Brunswick (NANB)

• Be fluent in both English and French

What Makes Our Clinic Different
Our clinic was intentionally designed to maximize provider satisfaction while improving patient access.

We believe healthcare professionals should spend their time caring for patients-not navigating unnecessary administrative burden.

Our collaborative workflows, highly trained nursing team and efficient clinical processes allow providers to focus on what matters most: delivering exceptional patient care.

Schedule
Hours may be negotiated based on the successful candidate's preferences. Our physicians and nursing team currently work Monday through Thursday and benefit from paid Fridays off through our efficiency-based compensation model.

• No evenings

• No weekends

• No statutory holidays

• No after-hours coverage

What We Offer
Joining Clinique Médicale Accès means becoming part of a supportive, innovative team committed to both professional excellence and work-life balance.

## Compensation

• We offer a competitive compensation package starting at $150 000 annually.

• $20,000 sign-on bonus for a two-year commitment.

• In addition to the annual salary, successful candidates will participate in our efficiency-based bonus program, recognizing providers who contribute to improving patient access while maintaining excellence in care.

## Benefits include:

• Medical insurance

• Two weeks of paid vacation

• Clinic closed for two weeks over Christmas

• Clinic closed for two weeks during March Break

• Flexible summer schedule (employees may choose to work or access Employment Insurance, where applicable)

• Additional unpaid leave may be negotiated

• Collaborative multidisciplinary team

• No overhead or administrative costs

• Free on-site parking

• Efficiency-based bonus structure

Your Professional Success Matters to Us
At Clinique Médicale Accès, we recognize that clinical confidence is built through experience. We are committed to supporting both experienced Nurse Practitioners and new graduates as they grow in their roles. To ensure a successful start, patient volumes and roster sizes will be adjusted to provide the time and flexibility needed to develop clinical workflows, build confidence, and establish a strong foundation for practice.

As our clinic continues to grow, we are committed to continually optimizing our collaborative care model. To help Nurse Practitioners maximize both job satisfaction and eligibility for our efficiency-based bonus program, we are open to discussing dedicated Registered Nurse support. By allowing Registered Nurses to perform appropriate clinical tasks within their scope of practice, Nurse Practitioners can focus more of their time on clinical decision-making and delivering high-quality patient care. We believe every healthcare professional should be empowered to practise at the highest level of their training.

title: Chair, Board of Directors
employer: Workers’ Compensation Board of Nova Scotia
description:
## Chair, Board of Directors

The Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia (WCB Nova Scotia) is seeking its next Chair of the Board of Directors to provide strong governance and stewardship as the organization completes its transformational Protect More Strategic Plan 2024-2030.

WCB is the province's provider of workplace injury insurance. It works to prevent workplace injury, but when injury occurs, WCB supports safe and timely return to work. When that is not possible, WCB protects Nova Scotia's workers and families from the long-term impact of injury and tragedy.

The next Chair will join WCB at the midpoint of its strategic journey, as WCB continues to improve how it protects the workforce our province is counting on. Under Protect More, WCB has made significant progress. The workplace injury rate is the lowest it has ever been, return-to-work outcomes are improving, and WCB is in its strongest financial position ever. In 2027, employers will see the first rate reduction in a generation and workers will see benefit increases.

The guidance of the Board of Directors is key to continued success. With equal employer and worker representation, together with the Chair and Deputy Chair, the Board sets the vision and policy direction of the workers' compensation system and oversees the organization and its Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

The Chair leads the Board in fulfilling its governance responsibilities and ensures the organization remains accountable for its results. They foster collaboration among Board members and facilitate thoughtful, informed discussions, drawing out different perspectives and helping the Board navigate complex issues and reach collective decisions. Central to the role is a strong partnership with the CEO, grounded in trust, clarity of roles, and the appropriate distinction between governance and operations. The Chair also serves as an important link between WCB, government and key stakeholders.

The successful candidate will bring significant senior leadership and governance experience, with demonstrated experience contributing effectively at the Board level. Experience within a complex, regulated, public-interest and/or multi-stakeholder environment is important, together with strong strategic judgement and an understanding of organizational performance, financial stewardship, risk and reputation. The successful candidate will have the credibility to work effectively with a CEO, Board members, government and diverse stakeholders, and the ability to lead deliberations and build consensus across differing perspectives. Governance education or a designation such as ICD.D is considered an asset, as is knowledge of workers' compensation, occupational health and safety, insurance or other legislated systems.

The Chair is appointed by the Governor in Council for a five-year term and may be reappointed for a second term.

To learn more about WCB, please visit: https://www.wcb.ns.ca

Please submit a combined resume and cover letter online by clicking "Apply." For further information about this opportunity, please contact Amy Reid, areid@royerthompson.com or Kathleen Soder, ksoder@royerthompson.com in confidence.

WCB Nova Scotia is an equal opportunity organization, committed to an inclusive workplace culture and an accessible environment where diversity thrives. We welcome interest from individuals with diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences. This commitment extends to an inclusive, accessible and accommodating recruitment process. Accommodation is available throughout the recruitment and selection process and will be provided confidentially upon request.

Royer Thompson is a Canadian executive advisory firm focused on capturing the full potential of people in pursuit of leadership and organizational excellence. Our core services include executive search, management recruitment, executive development, HR advisory and inclusion & belonging.

CMN's Department of Social Enterprise and Economic Development (SEED) is currently looking for a motivated and knowledgeable candidate to fill the role of Manager, Stewardship Services and Project Delivery.

Under the direction of the Director of Social Enterprise and Economic Development and reporting to the Associate Director, the Manager, Stewardship Services and Project Delivery, will support the planning, coordination, and implementation of business development initiatives within the department.

The Manager, Stewardship Services and Project Delivery is responsible for the successful delivery of CMN Indigenous Stewardship Services following contract execution. The role serves as the primary owner of project delivery, client success, relationship management, quality assurance, subcontractor coordination, and continuous product improvement.

## Overview of Responsibilities:

• Lead projects from contract execution through final delivery and close-out.

• Manage schedules, budgets, milestones, risks, deliverables and resources.

• Act as primary client contact after contract award.

• Implement quality assurance processes and peer reviews.

• Budgeting, forecasting and operational planning.

• Ability to lead through influence rather than direct authority.

• Travel throughout Nova Scotia and to CMN member communities is required. Occasional travel outside Nova Scotia may be required.

• A valid driver's license and access to reliable transportation are required.

We prioritize candidates based on their qualifications in the following order: Advanced Care Paramedic, Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant.

If the competition is awarded to a PCP or EMR as the next highest classification, they will be temporarily awarded the position for the same number of hours indicated above and recruitment will continue for the higher classification.

## Job Summary:

The Advanced Care Paramedic (or Primary Care Paramedic, or Ambulance Operator/Attendant), works as an integral part of the paramedicine program. The successful applicant will work within their scope of practice, including responding to emergency and routine calls, providing skilled basic and advanced emergency care or assistance to people suffering from a variety of injuries or illnesses. The successful applicant is responsible for maintaining professional and organizational standards of practice.

The successful applicant must demonstrate an awareness of and be responsible for promoting and supporting person-and family-centered care, demonstrate a commitment to safety and partner with all team members to improve worker and patient safety by integrating safety into work practices, identifying risks and implementing improvements. The successful applicant may be required to provide preceptorship and mentorship to students and new employees during clinical placements and orientation periods.

The successful applicant will report directly to the Manager of District Operations of Paramedicine.

## Duties/Job Demands:

The Advanced Care Paramedic performs independent advanced medical care and intervention to patients at pre-hospital scene settings. This includes operating ambulances in responding to emergencies and routine calls; conducting physical examinations; performing comprehensive assessments and tests; interpreting a variety of tests and procedures; initiating a variety of advanced interventions; and performing other related duties as required. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The ACP functions as a leader and mentor within the paramedicine program.

The Primary Care Paramedic works as an active member of the health care team providing pre-hospital assessment and medical care to people with acute illnesses or injuries while maintaining a high standard of care to the patients. Work is performed with considerable independence and is reviewed through observation, examination of records and reports, and the presence or absence of valid complaints. The Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) functions as part of an interdisciplinary team within healthcare facility units and ensures client and staff safety, and other related duties as required.

The Ambulance Operator/Attendant (EMR) will be responsible for skilled work in the operation of ambulances in transporting patients while exercising care and skill in driving. The successful incumbent will aid the paramedicine staff in patient care, such as proper lifting of patients and other related duties as required.

## Job Demands:

By applying for this job, you acknowledge an understanding that regular requirements and demands of this job include (but are not limited to):

• Regularly lifts and moves patients and equipment (between 25-50 lbs.) and involved in heavy lifting/pushing/pulling of stretchers (100 lbs.) and patients;

• Constantly stands, bends, stretches, kneels or pushes and pulls; sometimes in small and cramped spaces.

• Constantly requires visual concentration or alertness to drive ambulances, complete site and patient assessments and to administer medications. Regularly there are time pressures in the pre-hospital emergency setting.

• Regularly there is lack of control over work pace occurs due to the unpredictable situations during a medical emergency, or unpredictable call volume

## Qualifications:

• Graduation from an approved Advanced Care Paramedic or Primary Care Paramedic program, or Emergency Medical Responder course (10-day course) accredited by the Canadian Medical Association;

• Current registration with the NL Paramedicine Regulation as an ACP, PCP or EMR;

• Possession of a valid Class 4 Driver's License as issued by the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador;

• Medical authorization with the Office of the Provincial Medical Director (OPMD) is required and must be obtained upon successful completion of program orientation;

• Current certification in Basic Life Support;

• Current ACLS certification (ACP only);

• Current certification in PALS, or willingness to complete (ACP only)

• Effective oral and written communication skills;

• Critical and sound decision making skills;

• Successful completion of the Physical Capability testing certificate (within the last 3 months) and continued responsibility to meet the minimum standards of physical capability as outlined in provincial policy;

• For standby, must be able to report to work within the required timeframe of 10 minutes or be willing to stay at the base.

• A satisfactory record of work performance and attendance is required for this position;

• A satisfactory Driver’s Abstract from Motor Vehicle Registration is required;

• A satisfactory certificate of conduct from the RCMP or local police authority;

• Consistent demonstration of NL Health Service's core values; Innovation, Compassion, Accountability, Respect and Excellence (ICARE)

To assist us in processing your application, please include your Class 4 License, Driver's Abstract, and NLPR Registration (if obtained), along with your up-to-date resume, when applying for this position.

description:
## About NLHC

The Newfoundland and Labrador Housing Corporation (NL Housing) is a crown corporation whose mandate is to develop and administer housing assistance policy and programs for the benefit of low to moderate income households throughout the province. As the largest landlord in the Province, NL Housing manages a portfolio of over 5,500 units province-wide. The services provided by NL Housing provide clients with access to safe, stable and affordable housing, which is essential to the social, financial, and physical well-being of individuals, families and communities. There is a wide range of housing needs across the province, from those facing homelessness or at risk of homelessness, to low income households needing assistance to pay rent or complete much-needed repairs on their homes. For more information on our programs and services, and strategic priorities, please visit our website www.nlhc.nl.ca.

## About the Department/Region

Context:

The Community Partnerships and Homelessness Department provides research and analysis of best practices in social and transitional housing, homelessness prevention; and supports the development of the Provincial Housing & Homelessness Plan. The Department supports the CEO and the Minister Responsible for Housing through the development of position papers and briefing materials to support engagement and partnership across the housing continuum. The Department also provides oversight of the corporation's eviction prevention framework, tenant and community relations program as well as the delivery of the provincial supportive living program, emergency accommodations (including shelters), as well as transition houses.

## Position Details

Competition Number:2026/27-047-200813P

Employment Type: 1 Permanent Position

Department/Region: Community Partnerships and Homelessness

Location: Head Office, St. John's

Competition Status: Internal

Closing Date: October 9, 2026

Salary Scale: $51,615 to $57,330 per annum (CG-30, $28.36 to $31.50 per hour), 35-hour work week. Where applicable a shift differential will apply as per the Collective Agreement.

Note: The shift schedule and compensation model is currently under review and subject to change.

Duties: The incumbent will act as a resource person for the general public, clients, community agencies and other government departments to provide general information, guidance, support, and advice regarding policies, procedures and processes relating to the Emergency Housing Program. The Emergency Housing Officer determines eligibility for services by conducting preliminary investigations and/or gathering of information from external/internal sources; this may include, but is not limited to: assessing/verifying financial information, assessing complex needs and determining housing status, by consulting with homeless shelters, conducting in-person and telephone interviews with clients, and securing declarations to obtain information of a highly confidential nature. The incumbent provides information and refers clients to programs and services offered by NL Housing and other government departments/agencies. The Emergency Housing Officer maintains a caseload of clients in shelters, private accommodations and other living arrangements and coordinates with Social Work resources to ensure they are progressing through the housing continuum. The incumbent inputs daily call statistics and prepares service authorizations. The incumbent maintains regular contact with participants and organizations via phone, in person, appointments or on-site visits, and attends case conferences. The EHO also works as a part of the wider collaborative team to conduct shelter inspections. Work also includes representing NL Housing on various internal/external committees, reviewing and providing input on corporate policy, and contributing to the development of briefing notes. The incumbent must be able to organize and prioritize work in a fast-paced environment. This position is part of the after-hours on-call rotation. Other related work may be required.

## Screening Criteria

Crisis management and dispute resolution skills

Ability to effectively exchange information

Relationship building

You will be responsible for maintaining Utility Tractors, Rubber Tire Loaders, Graders, Tandem Trucks and all associated attachments including wings, plows, and sweepers.

You will not only repair, rebuild and make adjustments to our fleet, but also determine the reasoning for equipment malfunctions. To minimize such occurrences, preventative maintenance is a critical component in this role.
We will ensure you have the right tools to do the job, and there is nothing more important than your safety. You have a clean workspace, and your ideas and input are valued and considered. Knowledge and experience of computer-controlled engine diagnostic technology, electrical schematics, dealer purchased engine programs, online service manuals, and safety inspections are considered assets.

Air Conditioning Certification and a Motor Vehicle Inspection license would also be considered assets.

Work is performed in a mechanical repair environment occasioned by noise, smoke and gas fumes and at times adverse weather conditions while operating in a field environment. Considerable standing, lifting, carrying and moving about is a requirement of this position.
